*Suddenly somebody jumped out of nearby bushes.*
*A girl wearing a bright red T-Shirt with 'USSR' written on it.*
You: "Such a perfect reproduction of the age."
*She looked quite short from a distance and was probably younger than both pioneer girls – the one at the gates and this girl at the door of the 'Clubs'.*
*At last I decided to come closer, but the 'USSR' (as I called her in my mind) jumped towards the first girl and started telling her something while wildly waving her arms.*
*The other girl in turn seemed confused and lowered her gaze, remaining silent.*
*I would have probably continued to observe their amusing dialogue, but the 'USSR' suddenly pulled something out of her pocket and started waving it in front of the first girl's face.*
*This something turned out to be a grasshopper.*
Lena: "Eeeeee-eee-eeeeee!"
*The first girl squealed.*
*She must not be too keen on insects, as she instantly rushed off towards the place where Lenin presumably made his speech about the workers' and peasants' revolution.*
*That is to say, towards the square...*
*The 'USSR' glanced at me, grinned playfully, and dashed after her.*
You: "Not a bad start to the day."
You: "I have absolutely no clue where I am, besides that, there are some kids here roleplaying as pioneers."
You: "And, as far as I can tell, this place is located thousands of kilometres away from my home. It might even be a different reality."
*And this was indeed a reality...*
*I mean, everything around me seemed so real (if a little embellished) that I was starting to think that in fact my previous life could have been just a dream.*
You: "And what am I supposed to do now?"
*...*
*I was picking at the cracked paving stones with my shoe and staring aimlessly at the 'Clubs' building.*
You: "Just few more seconds before I have to come up with some decision."
*That’s when I recalled myself rolling on the grass, weeping...*
*I cringed in disgust.*
*Perhaps it's another instinct: when all energy for whimpering and self-pitying is used up, the body either goes into hibernation or mobilises its reserves.*
*Mine seemed to have chosen the second option, because out of the blue, I found the determination to figure out what was going on.*
*And in order to do that, I had to act like a man – like a human: to maintain the dignity of a representative of my own world.*
*I followed the path to the left, on the right side of which stood small cabins, apparently the homes of the local pioneers.*
*Actually, they looked quite cozy from the outside.*
*Even though I was born in the Soviet Union, I had never been part of its childrens organisations, neither the Pioneers nor even the younger October Children.*
*I imagined the daily life of a typical pioneer camp a bit differently: huge barracks with long rows of metal bunks, wake-up call at six o'clock played by a siren, one minute to make your bed, then joining the formation at the drill square...*
You: "Or wait! Could I be confusing it with something else...?"
*Suddenly something struck me on the back!*
*I staggered but remained on my feet, turned around and prepared to fight heroically for my life...*
*But all I found was another girl standing before me.*
*My mouth hung open in surprise.*
Alisa: "Pick your jaw up off the ground."
*I closed my mouth.*
*The same pioneer uniform, but the way she was wearing it looked, let’s say, provocative.*
*Like all the girls I had met here before, this one was rather cute, but her overly arrogant expression killed any desire to get to know her better.*
Alisa: "New here, are you?"
You: "…"
Alisa: "Fine, see ya!"
*She threw a threatening glance at me and walked past.*
*I waited for the pioneer girl to turn at the corner... Who knows what else she might have been up to!*
*The most interesting thing was that even this hostile girl seemed completely normal to me, she did not give off the feeling of some deadly danger.*
*Except maybe the danger of getting punched in the nose.*
*At last, I managed to make it to the square.*
*There was no Lenin on an armoured car, although one could easily expect something like that after all this had happened.*
*Instead, however, a monument to a certain comrade towered in the middle of the square. The letters on the pedestal read 'GENDA'.*
You: "Must be some big figure in the Party."
*There were some small benches at the sides.*
You: "It's quite pleasant here."
You: "Where did that girl tell me to go? To the left or to the right?"
You: "To the left, to the right, to the left, to the right…"
You: "And why am I going there anyway...?"
You: "Ah, right, I've decided to pretend to be normal..."
You: "So, to the right!"
*Through a small grove...*
*I came out at a pier.*
You: "I must have taken a wrong turn."
Slavya: "Hey, wrong way!"
*I turned towards the voice.*
*That first girl stood before me.*
Slavya: "Now what did I tell you? Take a left at the square, wasn't it?"
*She had changed from her pioneer uniform into a bikini.*
Slavya: "Oh, I still haven't introduced myself! My name is Slavya!"
Slavya: "Actually, my full name's Slavyana, but everyone calls me Slavya. So you can too!"
You: "Uhm... yeah..."
*I still felt a bit confused, so I could not come up with more meaningful answers.*
Slavya: "And what's your name?"
*It felt like she could see right through me.*
You: "Uhm... I... yeah... Semyon..."
Slavya: "Nice to meet you, Semyon."
Slavya: "All right, I'm almost done here. Could you wait here a minute, I'm going to change and we'll go to Olga Dmitrievna together, agreed?"
You: "Agreed..."
*After this exchange she ran off. I sat on the pier and let my feet hang into the water.*
*I was wearing heavy winter boots, but in such weather there was nothing wrong in getting my feet wet.*
*Furthermore, it let me cool myself a little.*
*Looking at the river, I was brainstorming and processing everything that has happened.*
You: "If this is some kind of conspiracy, it's a weird one, even too friendly at times."
You: "No, it really looks more like a random event."
You: "Some entirely incomprehensible random event."
Slavya: "Shall we go?"
*Slavya was standing beside me, dressed in the pioneer uniform again.*
You: "Let's go…"
You: "I've been here for a very short time, but of all the people I've met, she looks the least suspicious."
You: "However, this fact is already suspicious itself!"
*We walked to the square.*
*The 'USSR' girl and the girl who hit me on the back were there, chasing each other.*
You: "Is that some kind of game they’re playing?"
Slavya: "Ulyana, enough running! I'll tell everything to Olga Dmitrievna!"
Ulyana: "Aye-aye, captain!"
*I decided not to question Slavya for a while about what was going on or the local residents.*
You: "Better meet with this mysterious Olga Dmtrievna first."
You: "Sounds like she's the boss here."
*We walked past the rows of almost identical cabins, some of which looked like fat beer barrels, while others looked more like household sheds.*
*Finally, Slavya stopped in front of a smallish one-storey cabin.*
*It looked like an artist's painting: the faded paint, chipping here and there with age, was sparkling in the sun; the window shutters, slightly ajar, were swaying almost unnoticeably in the wind; and huge lilac bushes were growing at the sides.*
*It seemed as if this ramshackle hut was drowning in a storm of purple silk, and the lilacs, like some elemental force, were inexorably destroying the troop leader's house.*
Slavya: "What are you standing around for? Let's go!"
*Slavya snapped me out of my daydreaming.*
Olga: "... and stop teasing Lena already..."
*Rena?!*
You: "Sounds like there's someone inside."
*Indeed, a moment later the door swung open, and Ulyana ran out and dashed past with the same mischievous grin.*
*The pigtailed girl came out next.*
Slavya: "Don't let it bother you, Lena!"
You: "So her name is Lena... Gotta be thankful it's not Rena, at least!"
Lena: "But I don't..."
*Instead of finishing her sentence, she blushed and quickly headed towards the square.*
*For some reason I felt like turning and following her with my eyes, but Slavya said:*
Slavya: "Come."
*We entered the cabin.*
*Inside it looked something similar to what I'd imagined: two beds, a table, a couple of chairs, a simple carpet on the floor, a wardrobe.*
*Nothing special, but at the same time it felt homelike and cosy, although this room was almost in the same state of disorder as my own flat.*
*The girl standing near the window appeared to be about twenty five years old.*
You: "Nature had obviously gifted her with a pretty face and a good body..."
You: "At least one thing can keep you happy in this pandemonium: the locals are beautiful."
Olga: "You're finally here! Excellent! My name is Olga Dmitrievna, I'm the camp leader."
You: "Nice to meet you, I'm Semyon."
*I decided to talk as if I wasn't surprised by anything that was going on.*
*She came closer.*
Olga: "We've been expecting you since early morning."
You: "You've been expecting me...?"
Olga: "Yes, of course!"
You: "And when does the next bus come, 'cause I... "
Olga: "And why do you need it?"
You: "Yeah, right, why would I need it...?"
You: "Guess I shouldn't ask direct questions: the people here may react to them quite unlike how I'd prefer."
You: "And I doubt I'd get any answers."
You: "No reason, just curious..."
You: "By the way, where are we exactly? Our mailing address, I mean?"
You: "I wanted to send a letter to my parents to tell them I got here fine."
*For some reason, I had the desperate idea that if I played along, I would find something out.*
Olga: "Oh, but your parents called just half an hour ago! Sent their regards to you."
You: "Now that's a surprise..."
You: "So, can I call them? 'Cause I forgot to tell them something before I left."
Olga: "No."
*She gave me a sweet, spontaneous smile.*
You: "Why not?"
Olga: "We don't have a phone here."
You: "…"
You: "Then how could my parents make a call to here?"
Olga: "I've just come back from the district's central town, I talked with them there."
You: "Ah, so that's how it is?"
You: "And can I somehow get to the town?"
Olga: "No."
*She kept the same smile.*
You: "Why not?"
Olga: "Because the next bus only comes in a week."
*I decided not to inquire how the troop leader managed to get there and back; I would get no answer anyway.*
*All this time, Slavya was standing next to me and seemed to find nothing odd in our conversation.*
Olga: "Oh, we need to find a uniform for you!"
You: "I've got absolutely no desire to put on pioneer shorts or to wear the ridiculous red neckerchief!"
You: "However, wearing winter clothes in summer isn't a great idea either."
You: "Right, thank you…"
You: "I wonder if I'm the only one here who finds it strange that someone's wearing a coat and winter boots in such heat?"
Olga: "Righty-o, I'll be off then, and you can get yourself acquainted with the camp! Don't forget to come to dinner in the evening!"
*Having said that, she walked out of the cabin.*
*No, 'walked' is not the right word- she rushed out.*
*I ended up alone with Slavya.*
Slavya: "I must go too, got things to do."
Slavya: "Take a walk, look around the camp a bit. See you in the evening."
You: "If there is no threat or catch to this then this reality, as embodied by Slavya, becomes more and more appealing."
*...*
*For the first time today I realised that it was awfully hot here.*
*Although, obviously, my winter clothes were to blame for that.*
*I took off my coat and dropped it onto the bed, my pullover followed it; I was now wearing only the shirt.*
You: "That's much better!"
*All I could do now was follow their advice and go look around the camp.*
You: "I'll try to find something out in the meantime."
*Passing the local 'residential district', I saw a pioneer guy coming my way.*
*And it was really a pioneer guy, not a pioneer girl. Apparently there were men even in this kingdom of Amazons.*
Sergei: "Hello, you're new here, you must be Semyon, right?"
You: "And how do you...?"
Sergei: "Everyone knows already! I'm Electronik, by the way. The real one. You can call me that."
You: "Electronik. The real one. Things were going from 'crazy' to 'completely insane'."
You: "All right..."
Sergei: "Ulyana also calls me Cheesie."
You: "Cheesie?"
You: "On toast, with mushrooms?"
Sergei: "Because my last name is Cheesekov."
You: "I see..."
Sergei: "Let me show you around!"
*I accepted his offer, as it would have taken much longer to get to know this place alone.*
You: "Fine, let's go."
*We ended up at the square again.*
You: "As if this place was all there is to this camp..."
*Lena was sitting on one of the benches, reading some book. Electronik confidently approached her.*
Sergei: "Hello, Lena! Meet the new guy, Semyon."
*He started briskly.*
You: "Hello. Well, you could say we've already met, in a way."
Lena: "Yes…"
*She looked away from the book for a moment, glanced at me, blushed and went back to reading, as if not noticing that we were still here.*
Sergei: "All right, let's go on."
*I was at first surprised that 'meeting' this girl was reduced to a couple of words, but then I thought that it was better that way. Electronik's vigorous activity did not fit well with Lena's shyness.*
You: "Let's go."
*Next we came to a building, which I instantly identified as a canteen.*
Sergei: "And this here..."
You: "I know! This is where you consume organic food!"
Sergei: "Yeah, something like that…"
*On the canteen's porch stood the unfriendly girl who hit me on the back earlier.*
*At the sight of her, my joking mood vanished in a blink of an eye.*
You: "Really, now is not the best time to be pulling this guy's leg, even though he is quite hilarious."
You: "First I need to figure out what's what here, or at least where I am!"
Sergei: "Her, over there, that's Alisa Dvachevskaya. Be careful around her."
*He spoke in a whisper.*
Sergei: "Don't ever risk calling her DvaCheh, she doesn't like that!"
Alisa: "What did you say? What did you call me?"
*She must have heard him.*
*In the blink of an eye, Alisa jumped down from the porch and dashed towards us.*
Sergei: "All right, you'll manage from here onwards..."
*Electronik took to his heels.*
*I decided that I had no wish to come across this aggressive Alisa girl again and darted after Electronik.*
*Running to the square, I lost sight of him.*
*But Dvachevskaya wasn't chasing me either.*
You: "However, I really should not risk calling her that. Even in my mind..."
*After catching my breath, I wondered why I had reacted like that.*
You: "All right, she is a girl... an aggressive one... But why run away?"
*Failing to find a good answer, I sat down on a bench and stared at the monument to Genda.*
*Alisa, running past, stopped for a moment and growled:*
Alisa: "I'll deal with you later!"
You: "Deal with me? What did I do wrong!?"
*I added a forced guilty smile to my words.*
You: "But what am I guilty of...?"
*She made no reply and carried on chasing Electronik.*
*...*
You: "Looks like I'll have to kill time alone, waiting for dinner."
*I decided to go east. At least in the direction where east would be in my world.*
*Soon after, I found myself near a football pitch.*
*A game was in full swing there.*
You: "I guess watching it for a bit wouldn’t do any harm."
*In my childhood and teen years I was not a bad player myself and even thought of going professional, but a few injuries in a row killed my desire to risk my health for the sake of uncertain chance in the game.*
*Kids of different ages were running around the pitch: I could see a boy of about ten and a girl of about fourteen years old...*
You: "A girl... Hey, that's Ulyana!"
You: "All right, so she plays football - what's so surprising?"
You: "She seems a restless one, after all."
*I was standing quite far from the pitch, but she still noticed me.*
Ulyana: "Hey, you!"
*Ulyana shouted.*
Ulyana: "Wanna play?"
*I didn't know how to answer.*
You: "On the one hand, running around for ten minutes is no big deal."
You: "On the other hand, any wrong move in my situation could be my final one."
*But in any case, my attire wasn't suitable for this weather.*
*If I played in winter boots and warm jeans, I would sweat like a pig.*
You: "And playing barefoot and without jeans would be simply unethical."
You: "Maybe another time, all right?"
*I shouted in response, turned around and walked back.*
*I was followed by Ulyana's screams, about my pants, or about me being a pansy, or something like that...*
*...*
*Evening was falling, making me feel tired and empty after a day wasted with no real purpose.*
*...*
*I came back to the square, sat down on a bench and gave an exhausted sigh.*
You: "I'd better sit here and wait for dinner. After all, it's easier to search for answers when you're not hungry."
You: "They do give food to the people here, right...?"
You: "You know, it's curious how the simplest human needs can break the will to ponder on things, to strive for something."
You: "For example, I feel hungry now, so I care much less about where I am or what is happening to me."
You: "Could great people also be affected by this?"
You: "And in that case, how did Spartacus start the slave uprising in ancient times...?"
You: "I can only conclude that I am not a great person, and it does not really matter which mechanism I serve as a gear in: society, the Matrix, or a weird pioneer camp."
*My thoughts were interrupted by the sound of bells chiming from a loudspeaker on a light pole.*
You: "It must be the dinner call!"
*I headed towards the canteen; it was a good thing that now I knew where it was.*
*Olga Dmitrievna was there, standing on the porch.*
*I stopped and looked closely at her, as if I were expecting something.*
*She looked back at me for a while, but at last came closer.*
Olga: "Semyon, what are you waiting for? Come in already!"
You: "Guess nothing bad can happen if I go with her."
*My stomach backed me up here.*
*The two of us went inside.*
*The canteen looked like... a canteen.*
*I'd had a chance to visit a factory canteen at some point in my life... This one was exactly the same, just maybe a bit cleaner and more modern.*
*Metal chairs and tables, glazed tiles on the walls and on the floor, unsophisticated tableware with the occasional crack.*
You: "Guess that's what a canteen in a pioneer camp supposed to look like."
Olga: "Semyon, wait a moment, we'll find you a place to sit…"
*She looked around the place.*
Olga: "Dvachevskaya, hold it right there!"
*Olga Dmitrievna shouted at Alisa who was passing by.*
Alisa: "What?"
Olga: "What's up with your clothes?"
Alisa: "Anything wrong with them?"
*Indeed, her attire looked somewhat provocative...*
Olga: "Get your uniform nice and neat right now!"
Alisa: "All right, all right..."
*Alisa got her shirt right and walked past, shooting an unpleasant glare at me.*
Olga: "So, where can we find you a place to sit?"
*There weren't a lot of free seats.*
Olga: "Go over there, next to Ulyana!"
You: "Uhm... Maybe I..."
Olga: "Yeah, it's fine, the food's already on the table, too!"
*I had no other choice but to accept.*
*Of course, there was the probability that the cutlets were poisoned with curare, the mashed potatoes generously seasoned with arsenic, and the glass filled with excellent antifreeze instead of kompot...*
*But it all looked so tasty that I had no chance to resist!*
Ulyana: "Hey!"
You: "Whaddaya want?"
*I replied rather rudely to Ulyana, who was sitting next to me.*
Ulyana: "Why didn't you play football with us?"
You: "Because of my clothes."
*Said I, pointing at the source of the problem.*
Ulyana: "Oh, all right then, eat."
*However, there wasn't much left to eat: my cutlet was missing from the plate!*
You: "Only she could have done it."
You: "No, more precisely, none but Ulyana could have done it!"
You: "Give me back my cutlet!"
Ulyana: "In a big family, you snooze, you lose! It can cost you a cutlet if you are careless!"
You: "Give it back, I'm telling you!"
*I looked at her menacingly and was about to reach out my hand...*
Ulyana: "See, I don't have it!"
*And indeed, Ulyana's plate was empty; it seemed that this little girl eats as fast as she steals someone’s cutlets.*
Ulyana: "Take it easy, we'll work something out now!"
*She grabbed my plate and ran off.*
*There was no point in following her: if they wanted to poison me here, they could have done it in a much easier way.*
*About a minute later, Ulyana returned and handed me the plate with a steaming hot cutlet on it.*
Ulyana: "Here's one for the starving!"
You: "Thanks…"
*It was all I could say.*
*I was so hungry that my suspicions were gone in a flash. I picked up the cutlet with my fork and...*
You: "What the!? Some bug! No, not a bug! An insect! It got legs and it's wiggling!"
*The plate fell to the floor and broke into pieces; the chair hit me hard on my leg while falling.*
*I've disliked insects since I was a child, but when these creepy-crawlies appear in my plate, that's just way too much!*
You: "You little..."
*Ulyana seemed ready for such a twist and was already at the door, laughing as if she had just heard a fresh stand-up comedy joke.*
*I dashed after her.*
*We ran out of the canteen.*
*We were just a few dozen metres apart, and I felt I would catch this little girl easily.*
*We ran through the square...*
*Past the clubs' house...*
*And ran onto the forest path.*
*I started to gasp for breath.*
You: "I should have quit smoking I guess…"
*Ulyana passed out of sight on the next turn.*
You: "It can't be true that she managed to get away from me!"
You: "It simply can't!"
*I stopped and tried to catch my breath again.*
*...*
*Night was falling.*
You: "Looks like I'm lost…"
You: "It's a bad idea to stay in the woods at night; better get back to the camp."
*However, I had absolutely no clue which way to go.*
You: "Well, gotta choose at random."
*...*
*...*
*I wandered for quite some time in the forest and even thought of crying for help, but finally I saw the camp's fence beyond the trees.*
You: "Everything fell back into place."
You: "The bus is gone..."
*I mumbled quietly.*
*On the one hand, there was nothing strange about that: the bus couldn't just stay there forever.*
*On the other hand, it meant there was someone driving, because buses do not drive themselves!*
You: "Or do they?"
*This world seemed too normal, but every event here had at least two explanations for it: an ordinary, real, everyday explanation, and a surreal one.*
*Certainly, the driver could have just been off for a snack, and I left too soon, and that's why...*
You: "In any case, this is not the place for me!"
*Whether that bus drives itself or not was probably an important question, but it was much more important to know how I had got here at all.*
*And where this here was...*
*The fields and the woods, stretching towards the horizon, had no answers; there was nothing familiar about them.*
*...*
*A strange, odd, and alien world. However, at the same time it was absolutely not frightening.*
*Either my self-preservation instinct decided to resign from its job, or all this running around the camp and the local pioneers had lulled me so much with their carefree normality that I was simply forgetting what had happened to me just a couple of hours ago.*
*Although I probably just had no strength left to worry.*
*All I wanted was some peace, calmness; I wanted to just have a break from it all, and only after that would I continue looking for answers, ready and reloaded.*
*However, that would be some time later...*
You: "And what about now? Can I allow myself to relax?"
*...*
*It got completely dark, and in any case it was better to spend the night in the camp.*
*I was about to head back when someone came up silently from behind.*
Slavya: "Hello, what are you doing here so late?"
You: "..."
*It was Slavya standing before me. I was so surprised that I jumped.*
Slavya: "So, you didn't catch Ulyana, did you?"
*She smiled.*
*I nodded disappointedly and sighed.*
Slavya: "No wonder. No one ever has."
You: "Yeah, she's a real rocket girl. She could have found a better use for her energy than looking for adventures..."
Slavya: "You must be hungry, you didn’t manage to have dinner after all..."
*Indeed, I had completely forgot about my hunger, but after these words of hers my stomach drew attention to itself by giving a traitorous rumble.*
*Slavya smiled.*
Slavya: "Let's go then."
You: "What, is the canteen still open?"
Slavya: "It's all right, I have the keys."
You: "The keys?"
Slavya: "Yes, I have keys to all the facilities in this camp."
You: "How come?"
Slavya: "Well, I'm something like the camp leader's aide here."
You: "I see. Well, let's go."
*It was an offer you can’t refuse.*
*When we reached the square, Slavya stopped in her tracks.*
Slavya: "Excuse me, I should warn my roommate that I'll be late; she's so punctual herself that she'll be worried otherwise."
Slavya: "You go on to the canteen, and I'll come in a minute, alright?"
You: "Alright..."
*I really did not expect to find somebody aside from myself there at such a late hour.*
*And that somebody was apparently trying hopelessly to open the door.*
*Without any secret thoughts, I walked up onto the porch.*
*The lock picker turned out to be Alisa.*
You: "I should have probably kept off and waited... "
*She looked at me intently for a while, then said:*
Alisa: "Don't just stand there, give me a hand or something!"
You: "Meaning?"
Alisa: "Help me open the door!"
You: "Why?"
Alisa: "'Cause I want some buns and kefir! Dinner wasn't big enough!"
You: "Uhmmm... Is that really a good idea?"
Alisa: "Aren't you hungry yourself, huh? Ulyana didn't let you have a normal dinner, did she?"
*She smiled sarcastically.*
You: "It's true, she didn't..."
You: "It's fine, Slavya will come now and..."
Alisa: "WHAT?!"
You: "Guess I shouldn't have said that."
Alisa: "I'm off then!"
Alisa: "And you'll pay for this! You owe me two already!"
*Having said that, Alisa disappeared into the night.*
You: "And what was the first one?"
*...*
*Slavya didn't keep me waiting for too long.*
Slavya: "Is everything alright?"
You: "Yeah, why are you asking?"
Slavya: "No reason, it's nothing."
*It would be better if I didn't tell her about Alisa.*
You: "Everything's fine."
*I said that and immediately heard a note of dishonesty in my voice.*
Slavya: "Well, shall we go?"
*As for Slavya, she seemed not to have noticed anything. Or at least she was pretending she hadn't.*
*We entered the canteen.*
Slavya: "Wait a bit, I'll go get something."
*I sat down on a chair and obediently waited for my saviour.*
*My dinner was simple: a few buns and a glass of kefir.*
You: "No wonder: I bet hungry pioneers finished everything off."
*However, even that was far better than most of my usual diet.*
*Slavya sat across the table and looked at me while I was eating.*
You: "Is there something on my face?"
Slavya: "No, just…"
*She smiled.*
Slavya: "So, how did you like your first day in the camp?"
You: "Well, I don't really know..."
*It's silly to ask someone who suddenly found himself in a different reality whether he liked the food in the canteen, the camp leader, or his assigned hut.*
Slavya: "It's alright, you'll soon get used to it!"
*Slavya stared out the window dreamily.*
You: "Frankly speaking, I have no desire to get used to such things; but as for her, she doesn't know..."
You: "Or at least she wants me to think that she doesn't."
You: "Well, all in all, it's nice here."
*I had to somehow break the awkward silence.*
Slavya: "Do you think so?"
*She asked without any interest.*
You: "Yeah. This place is so..."
*I wanted to say 'retro', but I managed to hold that back.*
*After all, it was retro for me, but what about them? It might be the only kind of life they knew.*
*If the term life was applicable here at all...*
Slavya: "So how?"
*She watched me closely. As if something important depended on my answer.*
You: "Well, I don't know... lovely. Yeah! It's lovely here."
Slavya: "I guess you're right."
*She smiled again.*
Slavya: "It's very good that you think so."
You: "Why?"
Slavya: "Well, not everybody likes it here..."
You: "And what about you?"
Slavya: "Me?"
You: "Yes."
Slavya: "I love it here, it's great."
You: "Then you don't need to worry about what other people think."
Slavya: "Well, I don't really worry."
*Slavya laughed.*
*This conversation seemed to be leading me far astray from where I wanted to get to.*
Slavya: "And you're worried yourself..."
You: "Really? Why do you say so?"
Slavya: "Well, when someone is chewing so intensely..."
You: "I'm sorry."
Slavya: "It's okay."
*I couldn't bring myself to be more cautious around this girl.*
*But why her in particular? Why not any other local inhabitant?*
*Every one of them looked completely normal to me. Precisely normal, so normal it sends chills down my spine and into my marrow!*
*Normal, not like a neighbor with a power drill in one hand and a subwoofer in the other.*
*Not like a passenger you can often meet in a subway or on public transport.*
*Not like a coworker at the next table in an open plan office.*
*And not even like a friend who only differs from other humans in his constant insistence.*
*All of them looked normal – as I would expect them to be – with their own downsides but without any superpowers.*
*And Slavya was also... cute?*
*I glanced at her stealthily, not knowing what to say.*
Slavya: "I'm sorry, I wanted to show you the camp but was ran off my feet."
You: "I... didn't miss anything while on my own, I guess."
Slavya: "Are you sure you haven't missed anything at all?"
*She smiled so brightly that I had to drop my eyes in confusion.*
You: "Well, how would I know – it's my first day here."
Slavya: "Okay, and what have you seen so far?"
You: "I've seen the square, this canteen, the football field..."
Slavya: "And what about the beach?"
You: "Just from afar."
Slavya: "You really should go there! Or let's do it together!"
You: "Yeah, ok... We will..."
*Her naturalness started to scare me, but then I thought – what if everything that happens here is how it supposed to be and this world looks strange only to me, while for them it is... normal?*
*Maybe I was thrown into the past...?*
*Yes, that would explain a lot.*
You: "Can I ask a stupid question?"
Slavya: "No."
*Slavya smiled and stood up from the table.*
Slavya: "It's late... Can you find the way to Olga Dmitrievna's by yourself?"
You: "Of course I can, but why should I go there?"
Slavya: "She'll settle you with someone."
You: "What for?"
*Probably this question seemed stupid, because Slavya bursted into good-natured laughter.*
Slavya: "You need to sleep somewhere, right?"
You: "That makes sense..."
Slavya: "Fine, I'll be off then. Good night!"
You: "Night..."
You: "It's strange that she left in such a hurry..."
*A bundle of keys left in the door lock caught my attention.*
*I was going to catch up to Slavya, but where does she live?*
*And knocking on every door during the middle of the night didn't sound like a bright idea.*
You: "I'd better take them – I'll give them back tomorrow because who knows what happens here at night."
*Such thoughts gave me chills – it's me who needs to be careful here in the first place.*
You: "On the other hand why would I need them..."
*The night, though dark, wasn't silent at all – one could hear chirping crickets, the songs of the night birds and rustling trees from everywhere.*
*A sudden desire to follow Slavya's advice and go to the camp leader’s cabin appeared.*
*I don't know why but the sight of the unknown bronze builder of communism put me in a constructive mood.*
*I sat on the bench and started to recall everything that happened today. That was all my constructive mood could offer.*
*Here was much brighter than near the canteen, and tardy pioneers were running by, so this place didn't seem scary at all.*
You: "Bus, summer camp, girls…"
*I was so tired from everything new and strange that I could not come up with a single explanation for what was going on.*
*I heard a barely noticeable rustle nearby.*
*I shivered and looked in that direction.*
You: "A girl. Reading a book."
You: "Lena."
*I decided to move closer and talk.*
*She was the only new person I had met here without exchanging even a few words.*
You: "Hi, what are you reading?"
*Lena was so surprised that she even jumped.*
You: "Sorry, didn't mean to scare you!"
Lena: "Never mind..."
*She blushed and stared at the book again.*
You: "So what are you reading?"
*On the cover was written 'Gone with the Wind'.*
You: "A good book…"
Lena: "Thanks."
You: "Honestly speaking, I haven't read it but I think that such literature suits her very well."
*Lena didn't seem to be interested in continuing the conversation.*
You: "Well, if I'm bothering you..."
Lena: "No."
*She answered while still looking at the book.*
You: "Can I sit beside you for a while?"
Lena: "Why?"
You: "And really, why...?"
*Maybe just because I was very tired and having company is better than being alone.*
*And maybe I wanted try to find something out from her.*
*I carefully examined Lena.*
You: "But no, I doubt that..."
You: "Well, I don't know... I'm not allowed to?"
Lena: "Feel free..."
You: "But if I'm bothering you..."
Lena: "No, you're not."
You: "I can leave, just say..."
Lena: "Everything’s alright."
You: "Ok then..."
*I sat on the end of the bench carefully.*
*After such an intense talk, staying here was the last thing I wanted, but it wouldn't be nice to just stand up and leave.*
You: "That didn’t really go well, huh?"
*Lena hasn't answered anything.*
*It seems I made a fool out of myself.*
*I bet if Ulyana was here she'd have a good laugh at me.*
You: "Do you enjoy being here?"
*I recalled the Slavya's question and thought it would be a good start for a conversation.*
Lena: "Yes."
*She smiled slightly.*
You: "I guess I like it too..."
*Lena definitely isn't very sociable and probably can't carry on a meaningless conversation as easily as Slavya.*
*But there was something about her that attracted attention.*
*Like a momentary glimpse of a reflection in the glass on a rainy autumn evening, which makes you turn around and stare into darkness searching for something that you saw out of the corner of your eye.*
*Of course you weren’t able to distinguish or understand what it was but it still felt so tempting...*
*Lena was still reading the book without paying any attention to my presence.*
*And I had no intention of asking her anything about this camp or this world in general.*
You: "Beautiful night..."
Lena: "Yes..."
You: "How in a world would you start a conversation with her?"
Lena: "It's late, I have to go…"
You: "Yes, it's quite late…"
Lena: "Good night."
You: "Night…"
*There was something strange about this girl.*
You: "At first glance she is a typically shy and modest pioneer girl, but…"
*The mystery of Lena took its own place in the massive list of mysteries about this camp which I had started to put together in my head.*
*...*
You: "A lazy evening, there’s nothing like a good time with nothing to do…"
*I headed towards Olga Dmitrievna’s cabin.*
*The light in the house was on.*
Olga: "Hello, Semyon! You're quite late!"
You: "Yeah… I went for a walk to look around the camp."
Olga: "Alright. You will be sleeping here."
*She pointed her finger at one of the beds.*
You: "Right here...?"
*I was a bit surprised.*
Olga: "Yeah, is something wrong? We are out of free cabins anyway."
*The camp leader smiled, but I rather think it was just out of politeness.*
Olga: "You do want to be a decent pioneer, don't you?"
*There was a clear emphasis on the word 'decent'.*
You: "Yep... Sure..."
*I was lost in thought for a moment.*
You: "Don’t ya mind it mademoiselle?"
*She looked at me oddly. With surprise and some offense in her eyes.*
Olga: "A pioneer should respect their elders!"
* Olga Dmitrievna said strictly.*
You: "Of course he should, no one argues with that…"
*I blathered, not realising what was wrong.*
Olga: "Shouldn't you also...?"
*She stared at me.*
*Under such a gaze even mithril forged by the best dwarf masters from the deepest dungeons would melt.*
You: "Should I what? What's up, toots?"
*Annoyance and a lack of understanding made me raise my voice.*
Olga: "You must address adults appropriately!"
You: "Yes, of course there are a lot of strange things here… But this girl is just a couple years older than me..."
You: "Or maybe even younger..."
*But I decided not to argue – while just a few minutes ago I would never have called her an adult, I have to admit that she was also given a strong character.*
*And in any case I wasn't in a position to argue.*
You: "As you say… ma'am."
*I mumbled.*
Olga: "That's much better! That is how a decent pioneer should conduct himself!"
Olga: "And now it's time to sleep!"
*Honestly speaking, I was going to become neither a decent nor an indecent pioneer.*
*Just yesterday I wasn't going to become a pioneer at all...*
You: "But do I have choice now?"
*'If you don't want to, we'll have to make you' – this is the motto Olga Dmitrievna was probably going to use.*
*I climbed onto the bed and closed my eyes only to realise how tired I was after today.*
*Something hammered in my head awfully, as if my brains had started a night shift.*
*And they seemed to be aimed more at rolling steel than working on something more sensitive.*
*The bus flew through my mind...*
*And the square with the monument...*
*The canteen, full of pioneers... And the malicious face of Ulyana.*
*Slavya...*
*Lena...*
*And even recalling Alisa didn’t give me too much of a negative feeling.*
You: "What if I'm here for good...?"
*I was having a dream...*
*It seemed like I was in some kind of vacuum, with nothing but nothing around me.*
*But not only around: I was the only creature in the universe.*
*As if the universe had returned to a state of singularity right before the Big Bang.*
*And something was just about to happen.*
*Suddenly I heard a voice.*
*I could not make out the words, but it sounded familiar.*
*The voice was whispering something gently, as if soothing me.*
*And then I realised.... It was the voice of that strange girl from the bus. The girl from the dream.*
You: "But what is she trying to tell me? Who is she...?"
*I woke up.*
*Bright sunlight struck my eyes.*
*It was almost noon.*
*After stretching lazily on the bed and yawning, I started to recall the previous day.*
*In few seconds, all its events passed before my eyes: the bus, the camp, the local inhabitants.*
You: "No, that's just wrong!"
*Not this whole situation, not me being here – it was wrong by default – my attitude towards what was happening was wrong.*
You: "Because yesterday I fell asleep here just like that, and before that I chatted nicely with the local pioneers, even managed to crack a few jokes!"
You: "How could I act like that in such a situation?!"
You: "I should be frightened, startled by every little rustling, should avoid all contact with the potentially hostile creatures."
*The last day's events were getting hazy, like I had a hangover.*
You: "This really feels like the morning after a heavy drinking party - yesterday's natural, flawless, absolutely normal conduct becomes a nightmare in the morning, a grotesque illustration from 'The Divine Comedy'."
You: "Yes, it's just like that, and I can't change the past now."
*Then again, I had probably assessed the situation and was acting accordingly.*
*I glanced around, trying to figure out whether I had been thrown somewhere else, but Olga Dmitrievna's cabin looked the same as yesterday.*
*Everything seemed to be in its place, except for a pioneer uniform, which was hanging from the bed-head.*
*I fumbled with it in distrust and tried it on.*
You: "At least this is better than walking around in winter clothes."
You: "Wish I could see myself – bet I look like a clown!"
*And for that, I needed a mirror. At least a tiny one.*
*I finally found one on the wardrobe door.*
You: "Holy...!"
*I looked at the newfound pioneer and jumped away in surprise!*
*There was some teenager on the other side of the mirror!*
*He resembled me, but he wasn't me!*
*Where did the week's stubble go, where were the bags under my eyes, the slouch, that deathly fatigue on my face?!*
*It seemed that I had not been thrown back in time or into a parallel reality, but instead had simply changed bodies with someone else.*
You: "Right, that's real simple! Such things happen every day!"
*I took a closer look at this stranger and only then I realised that it actually was me!*
*It just wasn't today's me - maybe the one from between my school and university years.*
You: "Well, at least that's something."
You: "There you go, the person in an extreme situation did fail to notice the elephant in the room after all."
You: "But the camp leader noticed it, and last night she told me off for addressing her without proper respect..."
You: "Ah, screw that!"
You: "I doubt my appearance affects anything else."
*If the clock was not lying, breakfast was long over.*
You: "Oh well, I'll try to find something in the canteen."
You: "It worked out well yesterday with Slavya, didn't it?"
*Those memories made me smile involuntarily.*
*The sun was shining brightly outside, a light breeze was blowing.*
You: "A beautiful summer day."
*I had not felt so good in the morning for several years.*
*All problems were gone, vanished into clouds that were white as snow.*
*Olga Dmitrievna came out of nowhere.*
Olga: "Good morning, Semyon!"
You: "Morning!"
*I smiled, doing my best to show that, no matter what, my morning was indeed good.*
Olga: "You only arrived yesterday, so I decided not to wake you up, but breakfast..."
Olga: "Nevermind! Here, take this!"
*She handed me something wrapped in paper.*
*Judging by the oily stains, there had to be sandwiches inside.*
You: "Oh, thank you!"
Olga: "Now go wash yourself!"
*I was about to leave.*
Olga: "Wait a second."
*Olga Dmitrievna quickly ran into the house and came out to shove a small bag into my hands.*
*Inside it I found a toothbrush, soap, a small towel and something else – I did not look too closely.*
Olga: "A pioneer should always be clean and tidy!"
Olga: "Let me do your neckerchief properly this first time, yours is askew. You should do it yourself once you learn how to."
You: "Do we have to? I am going to wash myself now."
You: "Yeah, right, it could get hooked on the tap and strangle me..."
Olga: "Fine, later then. And don't forget about the lineup."
You: "Pencils, paper, drawing lines... You don't forget such things!"
You: "What lineup?"
Olga: "What do you mean 'what lineup'?!"
*She frowned.*
Olga: "It's Monday today!"
You: "Weird, by my approximation it should have been Sunday."
You: "Then again, a shift in the day of the week is hardly the worst thing."
Olga: "Usually we have lineups early in the morning before breakfast, but it's Monday today, so we are having it at 12 o'clock."
Olga: "Don't be late!"
You: "Alright. But where?"
Olga: "At the square, where else?!"
*There was no reason to argue.*
*I headed to the 'bathing place'.*
*I knew I could forget about separate showers and toilet, but at the sight of this malfunctioning symptom of decaying socialism – a funny turtle with a tin shell, paw-taps and a ceramic belly – I felt sick.*
*I was not a squeamish person, but nevertheless, standing there I realised that there was still some minimal level of habitual comfort which I found it troublesome to do without.*
*It's often like that – when you lose things that you thought were ordinary and common you suddenly understand just how essential they were.*
You: "Ah, screw this! As if I have any choice."
*The water was ice-cold.*
*While washing my hands was not an issue, washing my face and my mouth became a big problem.*
*There was no toothpaste in the bag which Olga Dmitrievna gave me.*
*I could brush my teeth without it, but there was a small round box wrapped in the towel.*
*'Tooth powder'.*
You: "Cute! One point for me being somewhere in the past."
*I washed myself quite quickly, also due to the ice-cold water.*
*Someone was coming quickly, or more like running towards me.*
*I turned around.*
*It was Slavya, dressed in a tracksuit.*
*This girl would probably look good in anything: pioneer uniform, bikini, probably even a spacesuit.*
Slavya: "Hey there!"
You: "Ohayo... I mean, wassu... Good morning! Yeah..."
*Oh yeah, real smooth.*
Slavya: "Why didn't you come for breakfast?"
You: "I overslept."
*I said it as if I was proud about it.*
You: "But Olga Dmitrievna gave me some sandwiches."
Slavya: "Oh, great then! Don't forget about the lineup!"
You: "Yeah, sure."
You: "As if I could forget."
Slavya: "Right, I gotta run! Enjoy yourself!"
*She waved goodbye to me and disappeared around the path's bend.*
You: "Looks like it's a couple of minutes until the lineup."
*I should quickly pass by my 'home' to drop off my washing bag and eat the sandwiches, and then head to the square.*
*I swung open the door of the camp leader's cabin and rushed inside, as if jumping into the last car of a departing train.*
*It didn’t turn out to be the best idea, because inside I found Olga Dmitrievna...*
*Who was changing!*
*I froze on the spot, trying not to breathe.*
*Finally the camp leader noticed me.*
Olga: "Semyon!"
*I looked away immediately.*
Olga: "Have you heard of knocking!? Now get out!"
You: "Yeah, that was real clumsy."
*Although I did enjoy the sight.*
*Olga Dmitrievna followed me out in a minute.*
Olga: "Here, take this. Now it is your home too."
*She handed me a key. I put it in my pocket.*
You: "Home…"
You: "Of course, if you disregard how fantastical the current events were, this camp was far from being the worst place on Earth, but to call it home..."
You: "Just after one day spent here!"
You: "I doubt I'll ever be able to do so."
Olga: "Alright, let's go, we're late."
You: "But what about the sandwiches...?"
Olga: "Just eat them on the way!"
*We were passing along the lines of the pioneers' cabins while I was tucking into the ham sandwiches and Olga Dmitrievna kept on talking and talking. She was buzzing like a game of Operation with parkinson’s!*
*But I cared about nothing but the food.*
Olga: "Understood?"
You: "Huh?"
Olga: "You weren't listening!"
You: "Sorry…"
Olga: "Today is the first day of your new life as a pioneer!"
Olga: "And you should do your best so that it becomes a happy life!"
You: "Ah, yeah, definitely..."
Olga: "I'm serious! A pioneer has many duties, great responsibility is conferred upon him: to participate in social work, to help his juniors, to study, and study and study again!"
Olga: "We here are all like one big family. And you will become a part of it."
You: "Yeah, a part... I'd even sign a Party membership card, if it could save me from listening to this nonsense."
Olga: "I hope that after your term here is over, you'll keep the most pleasant memories about our camp."
Olga: "Memories that will last your whole life!"
You: "And when will this term end?"
Olga: "Why do you keep asking silly things?"
You: "It seems I won't get any information from her ."
*A shame really. This world appears to be so friendly, but it never bothered to introduce itself to me.*
You: "Perhaps now I can take things somewhat easier than yesterday?"
*It seems like I have some unspoken ceasefire with it – it isn't trying to hurt me, but I'm forbidden from asking questions.*
*Of course, this situation isn't a pleasant one, but what can I do about it? A bad peace is better than a good dispute.*
Olga: "The most important thing for you now is to make the best of the time you will spend here."
You: "I'll do my best."
*Honestly, I was very tired of this conversation.*
*It would be good to know where that 'here' is! But...*
*We came to the square.*
*The pioneers were already lined up.*
You: "What, is somebody not here yet?"
Olga: "Hmm, nope. All here."
*She looked around at her brave pioneer troops.*
Olga: "Alright, go stand somewhere."
You: "Weird. Why did she tell me there are no more sleeping places?"
*While the chief was running her mouth about our plans for the week, I stared at the people.*
*A few heads away from me stood Electronik, a little further – Lena and Slavya, and at the end of the line – Ulyana and Alisa.*
You: "Everyone I had met was here."
*Olga Dmitrievna spoke about some competitions, and I turned my attention to the monument.*
You: "'Genda'..."
*I could not remember any revolutionary with a similar name...*
*He had a weird posture too– as if he was looking around with distrust, maybe contempt, or even disdain.*
You: "Probably some local leader…"
Slavya: "Daydreaming again?"
*Slavya brought me back to reality.*
*Olga Dmitrievna stood nearby.*
Olga: "Still remember the plan for the week?"
You: "The plan? I will never forget the Plan!"
Olga: "Perfect!"
*She looked at Slavya.*
Olga: "Did you bring it?"
Slavya: "Yes."
*Slavya handed me a piece of paper.*
Olga: "It's a checklist. Here are four tasks to check off. Do it all today."
Olga: "Before you start, sign up for a club. There are some clubs in the clubhouse, and a musical club in the separate building."
Olga: "Then, visit the infirmary."
Olga: "And finally, visit the library."
Olga: "Got it?"
You: "Yes."
*The checklist seemed like a good chance to find out something, since I had to go to places I haven't been before.*
Olga: "Then come on, start right now."
You: "What about lunch?"
Olga: "Don't worry! I'll bring you more sandwitches. The checklist is more important!"
Slavya: "Good luck."
*They departed too fast for me to ask anything else.*
You: "Missed breakfast, now I'll miss lunch too."
You: "This ain't good."
You: "Maybe I'll manage it in time somehow?"
You: "Lunch starts at 1 pm. Then again if I'll go there I might miss a place from the checklist. "
You: "Okay, it's too early to go to the canteen anyway!"
*The music club, a small one-level building, was located some distance from the other camp buildings.*
*I opened the door and entered without hesitation.*
*There were enough instruments for a whole orchestra here: drums, guitars, even a piano.*
*I spent some time looking closely at every instrument, wanting to guess the time period they were from, but suddenly I heard a crawling sound coming from underneath the piano.*
You: "A girl. Seems like she was looking for something."
*She was standing on all fours in such a suggestive pose that I hesitated to speak at first.*
You: "Excuse me…"
Miku: "Aaaah! Who's there?"
*She tried to stand up but the bottom of the piano prevented her from doing so.*
Miku: "Ouch!"
*She struggled out.*
You: "Sorry, I scared you…"
Miku: "It's nothing! Oh, you got a checklist, you must be new here?"
You: "Ah? Yes."
Miku: "My name is Miku."
Miku: "No, really, I'm serious! Nobody believes me, but it's my real name. My mother is Japanese. My dad met her when he was building… Well it wasn't him who was building, he's an engineer…"
Miku: "And he was working on a nuclear power plant there! Or a dam… Or a bridge…? Whatever!"
*She was talking so fast she swallowed half the words she tried to pronounce.*
You: "I'm Semyon."
Miku: "Great! Want to be in our club? It's only me here now, but it will be two of us then! Do you play anything?"
*When I became antisocial I bought a guitar and learned a few chords, but then I forgot about it – since I quit everything that required more than a couple of hours to learn.*
You: "You know, I wasn't planning to do anything like that really…"
Miku: "Oh it's ok, I'll teach you! Maybe a trumpet, for example? How about a violin? I know it all, honestly!"
*There was no point in arguing with the orchestra-girl, since there was only another cascade of words waiting to blast at me.*
You: "Hey, I'll think about it, can you just sign it for now?"
Miku: "Yes-yes, sure, give it to me! Be sure to come around! I sing too! I'll sing you some Japanese folk songs. Or maybe if you're not into that, something more contemporary?"
You: "Suuure… thanks, gotta go now!"
Miku: "Of course, come any time…"
*The end of her sentence stayed inside.*
*It might be nice to hang around with a guitar in the evening, but in such company…*
*I turned to leave and came face to face with Alisa.*
*She eyed me suspiciously.*
Alisa: "Why did you come?"
You: "The checklist…"
Alisa: "Got it signed?"
You: "Yes…"
Alisa: "Then move it!"
*Alisa went inside, and I hurried to leave the place.*
*I went to the clubhouse.*
*To tell the truth, I never really liked extracurricular activities.*
*At school I used to find any excuse to skip extra classes. At university I had no interest in participating in the student council.*
*I wasn't interested in boxing, aeromodelling, or sewing.*
*So I came here just to check off the box.*
*Nobody was there.*
*I found myself in something like a hut of a junior robot enthusiast: there were wires and simple printed circuits scattered everywhere, chips, and on the table proudly stood an oscillograph.*
*I heard voices from another room, and then two pioneers appeared.*
*One was Electronik, the other one I didn't know.*
Sergei: "Hi, Semyon! We've been expecting you."
You: "It seems he knows everything about everyone..."
You: "Why were you expecting me?"
Sergei: "Well of course, because you came to sign up to our cybernetics club, didn't you?"
*He didn't let me answer.*
Sergei: "And this is Shurik, he's in charge here!"
You: "I assume there's only two of you in the club?"
Sergei: "Well, you can say that it's three now."
*Shurik came up to me and assertively offered his hand.*
*His face was somewhat familiar.*
Shurik: "Welcome to the club!"
You: "Yep..."
Sergei: "Now, I'll show you around! Make yourself at home."
You: "Err, guys, I just wanted to..."
Shurik: "We're always welcoming new members."
*He said it in such a way that the anthem of the Soviet Union suddenly started playing in my head.*
*It's amazing, I even remembered the words – in the first grade I had a textbook with the lyrics in the back.*
You: "Uh, no, I just wanted you to sign my checklist."
Sergei: "Yep, you sign up to the club, we'll sign your checklist."
*He grinned.*
*I was getting ready for a long and boring argument, but then I heard someone enter.*
*I looked back and saw Slavya.*
Slavya: "Ah, Semyon! I hope they're not giving you any trouble?"
*She narrowed her eyes, looking at the future of the motherland's robotics industry.*
Slavya: "I know these two – they can!"
You: "Well, you know, actually I just need to get my checklist signed..."
*I decided to take advantage of the situation.*
Slavya: "No problem, give it to me."
*Slavya took the paper and marched up to Shurik.*
Slavya: "Sign it!"
Shurik: "Hold on, we're not done yet..."
Slavya: "You're done! Sign it now!"
*She gave Shurik such a threatening look that it made him lose every possible objection.*
*He wrote some squiggles on the checklist, I thanked Slavya, then I moved on in a mellow mood.*
*Actually, I love reading – but spending my days in a library under the current circumstances was well beyond my scope.*
*So I'd better hurry up with this 'checkpoint'.*
*As I stepped inside, a memory from my childhood emerged in my head.*
*It was very vivid.*
*I'm 7 or 8 years old, I'm at the library with my mother.*
*While she's looking through the books I might need for my studies, I'm sitting in the corner and looking through their collection of comic books.*
*Back then I didn't know why they had so many, or why couldn't I take some with me.*
*The notion of collective property was something my mind hadn't grasped yet at that age.*
*However, back then whole concept of property was pretty hazy to me.*
*This memory seemed even stranger now, while I was standing in this particular camp, where they might have managed to build communism 'in three years'.*
*Soviet symbolism was all over the place and the shelves were full of related literature.*
*Of course I wasn't planning to read any of these. Getting aquainted with a full collection of books by Marx was the last thing on Earth I would think of.*
You: "Where's the librarian?"
*I didn't spend much time looking for her.*
*I looked closely. Short hair, thick glasses, rather cute face.*
*She was snoring so peacefully, I couldn't just wake her up.*
You: "I can wait. If she doesn't wake up in half an hour, maybe then..."
*I couldn't just sit there, so I took a random book from the nearest bookshelf.*
*Arthur Schopenhauer, 'The World as Will and Representation'.*
*I opened it roughly in the middle and started reading:*
*The life of a man, with its endless upkeep, wants, and suffering, is to be regarded as the explanation and paraphrase of the procreative act i.e. the absolute claim of the will to live; and furthermore, it is also the reason the man owes nature his death, and thinks with anxiety of this debt.*
*Is this not the evidence that our existence involves guilt?*
*At any rate, we always exist, from time to time paying with death for our birth, we always exist and alternately bear all the joy and sorrow of life, since neither of both can pass us without some effect – that is a result of our stated will to live.*
*Thus the fear of death, which in spite of all the miseries of life holds us firmly to it, is really illusive; but just as illusive is the impulse which has attracted us into it.*
*This attraction itself may be seen objectively as the mutual longing glances of two lovers; they are the purest expression of the will to live, in its affirmation. How gentle and tender it is!*
*It wants happiness, and quiet pleasure, and mild joys for itself, for others, for all.*
*Someone knocked on the door.*
*I closed the book quickly and put it back in its place.*
You: "What a nice habit – knocking on the door. I should pick it up."
*It was Lena.*
Lena: "Oh..."
You: "Hi!"
*I smiled.*
Lena: "Hi, I, uh, just wanted to return a book..."
*She had the copy of 'Gone with the Wind' that I saw yesterday.*
Lena: "Oh, Zhenya is sleeping, I'll come back later..."
Zhenya: "I'm awake."
*I turned around in surprise to look at her.*
*She eyed me closely from behind her table.*
Zhenya: "What is it you wanted?"
You: "I need you to check here..."
Zhenya: "Give it here."
*She quickly signed the paper and gave it back to me.*
*She had this look on her face that made me want to keep quiet.*
*Lena came up to her to return her book, I thanked Zhenya and went out.*
You: "What's the point of visiting the infirmary?"
*My health was fine, the fresh local air clearly did me some good – I felt fresher than usual.*
You: "But I just have to visit it."
*I entered.*
You: "A common infirmary, like my school doctor's room."
*A middle-aged woman sat at the table. Obviously, she was a nurse.*
*She gazed intently at me, assessing me while continuing to write something.*
Violetta: "Well, hello... pioneer."
*Said the nurse without being distracted from her work.*
You: "Good afternoon, ma'am... I have something..."
Violetta: "Sit down, please."
*I looked around the room.*
Violetta: "On the couch."
*I sat down.*
Violetta: "Strip."
*She said all of it with an even tone.*
You: "What for...?"
Violetta: "To inspect, to auscultate, to check on your health, you know."
Violetta: "By the way, my name is Violetta, but you can call me Viola."
*She turned to me.*
Violetta: "What are you waiting for? Strip."
You: "But I have no health issues. I’ve got this..."
*I neatly gave her the paper.*
Violetta: "Later."
*She took the stethoscope off her neck, seeming like she intended to probe me with it.*
*But then someone knocked on the door.*
*The nurse answered unwillingly:*
Violetta: "Come in!"
*In a moment the door opened widely and Elektronik rushed inside.*
Sergei: "Hello! I... fell during the football game. Nonsense of course, I'm okay, but Olga Dmitrievna..."
*There was a massive bruise under Elektronik's eye*
You: "I doubt that this could be a football injury"
Violetta: "Sit down, I'll have a look."
*She said to him*
Violetta: "And you, pass me your checklist."
*The nurse quickly signed it and continued:*
Violetta: "If something hurts, come to me immediately... pioneer"
*I decided not to answer and went out, closing door behind me*
You: "That nurse is surely something else..."
*Nonetheless, I decided to go have lunch.*
You: "The checklist isn't going to run away (I'll get it signed later), while my stomach clearly won't wait till dinner."
*With these thoughts I entered the canteen.*
*There was almost nobody inside – apparently, most pioneers had lunch already.*
*A lunchlady of impressive proportions provided me with a glorious meal of three dishes: a soup 'Ypres broth', goulash 'from Lavrentiy Pavlovich' garnished with potatoes boiled according to the craziest fashion of XV century, and a 'Periodic Table' kompot.*
*Hardly a menu five-star restaurant would envy, but I was too hungry to care.*
*After all, compared to my usual meal of ramen or macaroni & cheese this indeed wasn't too bad.*
*I sat at the nearest table and concentrated on chewing.*
*My focus was soon disturbed by a sudden mighty slap on my back. I even choked.*
*Ulyana was standing in front of me, with a victorious look on her face.*
You: "I'll choke the life out of you one day!"
Ulyana: "Catch me if you can!"
*She stuck her tongue out!*
Ulyana: "You tried once and couldn't."
You: "All right, then I'll ambush you somewhere!"
Ulyana: "That's not fair!"
You: "Look who's talking, Miss Fair-play!"
*I grinned.*
Ulyana: "Ok, you wait, I'll get some food and come back, we'll eat together."
*I could do without such company. Better hurry up with my lunch.*
*However Ulyana came back after just half a minute.*
*She had a huge roast beef on her plate and few large boiled potatoes.*
*Compared to my 'royal' feast...*
You: "How do you... where did you get that?"
Ulyana: "Gotta know places!"
*She looked at me and grinned with all her 32... or however many she had... teeth.*
You: "I won't stand for this!"
*I never was a master of pranks, and in school I often found myself on the bullied side.*
*But I had to get back at her somehow.*
You: "And what if Olga Dmitrievna finds out that you're stealing food?"
Ulyana: "I'm not stealing!"

Olga: "You'll find that out at the lineup!"
*She gave me a wily smile.*

Olga: "Watch yourself!"
Olga: "You must take part in the camp activities today!"
You: "You bet!"
You: "Definitely! And now I'd rather..."
Olga: "Come on, let's hit the road!"
*I came out of the cabin and hid in the bushes behind it, waiting for Olga Dmitrievna to leave.*
*Actually, I didn't have any particular reason to behave this way.*
*But the voice within me kept telling me that I have nothing to do at the lineup.*
*...*
*After the camp leader left, I went back to the cabin and decided to wait for breakfast there.*
You: "Well, I'm not planning on taking part in community life today."
You: "Cleaning and organising – that's not what someone in my situation should be doing."
*Two days have passed, and I'm still right where I started.*
*All the residents seemed to be perfectly ordinary people. They weren't involved in any conspiracy, weren’t communicating with aliens and had no idea about time warps.*
*Of course, each of them is a bit peculiar. But those peculiarities do not seem out of line at all.*
*Moreover, if I had met any of these pioneers in my familiar world, I wouldn't suspect anything wrong.*
*They seemed to be even more normal and natural than, let's say, yours truly.*
*This line of reasoning was quite logical, the illogical part was the absence of answers.*
You: "Ordinary people in an extraordinary place."
You: "I've heard and seen that already, somewhere..."
You: "Dozens of pioneers (or even more) live their familiar lives and do their regular stuff day by day. They don't understand that the world around them is not what it looks like."

You: "Can they give me any answers?"
*Or do I have to seek the truth somewhere else?*
*...*
*It seems I overdid it a bit with the thinking – there's no usual crowd of hungry pioneers near the canteen.*
*Or even inside the canteen.*
*Most of them probably had their breakfast before 9 a.m.*
You: "That's even better. Two's company; three's a crowd."
*Lena was sitting in the farthest corner of the canteen, lazily picking with her fork at an amorphous lump that vaguely resembled porridge.*
*Having a breakfast with her seems like a good idea. We can have a chat in peace.*

*I was on the way to her table when suddenly somebody grabbed me by the sleeve.*
*Zhenya, the librarian.*
Zhenya: "Get your meal and come. We need to talk."

Zhenya: "What are you waiting for?"
*I was a bit confused.*
You: "Pardon, isn't this a bit too... sudden?"

*I suppose that she considers her behaviour completely normal.*
*I was sure that Lena wouldn't mind if I sat next to her.*
Zhenya: "Hold on! Wait a second!"

*Zhenya was shouting something in my direction, but I tried to ignore her.*

Lena: "Morning..."
*Strangely enough, she didn't blush, but smiled instead.*

Lena: "Yes, sure."
*...*
*In a minute I was already sitting in front of her with a simple set of plates on a tray: porridge, 2 poached eggs, 4 pieces of wheat bread, a boiled sausage, and a glass of kompot, made of unknown fruits and berries.*
You: "Have a nice meal!"
Lena: "Thanks."
*I was trying to eat as neatly as I could – no chomping, smearing the food, or spilling the kompot over myself.*
You: "It seems that eating like a human and not like a hog was not that hard at all."
*As usual, Lena remained silent, which means I should start the conversation.*

Lena: "Probably..."
*She was silent for a while.*
Lena: "And you?"

*Though I didn’t want to go there at all.*
*I didn't like dance parties since my school days...*
Lena: "Why so?"

*My mind was still far away, in my school times.*
Lena: "Why don’t you want to go?"

Lena: "Okay then."
You: "But if you’re inviting me..."
*Lena turned red and looked away.*
Lena: "Um, I don't really..."

*I felt confused. I'd better not joke like that.*

*Lena said indifferently and focused on her food, while her face turned even more red.*

Lena: "Huh?"

Lena: "I don't know..."
You: "I see."
*The conversation reached a dead end, so I tried to seem fully focused on my meal.*
*Lena finished her breakfast first.*
Lena: "I should go. See you later!"
You: "See you!"
*I'm not sure why, but I accepted the invitation.*
You: "What if I can learn something new? She is such a bookworm."
*Minute later I was sitting in front of Zhenya, with the tray and the simple meal on it: porridge, 2 eggs, 4 pieces of white bread, a sausage, and a glass of kompot.*
You: "Bon appetit!"
Zhenya: "Thanks."
*I decided to act as politely as I could, and also eat more neatly – without chomping and spilling crumbs of food or drops of kompot.*
You: "So, what do you want to talk about?"
Zhenya: "Today at the library..."
*I wasn't listening from this point onwards, I immediately recalled Olga Dmitrievna’s words about the scheduled events for today.*
Zhenya: "...don't forget!"
You: "Oh? What?"
Zhenya: "I said, don't forget to visit the library after lunch."
You: "What for?"
Zhenya: "Were you even listening?"
You: "Nope."
*I admitted honestly.*
*Zhenyas face turned red, then appeared green, then took on a soft purple colour.*
Zhenya: "Today! After lunch! You! In the library! Got it, dunce?"
You: "Dunce? What kind of curse is that? Though 'a pioneer must never use a curse word', how could I forget this rule?"
You: "Oh, yeah, sure! I apologise! Of course, I'll be there!"
*Actually, I wasn't really planning to go anywhere, but if you want to make someone speak, you need to sacrifice a bit first.*

*I decided to play fair.*
*She looked at me perplexedly and answered:*
Zhenya: "Have you gone completely bananas?"

*Zhenya didn't reply.*

*I smiled kindly.*
Zhenya: "Listen, why don't you visit the infirmary?"

*Zhenya stood up and headed to the exit.*
You: "Wait, you didn't finish your meal..."
*But it looks like she won't turn back.*
*I was finishing chewing on the sausage, which tasted like a twisted-pair cable.*
You: "I wonder if they have internet access here?"

*A pioneer sitting at the next table noticed me talking to myself and stared at me. I smiled and waved to him in return.*

*Some time later I finally came to the infirmary.*

*Though the nurse seemed quite caring, it's better to keep a distance from her.*
*Such benevolence is actually scary!*
*She may know something, but I just hadn't the courage to enter the infirmary.*
You: "Moreover, I had no reason to. Not a single one."
*Immersed in my own thoughts, I didn't notice the nurse, who was standing on the porch.*
Violetta: "Hi there... pioneer!"
*She came closer.*
Violetta: "You must be sick, did you come for medicine?"

Violetta: "Oh, a truant I see."
Violetta: "But if you're here, I have a serious task for you."
*I gave her a look of inquiry.*

Lena: "Hi again..."
Lena: "Hi..."
*Lena emerged from behind the nurse’s back.*
*It seems strange that I hadn’t noticed her until now.*

Violetta: "Alright then... pioneer! So tonight, after dinner, you'll be here!"
Lena: "Maybe I..."
*Lena was barely noticeable this whole time.*
*Surely, she's able to remain invisible like a skilled ninja.*
Lena: "I could do it on my own."
*Strange, she seemed more spirited during lunch.*
Violetta: "No way! There are lots of boxes."
Violetta: "And a pioneer is always ready!"
Violetta: "Isn’t that so... pioneer?"
*She gazed at me and smiled menacingly.*
*I don't want to spend the whole evening doing something like this, and also I’ve got more important things to do.*
*But rejecting this request would be really improper.*
*If it wasn’t Lena who was standing here, I would definitely think my way out.*
Violetta: "Nice! That's how a true pioneer should answer!"
*Even after these words I barely came a step closer to the 'Be prepared! Always prepared!' motto.*

*I looked at Lena, who was still staring at the ground.*

*I need to find a way to ease this situation.*

*She walked off somewhere beside the clubs, and I just stood at the square for some time.*

*I should think before I say something.*
Violetta: "Oh really? And what exactly are you going to be helping her with?"

Violetta: "Sure, she asked you to tidy up her closet too?"
*The nurse looked at me so intensely that Napoleon's fiasco at the Battle of Waterloo seemed now a small annoyance compared to my current flop.*
*I was going to say something, but she continued to speak.*
Violetta: "Okay then... pioneer. We'll manage it without you."

*I said and looked at Lena.*

*I wanted to sink into the ground because of my lame lie that had probably offended Lena.*
Lena: "Well, goodbye then?"

*The nurse was still smiling spitefully.*
*I turned and walked away, almost running.*
*Though in fact, I really wanted to run, common sense advised me not to.*
*I came back to my senses when I reached the square.*
You: "So, what's next?"
*I decided to visit my cabin, in order to collect my phone.*
You: "I don’t know where I'll find myself today, but having a watch is always useful!"

*Suddenly I heard a different tune, which was cutting through the usual noise of the camp.*
*I listened to it carefully. Sounds like an electric guitar.*
*Three repeating chords, no more.*
*But this melody still felt somehow warm, as if a vacuum tube-based audio amplifier was used.*
You: "Could there be such a luxury here?"
*The sound was definitely coming from somewhere near the stage area.*
You: "I wonder who that could be?"

*I came back to the leader’s cabin.*
*Olga Dmitrievna was lying lazily on her bed and reading a book.*
Olga: "Semyon! What are you doing here?"

*Honestly, none of those options suited me.*

*Every one of the leader’s attempts to keep me busy seems to serve only one purpose – to prevent me from finding out my current location.*
*Really, all the deep and vital questions concerning my existence are swept away by a broom, together with all the rubbish and litter.*
*In my case taking some time to work would probably pay off, but just like someone suffering gangrene and rejecting an amputation, I will stand by my beliefs.*
You: "You know, I already had my own arrangements."
Olga: "Oh, really? What kind of arrangements?"
*She bucked up.*
You: "Well..."
You: "I can't just tell her what I'm really thinking about!"

Olga: "You probably have not yet realised how important it is to participate in social life. This is the only way to become a pioneer capable of being a role model."

Olga: "So? Should I choose for you?"
*The leader’s voice turned authoritative.*
You: "I can do it myself, thank you..."
*I mumbled and left the cabin.*
*Always choose the lesser of two evils, they say – well, of three in this case.*
*Slavya wasn't evil at all – so my choice was obvious.*
*Any rational being keeps his house clean, but I usually perceived housecleaning as somewhat akin to gym workouts – yeah, it's a good for you, but not my sort of thing at all.*
*However, I liked the ideas of painting benches or of helping two future geniuses of Russian (or Soviet?) science even less.*
*There were about a dozen pioneers at the square.*
You: "Where did they all come from, I wonder?"
*I approached Slavya.*
You: "Hi there!"
Slavya: "Oh hi! You've come to help?"
You: "Well, not of my own free will of course..."
*I thought it over again.*
Slavya: "I see."
Slavya: "Take this broom, your area is right next to the monument."
*Frankly speaking, there was nothing to sweep there. It seemed pretty clean to me.*
*Though some rubbish was still laying around.*
*...*
*After sweeping for a while I came back to Slavya who was sitting on a bench and taking a break.*
You: "What a nice day, eh...?"
Slavya: "Yeah, though it's a bit too hot."

You: "I don't really know..."

*There was some truth in Slavya's words. I suppose that she was good at reading other people's minds.*
*Or at least, at reading mine.*

You: "What do you mean?"

*I've already achieved grand mastery at all of my professions – watching anime and surfing the internet.*

*It sounded pretty strange – are there any private farms in the USSR, where all the farming has to be collective?*

*My parents were not a good subject for discussion.*

*That wasn't actually true. More like a half-truth.*
Slavya: "Cool."
*She really seemed to consider that a cool thing.*

*The conversation had reached a dead end, so I was trying to take my eyes off Slavya – and kept gazing under my feet, up in the sky or just looking around.*

*After this conversation I felt ill at ease.*

*I was just glad that Slavya supported me.*
*...*

*Well, they might be not-so-giant afterall.*
*That was surely a hard decision to make.*
You: "Indeed, is there any reason to spend extra time with weird chaps fond of early-to-mid-20th-century sci-fi?"
You: "But what if I manage to find out something useful from them?"
You: "At least I can try."
*Standing on the threshold of the clubhouse, I hesitated for a while. Finally, all my doubts were swept aside. I opened the door and went in.*
*Electronik and Shurik were bending over the table, studying something closely.*
You: "Hi there, cyberneticists! How's it going?"
*I was itching to behave as friendly as I could.*
Sergei: "Hi! We were waiting for you!"

*Electronik obviously intended to be called 'the Oracle'.*

Shurik: "You'll help us to complete the robot."

Sergei: "... but I am fair!"

Shurik: "What's the question?"
*He inquired guardedly.*

Sergei: "Why would you think such a thing?"

You: "It's not only my idea..."

Shurik: "O-oh..."
Sergei: "Wanna leap to the future, see how life is there?"
You: "Nah, not really. I'm more interested in travelling back in time."
Sergei: "Why is that?"
You: "I don't know. Why not...?"
You: "Well, and what do you think about it?"
Shurik: "General Relativity Theory postulates the existance of worm holes, also known as tunnels in space. But you wouldn't understand it all anyway."
You: "I bet I won't."
Shurik: "Anyway, in any such a supposition we'll encounter a whole bunch of paradoxes."
Shurik: "For example, if you'll travel to the past and kill yourself, then it would mean that you from the present won't be able to exist."
You: "Well... It seems so..."
Sergei: "In a nutshell, it's all too unscientific."
You: "I see, but what if it would be possible...?"
You: "I mean, do I need some kind of a machine, a device, or a program to get to the past?"
You: "Or it's enough just to fall asleep in a wrong place and wake up in another time and reality?"
Shurik: "I'm sure that modern science has no answer for your question yet."
You: "Oh, yep! He sounds just like 'Popular Mechanics' magazine. I've seen a couple of issues lying around my shelves too."
You: "I see."
You: "It appears that coming here was a bad idea..."
Shurik: "However if we assume that known laws of physics are incorrect... Or alternatively, the laws themselves are correct but we don't know everything about them..."
Shurik: "Then it's definitely possible."

Sergei: "Or it could be somebody, for example, a more advanced race than humans that possesses superior knowledge of the nature of things."

You: "Well, thanks, guys!"
*I was about to leave.*
Sergei: "Hey, hang on! And what about our robot...?"
You: "I'm sure that everything will be just fine with it!"
*The junior cyberneticists' arguments were quite logical but, alas, I wasn't an inch closer to solving the mystery of my arrival in this world.*
*I strolled around the camp for some time and then headed to the canteen.*
*I was hoping that I could escape the obligatory work if I pretend that I'm helping the sports club.*
You: "They obviously have tons of members and could probably do just as well without a single extra pair of hands."
*However, I'd better visit the sports ground – at least to check in there.*
You: "Just in case Olga Dmitrievna finds out that her 'ideal pioneer' slacks off and dodges community service!"
You: "You never know. I could imagine worse punishments than a public telling-off at a party gathering."
*I wasn’t really planning for that to happen.*
*All of a sudden, I saw no cleaning, painting or repairing but a football match.*
*They were playing 5 vs 6.*
*I took a closer look at the players and recognised Ulyana.*
You: "I won't interfere, I'll just watch."
*The teams were obviously mismatched.*
*One team consisted entirely of younger kids that looked about twelve years old.*
*The other team consisted entirely of teenagers.*
*Besides, they had one extra player – Ulyana.*
*Mind you, what can just one extra person, moreover, one girl do?*
*Soon enough, I realised that I was mistaken.*
*Ulyana had a good dribbling technique, cutting through the defenders one by one.*
*She obviously lacked teamwork skills but they weren't even required at this level – she scored with enviable regularity.*

Ulyana: "Hey! Come and join us! They're short one man on their team."

Ulyana: "We've already finished everything!"
*Said Ulyana, sounding insulted.*

You: "How did they manage to get through all of this stuff?"
Ulyana: "Come join their team!"
You: "Well, given that I escaped the last time, I should indeed play now."
*Ball at the centre. We start.*
*With the very first touch I put the ball into the top corner with a delicate strike.*
