*There is a far away space station, the last boundary of humanity, located on the border with a hostile civilisation. The third month of the ceasefire.*
*It can't be really called a ceasefire, more like 'not-a-war'. A small group of survivors is exhausted by a long siege.*
*On one hand they can't retreat, leaving the outpost. On the other hand, they understand that they won't last even a minute if the enemy attacks.*
*Despair is the best word to describe their situation.*
*The food is running out, there is ammo only for a few shots which will only seem like greeting fireworks.*
*There is only plenty of air and water, owing to the regeneration systems.*
*People didn't talk to each other for weeks at a time. They may just not see the point of wasting their time on communication while death is at the door.*
*Or behind metres-thick station armor to be precise.*
*It is really better just to wait for the rescue or enemy's attack. Both outcomes will lead to the end of this torture.*
*This situation looks like a chess game against an invisible opponent. It's the hardest part – end-game. Any wrong move will lead to defeat. Yours or your enemy's.*
*But does the enemy know about it? They may be afraid of making a wrong move too. Meanwhile the humans may move their king. But only one square forward and then one square back again.*
*Any other move will automatically lead to defeat. A step forward is an implied threat to attack. And a step backward is a deliberate necessity of defence. The game would be much easier if the opponent was sitting in front of you. Even an experienced chess player can't hide nervous eye movements, the occasional drop of sweat or shaky hands.*
*On the one hand everything is futile, everyone realises that the situation is hopeless, because no-one would decide to make a move to escape the imminent defeat.*
*On the other hand, when seeing the opponent in front of you, understanding that he is totally like you and can make a mistake, you can more easily stake everything. The opponent may feel the same difficulties.*
*These are the circumstances of the few men and women on the edge of the universe. There were no orders from headquarters for several days.*
*Though the last orders had contained nothing useful, only the usual demand to keep on defending.*
*One square forward, one square backward. The swinging of an eternal pendulum.*
*At the beginning of the fourth month the commander decides to retreat.*
*He reasons that the lives of his soldiers are more important than the mythical ideals of Humanity. No one will judge him for this.*
*Moreover, they can't change anything.*
*The preparations don't take much time. The greatest asset you can save from a sinking ship is your life.*
*The whole station crew board the rescue vessel. The launch sequence starts. Three, two, one... and nothing. The bay doors don't open.*
*They send mechanics to check for malfunctions. But they don't find anything. The doors should open. But they don't open the second time. Or the third time...*
*The commander orders his crew to leave the station in rescue pods. But they can't launch either. They explain it as technical malfunctions. The crew tries to communicate with headquarters in vain.*
*After a few days the executive officer notices that there is nothing on the radars. Nothing at all – no planets, no asteroids, no enemy ships. Just a endless darkness.*
*They run out of food in a month. Everybody thinks that that is the end. But no-one dies, not after a day, a week, not even after a month.*
*As if there is no need for food to sustain human life.*
*At this moment the majority of the crew goes insane. Some of them just stay in their rooms and pray, some wander around the station, some try to commit suicide.*
*But neither point-blank shots with a plasma gun, nor hydrotank diving, nor even simply slitting the veins brings any results.*
*Days pass by, months or maybe even years – nobody keeps a track of time. Insane people recover their minds again and normal people go insane. It repeats many times.*
*In the end, the crew accepts its condition.*
*They start to make up occupations: theatrical stagings, sports tournaments, readings of self-written books.*
*A lot of family couples appear and many more break up.*
*It is an infinite flow of time, an enclosed loop of a human life. And only the darkness on the radar reminds them of the emptiness outside. But there is an emptiness inside the station too.*
*In the end people stop living. They just lie in their rooms and sleep. Not 24/7 at first, but as the time goes by they learn to fall into a trance.*
*Every person has his own dreams – one returns to his childhood, one gets his lost love back, one defends the ideals of Humanity with a blaster in his hands. Some others just wander in space...*
*Shabby from skirmishes with the enemy, a rescue vessel docks with the station. The boarding squad gets inside.*
*The whole station looks like a piece of scrap-metal which has floated in space for thousands of years. The reactor had shut down a long time ago. There were marks of the laser shots on the walls. The equipment was all smashed.*
*They found decayed skeletons of people who died horribly defending the frontier of humanity in almost every room*
*And only one cryptic message sent to the headquarters implied that something was wrong.*
*'Save us!*
*We just want to die...'*
*I finished the story and looked at Ulyana.*
*Her face was concealed by the darkness.*
You: "So that's the story..."
*I blew out the light.*
*Ulyana shrieked, rose up and threw herself towards me.*
*We fell on the floor.*
You: "What's up with you?"
Ulyana: "Nothing..."
*Her voice sounded very scared.*
*Looks like my story hit the jackpot.*
*I mentally congratulated myself.*
*Ulyana wasn't having fun though.*
*She embraced me, shivered and sobbed.*
You: "What's wrong with you, you silly thing?"
*I patted her head.*
You: "It's just a story. It's not real."
Ulyana: "You and your stupid stories!"
*Ulyana cuddled up to me more.*
You: "Were you that scared?"
Ulyana: "Yeah..."
*Frankly, I didn't expect such an honest answer from her.*
You: "Everything’s alright."
You: "Time heals all wounds. She'll calm down."
Ulyana: "Listen, Semyon..."
You: "What?"
Ulyana: "Never mind, it’s nothing."
*She buried her face in my chest.*
*Minutes passed.*
You: "Okay, I understand... Maybe we should go?"
*I listened. Ulyana snored quietly.*
You: "Hey! Wake up!"
You: "Can you even fall asleep from fear?"
You: "Wake up, I said!"
*No reaction.*
*I tried to stand up.*
*Ulyana certainly didn't weigh more than 40 kilograms, but imagine youself lying under such a weight.*
*It's really not easy to stand up!*
*You would think that Ulyana was dead if not for her breathing.*
*I certainly could make more effort...*
You: "But then I'd wake her up and it all will start again!"
You: "Such an unenviable situation."
You: "There is the option to wait until she wakes up by herself, though."
You: "She certainly won’t sleep all the way until morning after such a story."
*I looked through the window at the starry sky.*
You: "I wonder if there really is a distant outpost with a ghost crew..."
*My eyes slowly closed and in a moment I fell asleep...*
*A few minutes later I approached the stage.*
You: "Maybe it was a bad idea accepting her offer?"
You: "Just talking to Dvachevskaya means danger..."
You: "On the other hand I wasn't eager to go to the dance."
You: "What can I do there? I'd only disgrace myself..."
You: "No, I'm better off listening to Alisa play the guitar."
*Coming closer I saw a person sitting on the edge of the stage with her legs dangling.*
Alisa: "So you came after all!"
*Alisa put the guitar aside and jumped to the ground.*
*There was even a trace of joy on her face for a moment. Playing for someone is surely more interesting than being alone.*
You: "As you can see..."
Alisa: "What are we going to do?"
You: "What do you mean 'what'?"
Alisa: "I’m asking you."
You: "Well... you wanted..."
*I got a sudden idea that this situation is one of her usual pranks and I should never have expected to hear any guitar songs.*
You: "I'm going to bed. Bye!"
*I turned around and waved a hand intentionally slowly.*
Alisa: "Hey!"
*Alisa grabbed my sleeve.*
You: "What?"
Alisa: "Don't you want to listen?"
You: "Listen to what? You yourself don't know what you're going to do."
Alisa: "Of course I know!"
*She took the guitar and hit the strings with a plectrum a couple of times.*
Alisa: "Sit next to me."
*I didn't object and in a moment I was sitting beside her.*
You: "It's better this way."
You: "Miss the dance, leave now, and then what would I do?"
*The role of a stranger was more suitable for a passive observer and not for the eager seeker of answers, who I wanted to be so badly.*
Alisa: "So, I'll show you how to play this song now."
You: "Just like that? Right away?"
Alisa: "What do you mean 'right away'?"
You: "I haven't held a guitar for a long time..."
You: "She could probably guess how long it had been since I'd held one. My skills were enough to make a cat laugh."
Alisa: "It's not difficult!"
*I threw an intense look at Alisa.*
*It distinctly seems to me now that she just can't express her feelings.*
*She could lose her strange self-control for a moment and I'd get to see a casual and even funny and friendly girl.*
*And then when her self-confidence and impudence turned back on, it was bitchness as usual.*
You: "And which is the real one?"
Alisa: "Hey!"
You: "What?"
Alisa: "Stop daydreaming!"
You: "Oh, yeah, sorry..."
Alisa: "So, are you watching?"
You: "I am. What song is this?"
Alisa: "The one I played this morning of course!"
You: "Oh... Okay. I'm listening."
*Alisa made up her mind and started to play.*
*...*
Alisa: "That's it. Did you get everything?"
You: "I may have understood it, but I probably won't be able to replicate it."
You: "How shall I put it..."
Alisa: "It's okay. Practice makes perfect."
*She is undoubtly right on this point, but I've had problems with practice all my life.*
You: "Well..."
*I took the guitar from Alisa and tried to play the first chord.*
*It was hard, as if my fingers were tied in a knot and didn't want to be in the right place.*
*I used to be better before, but now I wouldn't even be able to play 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Star'.*
Alisa: "Well?"
You: "Wait a moment..."
Alisa: "Looks like you won't be a rock hero!"
*She laughed kindly.*
You: "It may be better this way..."
*I hissed, vainly trying to remember the order of strings to press.*
You: "Well..."
*The guitar started to make devilish sounds resembling the groans of a wounded dinosaur.*
*My left hand fingers constantly missed the right frets and my right hand didn't strike in rhythm.*
You: "Let's call that progressive rock."
Alisa: "Progressive? Well, well! Give it back!"
*She took the guitar away and it sounded completely different in her hands.*
*I felt embarrassed by my clumsiness for a moment.*
*Alisa's skill may not be on the level of a professional guitarist, but nevertheless she played simple things like this with confidence.*
*She must have had a lot of practice.*
Alisa: "Did you get it this time?"
*She finished and offered the guitar to me.*
You: "Well..."
*I did better the second time, but it was still a long way from Alisa's level.*
*Or from any decently adequate level.*
*I was aware of how totally worthless I was compared to her.*
You: "It seems so simple – just play a song with three chords!"
Alisa: "The tune is too simple, though."
*I put the guitar aside.*
*Alisa was lost in thought for a moment.*
Alisa: "Even a pre-school kid could play it better!"
You: "Thanks, I tried!"
Alisa: "So I noticed!"
*She might be trying to demonstrate her evident superiority at playing the guitar.*
You: "It’s not like everyone can be a musician."
Alisa: "Not really..."
*Alisa looked up at the sky.*
Alisa: "Though you can’t be one, that's for sure!"
You: "Why is that?"
Alisa: "You should have heard yourself!"
*I started to regret coming here.*
You: "Well, don't mind me. Why does Alisa need to do this? It's obvious that I'm a horrible guitarist."
You: "Obviously. But if I had some practice..."
Alisa: "So, will you practice?"
You: "I don't know... Maybe I will."
*The guitar was the least of my problems though. I'm stuck in a strange world I can't escape from... That's more important than a stupid argument with Alisa.*
*I suddenly felt an annoying self-pity, apathy and an urge to leave this place, to forget this evening.*
*Those feelings left a nasty impression and a burning desire to do (or say) something stupid.*
You: "As if it would change anything!"
Alisa: "What?"
You: "Me learning to play the guitar!"
Alisa: "You surely couldn't! You'd strum the guitar for a couple of days and give it up."
*Alisa's words pierced my heart.*
You: "You know what?!"
*Oh well, should she know? Is it any concern of hers?*
*Am I reacting this way just because it's true, and that it’s Alisa who spoke that truth?*
You: "You can't know how to do everything!"
Alisa: "Probably not... But you should be able to at least do something."
You: "So, are you saying that I can't do anything?"
Alisa: "How should I know?"
You: "You know, I..."
You: "I what?"
You: "Should I tell her about my computer skills? Or about the books I've read and movies I've watched?"
You: "Ah well, this is a pointless conversation."
Alisa: "That goes without saying."
You: "You’re only concerned with having fun!"
Alisa: "And you do nothing but whine!"
You: "Forget it!"
*I jumped down from the stage and walked away from a concert area.*
Alisa: "Go then!"
*I heard Alisa yelling to me.*
You: "I'm already going!"
*I hissed.*
*The path led me back to the square.*
*There was Slavya in the centre of it, sweeping the area.*
Slavya: "Oh, Semyon, hi! I thought everyone was already asleep."
You: "No... What are you doing?"
Slavya: "Cleaning up after the ball. Why didn't you come?"
You: "Just..."
Slavya: "And where have you been?"
You: "I..."
*I hadn't a slightest intention of telling Slavya how I embarrassed myself on stage with the guitar in front of Alisa while the whole camp was having fun at the square.*
You: "I took a walk."
Slavya: "Okay... But you should have come. It was fun."
You: "Glad you enjoyed yourself."
*I'd been sweating like a pig today because of worries or just the hot night.*
You: "Hey, do you know where I can have a bath?"
Slavya: "Certainly. Go straight, then a bit to the left by the path, then to the right and there will be a bath-house."
You: "..."
Slavya: "Should I accompany you?"
You: "No, no need. I'll find it myself!"
*I totally didn't want to burden her more.*
*I walked along the forest path in the direction Slavya showed.*
*My whole body was itching.*
You: "How didn't I notice it before?"
*And more importantly, what else hadn't I noticed?*
You: "If things keep going like this then I'll have to stay in this world forever."
*I shivered at the thought.*
*Probably at the idea that I didn't feel any terror, or even just fear.*
*Just like it’s all the natural flow of things.*
*I could see a bathhouse behind the trees.*
You: "And why do the pioneers have baths here?"
You: "Olga Dmitrievna had said something about repairs to the showers though."
You: "No reason to worry about it now..."
*There were soap and clean towels so I quickly washed myself, went outside and breathed in a chest full of fresh night air.*
You: "Ah, it so wonderful that physical cleanliness brings spiritual cleanliness!"
*All of my problems, if not went away, then at least became less important. It’s like the water washed away not only dirt from body, but also the anxiety from my mind.*
*I suddenly started yawning so I headed to the leader's cabin, rubbing my eyes.*
*I didn't take even a few steps before Alisa jumped out from the bushes.*
Alisa: "You... What are you doing here?"
You: "I was just washing myself."
*She came to her senses and spoke again.*
Alisa: "And?"
You: "And what?"
Alisa: "How should I know?!"
You: "Then why do you speak if you don't know?"
*All my peace of mind vanished in a moment, only the irritation and the weariness remained.*
You: "Okay, well if you don't mind..."
Alisa: "Wait..."
You: "Now what?"
Alisa: "If back there on stage you thought that... well... I didn't want to offend you or anything..."
You: "It's okay, I'm not offended. I just can't play the guitar. Nothing special, a lot of people can't."
*I felt that there were obvious signs of irritation in my voice, but I couldn't do anything about it. I wanted to say everything to her face right here, right now.*
Alisa: "Exactly, you can't!"
*Alisa obviously restrained herself from laughing.*
You: "Oh, I've already had enough of you!"
*She totally drove me out of my wits at that moment.*
*In another second I would have started to yell at her... Or worse.*
Alisa: "Wait."
You: "Would you just leave me alone!"
*Alisa followed me but didn't try to stop me.*
Alisa: "I really didn't want to offend..."
*Some invisible power made me to turn around.*
You: "Okay. Can I go now?"
Alisa: "Yes... Of course..."
*In the moonlight Alisa looked very beautiful with a brief guilty expression on her face.*
You: "If she could only keep her mouth shut..."
Alisa: "What are you smirking at?"
You: "Although..."
You: "Nothing. I just thought that if only you were a little bit more polite..."
Alisa: "Then what?"
*I shouldn't say such things, people could get ideas, depending on their intellectual abilities.*
You: "Then nothing."
Alisa: "You should finish what you started!"
You: "There's nothing to finish. I'm very tired and I am going to sleep."
Alisa: "Stop right there!"
You: "Don't make me run away from you!"
Alisa: "As if you could!"

Alisa: "So what?"
You: "What?"
Alisa: "If only I would be more polite, then what?"
You: "Try it and you will see."
Alisa: "Why should I do anything for a fool like you...?"
You: "Then don't try. What does it have to do with me?"
*I sighed and dragged myself to the square.*
Alisa: "And what about you then?"
You: "What?"
*I replied without turning to her.*
Alisa: "Well, if I would, then you...?"
You: "I don't know what are you talking about, but let's think that 'I would' if it is easier for you."
Alisa: "Moron!"
*Alisa yelled at me and headed to the bath-house.*
*The square shined with the cleanness of a German road, which were washed with shampoo, or so people said.*
You: "That's Slavya for you!"
You: "And I just argued with Alisa and nothing else..."
You: "What for?"
You: "As if it was really necessary!"
You: "And her behaviour..."
*In any other situation I would have surely said that Alisa likes me and just hides it behind her rudeness.*
You: "That's not important right now though!"
*Relationships, love, anything...*
You: "Maybe she isn't even a human!"
You: "And what if she was a human and all this was happening in the real world...?"

You: "Olga Dmitrievna certainly would like to know where I was and why missed the dance."

You: "Nothing special actually..."

You: "So..."

You: "Well, I'll decide on the spot."

*The most quiet place here is the bus station, which might never be visited by the 410 route again.*

*Finding a charger in the eighties would mean inventing it.*

Shurik: "It’s alright... That's fine... I know where the exit is! Follow me!"
You: "Follow you where?! I can't see a damn thing!"
Shurik: "Follow my voice."
*I had no other choice.*
Shurik: "Here..."
*Shurik's voice was heard from somewhere further on.*
You: "How do you know where to go?"
Shurik: "I walked all over here..."
You: "Then why didn't you leave?"
Shurik: "The voices... Quiet! They can hear us!"
*In theory I could believe that there are some supernatural forces here.*
*In the Sovyonok camp they’d just be a daily occurence.*
*But there was no reason to panic yet.*
*Though my hands were shaking non-stop.*
Shurik: "Here..."
*I slowly followed his voice and eventually lost track of time.*
*We could have been roaming for a few minutes... or a few hours.*
*Finally a dim light appeared in the distance.*
Shurik: "We're here..."
*We reached the wall. The way towards freedom was blocked by a lattice on the ceiling.*
*I pulled myself up and recognised the square from the bits of landscape I could see.*
You: "Lift me up!"
*Shurik obediently followed my request.*
*I started to hit the grating with my fists so hard that in just a few strikes my arms were all covered in blood...*
*But in return the grating gave way and pushed open.*
*A minute later we were out on the surface behind the monument of Genda.*
*When I saw this grating before I had no idea that there could be catacombs below it...*
Shurik: "They will come for you!"
*I fell to the ground, exhausted.*
You: "Who?"
Shurik: "They will come!"
*Said Shurik again and ran away...*
*I was so exhausted that I could not even be bothered thinking about some voices, or recalling the forsaken camp, the bomb shelter, or the mine.*
*Almost unconscious, I reached the camp leader’s cabin.*
*But I couldn't go to bed right away.*
Olga: "Well look who’s here!"
You: "Olga Dmitrievna..."
*I started tiredly, attempting to cut the explanation to a minimum.*
Olga: "You said you were 'going for a walk', but instead...!"
Olga: "And I... I was going to go and call the police! And..."
You: "Olga Dmitrievna, can it wait until tomorrow? I'm really, really tired."
*The camp leader eyed me all over.*
Olga: "Ok, fine..."
*I was a bit surprised that she agreed so fast but decided not to waste this opportunity and quickly turned the light off and darted under the covers.*
*And then that girl from the mine appeared just before my eyes.*
*I saw her so clear it was as if she was really in front of my bed.*
You: "No, I'm just seeing things..."
You: "But still, why didn’t I get scared back then? I just went and spoke to her normally. Just like that."
You: "All the answers are here. That cat-eared girl knows something for sure."
*Maybe I was too exhausted because of the old camp, mine, and labyrinth and my nerves were stretched to breaking.*
You: "I should have asked her about something…"
You: "But I still have time…"
*Around the next turn the flashlight beam illuminated a big shadow.*
*I was trembling with fear and couldn’t move even one step further.*
*I was woken from my stupor only by the thought that it could be Shurik.*
You: "Shurik!"
*No answer…*
*Around the corner the shadow disappeared, I saw a blurry human shape…*
*Someone was sitting on a stone. Or maybe something…*
*I stopped dead.*
You: "What are you doing here?"
*I heard a lovely voice:*
Yulya: "Catching mice."
*I opened my mouth… …but couldn't say anything.*
You: "…"
Yulya: "Did you see any here?"
You: "No, but I'm sure there are plenty of them…"
*I shined the flashlight at her face…*
*Either something was wrong with her head or with her biological species. Because of her ears and tail, she doesn’t really look like a human.*
You: "And how many have you caught?"
Yulya: "Not a single one."
*She answed seriously.*
*She didn't look hostile. SubconsciousIy I felt that I shouldn’t be afraid of her, but at the same time I had absolutely no idea what to ask her, how to ask her, who she is, or what she is doing.*
*But on the other hand, normally if you suddenly met someone in a deserted mine you'd have a heart attack from shock.*
*And the girl in front of me was definitely not a pioneer from the camp!*
You: "And you... Who are you?"
Yulya: "You're probably looking for him..."
You: "For who?"
Yulya: "That boy..."
You: "Well... Yes..."
*I answered after a small pause.*
You: "But still..."
*The girl interrupted me.*
Yulya: "He has been walking around here for a long time. I tried talking to him, but he didn't hear me."
You: "And where is he now?!"
Yulya: "I don't know... Maybe he is still wandering somewhere."
*It seems she wasn’t interested in this conversation at all.*
You: "And you... How did you... get here?"
Yulya: "The same way you did. From the surface."
You: "Without a flashlight?"
Yulya: "Why not?"
*She gave me a perplexed look.*
*I completely lost all comprehension.*
*The flashlight flickered. Terrified, I started banging it with my fist.*
*When the light lit back up the girl wasn't there...*
You: "I don't know who or what she is, but it seemed like she could help me find the answers."
*It's the strangest thing, but I wasn’t scared of her. I just felt that this girl wouldn't do me any harm.*
*But now I must find Shurik!*
You: "I have a feeling that this is not the last time I will meet this girl..."
*I don't know why, but I'm sure about it.*
Slavya: "I'll go with him!"
Olga: "Very well! It's better together."
You: "Are you sure?"
*I asked Slavya in a whisper.*
*I wanted to be sure, but...*
*She didn't answer, just smiled.*
*I looked speechlessly at Slavya for some time.*
You: "Why is she always helping me?"
Olga: "Very good! Good luck then, both of you."
You: "We’ll need it..."
*The camp leader and the other girls said their goodbyes and went their own ways.*
*I was quite surprised that they're treating our night walk... through the forest... to the abandoned camp as something normal.*
You: "Well... it can’t really be helped."
Slavya: "Wait a minute, I'll bring a flashlight."
You: "A flashlight, sure..."
*While I was waiting for Slavya, I has a strange thought.*
You: "Why is she always so kind, sympathetic and ready to help?"
You: "Why did she offer to go with me to God-knows-where?"
You: "It’s always the quiet ones…"
You: "Should I be concerned about her?"
Slavya: "I'm back!"
*With a smile Slavya gave me a flashlight.*
Slavya: "Shall we go?"
*From what Electronik told us, the old building was built right after the war.*
*It looked like a kindergarten (or like a barracks, I expected) and definitely could hold less pioneers than today's camp.*
*It had been abandoned for about twenty years…*
*It was now totally dark.*
*It seemed like the forest was as afraid of us as we were of it. Trees politely moved away, grouping at the sides of the path and patiently watching us.*
*An owl 'whoo'ed somewhere far away, but more quietly than usual.*
*I wasn’t afraid walking next to Slavya.*
*Probably in any other situation, even in the real world, I would be too scared to go into a forest without a proper path.*
*But I tried to get rid of these thoughts.*
*Although it was strange, Slavya probably soothed my self-preservation instincts and my sense of reality was blunted.*
*If it continues this way, I'll jump towards some beast with a smile on my face…*
You: "You're not afraid at all, are you?"
Slavya: "Meaning?"
*Slavya turned round and looked at me, smiling in a strange way, either with misunderstanding or with gentle mockery. Or maybe I was just seeing things.*
You: "Well… Night, the forest, the old camp…"
Slavya: "Yes, it sort of gives me the chills."
You: "Just sort of?"
Slavya: "Are you afraid?"
You: "No… Well… Yes, but it's a natural human reaction in this kind of situation."
*I didn't want to show my fear, but I wasn’t really scared. I just felt that being scared is what I should be in a situation like this.*
*It was like my body had stopped producing antibodies to fight against an infection. I was scared, not by the night forest, but by the fact that I was reacting to everything that was happening in the wrong way.*
*On the other hand, I didn't want to make a fool of myself.*
Slavya: "I see."
*Slavya smiled again and continued walking.*
*...*
*The path, surrounded by trees and bushes, was becoming more narrow.*
*The deeper we went into the forest, the less clearly we could see the moon.*
*For a moment clouds hid the moon and everything was submerged into almost pitch black darkness.*
*I closed my eyes tight and when I opened them the moon had taken its place again and painted the world in the bright-white colors of its night shroud.*
You: "I only just realised how much I hate the dark!"
*Finally a clear space appeared far away ahead and a minute later we were standing at the edge of a forest glade.*
*There was a ramshackle old camp building, eroded by rain, rust and beetles.*
*It smiled at us with broken windows like a gap-toothed mouth. A silent rebuke from the dead to the living could be read in this smile.*
*A cemetery fog clouded the whole glade so ghosts, ghouls, zombies, devils and other evil entities seemed to loom from the haze.*
*This sight was enough to give the average person a heart attack, or at least a panic attack.*
*If Slavya hadn’t taken my hand, I surely wouldn’t have been able to stand it…*
Slavya: "It won’t be as scary this way."
*She smiled.*
*I couldn't say anything else, just grasped her hand tightly.*
You: "What am I even doing here? Looking for Shurik at night in the forest, here?!"
You: "How could I ever agree? There's not a single normal person who would..."
You: "But the world around me can’t be really be called normal."
*I tried to persuade myself that I was finding answers and that it can’t really get any worse.*
*To be honest, nothing bad had actually happened to me during the last four days in this camp. Besides, I had no special reason to think that something bad would happen.*
*Maybe it’s just the way the world works – people can't live without adventures?*
Slavya: "Shall we go?"
You: "Um, yes, I guess..."
*But we didn't make a move.*
*Slavya seemed to be waiting for me to take the first step, but I had just enough courage to stand still without running away.*
*The moon showed up from behind the clouds again and lit up the old camp building.*
*Now it less looked like a tomb, but all dead pictures in my imagination grew real. Visions of ghosts became more focused, the wailing of the wind and the grass rustling got clearer. Noises of the unknown origin could be heard from afar.*
Slavya: "Seems like it was a great place, before..."
*I looked at Slavya carefully.*
*Maybe she was scared, but she was trying to hide it. Knowing that I felt a little better and calmer.*
You: "Maybe. Let's go?"
Slavya: "Sure..."
*I stepped carefully, watching every step, trying not to touch the old fence, the crooked merry-go-round, or the rusty slide.*
*In some places the grass was waist-high, so any wrong move could lead to broken legs or hands.*
*At last we came to the entrance and I pointed my flashlight inside.*
*The darkness that looked back at me was much scarier than the view outside – at least the moon shone brightly there.*
*I gathered up all my courage and crossed the threshold.*
*The inside of the old camp building looked like a kindergarten from my childhood. The layout of the interior, even the rotten furniture was similar.*
You: "Well..."
*I shivered, picking out more and more remains of the joy of children long gone with the flashlight.*
Slavya: "Creepy."
*Slavya was not only holding my hand by now, but embracing it, firmly pressing herself against me.*
*However I didn't sense fear in her voice.*
You: "I wonder whether it was a good idea to come here in the middle of the night?"
Slavya: "Perhaps not."
You: "Shall we go back then?"
Slavya: "No! What about Shurik?"
*She said in genuine astonishment.*
You: "Well, Shurik... Why did he even come here in the first place? Maybe he isn't even here?"
Slavya: "Where else could he be?"
You: "I don't know. Eaten by wolves, maybe?"
Slavya: "Don't say that!"
*Slavya frowned and stepped away from me.*
*I was already so used to being with her that I was slightly upset by her reproach.*
You: "Well, okay, okay... let’s assume that there are no wolves."
You: "Though you can never be sure..."
You: "Well, since we're here, let's search."
*...*
*We searched all the rooms of the old camp: play rooms, bedrooms, canteen, kitchen and toilets. I even looked into the closet, which was choked with empty, decayed cardboard boxes.*
Slavya: "Look!"
*When we returned to the place we started from, Slavya picked up something from the floor and gave it to me.*
*It was an old doll with torn, frayed threads, missing an hand and an eye, faded from damp.*
You: "So what?"
Slavya: "I pity it..."
You: "What? This doll?"
Slavya: "Yes."
You: "Why would you pity it?"
Slavya: "Someone played with her, then just threw her away and forgot about her. And she's been here alone all these years, in the rain, in the cold..."
*I couldn’t really tell if Slavya was serious or not.*
*I don't think this is the time to think about such things.*
*On the other hand, what would be the proper time for that?*
*Slavya looked really upset.*
You: "Yes, maybe."
*I took the doll and examined it.*
*I remember how I once found a stuffed lion the same way that Slavya just found this doll. I took him home, washed him and was as careful with him as with other toys, even though he was long past his retirement age.*
You: "You should give it to Ulyana."
*Slavya laughed.*
*Suddenly the wind howled down the passage, singing some kind of eerie tune.*
*A light flashed and I instinctively jumped, caught my leg on something and tumbled to the floor.*
Slavya: "Are you alright?"
*Slavya ran over to me and helped me get up.*
You: "Yes, more or less..."
*I'd tripped on a trapdoor.*
*It's strange that we hadn't noticed it already – the dirt around the door was cleared. It seems like it was opened not too long ago.*
You: "We're not going down there, are we?"
*I asked, trying to pre-empt Slavya's suggestion.*
*She only gave me a sad glance.*
You: "Come on... are we playing at diggers now?"
*I moaned, while lifting the hatch cover with quite an effort.*
*My common sense was crying out, telling me I shouldn't do this, but contrarily my logic suggested that if this world wanted to kill me, I'd already be dead.*
*But it's only because of Slavya, otherwise there's no way I would go down there!*
*Two metres of a rusty metal ladder led down to a dirty concrete floor.*
*I leaned over the edge and illuminated a narrow passage, going somewhere into the darkness.*
You: "And what is there?"
Slavya: "I think I heard about a bomb shelter under the old camp."
You: "A bomb shelter?"
*Well, that's pretty logical, considering the time it was built.*
You: "Why would Shurik need to go there?"
Slavya: "I don't know."
You: "Of course, it wasn't necessarily him who opened the hatch (and it's obvious that someone had opened it just recently), but who would be more likely to get the idea of going down there than a mad inventor?"
You: "If we discard theories of supernatural involvement, there can be no other humans in this forest."
*At least that's what I thought.*
You: "Alright, I'll go first, then if everything is fine you follow me."
Slavya: "What might not be fine?"
*Slavya looked scared, but seemed to ask more out of politeness.*
You: "Well, I don’t know... Rats, for example. Are you afraid of rats?"
You: "Guess I shouldn't have asked."
*I sighed deeply and began to descend.*
*...*
*We advanced slowly, holding hands.*
*In the pitch darkness, the flashlight was not helping much. Only occasionally it would illuminate pieces of old newspapers and scrap metal lying here and there.*
*Suddenly it began to feel as if the walls and the ceiling, covered in endless twisting cords, were pressing in on me, as if the passage was getting narrower.*
*I spread my arms, trying to measure the passage's width.*
Slavya: "Are we still far off?"
*Asked Slavya sadly.*
You: "Far from where? I've got no clue."
Slavya: "Alright..."
*Just then a massive metal door appeared before me as if from nowhere.*
Slavya: "Oh..."
*Cried Slavya softly.*
*I tried the handle, and it seemed to yield a bit.*
You: "You ready?"
Slavya: "Not sure..."
*Though, speaking frankly, what could you prepare for in such a situation?*
*The wheel turned a few times, squeaking horribly, then finally reached its limit and went quiet.*
*I pulled on the door with all my weight, and it reluctantly opened. There was some sort of chamber behind it...*
*Which turned out to be the bomb shelter itself.*
*When we entered, the lights suddenly went on, making me flinch.*
*Though it was likely that there was an independent power source here: at the time when these catacombs had been dug, people had been building things to last.*
*The bomb shelter looked exactly like what I imagined. It had everything needed to sustain prolonged human existence during a war: the lockers contained chemical protection suits, gas masks, dry rations and water cans. At the far wall, I noticed a lot of various tools: pressure metres, radiation metres, a radio and some others.*
*However, this place looked like nobody has ever used it (which was not actually that surprising). Furthermore, it looked like nobody had ever entered it after it was built.*
*Slavya gave me a questioning look.*
You: "Well, Shurik is definitely not here."
Slavya: "But was he?"
You: "No idea. But if he was here, he couldn't just vanish."
*I looked around the room again and noticed another door in the wall to my left.*
You: "Maybe there?"
*However, the door wouldn't open.*
Slavya: "What if he barred it from the other side?"
You: "But why?"
Slavya: "I don’t know..."
*Still, it was quite possible, assuming he was there at all.*
*By the look of things, Shurik was hiding, maybe running from someone.*
*Such thoughts made me uneasy, and I felt like putting myself on the other side of the door as fast as I could.*
*I pushed hard, but the door only gave a dull creak.*
Slavya: "Here, maybe this could work?"
*Slavya handed me a crowbar.*
*I fumbled with it, considering how I could better tackle the door.*
You: "Let's give it a try."
*Using all my strength, I managed to pull the door off its hinges, and it crashed onto the floor.*
*While I was recovering from my effort, Slavya pointed the flashlight down the newly opened passage.*
Slavya: "There's a corridor here, just the same as the previous one."
You: "Geez... This place is a real maze."
Slavya: "Shall we go?"
You: "Hold on..."
*I sat down on a bunk, took a dusty pillowcase off a pillow and wiped my forehead.*
You: "Let me catch my breath."
*Slavya sat down next to me and began to study the details of the floor tile patterns.*
You: "Better turn off the flashlight for now."
Slavya: "Oh, yes..."
*She blushed slightly and clicked the switch off.*
You: "It's just plain creepy..."
*I caught myself thinking that I have not been treating these events as real for the last half an hour.*
*As if they had not been happening to me, as if they were just a dream.*
*Just like back then, four days ago, in the first minutes after I found myself here.*
*Yes, lately I might have started getting used to this world, this reality – as it has become reality for me.*
*And that feeling deep in my soul that I had to find an exit was not so acute anymore.*
*But now again, in a blink of an eye: the forest, the old camp, the bomb shelter.*
*There was absolutely nothing supernatural about any of it – but neither was it anything normal, like anything from my previous life.*
Slavya: "Yes..."
*Agreed Slavya.*
You: "Don't you find any of this strange?"
Slavya: "What exactly?"
You: "Well, the fact that we are sitting here, just you and me, in the night. Wouldn't it be normal in such situation to instead wait till morning and call the police?"
Slavya: "Yes, I guess so."
*She replied thoughtfully.*
You: "Of course, I almost volunteered. I shouldn't have."
*Well, ‘almost’ isn't quite right, but still.*
Slavya: "But you just wanted to help. If Shurik is here, we should find him as soon as possible."
You: "At this rate we will be the ones they're looking for. You know, he did manage to get lost here."
*Slavya looked frustrated.*
You: "Alright, alright, I didn't mean anything like that. Maybe he's not here, maybe he actually went back to the camp a long time ago."
Slavya: "Yes, maybe."
You: "But we should still check, right?"
Slavya: "Of course!"
*Slavya got up and held out her hand to me.*
*It seemed she wasn't as afraid as me.*
*Though I was already tired of being scared myself, and now only wanted all of this to end as soon as possible.*
*....*
*This corridor was identical to the other one which we came through to get to the bomb shelter.*
*I was walking at a slow pace, carefully watching the floor and checking from time to time whether the passage was getting narrower.*
Slavya: "Look!"
*Slavya held my hand tighter and pointed at a breach in the middle of the tunnel.*
*It was wide enough for a man to climb through (or to fall down).*
Slavya: "Maybe..."
*I pointed the light down, but there seemed to be nothing but ground at the bottom.*
You: "I think we should check this out."
*The hole was shallow enough for us to climb out afterwards, so at first sight there was nothing to be afraid of.*
*I climbed down carefully and helped Slavya.*
*We found ourselves in some kind of mine.*
*The walls and the ceiling were reinforced by wooden beams, and rails stretched out into the distance.*
*Here and there the earth pressing down against this fragile design broke through the boards, which were rotting with age. It made the whole structure look a bit unreliable.*
Slavya: "Where do you think we are?"
You: "Don’t know, some kind of mine. What could they have mined here?"
Slavya: "Coal, perhaps?"
You: "Perhaps..."
*We started to advance slowly.*
*Stones would treacherously shift under our feet now and then; the beam coming from the flashlight trembled and jumped from one wall to the other, often casting shapeless shadows which disappeared as soon as the light was pointed at them.*
Slavya: "It's scarier here than above..."
You: "Guess so."
*The further we went, the stronger my confidence became that Shurik had absolutely nothing to do with this place!*
You: "He couldn't have been taken by a chupacabra, could he? Alright, we can't rule out that possibility either."
*At last we came to a fork in the tunnel.*
Slavya: "Where do we go now?"
You: "I don’t know."
*I tried to inject at least some semblance of calm into my voice, but I really had no clue. None at all: not where to go, not where Shurik was, not even why we were here!*
Slavya: "What if we get lost...?"
You: "Yeah, right, let's leave a mark that we have already been here."
*I picked up a rather large stone and carefully carved a cross on one of the logs supporting the ceiling.*
You: "There, now we'll know that we have already passed this spot."
Slavya: "Good."
*Slavya smiled.*
Slavya: "So, which way?"
*...*
*We have already been here.*
*Finally we walked out of the tunnel into a rather large hall with a high ceiling.*
*Though it hardly could have been called a hall; they must have used to mine something here. Coal, probably, or maybe gold.*
*The walls had been cut by pickaxes or pneumatic drills.*
*This place was pitch black, so our only salvation was the flashlight.*
You: "If it breaks, it's unlikely that we'll ever get out of here..."
*By its light, I noticed a piece of red cloth in the corner.*
*That's a pioneer neckerchief!*
*Shurik was obviously here somewhere.*
You: "Shurik! Shurik!"
Slavya: "Shurik! Shurik!"
*Only the echo answered us.*
Slavya: "Don't worry, he's alright!"
*Frankly speaking, at that moment I was far more worried about myself...*
You: "But where could he have gone from here?"
*This chamber had no other exit...*
You: "Of course, there are probably still places in these tunnels which we haven't been to yet."
You: "Then we have to keep searching!"
*After another turn, the flashlight lit up a wooden door.*
You: "Well, at least that's something."
*To tell the truth, I was so tired of wandering around this mine that I had completely stopped thinking about Shurik. I only wanted to find an exit as soon as possible.*
Slavya: "What's behind it?"
You: "We're just about to find it out."
*Past the door there was a small chamber, which looked either like the utility room of a boiler house, or like one of the bomb shelter's rooms.*
*The floor was littered with empty bottles and the walls were painted with a mess of graffiti, which meant that other people had more than once visited this place before us. Although, from the look of things, they had done so rather long ago. *
*I was running the flashlight's beam around the room, trying to check every part of it, when suddenly...*
*I found Shurik curled up in a corner.*
Slavya: "Shurik!"
*Cried Slavya.*
*However, it looked as if he was not paying any attention to us.*
You: "Here you are! We've been looking for you all night! Why in the world did you come here?"
*Shurik looked up at me with hazy, unseeing eyes.*
Shurik: "And who are you?"
You: "What do you mean ‘who are you’? Get up already and let's go."
Shurik: "I'm not going anywhere with you."
*Shurik turned away and stared into the darkness again.*
Shurik: "You want to trick me again. You'll make me go in circles through the tunnels, won't you? Yes, you will! I know you for what you are!"
*Shurik's voice turned into an infernal whisper.*
You: "Cut this nonsense out already."
*I wanted to approach him and pull him upright, but Slavya stopped me.*
Slavya: "He's not quite himself."
You: "Well, I'm not quite myself either! You wander here all night – you sure won't be quite yourself."
*She shook her head reproachfully and slowly went up to Shurik while carefully staying in the light.*
Slavya: "It's alright, it's me, Slavya."
Shurik: "For real?"
*Shurik looked at her and immediately started sobbing quietly.*
Slavya: "Of course! Who else could it be? And that's Semyon with me. We came to find you. Everything's fine now!"
Shurik: "Are you really not them?"
Slavya: "Certainly not! We're us."
*He tried to get up; but he was apparently disoriented and would have fallen if not for Slavya, who caught him by the arm.*
Slavya: "Easy there! Careful!"
*When they came up to me, I said:*
You: "Alright, time to get out of here!"
Shurik: "We can't go back..."
You: "Back where? Into the mine?"
Shurik: "Yes."
*Shurik was speaking calmly, but at the same his voice was trembling slightly.*
You: "Why is that?"
Shurik: "It's where... they are!"
You: "Who are 'they'?"
Shurik: "The voices."
You: "What voices?"
*I was starting to lose my patience.*
*This place and this situation certainly weren't normal, but if there had been anything paranormal here then, by the laws of horror cinema, it should have long since showed its face by now.*
Slavya: "Calm down, Shurik. Just tell us everything in detail."
*He took a few deep breaths and started:*
Shurik: "I needed some spare parts for the robot, and I heard that there was a bomb shelter in the old camp. And there's usually a lot of different equipment in bomb shelters. It's old, of course, but worth disassembling: "
Shurik: "So I went early in the morning, I thought I could finish quickly and get back by breakfast."
Shurik: "I got everything I needed."
*He took some light bulbs and wires out of his pocket and showed them to us.*
Shurik: "But then, up there in the bomb shelter, I heard some sounds from behind the door. Something like moans or wailing. At first I got scared, but then I thought that a person could be in danger. So I went there..."
Shurik: "And here was this mine, this damn maze! I got completely lost. And the voices, the voices always telling me something, sometimes shouting, sometimes whispering, and I can never make out the words!"
*He was ready to burst into tears, but Slavya patted him gently on the head, and Shurik continued:*
Shurik: "Anyway, I found this room, at least here you can't hear them..."
You: "So you decided to sit and wait for rescue, like in a B-film?"
*I asked sarcastically.*
*Slavya shot an angry glance at me.*
You: "Well, in any case, it's time to get out! If there are no objections."
Shurik: "Come, I know a short cut!"
You: "A short cut?"
Shurik: "Yeah, you know, I walked all over this place."
You: "Alright..."
*...*
*Shurik did not lie.*
*Indeed, after wandering for just about two minutes in the mine, we found ourselves under a grate, through which we could see the sky.*
You: "Then why didn't you get out yourself?"
Shurik: "Try it, you'll see."
*I pulled myself up and pulled on the grate a few times.*
You: "It's true, you can't break it just like that. Gotta use something heavy..."
*I looked down at Slavya and Shurik.*
Slavya: "Try the flashlight, maybe?"
You: "The flashlight..."
*I fumbled with it: it was not one of those cheap Chinese fakes from the 90s, which I used to have a lot of in our summer cottage; no, it was a real Soviet durable metal flashlight. Not a hammer, of course, but if I tried hard enough...*
*I swung it and started smashing at the grate, aiming for the spots where it was attached to the wall.*
*Soon I got lucky: I heard cracking sounds, and a few bolts fell down.*
*...*
*A minute later, I was lying on the grass under the monument and breathing in the fresh night air with delight. Although after the mine, any air would seem fresh.*
Shurik: "Well then, I'll be going, thank you..."
*Shurik looked a bit lost.*
*I eyed him questioningly for a bit, but ended up saying nothing and just waved my hand for a goodbye.*
*After all, I had neither the strength nor the will to talk with him.*
You: "And what would I say to him? Scolding him now is no use, and the same probably goes for trying to learn anything."
Slavya: "What a night..."
*Slavya was sitting next to me and looking dreamily at the moon.*
You: "Right so... If someone told me just a week ago that I would go to a pioneer camp and would even have to crawl through bomb shelters..."
Slavya: "But it was fun."
You: "In a way."
*There was indeed something amusing about all of this. But there was also something strange: during the last few hours, absolutely anything could have happened to me, but in the end, nothing at all had happened.*
*In a couple of years, I would probably remember this as just a funny incident from childhood. If I live that long.*
You: "What do you think, did he really hear something there?"
Slavya: "I don't know... It's possible, of course, but most likely it was just his imagination. In such a situation, anyone could start imagining things."
*That was not only the most logical explanation, but also the most probable one, because nothing had happened to me and Slavya.*
You: "Well, I for one think he should go see a psychiatrist."
Slavya: "Guess he should!"
*Laughed Slavya.*
Slavya: "Alright, time to go to bed."
You: "Aye."
*I felt like I needed to say something to Slavya. I was not sure that I wanted to, but I could feel the need.*
You: "Thank you!"
Slavya: "For what?"
*She gave me a surprised look.*
You: "I wouldn't have managed without you."
Slavya: "It was nothing..."
*Slavya blushed.*
You: "I was in her debt. Again."
You: "I wonder how I could repay her, at least partially, for all that she has done for me."
*I stared at the night sky, slowly falling asleep.*
*All of today's adventures left me so tired that I had no more strength left.*
You: "You know, under different circumstances, I would have surely confessed my love to you..."
*I said, losing touch with reality.*
*Thoughts usually work much faster than common sense...*
*But Slavya wasn't there anymore.*
You: "It's probably for the best - at least she didn't hear..."
You: "Though it's strange - why did she leave without saying goodbye?"
You: "Well, whatever, I'll sleep on it and see in the morning."
*I was so tired that I barely made it to the camp leader's cabin... But there was a light in the window!*
You: "That means she's waiting for me."
You: "And that, in turn, means that I'm in for a lecture again."
You: "And this time it will be just as pointless as ever!"
*I had absolutely no desire to discuss whether I was right or wrong.*
*The deckchair standing nearby was beckoning to me like a friend, as if suggesting I should sleep in it, forgetting about the mine, Shurik, the camp leader...*
You: "Here you are..."
*I said blankly, still looking at my cherished deckchair.*
Olga: "Semyon!"
You: "Yeah, yeah... We found Shurik, Slavya will give you the details tomorrow, and now I'd really like to sleep..."
*She looked at me confusedly for a moment, and then replied:*
Olga: "Oh well, fine..."
*I don't know if mentioning Slavya played its role, but half a minute later I was already in my bed.*
*The events of the day kept turning over for a short while in my head, but soon it started to ache, and it was as if my consciousness switched to safe mode and started to reboot.*
Olga: "And Dvachevskaya goes with you!"
*It was as if Olga Dmitrievna had read my mind.*
Alisa: "Why's that?"
Olga: "Well, who tried to blow up the monument? And as if that wasn’t enough, who also tried to slander Semyon?!"
*She said it in such a voice that Alisa did not dare to argue.*
Alisa: "Happy now?"
*She blurted once we were left alone.*
You: "What do I have to do with this? Was it me who tried to blow up the monument?"
*Alisa grunted and turned away.*
Alisa: "I’m not going anywhere with you!"
You: "Oh, please don’t!"
Alisa: "Great then!"
You: "Excellent!"
*We stood silently for a while, not looking at each other.*
*I dared break the silence first.*
You: "Is that all?"
Alisa: "All what?"
You: "All that you wanted to tell me?"
Alisa: "Yes, that's all!"
You: "Do you mind then if I inquire why you tried to blow up the monument?"
Alisa: "I was bored..."
You: "Ah, right, blowing it up would have definitely cheered you up!"
*Alisa seemed really reluctant to go with me.*
*As for me, however, I've decided to find Shurik after all.*
*It wasn't him who interested me the most, but the abandoned camp.*
*For some reason, I had a feeling that I might find out something there.*
*And I really did not like the idea of going alone at night...*
You: "So, you scared then?"
Alisa: "Are you daring me?"
*She gave me a sarcastic smile.*
You: "Oh no, I'd never... Good luck if you're staying then!"
*I turned around and started walking in the direction where the old camp should have been.*
*Alisa caught up with me at the forest edge.*
Alisa: "Wait up! I'm going with you!"
You: "Why did you deign to change your mind all of a sudden?"
*I asked ironically.*
Alisa: "You don't need to know!"
*She snarled and handed me a flashlight.*
*That was quite wise.*
*I don't know what I would have done there alone in the dark if it wasn't for Alisa.*
*Electronik had told us the old building was built right after the war.*
*It looked like a kindergarten (or like a barracks, I expected) and definitely could hold fewer pioneers than today's camp.*
*It had been abandoned for about twenty years...*
*The night forest was completely unlike during the day.*
*Just a couple of hours ago it seemed like just a small grove where even a blind man wouldn't get lost.*
*However, as the darkness fell the trees seemed to grow up, the bushes suddenly took up all the free space, and the paths, so wide in daylight, turned into barely visible waves in the dark green forest ocean.*
*The final strokes to this picture were the birds, the insects, and the beasts, who were giving a concert, each with its own instrument, creating together an amazing yet frightening nocturnal symphony.*
*We walked slowly, Alisa a bit ahead and me in her wake, trying not to fall too far behind.*
*She acted self-assured to a fault. Absolutely not like me - every rustle of bushes nearby or hoot of an owl overhead made me cringe and look around timidly.*
*Of course, it was obvious that there was not much to fear here - the local woods weren't likely to be teeming with wild beasts, and it seemed there were no people at all in this world, apart from those in the camp.*
*However, the fear was there on the instinctive level, and I tried to walk carefully and to stay as watchful as I could. Discretion is the better part of valour, after all.*
*Alisa stopped suddenly. So suddenly that I nearly bumped into her.*
Alisa: "Now where?"
You: "What? Well... Straight ahead, I guess?"
Alisa: "Are you sure?"
*I tried to figure out the directions.*
*It looks like we were going the right way. Or at least the way suggested by Electronik.*
*However without a map, without a GPS or GLONASS navigation, I wasn't even sure that we were still on the same planet (wherever it was).*
You: "We haven't taken any turns, we've been walking straight forward all the time, just as Electronik said..."
Alisa: "Then why haven't we made it to the old camp yet?"
You: "How should I know?!"
*Alisa's rude way of talking was already getting on my nerves.*
Alisa: "Are we already lost?"
You: "Why would you say that? We are barely a kilometre away from the camp."
Alisa: "So what?"
*She looked visibly sadder.*
You: "So nothing! If you don't like it, you can go back!"
*Alisa eyed me disappointedly for a while and then her face changed sharply.*
Alisa: "Well I will then!"
*She suddenly turned around and started marching briskly back towards the camp.*
You: "Good luck there!"
*I shouted as she was going.*
You: "However, Alisa may be right, and we are in fact lost. In which case it's not a good idea to stay here alone..."
*The cool night breeze blew stronger, and I shivered.*
You: "But going after her would mean losing face; even worse, admitting she's right. No, I'm not ready to accept that!"
*I could have probably spent until morning arguing with myself about this, if it weren't for Alisa's scream.*
*My legs carried me on their own towards where she went.*
*About twenty metres on I nearly fell into a hole, just managing to jump over it at the last moment.*
*As for Alisa, it looked like she had not managed to.*
*I was about to point the flashlight into the darkness when I realised that she'd taken it with her. Well, that had to be expected.*
You: "Are you alive?"
Alisa: "Yeah..."
*Her muffled voice sounded up from below.*
You: "Did you break anything?"
Alisa: "Hell if I know! Idiot!"
*A light flickered in the hole. I stepped closer and bent to it to examine how deep it was.*
*The crumbling hole went about three metres into the depths, but it was pitch black below.*
Alisa: "Help me get out!"
*Alisa yelled angrily.*
You: "And how do you imagine I should do that?"
Alisa: "I don't know! Think of something!"
You: "Well, what do you see now? Describe it."
Alisa: "Well, it's sort of a tunnel and... Nah, just a tunnel."
*A tunnel? That's weird.*
Alisa: "Come on, get down here!"
You: "Is that the best idea you have? I'd rather run to the camp for a rope."
Alisa: "You're gonna leave me alone here?"
*Alisa's voice lost much of its impudence.*
You: "But you're alone down there anyway..."
Alisa: "Hey!"
*She cried out loud and directed the flashlight right into my eyes.*
You: "Well, don't panic, trolls aren't gonna eat you there, I'll be back in a flash!"
*Alisa was screaming herself into a fit from down below but I couldn't make out the words.*
*However, I only managed to take a few steps before the ground yielded under my feet and before I knew it I was tumbling down.*
*I grabbed a thin root that somehow slowed down my fall...*
*... but it snapped under my weight and went flying down with me.*
*...*
Alisa: "You're alive?"
*I barely opened one eye as I felt a searing spotlight upon me.*
You: "Argh, put it away..."
*Alisa was squatting next to me and looking at me in an nervous manner.*
Alisa: "Any limbs broken?"
You: "I don’t know..."
*I've moved my hands and feet – everything seemed to be fine.*
*Given the height, I was pretty lucky to make it down alive!*
*I barely managed to stand up and examined the crash site.*
*Indeed, we were in some kind of long corridor. There was some kind of heavy wiring all along the walls and lamps encased in heavy metal holders attached to the ceiling.*
*In any other situation I would have guessed that it's a subway service tunnel, but it was hardly likely that Sovyonok has already reached such a level of infrastructure...*
Alisa: "Where are we?"
You: "I don't know but we have to get out of here!"
*Climbing the crumbled wall was hardly an option. In fact, I was wondering how we even survived a fall from such a height.*
You: "Well, it seems that we've got to find an exit somewhere else."
Alisa: "How do we do that?"
*Alisa asked, slowly turning pale.*
*Not a single trace of her usual arrogance remained on her face.*
You: "Well, I guess... There's gotta be an exit here, right?"
Alisa: "Probably, but which way do we go?"
You: "Now that's a good question."
*At first glance, it seemed like a good idea to head towards the camp (at least in the direction I thought it was), but I hadn't seen anything there that resembled an exit from the catacombs. And that means that we should rather try the opposite direction.*
You: "Give me that!"
*I snatched the flashlight from Alisa's hand and pointed its light into the darkness.*
You: "That way!"
*...*
*We were slowly proceeding forward, with Alisa keeping a firm grip on my hand.*
*In other circumstances I might have been surprised, embarrassed, or even rejoiced (how should I know?) but right now I was just eager to get out of here as soon as possible.*
*My bruises from the fall were aching. The blood was pulsing in my head like a heavy pendulum. Even the flickering spotlight that kept illuminating the same cement walls continually wasn't exactly raising our morale.*
You: "Damn. There's also Shurik..."
Alisa: "What?"
You: "Why did we go into the night forest in the first place? To find Shurik!"
Alisa: "Oh, just forget him."
You: "He might have fallen down here just like us."
*Of course, Alisa has a point – this wasn't exactly the best time to engage in a search mission. If we don't manage to get out, there would be a search mission for us instead.*
*But I couldn't just take my mind off this thought.*
*It was as if Shurik was standing right before my eyes, giving me a reproachful look.*
Alisa: "Look out!"
*Alisa yelled.*
*I almost crashed into a massive metal door...*
*A biohazard sign immediately caught my eye.*
You: "This means that we're in a bomb shelter..."
*I mumbled under my breath.*
Alisa: "Yeah, I've heard of something like that..."
You: "You have? Why didn't you mention it before?"
Alisa: "How would I know it'd be important?"
You: "I guess you're right... Fine."
*I grasped the door's wheel and pushed it as hard as I could, trying to turn it.*
*The rusty metal grated but refused to budge.*
You: "Stop slacking, help me!"
*Alisa hesitated a little but then grasped the handle and started to pull.*
*Finally we managed to turn the wheel and the door opened.*
*It was hard to mistake the room we entered for anything else. It was definitely a bomb shelter.*
*Cabinets full of gas masks and dry rations, lots of equipment, bunk beds and air recirculation systems – there was everything one would need to survive a nuclear war. Well, at least to survive the first blast.*
*Alisa clenched my arm even tighter.*
You: "What is it?"
Alisa: "What 'what'...?"
*She blabbered under her breath.*
Alisa: "I'm scared..."
You: "What are you scared of?"
You: "Indeed. What of?"
You: "We'd tumbled down into an abandoned bomb shelter, now we're wandering here in the dark, trying to find an exit... Oh, yeah, nothing to be afraid of."
*Those thoughts made me squirm and I instinctively drew nearer to Alisa.*
*She didn't say a thing, just blushed a little and turned her back to me.*
You: "Well, in any case..."
Alisa: "What?"
You: "We have to keep searching for an exit."
Alisa: "Well, there's another door."
*Indeed, there was a door on the far wall, just like the one that we came in through.*
*However, no matter how hard I tried to open it, it was stuck.*
Alisa: "Need some help?"
You: "Nope, it's jammed for good..."
*I glanced around the room, trying to find something that would work as a lever and noticed a crowbar in the far corner.*
You: "Great!"
*Alisa gave me a blank stare.*
You: "Watch it!"
*However, I still couldn't move the handle an inch even using the crowbar.*
*Totally exhausted, I flopped on a neatly made bunk and gave a sigh.*
You: "We have to walk back."
Alisa: "But we just came from there!"
*Alisa seemed to regain a bit of her self-control, as well as her usual rudeness.*
You: "Well, you can stay here if you want – there's water, ration kits, probably the radio's still working..."
*She looked at me spitefully but said nothing.*
*My whole body ached terribly.*
*It was only now I tried to relax that I began to realise how badly.*
*A deep wound on my leg was bleeding profusely, my hands were heavily bruised, blood was thickening in my hair.*
You: "And are you... okay?"
*I asked Alisa, either just out of courtesy or because I was really worried about her.*
*It took her some time to answer.*
Alisa: "How can we be okay in a situation like this?"
You: "Well, I mean that..."
*I pointed to the wound on my leg.*
Alisa: "Oh!"
*Cried Alisa.*
Alisa: "We need to sanitize it urgently!"
You: "No need. I'll survive."
Alisa: "Oh stop! We must do it, or you'll risk it getting infected and then they'll take your leg off! My granddad lost his leg that way in the war."
*Alisa looked truly concerned and I decided not to argue.*
You: "Okay, but it's kind of a long way to the infirmary."
Alisa: "Hang on."
*She smiled and started to rummage through the cabinets.*
*There was a fair chance of finding some kind of medicine in a bomb shelter, and soon enough Alisa pulled out a first aid kit with a triumphant look.*
Alisa: "Ok, hold still."
You: "Well, I'll try."
*Treating the wound with an iodine-soaked cotton swab felt like the touch of a red-hot iron. I clenched my teeth hard and hissed with pain.*
Alisa: "Oh, come on, it's not that painful."
You: "It is! Maybe you should try it yourself?"
*It was easier with my other wounds and soon enough I looked like a leopard – all covered in brown spots.*
You: "Thanks..."
Alisa: "Don't you think that was anything special, we just had to treat your injuries!"
*Alisa snorted and turned her back on me.*
You: "Sure, sure..."
*I refrained from arguing and got up from the bunk.*
*Even a short rest had definitely been good for me.*
You: "Well, shall we go?"
*…*
*Alisa clenched my arm, walking close in step with me.*
*We headed back slowly, carefully looking for a hole in the ceiling.*
*The tunnel seemed endless. We couldn't find the place where we fell down, not after five nor even ten minutes.*
Alisa: "Are we lost?"
*Alisa asked sadly.*
You: "It might be possible to get lost in the forest..."
*It just came to me that that's exactly what we'd accomplished half an hour ago, so to refrain scaring her even further, I continued with confidence:*
You: "But this is a single straight tunnel – you can't get lost here!"
Alisa: "So, where are we gonna end up then?"
*My words didn't seem to calm Alisa down enough...*
You: "We'll get outta here, there's always an exit."
Alisa: "Really?"
You: "Of course, there is! The workers that built it somehow got back up to the surface, didn't they?"
Alisa: "Yeah, I guess."
*It appeared that she was trying hard to look as bold as usual but it wasn't turning out well. In the dim light it was evident that Alisa was shivering. A look of extreme exertion was plastered on her face.*
You: "Fine. Let's move forward!"
*...*
*In a few minutes I noticed a hole in the floor. It looked like a shell crater, large enough to get ourselves through.*
Alisa: "What's down there?"
You: "Hell if I know..."
*I kneeled and pointed the light downwards. Damp ground, some kind of rail tracks.*
You: "Must be a mine."
*Alisa looked at me questioningly.*
*Of course, we could easily sidestep the hole but my instincts insisted that we wouldn't encounter anything good proceeding down the tunnel either – there would be either a dead end or yet another jammed door.*
*On the other hand, it was naïve to believe that we would find an exit in the mines.*
You: "We could give it a try. In the worst case we'll just come back – it's low enough to let us climb back up later."
*Her face took on a suffering expression. Then Alisa turned away from the light and quietly said:*
Alisa: "If you say so..."
*...*
*As I thought, we were in a mine. Miles of rust-eaten tracks stretched far away down the corridors. I could virtually see the overloaded minecarts creaking along these tracks ages ago. The walls were propped up by rotten beams and water occasionally dripped from the ceiling.*
*I wasn't sure whether it was scarier here or in the catacombs of the bomb shelter above. I'd say that 'up there' it was like a post-apocalyptic setting and 'down here' occult medievalism reigned.*
*In any case I was even more eager to get out of here, and do so as soon as possible.*
*Alisa didn't utter a word after we descended into the mine. She just walked next to me, clenching my hand so hard I started to worry.*
You: "Are you alright?"
Alisa: "No."
*She said quietly.*
You: "I understand that it can't be okay, but how are you holding up?"
Alisa: "Fine."
*She replied with that indifferent voice.*
You: "That's good, because..."
*I really wanted to say 'because if you go nuts too, it's gonna be a massacre'.*
You: "Because we will find an exit. We'll definitely find one."
Alisa: "Yeah..."
*It seemed she wouldn't last much longer.*
You: "We should go faster!"
*I quickened my steps and we reached a fork after couple of dozen metres.*
You: "Well..."
Alisa: "So, which way?"
*Alisa seemed to have completely disconnected from the outer world and didn't worry about what would happen to us, or how we could leave this place.*
You: "Well, let's think..."
You: "To the left or to the right? And what if we get lost...?"
*I decided to put a mark on the wall in case we get lost and return to this spot again.*
*Soon, a large cross scratched with a stone decorated one of the beams*
You: "So, now we're ready to go..."
*We'd been here already.*
*Finally we came out of a tunnel into some kind of a hall with a high ceiling.*
*Though it could hardly be called a hall; they must have used to mine something here. Coal, probably, or maybe gold.*
*The walls had been cut by pickaxes or pneumatic drills.*
*This place was pitch black, so our only salvation was the flashlight.*
You: "If it breaks, it's unlikely that we'll ever get out of here..."
*I noticed a red piece of cloth in its light.*
*It was a pioneer's neckerchief!*
*Shurik was obviously here somewhere.*
You: "Shurik! Shurik!"
*Only my echo responded to me.*
Alisa: "Why are you shouting? It's not like he can hear you..."
You: "You never know."
*Alisa didn't reply, just sighed.*
*There was no other exit from this hall.*
You: "Obviously, it's quite possible that there are some nooks in these tunnels we haven't checked yet..."
You: "So, we have to keep looking!"
*Following the curve, I saw a wooden door in the torchlight.*
You: "There you go, here's something!"
Alisa: "You think so?"
*Alisa looked a little refreshed.*
You: "Sure!"
*Frankly speaking, I really wasn't sure that there would be an exit behind this door.*
*Bu it wasn't like we had any choice anyway.*
*I pulled the handle...*
*We found ourselves in some kind of room that resembled either a boiler room or a utility room under the bomb shelter.*
*Empty bottles, cigarette butts, and other bits of debris littered the floor.*
*That proves that there is an exit from these caves!*
*I scanned the room with the flashlight and in the farthest corner I saw...*
*Shurik, doubled up and trembling all over.*
You: "Shurik!"
Shurik: "Who... who is that?"
*He stammered.*
You: "Shurik! We've been looking for you for all night and you’re just sitting here?! Get up!"
Shurik: "I'm not going anywhere..."
*He started quietly but with every word his voice gained strength until he was shouting at the top of his lungs.*
Shurik: "No, I won't go with you anywhere! You don't exist! You aren't here anyway! It's a hallucination! It's unscientific! Yeah, unscientific!"
You: "What do you mean by 'you aren't here'?! Here we are, we came searching for you!"
*Alisa had remained silent until now, but then she let go of my hand and took a few steps towards Shurik.*
You: "What are you doing...?"
*I asked quietly.*
*She hesitated for a moment but proceeded as if not hearing me.*
*Finally, having come close to the lost pioneer, Alisa fetched him a scathing slap across the face.*
Alisa: "You! We nearly died while searching for you! Those damned woods at night, that bomb shelter, these freakin' mines! I'm one mass of bruises thanks to you! And you what, you're just hanging out, drinking booze and seeing pink spiders, you bastard?"
*Shurik stared at her with a bemused look.*
Alisa: "Now then, get your ass up and move!"
Shurik: "No..."
*He began to whisper quietly.*
Shurik: "No..."
*Somewhere deep inside me, on the very edge of my awareness, I got a feeling that something really bad was going to happen now.*
*It happened. A premonition, intuition, or just an analysis of the situation, from the way Shurik was sitting, or the expression on his face hinted at his following actions.*
*And probably all of that together. I rushed to Alisa, the light furiously jumping all over the room and highlighting Shurik's face for a second, twisted with madness.*
*He was wielding a metal rod and if I had been a moment too late, he would definitely have smashed in Alisa's head with it.*
*But I made it.*
*Everything was like a dream: the distant shout of a girl, a hollow thud, the flashlight going out and the eerie silence, except for the heavy breathing of Shurik.*
*It took me a while to come to my senses.*
You: "What are you doing, you jerk?!"
*I checked my arm and it felt okay – the blow landed on the flashlight. So now we were in complete darkness.*
Shurik: "You won't get it, won't get me!"
*Shurik's hysterical laughter was quickly fading away in the distance.*
You: "Hey! Where are you going?! Get back here now!"
Shurik: "Won't get..."
*The yell vanished into the distance...*
You: "What a freak..."
*I've tried to fix the flashlight in the darkness. No way, Shurik has smashed it into pieces with his rod. Then I suddenly thought of Alisa.*
You: "Are you okay?"
*I've heard a quiet sob and at the same instant I felt her embrace hugging me tightly.*
You: "Okay, it's okay, it's all over now, everything's fine..."
You: "Well, in fact nothing was fine, but I needed her to get a grip on herself. Otherwise we stood no chance of getting out of here alive."
*I tenderly caressed her head.*
You: "I wonder, Alisa crying – is that a funny thing? Maybe in different circumstances..."
Alisa: "I'm scared..."
You: "That's ok, I'm scared too..."
*I noticed this strong and sudden transformation in Alisa.*
You: "But what the heck, anyone would be scared in these circumstances. Moreover, she's a girl..."
You: "But why aren't I scared? No, not scared – why am I still able to keep my mind clear and speak sense?"
*Might it be because I have to worry about more than just myself?*
You: "Ok, come on, we have to get out out of here anyway."
Alisa: "Hold on, just a sec..."
*Said Alisa quietly and the room became illuminated by the dim flicker of a lighter's flame.*
You: "Where did that come from?"
Alisa: "The statue..."
*She forced a gentle smile and handed me the lighter.*
You: "Alright..."
*I quickly swept my eyes over the room, searching for something that could be used as a torch.*
*There were some tattered rags and a rod among the debris on the floor. One of the bottles contained some liquid that smelled like industrial alcohol.*
*For better or for worse, in a minute I was holding something that resembled a flaming torch in my hands.*
You: "I don't know how long it will last, so we got to move quickly."
Alisa: "Where to?"
*Alisa seemed to be returning to her senses.*
You: "Let's go back. At least we'll reach the bomb shelter. For one thing, there's light there."
*She gave me a quiet nod and took my hand.*
*…*
*The torch was burning poorly: we had to re-ignite it every other minute. One didn't have to be an oracle to predict an extremely short lifespan for that rag we were using.*
*I became more and more afraid that we wouldn't leave the darkness in the mine. You couldn't rely too much on just the lighter.*
*However, we reached the hole that led up to the catacombs quite fast – it seems that I memorized the route after all.*
*We struggled to get up, scrambling over the rocks almost blindly.*
Alisa: "Ok, where are we going now?"
*Asked Alisa, getting her breath back.*
You: "What do you mean? We're going to that room with the bunks and cabinets."
Alisa: "Which way is that?"
*I opened my mouth to reply, but suddenly realised that I had not the slightest idea.*
*The hole looked the same from all sides, just like the walls, the floor and the ceiling. We had not a single hint to indicate the right direction.*
You: "Well..."
Alisa: "Don't you know?"
*Alisa asked sadly and sat on the ground.*
You: "No."
*I replied quietly, put out the torch to preserve it and sat next to her.*
Alisa: "Are we going to die here?"
*She rested her head upon my shoulder.*
*Alisa's voice sounded flat, one might even say calm, but I could feel that her body was trembling – either with cold, or with fear, or with both combined.*
You: "Don't be silly! Sure, things are getting worse, but they're still pretty far from 'we're gonna die'... They will come and rescue us in the morning. Olga Dmitrievna will call the police. So..."
You: "I would love to believe that myself."
Alisa: "I see..."
You: "Yeah..."
*…*
*I lost track of time sitting there...*
*I was afraid to go forward or backward, I was afraid to make a choice, as our torch definitely wouldn't last both ways. Wandering in total darkness without any source of light was definitely worse than waiting for the rescue here.*
*This way at least we would have some light left for an emergency...*
*Suddenly a rumbling started echoing in the distance.*
You: "Well, here is that emergency!"
*That was definitely the clank of door bolts' mixed in that rumbling.*
You: "Get up!"
*I harshly pulled Alisa to her feet and lit the torch with shaking hands.*
Alisa: "What is it?"
*She asked in dismay.*
You: "I don't know, but it seems there is someone. We have to run!"
*To be honest, I wasn't sure that it was such a good idea.*
You: "What if the mad Shurik is there? And, in fact, that's the least of all the evils I can imagine!"
*But we had no choice left.*
*The stones scattered beneath our feet. I desperately tried not to fall down, holding my hand with the torch out in front and dragging Alisa with the other.*
*She ran along in silence, breathing heavily.*
*I really wanted to look back at her, but didn't have the strength or time.*
*Finally the outline of the open door appeared before us and I leaped into the bomb shelter, readying myself to fight any foe that was there...*
*But the room was empty...*
*I swept my eyes across the room, trying hard to spot hidden monsters, Shurik, or any other evil entity, but it was all exactly the same as it was the first time we'd been here.*
*Except for the door, the second door... It was open!*
You: "Somebody has passed through here!"
*I spoke up triumphantly.*
Alisa: "Who?"
You: "Don’t know, maybe it was Shurik..."
Alisa: "But how did he manage to open it?"
You: "Who the hell cares! Come on!"
*...*
*There was another corridor behind that door, and it was ascending slowly.*
You: "So, we're getting closer to the surface."
*I was right, after several hundred of feet I stumbled upon a ladder leading to a small hatch on the ceiling.*
*It didn't take much effort to open it.*
Alisa: "What's up there?"
You: "Who cares, it's better than staying down here anyway!"
*I climbed the ladder and found myself surrounded by gloom.*
*However, this gloom was definitely lighter than the darkness of the catacombs; as my eyes got more used to it, the outlines of the walls, the ladder, and the door leading to the outside were emerging in the pale moonlight.*
*I helped Alisa to climb up and we literally sprang out of the building.*
*The exit from the catacombs was located in some sort of ruined building that resembled either a nursery or a country school.*
Alisa: "It must be the old camp..."
*Alisa sat on one of the swings and wiped the sweat from her forehead with the back of her hand.*
You: "I see... So, we found it after all."
*I smiled involuntary.*
Alisa: "What are you laughing at?"
*She frowned and pouted with displeasure. To put it shortly, she'd returned to her usual self.*
You: "So, it's not so scary here anymore?"
Alisa: "I wasn't scared there either!"
You: "Oh come on!"
