Alisa: "That's right, I wasn't!"
You: "Ah, whatever..."
*I was angry.*
You: "I really felt hurt because of Alisa. If not for me, she would have still been down there, in that damn mine!"
Alisa: "Where are you going?"
*She asked in a less self-assured voice as I turned around and walked slowly towards the camp.*
You: "Back to the camp."
Alisa: "Hey!"
*Alisa jumped up right away and started to walk next to me.*
*For a moment I wanted to say something nasty, but I wasn't ready to start the next argument...*
*We found the path we had taken before surprisingly fast. Even the two holes we'd fallen into.*
*It was only about two hundred metres from the old camp.*
*...*
*I stopped at the square and turned to Alisa.*
You: "Well..."
Alisa: "Well..."
*She looked uncertain, even confused.*
You: "Then..."
Alisa: "Sure..."
*Deep inside I wanted to yell at her, to scold her, even to insult her. On the other hand, I wanted to have a meaningful conversation.*
*In the end I just kept silent, turned around and slowly headed towards the leader's cabin.*
*But something persistently disturbed the quiet of the night. I keenly listened to it and realised that it was the snoring...*
*... of Shurik, who was sleeping peacefully on a bench!*
You: "Hey!"
*I called Alisa, who hadn't walked too far away.*
You: "Get up, you!"
*Shurik slowly came to his senses and stared at us blankly.*
Shurik: "Oh, is it morning already?"
You: "Morning? Yeah, sure..."
*Sometimes one acts first, thinks later.*
*Of course, it all starts in the brain, then the current comes through the neural links, thereby transmitting the command to the body.*
*But sometimes the subconsciousness just works faster than the consciousness. That's exactly why my fist swung and smacked Shurik in the guts, and it was only then that I realised what I'd done.*
*He coughed, trying to catch his breath, and writhed in pain on the bench.*
You: "What the hell was all that about?!"
*I already felt bad about it – I shouldn't have treated him so rough...*
Shurik: "What are... what are you talking about?"
*Shurik looked at me in shock.*
You: "In the mine!"
Shurik: "What mine?"
*He turned his head, completely confused.*
Shurik: "And why am I here?"
Shurik: "And why are you here?"
Alisa: "Stop fooling around!"
*Alisa barged into the conversation.*
Alisa: "You nearly killed me there! And now you're going to pretend like nothing happened?!"
Shurik: "What happened?"
You: "You really don't remember?"
Shurik: "Not a thing..."
You: "Ok, so what is the last thing you do remember?"
*Shurik tried to concentrate.*
Shurik: "Well, I was on my way to the old camp in the morning. I knew I could find some hardware for the robot there, so..."
You: "So?"
Shurik: "And that's all... I don't recall anything since then. Then I just woke up here."
*I let out a heavy sigh as I turned away.*
You: "Well, go ahead, sweet dreams..."
Alisa: "Hey, where are you...?"
*I ignored Alisa and stumbled away to the Olga Dmitrievna's cabin. She stayed, arguing with Shurik.*
*...*
*I sat in the deckchair and looked up at the stars.*
*This night they seemed to be brighter that usual.*
*Perhaps they seemed so because not too long ago my only source of light was a dim flashlight, and then that torch.*
*The stars are brighter than a flashlight and obviously a torch. Most of the stars, I guess, are even brighter than the sun, but they're so far away...*
You: "So, why have you come?"
*I asked without even turning my head – Alisa's footsteps could be heard well in advance in the silence of the night.*
Alisa: "Well, I..."
You: "What did Shurik say?"
Alisa: "He said that he doesn't remember anything, that it's 'unscientific' and nonsense like that."
You: "I think he really doesn't remember because of shock and stress."
You: "Who am I to say? I was in the same boat not too long ago."
You: "I am still in it though. Do I have amnesia?"
You: "Well then, why did you come here?"
*Then again, I guess I knew the answer – that's exactly why I hadn't gone to sleep but waited for her here.*
Alisa: "Well, I..."
*Alisa sat down next to me.*
Alisa: "Kind of... Wanted to thank you... After all, down there... You... That, you know..."
You: "No problem."
*I said gently and leaned back.*
Alisa: "Well, all right then..."
*She got up and was going to go.*
You: "If you think that I'm angry with you, I'm not. Everything is okay."
Alisa: "I didn't actually think that!"
*Alisa got worked up.*
You: "Fine then."
Alisa: "Okay..."
You: "Yeah..."
Alisa: "Then..."
You: "Just go already!"
*I said kindly and waved my hand.*
Alisa: "I'll go when I want to!"
You: "So now you don’t want to?"
Alisa: "I want to!"
You: "Well? Is something preventing you from going?"
Alisa: "Moron!"
*Alisa stamped her foot and quickly walked away from the leader's cabin.*
*I took a deep breath and stood up.*
*My head was terribly dizzy from fatigue.*
You: "Well, at least Olga Dmitrievna is sleeping already and I won't have to explain anything..."
*However it wasn't that easy.*
*The camp leader was standing in the middle of the room and was obviously preparing for a lengthy conversation.*
*Or rather for a debriefing.*
Olga: "Would you care to explain?"
You: "What's the matter? In fact, you didn't mind when we were going to search for Shurik?"
Olga: "And what, have you found him?"
*It looks like she was more concerned about me coming back late than the fate of the lost pioneer.*
You: "Yes, we have. By the way, why are you standing here in the darkness?"
Olga: "What?"
You: "I said, why in the darkness?"
Olga: "Because it's time to sleep."
*I couldn't agree with her more, although I was slightly surprised by such an abrupt mood swing.*
*...*
*I just barely stumbled to my bed and collapsed on it without undressing.*
You: "But still, Alisa... Alisa..."
*I just didn't know what I should think of her.*
*It wasn't because she'd been acting strange recently. No, on the contrary, all of her behaviour was quite consistent and understandable.*
*Even her returning to thank me.*
*I thought of Alisa much more than anything else that had happened tonight.*
*Although, if you get down to it, there was nothing supernatural about it.*
*Uncomfortable – sure, frightening, even spine-chilling – sure. Something related to my arrival here – hardly.*
*These thoughts put me to sleep.*
Ulyana: "Count me in!"
*I looked at Ulyana, astonished.*
*Her thirst for adventure seemed to have no limits.*
Ulyana: "Look! Night, ghosts, an old camp – it's great!"
You: "On the one hand, such company always promises trouble, but on the other hand, it feels safer going together..."
Olga: "Perfect!"
*Having said our goodbyes to the other girls and Olga Dmitrievna, we were left alone.*
You: "Do you consider this just an entertaining walk?"
Ulyana: "Well, yes. What's the matter?"
*Ulyana giggled.*
You: "Never mind... Really..."
*I sighed.*
Ulyana: "Oh, hold on! I'm gonna fetch a flashlight!"
You: "Ok."
*I was just about to suggest that myself.*
You: "It seemed I would not only have to visit an abandoned camp at night, but also look after a fidgety child..."
*Well since it's Ulyana...*
You: "I should be twice as cautious."
*Electronik had told us the old building was built right after the war.*
*It looked like a kindergarten (or like a barracks, I expected) and definitely could hold less pioneers than today's camp.*
* It had been abandoned for about twenty years.*
*Ulyana skipped forward as if everything was just a game to her.*
*I was ill at ease.*
*Actually that was normal for a person in my situation – in the night forest with scary animals and birds eager to swoop down on you, the full moon and this whole other world I had come into not too long ago.*
*I might be better off all alone, without needing to look after Ulyana who was running in front of me.*
You: "How hasn't she tripped over something yet?"
You: "Listen. Be careful..."
Ulyana: "Or what?"
*She turned around so quickly that I shivered.*
You: "Nothing. You may hurt yourself."
Ulyana: "Are you worried about me?"
You: "Of course I am. I mean, that's normal in such a situation."
*Ulyana pouted.*
You: "Listen..."
*I decided to continue our conversation – it's more relaxing and less scary this way.*
You: "But what is it about that old camp? You were saying back there, at the square..."
Ulyana: "Yeah, it's a really scary place! They say that all the pioneers died there and became ghosts which guard their last earthly refuge."
You: "What did they die from?"
*It was kind of hard to believe her scary tales.*
Ulyana: "How should I know? I wasn't even born back then."
You: "But you say it so confidently."
Ulyana: "I got information from a reliable source!"
You: "And where would that be from? From Alisa?"
Ulyana: "Not gonna tell you!"
You: "So what happened next? They died and became ghosts?"
Ulyana: "That's all..."
You: "What do you mean 'that's all'?"
Ulyana: "And now the souls of the dead pioneers roam around the camp and take everyone who dares to enter the world of the dead!"
You: "Wow! Ok, move along!"
*...*
*Time passed. We went deeper into the depths of the woods where the trees enclosed everything. Suddenly I realised that the forest had gone completely silent.*
*As if the night-birds had hidden in waiting for something and the insects had dug into the ground. Even the wind had died away.*
*I imagined that the streams of moonlight breaking through the thick foliage were ringing like plucked strings.*
*At last trees parted and we walked out to a large glade...*
*In the middle of it was an old building resembling a kindergarten.*
*It was shrouded in a thick fog. It looked like we'd come out into a cemetery, and the old camp building at its centre was a crypt.*
*According to Ulyana there were pioneers' souls roaming here. Truly it was like a mass grave...*
*I shivered and clenched the flashlight tighter.*
You: "A dreadful place to tell you the truth..."
Ulyana: "Oh come on!"
*She patted me on the back cheerfully which only made me more scared.*
*I was about to move forward when the moon showed among clouds, illuminating the glade, the old camp building and us.*
*Under that light everything seemed not so old. The crumbling brickwork, rusty slide and merry-go-round, the few panes of glass that miraculously remained in some of the windows, they all became more vivid.*
*I started to imagine that unknown monsters came out to the glade from the forest, a place of eternal darkness where even the moon can't reign.*
You: "I hope that they fear the light, like vampires... Though, maybe they could turn into giant wolves at full moon, like werewolves..."
Ulyana: "Why have you stopped?"
You: "I'm thinking..."
Ulyana: "About what?"
You: "Wy would Shurik want to come to such a place?"
Ulyana: "How should I know? We'll ask him when we find him."
You: "Yes. Obviously..."
*I mumbled and followed Ulyana.*
*She walked more carefully now, looking under her feet, stopping occasionally and even looking back several times.*
*That's natural. In some places the grass reached her chest height and nobody knew what could there be on the ground – scrap metal, stones, shattered glass...*
*We finally reached the door. Ulyana stopped and said.*
Ulyana: "Well! Here we are!"
You: "As if you'd won a race... This isn't a game."
Ulyana: "You're... you're..."
You: "What?"
Ulyana: "Boring!"
*I made a displeased face and stepped confidently into the darkness. It was dangerous to let Ulyana go first, dangerous for her, dangerous for me and maybe even for all the humanity.*
*The inside of the old camp building made an even more depressing impression. I even felt sad for it for a moment. Or probably for the people who lived here back then.*
*It had surely been full of the joy of children in the past. Pioneers ran around, played games I'd forgotten, a strict leader like Olga Dmitrievna maintained order. One session ended, a new one started.*
*And now it's just standing here, crumbling, rotting, forgotten.*
Ulyana: "Look!"
*Ulyana gave me an old ruined doll, falling apart from the damp. One more piece of the past.*
You: "So what?"
Ulyana: "Nothing..."
*She moved out of the light, but I noticed sorrow on her face.*
You: "As sad as a cemetery."
Ulyana: "Scary!"
You: "I haven't seen anything scary yet."
*It was indeed more relaxing in here than outside.*
*It really was like a cemetery, as you look for a specific grave while walking among countless tombstones, feeling discomfort inside, but then you find it and your soul calms. As you lie next to it...*
*I shuddered and let the flashlight play around the room. There was no sign of Shurik.*
*However what did I expect to find here? His corpse?*
You: "Looks like he isn't here..."
Ulyana: "What about the second floor?"
You: "Shurik!"
*I called loudly, but only my echo answered me.*
Ulyana: "Shurik! Come out!"
You: "See..."
Ulyana: "We should check anyway."
You: "Okay, okay..."
*...*
*There were no signs of life on the second floor either.*
*I sat on the stairs and hung my head, feeling doomed.*
You: "Where to next? We can't walk around the whole forest. And I'm already sleepy..."
Ulyana: "Why do you whine so much?"
*Ulyana was irritated.*
Ulyana: "Whining and whining. Just like a kid."
You: "Oh, am I wrong?"
Ulyana: "Right or wrong – what's the difference? If we are looking for Shurik, we must find him!"
You: "But how?"
*I begged.*
Ulyana: "I don't know! Somehow!"
*Ulyana looked like a strict teacher and myself like a careless schoolboy.*
You: "But shouldn't it be the other way around?"
Ulyana: "Look!"
*I turned the light in the direction she pointed and noticed a trapdoor in the corner, surrounded by garbage. It looked like it had been opened not too long ago.*
Ulyana: "He must be down there for sure!"
*Ulyana rushed to the hatch and made a great effort to open it.*
You: "Why would he go down there? It was probably... I don't know. Some villagers. Is there a village nearby?"
Ulyana: "I don't know..."
*Ulyana replied, breathing heavily. She hadn't managed to open the trapdoor.*
*I started thinking.*
*There was surely a possibility that Shurik might be there.*
*I didn't know much about this world after all. Actually, I knew nothing. Why should the local residents act according to my logic? Could it be that he tried to escape down there, running away from wolves?*
You: "Are there any wolves, though? Maybe owls."
You: "Okay, let's check it out..."
*I strained my muscles and managed to open the trapdoor.*
*It crashed loudly on the cracked wooden floor and, at the same moment, Ulyana leaned over the hatchway, lighting up the basement with the flashlight.*
Ulyana: "It's some sort of a tunnel!"
You: "A tunnel?"
*I pulled her back by the scruff of the neck to look in there myself.*
Ulyana: "Hey!"
You: "Curiosity killed the cat!"
*There was indeed a long tunnel running into the darkness. It looked like a dungeon from a computer game.*
*There wasn't any danger at first sight, no waist-deep water, no rats, no zombies...*
You: "Okay. Let's climb down there to look. But be careful!"
Ulyana: "Roger that!"
*Ulyana beamed.*
*...*
*It was really dark down there. The flashlight did little to help. It dimly illuminated concrete walls, lamps hanging from the ceiling, entangled in wires, and garbage abundantly covering the floor.*
*We slowly moved forward. I held Ulyana's hand, fearing she would run ahead of me.*
*Probably I was a bit worried about myself too, not wanting to be alone in this thick darkness.*
You: "Maybe we should go back? Shurik couldn't have gone so far..."
Ulyana: "What if he had a flashlight?"
You: "Well, even with a flashlight... What would he be doing here?"
Ulyana: "I don't know! Aren't you interested in what lies ahead?"
You: "Not a bit, I am more interested in..."
*I didn't finished the sentence – a massive metal door suddenly appeared before us as if from the thin air.*
*I instantly noticed a biohazard sign.*
You: "A bomb shelter?"
*I realised.*
Ulyana: "Probably."
You: "Have you heard anything about it?"
Ulyana: "I don't know. Does it matter?"
You: "Does it...? What if there is radiation?"
Ulyana: "What radiation? Where from?"
You: "Yes, you're right..."
*I took hold of the door's wheel and tried to move it.*
*It yielded, to my surprise, and groaned like a dying dinosaur.*
*The door opened at last and Ulyana ran in there as soon as it did.*
You: "Hey!"
*Behind the door was probably the main shelter room.*
*There were several beds next to me, some devices near the farthest wall, lockers. Fluorescent lamps on the ceiling brightly illuminated the room.*
You: "Where does the electricity come from? Are the backup generators still working?"
*I turned off the flashlight to save the battery.*
*Ulyana started to rummage in the lockers at once, taking out gas-masks, packages, and various tools.*
You: "Don't you have anything better to do?"
Ulyana: "No!"
*She looked at me with displeasure.*
*I sat on the neatly-made bed and looked around one more time.*
*Right across the room from me was a door, the same as the one we entered.*
You: "Could Shurik have gone through there (if he was here at all)? And why?"
Ulyana: "Why the long face?"
You: "Just tired..."
*I honestly confessed.*
Ulyana: "Then rest for a while!"
*Ulyana jumped at me and pushed me in the chest.*
*I reeled back in surprise and hit my head against the wall.*
You: "What are you doing!"
*I grabbed her arms and pulled her towards me.*
*She lost her balance and fell next to me.*
Ulyana: "Ouch!"
You: "You started this!"
*Ulyana stuck out her tongue and sat up.*
You: "Well, what's next?"
Ulyana: "There, the other door..."
You: "Oh, sure... Shurik predicted a nuclear war and decided to hide beforehand, did he?"
Ulyana: "Maybe he did?"
You: "Maybe? This shelter is too close to the surface. It could protect against the radiation, but if the bombs fell close enough..."
Ulyana: "You're so serious about these matters."
*She smirked.*
*I really didn't know when to be serious with her and when to joke.*
*It seems like the age difference between us really matters here.*
You: "How big is it? 10 years, more?"
*I sighed and stood up from the bed.*
You: "Okay. Let's try."
*But that door was less compliant than first one.*
*The bolts creaked, but the wheel didn't budge a centimetre.*
You: "Seems jammed..."
Ulyana: "Let me!"
*Ulyana rushed at the door with a crowbar she got who knows where and applied herself to it with all of her unimpressive weight.*
*That gave us a chance. I helped her and soon the door fell to the floor with a bang.*
*The hinges turned out to be completely rusted.*
You: "Seems that not everything was made to last back then."
*Behind the door there was a tunnel almost the same as the one we had come here through.*
You: "Don't do anything stupid!"
*I took Ulyana by the hand and stepped out of the room.*
*...*
*It was another endless tunnel.*
*The ceiling seemed to become lower, even though I logically realised that it did not change.*
*Ulyana didn't seem to be bothered at all, though. She was humming as she walked.*
*It annoyed me more and more.*
You: "Looks like you're having fun..."
Ulyana: "Of course I am! Aren't you?"
You: "No. I don't see any reason to have fun. We should find Shurik quickly and get out of here!"
Ulyana: "He may not be here at all."
You: "Then why the hell...?"
Ulyana: "Look!"
*Ulyana snatched the flashlight from my hand.*
*There was a huge hole in the ground a couple of metres in front of us.*
Ulyana: "He may be down there!"
*She walked to the edge and leaned.*
Ulyana: "Some rails..."
*It looks like there was a mine under this tunnel.*
*The depth of the hole was low enough to let us climb out of it, so I knew what Ulyana would say next.*
Ulyana: "Come on!"
*I wanted to object, but she had jumped down, leaving me in complete darkness.*
You: "Hey!"
*I had to follow her.*
*I don't know what they dug for here, but the mine had been abandoned for a long time. The planks had become damp, the rails were rusted, earth broke through the walls in some places.*
*The whole tunnel, leading into the unknown, was suspicious. It looked like it was about to collapse and bury us.*
Ulyana: "Come on!"
*Ulyana desperately pulled on my arm.*
You: "Where to? Why? What would Shurik be doing here?"
Ulyana: "What if...?!"
*She made a serious face.*
Ulyana: "What if he is sitting here somewhere, injured and waiting for help, and we just turn around and go, leaving him to die...?!"
*I estimated the height of the ceiling one more time and walked slowly after the restless Ulyana.*
*...*
*Soon we reached a fork.*
Ulyana: "Let's go to the right!"
You: "Wait!"
*I grabbed her arm.*
Ulyana: "What's the matter?"
You: "What if it's a dead end? Or worse than a dead end – a whole labyrinth?"
Ulyana: "Well..."
*She thought.*
Ulyana: "Then let's mark the starting point!"
*Ulyana picked up a large stone from the ground and scratched a cross on one of the beams that supported the ceiling.*
You: "Do you think that will help?"
Ulyana: "It will!"
You: "Probably I will have to choose where to go. I just can't leave it to a little girl."
*We’ve been here already.*
*At last we left a tunnel and found ourselves in a hall with a high ceiling.*
*Though it could hardly be called a hall; they must have used to mine something here. Coal, probably, or maybe gold.*
*The walls had been cut by pickaxes or pneumatic drills.*
*This place was pitch black, so our only salvation was the flashlight.*
You: "If it breaks, it's unlikely we will ever get out of here…"
*By its light, I noticed a red piece of cloth in the corner.*
*It was a pioneer neckerchief!*
*Shurik was obviously here somewhere.*
You: "Shurik! Shurik!"
Ulyana: "Shurik!"
*Only our echoes answered us.*
You: "I hope he's okay..."
Ulyana: "Don't worry! We'll find him!"
You: "But where could he have gone?"
*There was no other exit from this room.*
You: "It's possible that there are places in these tunnels that we haven't visited..."
You: "Seems like we still have to keep looking for him!"
*At last the ray of the flashlight revealed an old wooden door in the darkness.*
Ulyana: "Here we are!"
You: "Where?"
Ulyana: "Somewhere. I don't know."
*But she was right about something – at least we'd gotten out of the labyrinth.*
*After all these turns and forks I wasn't sure that we'd ever make it back but, on the other hand, why wouldn’t this mine have any exits?*
*Ulyana opened the door and stared into the darkness.*
You: "So, you won't go first as usual?"
Ulyana: "Well..."
You: "Okay."
*I stepped over the threshold.*
*A small room was beyond the door – maybe a storage room for the bomb shelter.*
*There were bottles and cigarette stubs, which means that somebody had been here before us.*
*It wasn't an encouraging fact by itself, but now I was certain that there was another exit from the mine, since (they couldn't have come the same way as we did.*
*The ray of light moved around the room, examining every corner. Suddenly it lit up a human figure...*
*It was Shurik, huddling up against one of the walls!*
You: "Hey! There you are! We have been looking for you for all night and you..."
*It seemed he hadn't even noticed us, just sitting and mumbling something.*
You: "Shurik!"
Shurik: "Who... who's that?"
You: "What do you mean ‘who’!? Your rescue team! Get up and let's go!"
Shurik: "I won't go anywhere with you!"
*He mumbled.*
Shurik: "You'll lead me around these tunnels again, I know! I won't go anywhere! I'll stay right here, you won't get me!"
You: "Stop with your nonsense!"

*I don’t know, seemed like there was something special in the expression of her face that moment, I didn't care.*
*The camp leader had been waiting for me at 'home'.*
Olga: "I thought you wouldn't come back."

*Finally, the tunnel had led us into a hall with a high ceiling.*

You: "Even if somebody finds it, I'll claim that it's not mine – I could always think up of a suitable excuse from my enormous experience."
*It feels like I've gone through more things today than all the previous days combined.*
*Thus, approaching the clubhouse I'd even forgotten to think about how awkward it must be to look for sugar there.*
*Shurik and Electronik were enthusiastically building something.*
*They were so busy that they didn't even notice me.*
*I looked closely.*
*It was some kind of a robot… Or at least the body of one.*
*Moreover, this robot was female, and had animal ears.*
*I didn't want to make up theories about purpose of such a device for luminaries of camp cybernetics.*
*Even though the design looked practically workable, I had my doubts about this robot ever being able to conquer Earth, or at least being able to do anything on its own.*
*But they seem to be enjoying the process more that the end result itself.*
*And that was something we shared, even though I didn't want to admit it.*
*On the other hand they weren't afraid of possible failure, criticism, or jokes… They were working towards their goal without paying attention to others, who would call it unrealistic or even absurd.*
You: "Oh, it looks like I'm truly comparing then to luminaries of the sciences…"
You: "Hey guys."
*I greeted them uncertainly.*
Shurik: "Oh! Semyon! Come in, we’re always glad to see you!"
You: "I was actually already inside…"
Shurik: "You know… Sorry for what happened yesterday! I barely remember anything, but… Well…"
You: "Never mind! It's ok!"
Sergei: "And what brings you to our humble abode?"
*Electronik looked at me slyly.*
*Sometimes I feel that he makes such a face when he knows something about the other person, something he can use in a right moment.*
You: "Sugar. I need sugar."
*An image from an ancient video game suddenly came into my mind, where some kind of unit like a builder or something cried out with all of its five-pixel stature: “Gold! We need more gold!”*
Sergei: "We got it."
*Said Electronik calmly.*
Shurik: "Why would you want it?"
*I felt that I shouldn't explain to Shurik that they want to bake a cake for him. I shouldn't spoil the surprise.*
You: "I don’t know... Olga Dmitrievna told me to get some..."
Sergei: "Ok, hang on."
*Electronik disappeared behind the door into the next room.*
You: "And why do you have sugar here? Why not in the canteen?"
Shurik: "When the food truck came last time, it was the last thing to unload."
Shurik: "And given that our building is the closest one to the entrance, they decided to leave it here to save some effort..."
You: "That's reasonable, isn't it?"
*The door opened, revealing Electronik hauling a huge bag behind him.*
*I really don’t know what the size of the cake will be, but that was obviously too much sugar.*
You: "Well, thanks, but I don't need it all..."
Sergei: "But where would we put it?"
*Electronik gave me a surprised look.*
Sergei: "We don't have a place for it. You asked for sugar – so take it."
You: "It seems that that previous smile of his wasn't there without reason."
You: "Maybe you'll help me then? It's not that far to carry…"
Sergei: "We're busy."
*He pointed his hand at the robot.*
*I gazed at Shurik. He owed me, after all.*
*He hesitated and then looked away in shame.*
*I sighed, took the bag and headed to the door.*
You: "Thanks anyway…"
*I said at parting, exerting myself.*
*But I didn’t make it too far.*
*Just after a mere twenty metres I had to put the bag down to have a rest.*
*I had no idea how much it weighed, but it felt like more than twenty kilos.*
*On the one hand, it was just two hundred metres to the canteen.*
*On the other hand even such a distance with this payload on my shoulder (or alternately in my hands, or on my legs, or under my arm, or even on my head) looked impossible for me to cover.*
*And as I resigned myself to move in minor sprints with prolonged pauses between them (so I could get there by night at least), I heard a voice behind me:*
Lena: "Maybe I could help you?"
*I saw Lena in front of me.*
You: "I don't think you can…"
*It was one of those moments when I felt painfully how dramatically I was out of shape…*
Lena: "I can bring a handcart."
You: "A handcart… Why didn't I think of that myself?!"
You: "Yes, that would be great!"
Lena: "Wait here, I'll be right back!"
*She smiled and ran in the direction of the square.*
You: "What would I do without her...?"
You: "It's good that Lena isn't always that shy and can take the initiative sometimes."
*I started to think.*
*She seemed quite unusual now. With no trace of shyness on her face and actually the complete opposite – smiles and confidence.*
*The offer of help wasn't something extraordinary by itself, but getting it from Lena…*
*A few minutes later she came back with a smallish handcart.*
*I put the bag down on it.*
You: "Thanks."
Lena: "Don't mention it…"
*She blushed and looked down.*
You: "Oh, the Lena we all know is back!"
Lena: "So I'll go then…"
You: "Yes, see you! And thank you again!"
*I shouted after her.*
*Sometimes I felt like there are two different people living inside of Lena.*
*But the second one – confident, happy and sometimes even bold – only appears when she talks to me.*
You: "Or am I making things up again...?"
*I thought that it would be better if I get all the ingredients at once, so I headed to Olga's Dmitrievna cabin with the handcart.*
*If every other place on the cake ingredient list made at least some sense to me, then flour from the library made none.*
*I thought hard about who would put it in the library and why, but couldn't find any sane explanation after all.*
*Given Zhenya's harsh nature, I'd better knock first.*
Zhenya: "Open."
*Zhenya peered at me closely from behind her glasses.*
Zhenya: "What do you want?"
You: "Umm… Don't think anything weird, but I need…"
*I didn't want to look like an idiot and decided to explain things carefully.*
You: "I need some flour. Olga Dmitrievna said that it's here. I understand that it sounds strange to keep the flour in the library but..."
You: "I was sent to you. And it's needed for a cake, to celebrate Shurik's rescue."
Zhenya: "Yes, I have the flour, what's so strange about it?"
*Zhenya replied with surprise.*
*At that second I felt like I'd been hit on the head with a heavy weight and lost the ability to understand anything at all.*
You: "Flour in the library… Sure, what's so strange about it…"
You: "We're in Wonderland, I'm Alice, now I'm gonna eat that magic mushroom and I'll be back home..."
Zhenya: "Hey!"
You: "Ah? Yeah!"
*I was daydreaming.*
Zhenya: "Wait here, I'll be right back."
*She disappeared behind the bookshelves while I folded my hands and started waiting.*
*A moment later the sound of a trapdoor groaning on its hinges reached me.*
You: "Hey, you need some help?"
*I inquired loudly.*
Zhenya: "I'll deal with it!"
*Zhenya barked out to me.*
Zhenya: "It seems to be in the basement so I'll have to wait a little."
You: "Okey-dokey..."
*A few minutes passed but Zhenya still hadn't returned.*
*I was starting to get worried when the door was suddenly flung open and Alisa came into the library.*
*She looked suprised too, seeing me here.*
Alisa: "What are you doing here?"
You: "Am I not allowed to be here?"
*I said rudely to her.*
*Alisa was clearly a bit overwhelmed.*
Alisa: "Ah, what do I care...?"
*She snorted and headed to Zhenya's table.*
You: "And why are you here then?"
*Alisa measured me with her eyes carefully and almost opened the mouth to say something, but then seemed to change her mind and turned away, hiding her hands behind her back.*
You: "Returning a book?"
*I blurted the first thing off the top of my head.*
Alisa: "It's none of your business..."
*She replied with a hint of hesitation.*
You: "What book is it?"
*Alisa was silent.*
You: "Oh, come on, let me see it! I wonder what Miss 'High-voltage-keep-away!' reads?"
Alisa: "It's none of your business…"
*Her voice was even less confident.*
You: "Ok, ok, I don't insist or anything…"
*In fact, I was quite interested to find out what Alisa was reading.*
*Moreover, I was quite amused to see a book in her hands.*
*TV, movies, or a computer, if one were available here – all these things seemed to be much more appropriate entertainment for a girl like her.*
*But she had a book instead…*
*My curiousity won. I struck at the right moment, when Alisa was looking away from me, and snatched the book.*
Alisa: "Ouch!"
*She screamed.*
*In the following second her face took on such an expression that it made me question my decision.*
You: "If I'm about to die at least I will know what for."
*I held a copy of 'Gone with the Wind' in my hands.*
*That was the same book that Lena was reading that evening on a bench.*
*I was so astonished that I completely forgot about my imminent death.*
You: "Is it interesting?"
Alisa: "Yeah…"
*Alisa answered without any enthusiasm, blushing.*
You: "Ok then…"
*I handed the book back to her.*
*Alisa threw it on the table and left the library quickly without looking at me.*
You: "So human things aren't alien to her. In the end, she too is a girl."
*After a quick review of everything that just happened, I concluded that there was actually nothing that strange.*
*Curiosity killed the cat.*
You: "Anyway, it's Alisa – and that means it could quickly turn into a total mess, plus I still have ingredients to collect."
Alisa: "Well, I'll come later..."
*Alisa left the library quickly without looking at me.*
*It got me thinking.*
You: "What could this book could be about if she was so ashamed of it?"
You: "An ashamed Alisa is something extraordinary by itself… But Alisa, ashamed about a book…"
You: "But what's the point in guessing now – there's no way to find anything out."
*Finally, Zhenya's deep groan rang out, reaching each and every corner of the library.*
Zhenya: "Grab it!"
*I passed by the book shelves and beheld the perspiring librarian sitting near the trapdoor leading into the basement with a small sack next to her.*
You: "Well, they might have some sort of a storehouse down there…"
You: "Thanks!"
*I took the sack and left the library.*
*Thank goodness it wasn't too heavy, so I carried it down to Olga Dmitrievna's cabin without too much effort.*
*Finally, it seems that everything had been collected.*
*I took the handcart with sugar outside and put the sack with the flour in it, followed by the two baskets of strawberries that somehow fitted in between.*
*And the beer was hidden under my shirt, just in case.*
*The day was coming to its end so I had to hurry, as cake itself will need some time to bake.*
*Of course, I'd rather enjoy lying down, closing my eyes and getting a decent sleep, but I just couldn't let Olga Dmitrievna down.*
*Indeed, after all the trouble I'd gone to, I even felt personally responsible for the success of this event.*
*Coming to the square, I stopped for a moment to catch my breath.*
*It wasn't that the cart that was heavy – it ran smoothly without any noticeable effort required. It was just that any physical exertion caused pain to me now. Both a physical and mental one.*
*I sat down on the bench and closed my eyes for a moment.*
Strange Girl: "What's that?"
*I didn't really give a damn who it was – probably just a fellow pioneer girl taking an interest in an unfamiliar companion in distress.*
You: "What are you talking about?"
*I asked her tiredly.*
*She didn't reply.*
You: "Those're the ingredients for a cake... Do you like cakes?"
Strange Girl: "I don’t know..."
You: "What, you've never tried cake?"
Strange Girl: "I don’t know..."
*Obviously the girl didn't get what I was talking about, but it didn't surprise me at that moment.*
*I really wasn't interested in the conversation. I was so tired that I had zero intention of classifying external distractions and tagging them as either common or uncommon.*
You: "I see..."
You: "Come down the canteen later and have a bite."
Strange Girl: "Really?"
You: "Really."
Strange Girl: "And what are they made of?"
You: "What?"
*I asked indifferently.*
Strange Girl: "These... Cakes!"
You: "Well... Some flour, some sugar, various fillings..."
You: "Now that's a strange question, doesn't she know what cakes are made of?"
Strange Girl: "And you have it all here?"
You: "Yeah, sort of."
Strange Girl: "And sugar?"
You: "And sugar..."
Strange Girl: "Could you lend me a little?"
You: "What for?"
*I thought it was over the top.*
*A sudden gust of wind made me grab the cart instinctively and open my eyes.*
*However, nobody was there.*
You: "Am I daydreaming?"
*I noticed, though, that the sugar sack was untied and a small heap of it had poured out.*
You: "Could it be that she was scared by the wind and ran away...?"
*Having fixed the sack, I got up from the bench and continued on my challenging strawberry way.*
*There wasn't a single person near the canteen. No wonder – dinner was still an hour away.*
*I brought the handcart to the rear exit and handed the foodstuffs to the camp cook.*
*She must have already been told what to do with them as she gave me such an unpleasant look. I'm not sure how long it takes to bake a cake, but it seems she had to hurry.*
*I just wanted to relax for the remaining time up until dinner.*
*In short, I was so tired that I just sat on the steps and waited.*
*My eyes closed themselves – I guess I got so tired throughout the day that I didn't even notice how someone came up to me until they patted me on the shoulder.*
Miku: "Hi!"
*Miku was standing before me.*
You: "Yeah..."
*I didn't need a mirror to imagine the expression of scepticism and annoyance on my face.*
Miku: "Oh, excuse me, I must have interrupted you..."
You: "No problem, I was just sitting here."
Miku: "Ah, alright then!"
*Miku beamed with a smile.*
Miku: "I was just coming to dinner. I thought that it's time already and then it appeared to me that it's too early, but I decided to check just in case – maybe it's not me who's mistaken, but the clock is!"
Miku: "Well, not the clock, clocks can't be mistaken, it's just that I misread it..."
*She seemed to be ultimately confused now and fell silent.*
You: "It's still about half an hour before dinner."
Miku: "Oh, that's great, then I'll sit here and wait with you if you don't mind?"
*Frankly speaking, I do mind.*
You: "You know, I have some matters to attend to..."
*I stood up quickly and left without saying goodbye, ignoring Miku as I always did, while she screamed something after me.*
*A minute later I got to the square and sat on the bench with the firm intention of finding a quiet and safe place here to wait for dinner.*
*I think this is the first time in the last four-and-a-half days when I've felt like this.*
*I wasn't just irritated because of some insignificant details but, indeed, I was really angry.*
*I've completely stopped caring about where I am and why am I here.*
*I don't care about how to get out either.*
*What's driving me mad is that I always have to carry out some stupid task given by our camp leader and it's always me who gets into stupid situations and sometimes even ends up looking like a clown.*
You: "If all of this is some alien trick or a plot of the Universal Mind they better consult with their psychiatrist!"
*I gritted my teeth and clenched my fists.*
You: "And most annoying thing is that everything that happens seems to happen by itself somehow!"
You: "I'd be happier not having to carry around bags of sugar that weigh a ton, but I had no choice at all!"
You: "I mean, any other option would lead to much worse consequences than a muscle strain or hurt pride…"
Ulyana: "Who are you angry with?"
*Ulyana was standing in front of me and smiled slyly.*
You: "Nobody really…"
*I answered absently.*
*But my fists gave me away.*
You: "Just like that…"
Ulyana: "Ok, ok, It's up to you… You better tell me, why did you run around the camp the whole day with some kind of bags?"
You: "I had to."
*I've replied reluctantly.*
Ulyana: "I guess it was food."
You: "Maybe it was…"
*Ulyana was about to say something, but at that moment the bell rang, calling the pioneers for dinner.*
*I sighed in relief and quickly headed to the canteen, leaving Ulyana behind.*
Olga: "Semyon, thank you very much!"
You: "For what?"
*The camp leader gave me a friendly smile.*
Olga: "For the cake of course!"
You: "Ah, sure..."
*It was at that exact moment that I understood the true meaning of the saying 'Keep your thanks to feed your cat'.*
Olga: "You didn't tell anybody? This ought to be a surprise!"
You: "Yeah..."
Olga: "That's my boy! And now off you go to dinner!"
*Olga Dmitrievna waved her hand, pointing at the canteen.*
*I stepped through the doorway slowly and started to look for a free place.*
*It turned out there were plenty today so I got the chance to eat all alone.*
*There was fish with mashed potatoes for dinner.*
You: "What misfortune once again – I'll be left half hungry. And didn't we have fish for lunch...?"
You: "Is it a fish-only day today?!"
*Having pushed my plate with the fried sea dweller away, I laid my head on my hands and closed my eyes.*
*But soon somebody came up to the table.*
Slavya: "Hey, are you alright?"
You: "I'm fine..."
*I replied without changing my position.*
Slavya: "Just tired?"
You: "Yeah, a little..."
Slavya: "That's bad."
*Slavya said it seriously.*
You: "Of course…"
Slavya: "You remember that we are going for the hike after the dinner, don't you? Have you prepared everything?"
You: "What? Where?"
*I opened my eyes and lifted my head up instantly.*
*Lena was standing by Slavya.*
Slavya: "The hike…"
*She was surprised.*
Slavya: "Didn't you know?"
You: "No..."
*I put my head down on the table and covered it with my hands.*
You: "If only I could sink into the ground right away…"
*The girls remained silent.*
*I was left alone with my thoughts for some time and that was fine by me.*
*Maybe I could have sat that way until the end of dinner time, but the strong voice of Olga Dmitrievna was heard from the opposite end of canteen.*
Olga: "Guys! To celebrate the miraculous rescue of our friend and comrade Shurik, we baked this cake for you all!"
*I lifted my head idly and looked towards the camp leader, but couldn't see anything beyond the pioneers' backs.*
Olga: "A second… Just a second…"
You: "And nothing about me. Nothing about me rescuing Shurik or gathering the ingredients for the cake…"
You: "As if that's how it ought to be."
You: "Well, it would be wrong to expect anything else from our camp leader."
Slavya: "Let's go! Or we won't get our share!"
*Slavya smiled.*
Lena: "Let's go."
*Lena agreed.*
You: "Yeah, sure..."
*I got up reluctantly and tagged along behind the girls.*
*As we approached the crowd of pioneers, Olga Dmitrievna was just putting the cake in the centre of the table.*
Olga: "And now..."
*The camp leader wasn't able to finish as Ulyana rushed out from the pioneer crowd and dived into the cake.*
*She managed to nibble it a few times before she was pulled away.*
*She was kicking and screaming.*
*I stared blankly from the outside at all this drama: Alisa smiling; Lena picking up some cream with her finger; all the furious pioneers around.*
*I felt completely out of place here. I thought that if I closed my eyes now and opened them again – here I am, back to the safety of my apartment in front of a computer.*
*I blinked but nothing changed; only the noise and the confusion became sharper.*
Olga: "Ulyana! That's the limit!"
Ulyana: "I... I just..."
*Well, in fact behaving like this is a bit over the top even for her.*
*Shurik broke into the conversation – or is it a court-martial?*
Shurik: "Please, Olga Dmitrievna! Since the cake is celebrating my return, it's no big deal..."
*He hesitated.*
Olga: "It doesn't matter!"
*The camp leader turned to Ulyana.*
Olga: "And you... Today I'm going to punish you to the fullest extent, so you'll behave next time!"
Ulyana: "Ah, whatever!"
*She snorted and turned back.*
Olga: "You won't be going on the hike with us tonight!"
Ulyana: "As if I wanted to!"
*I was more than willing to switch places with Ulyana and skip the hike instead of her, but who knew...*
*If I had have guessed beforehand, I'd have been the first one to go berserk and smash the damn cake!*
*After a couple of minutes of confusion, the pioneers started to disperse.*
Olga: "You have to get ready too! There'll be a lineup at the square in half an hour."
*I looked straight into the eyes of the camp leader, trying to express my attitude non-verbally, but it seems that I failed.*
Olga: "Don't be late!"
*Ulyana was sitting at the table when I approached her on my way to the exit.*
You: "So why did you do it?"
*She looked very upset. But she had a right to be so.*
Ulyana: "I wanted to."
*Ulyana replied abruptly.*
You: "So, you're happy now?"
Ulyana: "Of course I am! And you – good luck with the hiking!"
*She smiled mischievously, sprang up and rushed out of the canteen.*
You: "Well, a little bit of luck wouldn't hurt..."
*'Walk and you shall reach' – is was exactly this proverb that kept whirling in my head all the way down to the camp leader's cabin.*
*Somehow I just couldn't manage to argue, to pretend that I'm sick, or to just skip it without a reason.*
*The events of this day taught me submissiveness. Although sometimes whatever was happening made no sense to me.*
*As I walked in, I had a thought.*
You: "Well, in fact, how should I get ready?"
You: "Clothes? I only have an overcoat and a pair of jeans. Anyway, I forgot to ask whether it's going to be an overnight hike or not."
*I couldn't think of anything better, so I grabbed the sweater that I had on me when I've arrived in the camp (the night might be fairly chilly) and shuffled slowly off to the square.*
*All the camp was already there, although it was about ten minutes before the time Olga Dmitrievna had designated.*
*I settled down near the edge and waited patiently.*
*Night was falling.*
You: "If viewed from the outside, what a fairly comical picture we would make: a crowd of pioneers, lined up out of a sheer habit, like they were awaiting a silent command from the bronze Genda."
You: "And all this happening in the scarlet rays of the sunset."
*And there he is, waving his hand and screaming 'attack' as roaring soldiers with red neckerchiefs charge into the battle against some ghostly enemy…*
*But Olga Dmitrievna showed up and started to talk instead of Genda.*
Olga: "It seems everybody is here… Great!"
*I was so tired today that I couldn't even think about anything, so I ended up just listening to the camp leader.*
Olga: "Now, today we'll go hiking!"
Olga: "It is essential for every pioneer to be able to come and rescue his comrade, to offer a helping hand in the hour of need, saving them from a hopeless situation!"
Olga: "We have to learn to do all these things together!"
*A whisper that ran through the pioneer crowd suggested that most probably this truly epic expedition would end in a clearing in the forest, several hundred feet away from the square.*
*Somehow I thought so too.*
Olga: "We'll walk in pairs. So, if you haven't chosen a partner for yourself yet, now's the right time do so!"
*Pioneers quickly caught on to the idea and started to match in pairs.*
*It looked like I was the only one without a partner.*
*Slavya was enthusiastically discussing something with Olga Dmitrievna, Lena was with Miku, Electronik was, of course, with Shurik.*
You: "Well, it might be not a bad idea to go alone after all."
Olga: "Semyon!"
*The voice of the camp leader pulled me out of my thoughts.*
*I went up to her reluctantly.*
Olga: "I see that you haven't found a partner."
You: "Seems like it..."
Olga: "Then you'll join Zhenya – she is alone too."
*I was struck with that special kind of despair that only a true loner can experience.*
*So, it appears that I'm left with the prickly librarian that I wouldn't risk spending a couple of hours with even if I was paid for it?*
You: "Although, we both seem to be in the same boat now..."
*I slowly approached Zhenya.*
You: "Well, I guess we'll be going together..."
*She looked up at me.*
Zhenya: "Don't you even think that I'm glad!"
*Said Zhenya seriously.*
You: "Why on earth you should feel glad?"
*I asked naïvely.*
Zhenya: "Never mind! It would be much better if you'd just shut up."
You: "Eh, it couldn't get any better than this..."
*She turned her back on me and followed the other pioneers.*
*I still haven't seen any special reason to walk in pairs.*
*Anyway, we were walking on the well-trodden forest trails and it would be quite difficult to get lost here even if I wanted to.*
*Moreover, while we'd already been hiking for half an hour, we weren't rushing into the depths of the forest, trying to face all the dangers that could test our courage and harden our pioneer spirits, but instead were just walking around in circles.*
*However, if we take into account that Olga Dmitrievna was our chief, this hike could be compared to a hobbit's march from the Shire to Mordor...*
*Just as Zhenya insisted, I was following her at a distance in silence.*
*The librarian seemed to be perfectly okay with it.*
You: "Hey, don't you know when we'll reach our destination?"
Zhenya: "Our what?"
You: "Ahem, the place where we'll settle down and set up camp."
Zhenya: "The whole point of this hike isn't to set up a camp but the hiking itself! You don't get it!"
*Yeah, it seemed that I didn't understand a thing about hiking...*
You: "I guess you're right, but still…"
Zhenya: "I don’t know!"
*She replied sharply and quickened her pace.*
*I caught up with her and asked:*
You: "Listen, why are you always so..."
*I was about to say 'mean', but stopped short.*
You: "I haven't done anything bad to you and I'm not going to!"
*She glared at me in surprise.*
Zhenya: "Always so... What?"
You: "Well, unsociable... Kind of... Or is it something about me?"
Zhenya: "Oh cut that stupidity out already!"
You: "As you wish..."
*I decided not to start a conversation with her for the rest of the hike.*
*...*
*At last Olga Dmitrievna decided to end this Sisyphean toil.*
Olga: "It's time to halt."
*The place chosen turned out to be a quite large glade with a few tree trunks laid in half circle to make an improvised arbour, with the remains of a campfire in the middle.*
*Obviously such hikes are a tradition of this camp.*
*I was sent to gather firewood together with the other boys.*
*It didn't take long because there were a lot of branches and logs of various sizes lying around.*
*Eventually Olga Dmitrievna lit the fire using some old newspapers.*
*I was eager to know what was written there but couldn't discern anything other than Soviet symbols.*
*Pioneers took their places on the fallen log benches and started to talk about things.*
*It seems that the final goal of this event had been achieved.*
You: "The only things missing were a pot of fish soup, aluminium cups of vodka, and a guitar."
*But I wouldn't be surprised if all if these would appear somehow.*
Slavya: "What are you thinking about?"
*Slavya sat next to me.*
You: "Oh, nothing special... Just enjoying the hike."
*I answered sarcastically.*
Slavya: "You don't look too happy."
You: "Well, I'm not about to jump for joy, sorry about that."
Slavya: "Okay, I won't disturb you. "
*She sat with me for a while, but after realising that I wasn't in the mood of talking she left me to enjoy my introspection all alone.*
*And all I wished for was to lie down in bed and fall asleep as soon as possible, but I was being surrounded by smoke and the useless chatter of pioneers around me instead.*
*They were cheering and laughing and in general enjoying this warm summer evening.*
*In the far side of the glade I noticed that Lena was arguing with Alisa intensely.*
*'Intensely' and Lena seemed like complete opposites to me.*
*Slavya had left to go somewhere after our conversation it seems.*
*Electronik and Shurik were trying furiously to prove something to Olga Dmitrievna.*
*Looks like I'm the only one who doesn’t belong here.*
You: "But on the other hand why should I care?"
*All I was doing was just watching the fire.*
You: "There is a saying that claims that one could watch it forever, as well as running water."
*But there was also some third thing there…*
You: "What was that?"
Olga: "One could watch three things forever: burning fire, running water and how other people work!"
*The camp leader pulled me out of my daydreaming.*

*Night had fallen onto the camp. An absolutely normal and unremarkable night.*
*One of those nights when the dark sky, stars or crescent moon don’t trigger any special emotions, when the crickets' chirping and the singing of night birds seemed more like an everyday routine than a nocturnal chorus.*
*I wandered around the forest with no special purpose, trying not to get too far from the camp.*
*After all, there was a chance to meet Ulyana out there, and that natural disaster would probably be even worse than the camp leader.*
*I sat down on a fallen tree and started thinking.*
*Why is this all happening to me? Why do I keep getting myself into foolish situations, every time and everywhere?*
You: "Even having suddenly appeared in a weird pioneer camp in the middle of nowhere, I don't get to become a subject in an experiment, a victim of a sick cosmic mind, or a participant in an intergalactic war on the side of a group of suicide-prone pacifists, like a regular hero of science fiction."
You: "No, I get to hide in a night forest from a raving camp leader and her workhorse pioneers..."
*The stars in the sky were shining brightly.*
You: "Perhaps they give their light not only to me and this camp, but also shine on the city where I was born, and where my old home is..."
*It was as if a pain settled in my chest.*
*I envisioned my old flat clearly, and a detestable burning started making its way from my stomach to my throat.*
*No, it was not wistfullness. More like a sad reminiscence.*
*Because despite all that's happened, I've felt more alive in less than five days here than I had for the last several years there.*
*Now I really wasn't sure if I wanted to get back.*
*Only one question still ate at me – how and why I ended up here. It flared up yet again in my mind.*
*I haven't spent much time seeking answers or even just thinking about my situation lately.*
*My thoughts were occupied with everyday, routine affairs.*
*And now, in order to break away and be able to wish to stay here for good, I need to understand the nature of this place.*
*It's just that even a nightingale in a golden cage has a right to know how and by whose will he got in there. And after that, to make the choice whether to stay or not...*
*Probably I would have been lost in my existential thoughts for a long time, but I heard voices approaching – Olga Dmitrievna and the pioneers.*
You: "Looks like they're proceeding with their hike..."
*I headed to the camp at a fast pace.*
You: "I have no desire to go back to the camp leader's cabin because I would surely be scolded, and just waiting for it is much worse."
*Soon enough I arrived at the beach.*
*And I wasn't alone here – a pioneer uniform was lying on the sand. A girl's one...*
*But no one seemed to be swimming in the water.*
*I almost thought it was some new devilry when suddenly a voice came from behind.*
Slavya: "Skipping out on the hike?"
You: "..."
Slavya: "I thought you were still in the woods."
*I turned around and saw Slavya in a bikini.*
You: "Sorry, I guess I interrupted you."
Slavya: "That's okay, I'm almost done."
You: "Why did you decide to have a swim during the night?"
Slavya: "Oh well, is it prohibited?"
*She smiled.*
You: "Well, no... It's just... Won't Olga Dmitrievna mind you leaving early...?"
Slavya: "But you did the same!"
*Slavya gave me a quick glance.*
You: "Yeah, I did..."
*I sat down on the sand and stared at the river.*
You: "You didn't like the hike, did you?"
Slavya: "No, it's not that... I just wanted to be alone for some time."
You: "And I've interrupted you."
Slavya: "No, not really."
You: "That's not like you at all."
Slavya: "What are you talking about?"
You: "Well, to leave like that..."
Slavya: "Well, I'm not a robot that can only act according to a predefined program."
*She laughed.*
You: "Yeah, that's right..."
*I was still puzzled, and my fatigue was also becoming stronger and stronger.*
*My mind was absolutely blank.*
*To be precise, it was so heavy and full so that not even a single idea would have the chance to dwell there.*
*If I would compare my brain at its prime to a broad highway full of speeding thoughts overtaking each other and causing giant chaotic crashes, then now it's nothing but a forgotten tiny path in a distant desolate forest, which is only used in times of absolute necessity.*
*So I said the first thing that crossed my mind:*
You: "Don't you think it's all pretty strange here?"
Slavya: "Strange?"
You: "Everything that happens here. It's the ideal model of a pioneer camp."
You: "Of course, it's not like I know a lot about them, but it looks exactly like I imagined it."
Slavya: "What are you talking about?"
*Slavya glanced at me perplexedly.*
You: "Did you ever feel that you're not where you belong?"
Slavya: "I don't know."
You: "More precisely, not where you are meant to be at all. As if thousands of kilometres away from home, or even in another galaxy."
Slavya: "I don't understand you..."
You: "We're similar in this..."
*I lay down on my back and looked at the stars.*
You: "And what would you think if I told you that I'm an alien from the future?"
Slavya: "Are you?"
*Asked Slavya in dead earnest.*
You: "Well, let's assume I am. How should I return to my time?"
Slavya: "Do you really want to?"
You: "Yeah, all the conversations with her that have to do with my situation, even the slightest hints of it, always end up at the same place."
You: "It's like she's offering me a chance to stay. Almost insisting on it."
You: "Well, let's say that I'm not sure. There, as we could call it, everything is like home to me... Or rather more familiar."
You: "Practically everything is known to me and I'm prepared for any situation."
You: "And here it’s the other way around, literally every little thing comes as a surprise. And everything's... different."
Slavya: "Is it really that bad?"
You: "I wouldn't call it bad... Unfamiliar. Unclear. Sometimes it can be hard to change something. Especially for people with my personality."
Slavya: "But what do you really want?"
You: "To start with, I can't answer that question until I find out exactly where 'here' is."
Slavya: "Then go and find out!"
You: "If only it was that easy..."
Slavya: "But what's so difficult about it?"
You: "Everything's difficult! I don't even know where to start... And I'm constantly being distracted!"
Slavya: "You are talking about it so seriously, it's almost like it's all real!"
*She laughed.*
You: "Who knows..."
*A pretty long silence followed. Suddenly, Slavya sneezed.*
You: "Bless you."
Slavya: "Thanks!"
You: "It wasn't a good idea to swim at night. You could get ill. Hurry to your cabin, it's cold out here."
Slavya: "It's nothing, I'd rather sit here with you a bit more. Now, just let me dress."
*Well, I was certainly flattered, but...*
You: "Let's go, I'll walk you."
*But we didn’t even walk a dozen steps before Slavya grasped my arm.*
You: "What's the matter?"
Slavya: "Oh, I suddenly felt dizzy..."
*I touched her forehead. It was burning.*
*I was never able to measure body temperature by touch, but in this case it was obvious.*
You: "I told you!"
Slavya: "Achoo!"
You: "Come on, come on!"
Slavya: "No... I could infect Zhenya... Listen, we'd better go to the infirmary."
You: "And what would you do in the infirmary at night alone? That's nonsense!"
Slavya: "No, it's not nonsense! If you don't want to help, I'll go by myself!"
*She let go of my hand, and was ready to leave.*
You: "Don’t get upset. Put this on, it's cold!"
*I handed her my sweater, which I'd brought with me on the hike.*
You: "Finally found some use for it, good boy."
Slavya: "Thanks!"
*She pulled the sweater on and gave me such a tender and caring look, that I just couldn't argue with her any more.*
You: "Okay fine, the infirmary it is, as you say!"
*Five minutes later we were standing by the infirmary door and Slavya was picking out the right key.*
*I still considered this idea quite foolish. Nobody ever died from the common cold.*
*At least not in the past century.*
*I couldn't see any good reason to spend the night in the infirmary.*
*Finally Slavya opened the door and leaned on my arm.*
Slavya: "I'm still a bit dizzy."
*She said guiltily.*
*Slavya landed on the bed, I sat on the chair nearby.*
You: "Still, listen! Alone for the whole night in the infirmary..."
You: "After all, at least Zhenya could get you a glass of water, if you needed one. She wouldn't catch the illness – she's young and strong."
Slavya: "It's alright. I don't want to bother anyone. And the nurse will come tomorrow."
*I suddenly imagined myself in Slavya's place. Imagined that I had to spend the whole night here, alone...*
*And shivers ran down my spine.*
You: "Listen, maybe I can stay with you for a while..."
*I owed a lot to Slavya. And in fact, I didn't even want to leave.*
Slavya: "What for? Everything will be fine. Thanks for walking me over. You should go and get some sleep."
You: "I still think..."
Slavya: "It's fine."
*For a moment I thought...*
*Of course, nothing terrible will happen to her here, but I myself would feel more relaxed if I stayed with her.*
You: "I think..."
Slavya: "Oh, come on."
*Slavya cried out, as if offended.*
You: "You won't throw me out, will you?"
*I smiled slyly.*
Slavya: "Alright. But if you get infected, you only have yourself to blame!"
*I was happy with my little victory.*
Slavya: "Ok, then what shall we do?"
*There should be some playing cards in the chest.*
You: "Durak?"
*In fact, I didn't know any other games except that one and poker.*
Slavya: "Okay."
*We spent a lot of time playing. I completely lost the track of time.*
*We chatted, laughed a lot.*
*Slavya didn't seem ill at all.*
*Then midnight came...*
Slavya: "Time to sleep."
You: "Probably..."
Slavya: "But where are you going to go?"
*She gazed at me.*
Slavya: "Come on. You shouldn't be sitting in here with me."
You: "I can do it anyway..."
You: "At the moment I could even fall asleep standing up."
*Slavya watched me for some time, and then drew the curtain and said.*
Slavya: "Good night!"
You: "Night."
*I lowered my head on my arms and fell asleep in an instant.*
*Despite being exhausted, I slept uneasily. It was more of a slumber.*
*My awareness kept leaving me and returning again.*
*The best possible state for dreaming something psychedelic...*
*Bus number 410 drove past the room, it was snowing from the ceiling, and my computer's monitor suddenly rose from the middle of the table.*
*Wallpaper blended through the walls, rubbish piles rose through the floor, and my old bed materialized in the corner.*
*I was in my old flat again.*
*The scenery changed to that of my home town.*
*It was like I was running through endless hordes of people, bustling in and out.*
*And then darkness fell on me. Primal, universal darkness.*
*I jumped up in terror. I was sweating like a river.*
*Slavya was looking at me worriedly from the bed.*
You: "Just a bad dream..."
*I attempted to smile.*
Slavya: "You were screaming..."
You: "Screaming what?"
Slavya: "I don't know. It was incomprehensible."
*The clock only displayed 0:30.*
Slavya: "Semyon."
You: "Huh?"
Slavya: "I'm freezing..."
*Slavya was rubbing the arms of her sweater, shivering.*
You: "Hang on, I'll find a blanket."
*I searched through one cabinet after another, swearing to myself about how the damn infirmary had nothing to cover up the patients.*
You: "I'm sorry, there's nothing here..."
You: "Wait, I'll run and fetch something."
Slavya: "You don't have to. Would you just lie here with me? It'll be much warmer."
*She was absolutely serious.*
*Her voice sounded so piteous that for a second I was left breathless.*
You: "Are you sure that... it... is okay?"
Slavya: "So it’s not?"
*She asked, blushing.*
You: "No, why..."
*I slowly took off my shoes and lay on the very edge of the couch, trying to occupy as little space as possible, trying to shrink and stop breathing.*
*Slavya gently embraced me and rested her head on my chest.*
Slavya: "Yeah, that's better."
*She purred.*
*I was unable to say anything and just lay there calmly.*
You: "Very good..."
Slavya: "Thank you."
You: "For what?"
*Slavya kept her eyes closed and seemed ready to fall asleep at any second.*
Slavya: "For being here."
You: "It's fine..."
You: "Two minutes ago she was desperately trying to get rid of me."
Slavya: "No, really."
You: "Then, you're welcome."
*She said nothing but I was sure that Slavya smiled.*
You: "Contact us any time, as they say!"
Slavya: "You're so kind, you care so much."
You: "Well, I try."
Slavya: "You're a good friend."
You: "Friend? Well, yeah, probably..."
*Somehow this word hit me painfully.*
*On the other hand, there was no reason to believe that I was something more to Slavya than just a friend...*
You: "What are these thoughts about anyway?"
You: "You too..."
*I just couldn't bring myself to find the right words.*
You: "What's up with the 'You too'? It's been a pleasure dealing with you, we hope for further mutually beneficial cooperation?"
You: "Or – yeah, it’s cool being friends with you too, let's go and play in the sandbox?"
*This was twice as hard to endure with Slavya lying right next to me – I can't run, I can't hide, and even without her looking me in the eyes, I know that she sees right through me.*
Slavya: "You're distressed by something, aren't you?"
You: "No, I’m fine."
Slavya: "But I can tell that you are."
You: "Well, maybe..."
Slavya: "Want to talk about it?"
You: "Well, not really... In fact, there’s nothing really to talk about."
Slavya: "Then you don't really know why you’re upset?"
You: "Yeah, probably."
Slavya: "Then why get upset in the first place?"
*Slavya laughed.*
You: "I guess I shouldn't."
Slavya: "That's great!"
*She hugged me even harder.*
You: "Not cold now?"
Slavya: "I'm fine. Just tell me if you're not comfortable."
You: "No, it's okay."
Slavya: "Like that time? On the boat?"
*My muscles, as if remembering that rowing competition, reminded me of it with a dull ache.*
You: "It's totally different."
Slavya: "Okay, okay."
*She said slyly and raised her head a bit.*
Slavya: "So, everything is fine?"
You: "Yeah, perfect."
*I started to worry. Slavya surely wanted something from me.*
*Wanted me to do or say something.*
You: "But what...?"
Slavya: "Are you sure?"
You: "Yeah... Probably."
Slavya: "Well then. Have a good night!"
You: "You too."
*...*
*After a while, she fell asleep.*
*I checked the clock out of the corner of my eye. It was only 1 A.M. and that meant that I still had to lie in this position until morning.*
*I wasn't really concerned about my arm going numb.*
*Just, being so close to Slavya, in such a dangerous proximity, I couldn't sleep at all.*
*Various thoughts were invading my head.*
You: "Did she really consider this whole situtation normal?"
*...*
*Just when I was thinking how bad it would be if anybody found us, the door opened, the light switched on and Olga Dmitrievna rushed in.*
*My heart jumped and stopped for a moment.*
Olga: "Semyon..."
*Started the camp leader in a diabolically calm voice.*
Olga: "I've been searching for you everywhere, and you – you escaped from the forest ahead of time, didn't come to the cabin to sleep, and now you're seducing our best pioneer!"
*Slavya instantly woke up.*
*She was staring at the camp leader with a sleepy eyes for a few seconds, and then instantly understood what's going on and jumped from the bed.*
Slavya: "Olga Dmitrievna! It's not what you think! I just fell ill and Semyon walked me here."
Slavya: "And then I got cold and... I told him to go to to his cabin."
Olga: "Oh, yeah, sure! So you're sick, are you?"
Slavya: "I am..."
*Answered Slavya humbly.*
Olga: "Then you have to get treatment!"
*She watched me menacingly.*
Olga: "And you! Get up and follow me!"
*I understood that arguing was not an option and left the infirmary, not even looking at Slavya.*
*We reached the square without saying a word.*
*Olga Dmitrievna viciously looked over at me and said:*
Olga: "Time to go home! I need to have a serious talk with you."
*I felt awful the whole way.*
*The camp leader silently followed me.*
*I think that once again I've got into a stupid situation which will be perceived totally wrong by everybody.*
You: "Ah... nothing to discuss..."
*What if I were in Olga Dmitrievna's place? Two teenagers cuddling in the empty infirmary... at night. It's hard to come up with any apologies.*
*The worst thing is that all these things always happen specifically to me!*
*I always considered myself to have an analytical mind. However, I rarely got to put it into practice.*

Olga: "Would you care to explain yourself?"
*She seemed to have calmed down a bit.*
*At least this side of her character was appealing. She was, of course, an impulsive woman, but she also cooled down quickly.*
You: "Slavya already told you everything..."
Olga: "You expect me to believe that?"
You: "I can't force you to believe it, but I am not going to invent any excuses either, because it's the truth."

Olga: "Tomorrow I will decide what to do with you."

You: "Interesting, why does she only blame me for what happened? I wasn't there alone, after all."
You: "Slavya is a role model pioneer of course, but..."
*No, I didn't intend to shift the blame to her. I just felt too ashamed for getting into an idiotic situation once again.*
*Involuntarily, with no malicious thoughts, not expecting any trap...*
*I could have lay there pitying myself for a long time, but fatigue overtook me, and I blanked out.*
*I didn't think about Ulyana that evening at all.*
You: "That thing with the cake... Like it didn't even happen..."
*Though I remembered well her resentful, disappointed face.*
*Maybe in some other situation I would never have decided to go to her, but now a fine reason to leave this place and end this stupid hike has appeared.*
*Recalling that Olga Dmitrievna told me to be prepared for new tasks, I decided not to ask for her permission, and after choosing a proper moment I disappeared in the woods.*
*Night fell on the camp.*
*I mentally thanked the camp leader for not researching the land too well, since this meant civilisation was only a few hundred metres away.*
*Another long walk through the night forest was not in my plans.*
*Soon I came to the square and hesitated.*
You: "Won't it look silly?"
You: "What would I tell Ulyana? Moreover, why would I go to see her in the first place?"
*My head was so heavy and full that there was no room in it for the development of any ideas.*
*If I would compare my brain at its prime to a broad highway full of speeding thoughts overtaking each other and causing giant chaotic crashes, then now it's nothing but a forgotten tiny path in a distant desolate forest, which is only used in times of absolute necessity.*
*So it's better not to think about anything and just act.*
You: "But where should I go? Maybe to her cabin? And what if she's not there?"
*All of a sudden, something knocked me down and I fell to the asphalt. It's a good thing I had time to stretch out my arms, otherwise I would have broken my nose...*
Ulyana: "Gotcha!"
*I quickly got up from the ground and saw Ulyana standing before me.*
You: "What are you doing?!"
*I couldn't stop myself from shouting, despite my best efforts.*
Ulyana: "You shouldn't be stargazing!"

*The smile instantly disappeared from Ulyana's face.*
You: "What, exactly, is my fault?"
Ulyana: "Everything!"
You: "You mean I am to blame all the time?"
Ulyana: "Yes!"

You: "Great..."
*I suddenly wanted to get away from this place as fast as possible.*
You: "But it was because of you I came here..."
Ulyana: "What?"
You: "I guess you are quite bored, given that everybody is hiking, and you're alone here..."
Ulyana: "I don't care!"
*She yelled cheerfully.*
Ulyana: "Well, if things are that way, what do you want to do?"
You: "What do you mean?"
Ulyana: "Well, if you came here because of me!"

You: "After such a greeting I no longer want to do anything."
Ulyana: "Then it's up to me to choose!"

Ulyana: "You go get them!"

Ulyana: "No retreat, no surrender! Are you ready? On the count of three!"
*I started scrolling through all the possible outcomes in my head feverishly. There weren't many of them.*

*And Ulyana is sentenced to the highest measure of punishment feasible under the laws of the pioneer camp.*

*She is sentenced to the highest measure, like in the first option, and I stay in relative safety.*

You: "Fool! Stop it! Come here!"

*It turned out to be not that hard, as she hadn't managed to get far.*
*Ulyana was sitting on a tree stump... crying.*
*I stood still, hesitating.*
*Of course, such an outcome was to be expected, but now I had absolutely no idea of what to do or how to comfort her.*
*And besides, I'd gone back to the camp intentionally, and I had agreed to participate in that show...*
*But it just got worse.*
*As well as that, I was tired, tired unto death.*
*At that moment I wished it would all just cease to exist. I just wanted to close my eyes and appear elsewhere.*
*Preferably in a quiet and peaceful place.*

You: "It was sure to end up this way."
Ulyana: "You're to blame for everything! You!"
*Ulyana shouted in tears.*

*At that time she didn’t seem like a dangerously explosive nuclear reactor in the form of a little girl, but just like a little sister of mine who'd messed things up.*
*I wasn't mad at her at all; on the contrary, it seemed I too was beginning to care about the failure of the ghost play-acting.*
You: "It's alright, it's alright... We'll scare them properly next time!"
Ulyana: "Yeah..."
*I don't know for how much longer we sat in silence.*
*Ulyana stopped crying, and I didn't want to disturb her, as she had just calmed down.*
*But I also had absolutely no desire to stay in the forest overnight.*
You: "Hey, let's get back to the camp."
*I shook her shoulder gently, but there was no answer.*
*Ulyana had fallen asleep.*
You: "Hey!"
*I shook her harder. No effect.*
*At that moment I wanted to cry.*
You: "Why does this always happen to me? Why do I get caught up in these foolish situations, always and everywhere?"
You: "Even having suddenly appeared in a weird pioneer camp in the middle of nowhere, I don't get to become a subject in an experiment, a victim of a sick cosmic mind, or a participant in an intergalactic war on the side of a group of suicide-prone pacifists, like a regular hero of science fiction."
You: "No, instead I have to spend the night in a forest with a little girl in my arms, who is muffled in a bedsheet."
You: "Next time, I'd rather have the monstrous experiments..."
*I stood up and put the sleeping Ulyana on my back.*
*Maybe there was a way to wake her up, but firstly, I didn't want to, and secondly, one more burden or one less – at that point it made no difference.*
*It's good that she's not heavy...*
*At the square I stopped, put Ulyana on a bench and threw myself down beside her, totally exhausted.*
*Even a little girl is hard to carry for too long.*
*The stars in the sky were shining brightly.*
You: "Perhaps they give their light not only to me and this camp, but also shine on the city where I was born, and where my old home is..."
*It was as if a pain settled in my chest.*
*I envisioned my old flat clearly, and a detestable burning started to make its way from my stomach to my throat.*
*No, it was not wistfullness. More like a sad reminiscence.*
*Because despite all that's happened, I've felt more alive in less than five days here than I had for the last several years there.*
*And now I really wasn't sure if I wanted to get back.*
*Only one question still ate at me – how and why I ended up here. It flared up yet again in my mind.*
*I haven't spent much time seeking answers or even just thinking about my situation lately.*
*My thoughts were occupied with everyday, routine affairs.*
*And now, in order to break away and be able to wish to stay here for good, I need to understand the nature of this place.*
*It's just that even a nightingale in a golden cage has a right to know how and by whose will he got in there. And after that, to make the choice whether to stay or not...*
*I don't know how much longer I would have been devoted to existential thoughts, but Ulyana's loud snoring brought me back to reality.*
You: "So small, but she snores so loudly..."
*I sighed, put Ulyana on my back again and headed to her cabin.*
*...*
*I had no desire to explain everything to Alisa, so I just put the sleeping Ulyana on the porch, knocked at the door and left quickly.*
*I approached Olga Dmitrievna's cabin with mixed feelings.*
*On the one hand, I had done what I intended to do – I had comforted and entertained Ulyana.*
*On the other hand...*
*The two crumpled bedsheets in my hands looked more like rags left over from some worn-out straitjacket.*
*I opened the door softly and went in.*
Olga: "Semyon!"
*Olga Dmitrievna was sitting at the desk, and it seemed she had been waiting for me.*
Olga: "Do you want to explain something to me?"
You: "Well... Just don't scold her again... It's my fault!"
*Just like that I became a hero, to my own surprise.*
*My tongue acted faster than my thoughts.*
*Perhaps some of my best traits, which even I wasn’t aware of, have shown themselves.*
*Humanity as opposed to common sense.*
Olga: "Really?"
*Having started this, I chose to stick to my decision.*
You: "Well, it was me who got the bedsheets. And I was standing behind a tree back then."
Olga: "Behind what tree?"
*The camp leader looked at me in astonishment.*
Olga: "So, what did you need bedsheets for?"
*I realised my mistake.*
You: "So, you are not talking about the forest thing?"
Olga: "Semyon, I don't understand you."
Olga: "I wanted to know where you disappeared to so mysteriously during the hike, but now I would be interested in listening to your bedsheet story."
You: "But it was impossible that she and all the others hadn't seen Ulyana's performance!"
You: "The pioneers laughing out loud couldn't have been only my imagination."
You: "Olga Dmitrievna, I'm serious... Didn't you see someone in a bedsheet spring out at you recently?"
Olga: "So, it was you?"
*She gave me a close look.*
You: "No, it wasn't me..."
You: "Couldn't she tell just from my height?"
Olga: "But you're holding the bedsheets..."
You: "Yes..."
*I couldn't understand if she was playing me for a fool, or she really didn't know what this was all about.*
You: "Olga Dmitrievna, let's act like this conversation never happened. I'm too tired for today."
Olga: "Alright, go to bed."
*To my surprise, she readily agreed.*
*Of course, I was astonished by such a reaction, but I decided to use the moment. I wrapped the blanket around myself and turned to face the wall.*
*But I couldn't sleep.*
*There were no thoughts, my head was aching, but I still couldn’t manage to fall asleep.*
*I rolled to the other side, and images of the day started to flash before my eyes.*
*I shut my eyes tight to drive them away, but it didn’t work.*
*Suddenly, I heard a knocking at the window.*
*Olga Dmitrievna seemed to be asleep.*
*I dressed myself and walked outside.*
*Ulyana was standing before me with a tricky smile.*
Ulyana: "How did you manage to carry me to the cabin...? Wasn't it hard?"
You: "Not really... What have you come for?"
*I couldn't sleep, but at that moment bed seemed to be the only place where I could reside with no suffering, which is why Ulyana's sudden visit didn't please me at all.*
Ulyana: "How was she? Did you get scolded?"
You: "No, I avoided it somehow..."
Ulyana: "That's great then! I always get lucky!"
You: "That's for sure..."
*My eyes began closing despite my will. It seems that slumber has finally come upon me.*
You: "Look, I'm very tired..."
Ulyana: "This won't take long. Close your eyes."
*It was the easiest thing to do, and I didn't even want to know what she needed it for – maybe that way she would leave me alone sooner.*
*I closed my eyes.*
*And in that moment I felt a brief kiss.*
