*My eyes opened by themselves, but Ulyana was already running away, waving her hand to me.*
*I stood still, benumbed, and I couldn't even manage to shout anything after her.*
*I don't know for how long I stood like that, but eventually the night chill cleared my stupor.*
*I shivered and went back to bed.*
*This time I didn't want to sleep, I wanted to think it all through, but my eyes, which had begun to close as I was standing before Ulyana, seemed to issue a command to the rest of the body and I fell asleep before I realised what happened...*
*Only Lena and Alisa stood out in all this splendour.*
*Well, of course it was quite natural for Alisa to be arguing with someone like that.*
*But hearing Lena talk in a raised voice...*
*I came closer silently, trying to find out what was going on.*
Alisa: "No, you listen to me!"
Lena: "I'm not going to listen to anything!"
Alisa: "Really? Great then!"
*Alisa turned away and her eyes met mine.*
*At first she obviously was confused about what was going on, but then...*
Alisa: "So, you're eavesdropping!"
You: "What? Me? No!"
*She began slowly advancing on me, and I took a few steps back.*
*Lena, however, remained standing where she was.*
Alisa: "Well, okay then, listen!"
*Alisa stopped halfway and turned back to Lena.*
Alisa: "By the way, did you know he was peeping on me today?"
Lena: "What?"
Alisa: "Peeping. And he saw everything!"
Lena: "Is that... is that true?"
*Lena wrung her hands distressedly, gave me a quick glance and started staring at the ground, as if she was cut off from the world.*
You: "No, no, nothing like that happened!"
*Having thrown an angry glance at Alisa, I came up to Lena.*
Alisa: "Why are you denying it? I even have a witness!"
You: "Your witness is even worse than you!"
Alisa: "So, you'll stick to your claim that it didn't happen?"
*I took a second to think.*
You: "But really, why do I have such a pathological desire to exonerate myself before Lena? As though I vitally need it, need her opinion of me to remain unchanged."
You: "Though, how would I know what she's thinking?"
You: "It didn't happen!"
*Lena threw an baleful look at Alisa and raised her eyes to me right after that, eyes full of discomfort and hope.*
*It suddenly became unbearable to stare into these eyes.*
You: "It didn't happen..."
*I repeated less confidently.*
Alisa: "Well, whatever."
*Alisa sneered from behind me.*
Alisa: "It's up you to decide who to trust."
*She said to Lena offhandedly, then turned away and headed to the bonfire.*
Lena: "Is that true?"
*I felt uncomfortable, like a fish out of water, feeling the urge to end this as fast as possible.*
You: "And why should I have to excuse myself to her?"
You: "Well, so what if it did happen?"
*I looked at Lena boldly, but noticed only a bright sunset gleam reflected in a tear which was going down her cheek.*
You: "No, I meant..."
Lena: "You don't need to lie."
*She wiped off her tears and tried to smile.*
Lena: "After all, it's none of my business."
You: "No, why isn't it..."
You: "But why is it?"
You: "It's just that I... Well... It was an accident, get it? An accident which was caused by Ulyana, nothing more."
Lena: "Yeah, sure..."
You: "It's true!"
Lena: "I believe you."
*Lena was saying everything with absolutely no emotion, like she didn't care at all about what was going on.*
*I was almost able to believe it, but her tears a few seconds ago...*
You: "It seems to me that you don't."
Lena: "What is this, some kind of a game?"
*Lena said quietly, but there was a hint of anger in her tone.*
Lena: "You really need to convince me of that? And even if I believed you, what then? Would it all become true?"
You: "I'm not trying to convince you of anything, I just want you to understand that I'm not guilty... and didn't want to..."
Lena: "Why should I care at all?!"
*Lena shouted.*
*I was standing with my back to the bonfire, but I was sure that all the pioneers had turned in our direction.*
Lena: "If you want to peep at someone – do it! Do whatever you want! But why do you bother me?"
You: "I'm not..."
*But really, from any point of view, it looked that way – I'm trying to excuse myself to Lena with no success. Like a guilty child, or maybe even like a husband who'd slipped up...*
Lena: "Just so you know! I don't care!"
*Lena turned away and headed back to the camp at a fast walk.*
*I didn't try to stop her – now it certainly wasn't the best solution.*
*She's on the edge, no attempts to convince her or appeal to reason would help.*
You: "Since when is she like that? Screaming that way, getting mad...?"
*With these thoughts in mind, I returned to the bonfire and sat down on a wooden log.*
*...*
Alisa: "So?"
*Alisa asked after seating herself nearby.*
You: "What?"
Alisa: "Not a great success, huh?"
You: "As you see..."
*I growled out while picking at the coals with a stick.*
*It grew completely dark and the glade was plunged in to darkness.*
*The surrounding landscape was reminiscent of a picture from a child's book about a wood monster – an unknown forest creature is just about to spring out from behind the tree, predatory owls hoot menacingly in tree branches, even mice looking out from snags stare at you with distrust.*
*I was not afraid at that moment. Everything was different from the previous day when I was in the dungeon at the old camp...*
*The moon was shining brightly, paying close attention to our brave troop. The world was sleeping, waiting for the morning, bathing in the moonlight.*
Alisa: "As I thought. Though it was expected."
You: "But why...?"
*I finally managed to pick up the largest burning log and throw it into the centre of the fire causing the flames to rise about a metre high and a vortex of sparks to spread out in all directions.*
You: "Does Lena often behave like that?"
Alisa: "How?"
You: "Screaming at others. I couldn't believe she would act in such a way."
Alisa: "She is human, like anyone else."
*Alisa giggled.*
Alisa: "As if you hadn't noticed this before."
You: "What hadn't I noticed?"
Alisa: "Her."
You: "What do you mean?"
Alisa: "I mean this is her true face."
You: "What do you mean ‘true face’."
Alisa: "Oh, you’re so stupid! "
You: "Finish what you started."
Alisa: "She's not what she seems like, not like how you thought of her before."
You: "So how is she?"
Alisa: "Okay, I'm sick of this..."
*Alisa stood up, intending to leave.*
*I didn't say anything, just sat and listened to the silence of the forest.*
Alisa: "By the way, if you want to follow her, I think she's on the island."
You: "On what island?"
Alisa: "The one where you were gathering strawberries today."
You: "And what is she doing there?"
Alisa: "Ugh, you really are an idiot!"
*Alisa stomped the ground, circled the campfire and sat opposite.*
*I must have really lost track of things.*
*My head was absolutely blank.*
*To be precise, it was so heavy and full so that not even a single idea would have the chance to dwell there.*
*If I would compare my brain at its prime to a broad highway full of speeding thoughts overtaking each other and causing giant chaotic crashes, then now it's nothing but a forgotten tiny path in a distant desolate forest, which is only used in times of absolute necessity.*
*I tried to think over what had happened, analyze it somehow, but it seemed I was bashing against an invisible wall.*
*Moreover, it was impossible for me to find a single emotion in my soul, any response. As if it had all happened to someone else.*
*I failed to convince Lena that I'm not guilty. Should I care?*
*Lena cried, screamed, and then left.So what?*
*I don't feel anything about it. Should I?*
*I bit my lip until it bled and stood up.*
*I couldn't bear to stay here among these laughing pioneers.*
You: "I should run away. It doesn't matter where to. To the forest, to the mine, even to space. I don't care. Just so long as I can get far away from here."
*I seized a moment when the camp leader was looking in the other direction and vanished into the forest shadows.*
*...*
*There had been no rain for a long time.*
You: "However, I'm not sure whether it rains here at all."
You: "What a stupid idea, of course it does. The plants need some moisture."
*The night was fresher than the afternoon, but the air still hadn't had enough time to cool. I felt a little dizzy from the evening stuffiness.*
*Suddenly, I realised that I really wanted to swim.*
*It's quite a normal desire because the days are hot and you constantly feel soaked with sweat during the daytime.*
*I didn't even notice that I'd been approaching the pier.*
You: "Why not the beach?"
*Thoughts of Lena came over me again. Everything that I tried to ignore came out and brought lots of inconvenient questions, inappropriate answers, and vague desires.*
*It was obvious that I had been led to the pier by my subconscious.*
You: "But what do I really want?"
You: "To apologise to her for something, to convince her of something? No, unlikely."
*I just wanted to get some sort of reaction from her. Wanted her to say 'Yes, I understand everything' and just smile.*
*And then I could stop myself from feeling like that…*
*It was necessary for me to be understood by someone, even in this world.*
*I untied a boat, pushed it into water, got in and took up the paddles.*
*...*
*It was easier to row this time – my hands were still hurting, but I managed to develop some sort of technique that allowed me to travel quite directly.*
*The river seemed frozen, spreading under the boat like a translucent veil.*
*The moonlight was piercing deep into the water, so it was almost possible to see the bottom.*
*I started rowing.*
*...*
*Surprisingly, the island now seemed the same as it did in the daytime.*
*Here usually everything is different. After dusk it felt like another world, a mystery world. Scary at times, but beautiful in its own way. A world of shadows and whispers, a nocturnal world.*
*I slowly walked around the island, looking for the boat which Lena took to come here*
*The grass softly rustled under my feet, the occasional waves peacefully struck the shore and bounced back like flies too tired from beating on the glass.*
*The breeze from the water lazily stirred the leaves of the trees, out of habit rather than a real desire to make the night grove sing.*
*I looked at this wonderful picture with such delight that I didn't even notice something until I stumbled into it.*
*It was a boat.*
You: "Well of course – she wouldn’t get here by swimming."
*I headed towards the centre of the island.*
*...*
*After a hundred metres I heard a rustling from behind a tree.*
Lena: "Don't come any closer..."
*Lena whispered.*
You: "..."
*I hesitated.*
Lena: "Don't come any closer."
*She said louder.*
You: "How did you know it's me?"
*Though she hadn’t indicated that she'd known that.*
You: "Alright..."
*I leaned against the tree, trying not to look behind it.*
You: "Alisa told me that you would be here."
Lena: "So what?"
*It was difficult for me to know what emotions Lena was experiencing.*
*Her voice was steady enough; even though I could read irritation and annoyance in it, I could not understand whether she was angry, or whether it was all the same to her.*
You: "That came out awkward."
*I was doing my best to avoid unnecessary apologies and excuses, but couldn't find other words to use instead.*
Lena: "Was that the only reason you came?"
You: "No... Well, I don't know."
Lena: "You don't know, but you still came?"
You: "Yes."
Lena: "You shouldn't have."
You: "Why? Of course, if I'm bothering you..."
Lena: "Why are you following me?"
You: "I..."
*She was right – it certainly looked that way. Moreover, I definitely felt attracted to her.*
You: "You shouldn't think like this."
Lena: "How should I think?"
You: "I don't know."
Lena: "I can only draw conclusions based on your behavior."
You: "I really don't know... I guess I'd better go."
*I was confused, and it was hard just to be near her.*
Lena: "Why? Since you came..."
*I seemed to hear a playful tone in her voice.*
You: "Alright."
Lena: "And?"
You: "What?"
Lena: "What did Alisa tell you?"
You: "Nothing special."
Lena: "I see."
You: "Yeah."
Lena: "Well then."
You: "Yep…"
*We just stayed silent for a while.*
Lena: "Since you came, tell me about something."
You: "Well, I don't know..."
Lena: "For example, about what happened this morning."
You: "What about what happened this morning?"
Lena: "You know."
You: "You yourself didn't want to talk about it."
Lena: "I didn't want to, but now I want to!"
*Lena's voice trembled.*
*I couldn't understanding what was happening at all any more.*
You: "Maybe it's not her behind the tree?"
Lena: "Don't look!"
You: "Okay, okay... But what's wrong?"
Lena: "Nothing. Just don't look."
You: "Alright, as you wish."
Lena: "So, nothing happened?"
You: "Well, something did... But that was all just a silly accident!"
Lena: "Then why are you so worried about what I think about it?"
You: "I'm not worried!"
You: "And anyway, you yourself!"
*I said louder, beginning to feel irritated.*
Lena: "What about me?"
You: "Why are you so concerned about this situation?"
Lena: "Who said that I'm concerned about this situation?"
You: "Then what?"
Lena: "Nothing..."
*She said in a whisper and fell silent.*
*Such talk would lead us to nowhere.*
You: "Lena won't say anything, and I seem to be too stupid to guess, or even just to be sure about myself."
You: "Sorry, I guess it’s all my fault. I just cannot understand..."
Lena: "Why..."
You: "What?"
Lena: "Why do you keep apologising? For everything. For what you did, for what you are doing, even for what you haven't done yet."
You: "But..."
*Maybe she was right, but I couldn't behave differently. I felt the need to apologise to her, to everyone.*
*So they would not think badly of me, wouldn’t laugh at me. So I can put away something unsaid and eliminate misunderstandings.*
Lena: "Anyway, that's your business!"
*Lena got angry.*
Lena: "Apologise, make excuses! Why should I care...?"
You: "Okay, well, I'm not guilty! In fact, I don't think I could be blamed for anything, but then what's wrong? What is wrong with you?"
Lena: "Why would something be wrong with me?"
You: "I don’t know... I just think so."
Lena: "Oh! You just think so!"
*She laughed.*
Lena: "You speak as if you know me."
You: "..."
*I did not answer.*
Lena: "Please leave..."
*Lena said after a while.*
*I didn’t move, just could not, had no strength to do so.*
*I wanted nothing at that point – didn’t want to excuse myself, to apologise. I didn't even want her understanding.*
*I was too tired of everything.*
You: "Why?"
Lena: "Just leave..."
*She whispered.*
You: "I don't want to."
Lena: "Then I'll leave."
You: "Let's just go together."
Lena: "No."
You: "How long are you going to be offended? By what? What’s wrong with you? Everyone here behaves normally, except you."
*I did not care what my words meant. As if they had been said by someone else and the topic of conversation meant nothing.*
Lena: "You really don’t understand anything. Alisa was right."
You: "About what?"
Lena: "Nevermind..."
*I closed my eyes to think it over.*
You: "No, I can't go. I don't understand, don't know what to think, what to do."
You: "And since when did I stop worrying about my situation in this world, or how to get back?"
You: "Since when was the only thing I could think about Lena, or how others would look at me, or how my actions looked from the other side?"
You: "It's just stupid and it's not like me; in fact, it's inappropriate in this situation."
You: "In short, I didn't do anything and don't intend to justify things which I didn't do!"
*There was no reply.*
You: "Hey! Do you hear me?"
*I finally decided to see who was actually hiding behind the tree, but no one was there.*
You: "So she left!"
*I rushed over to Lena's boat, but she was already far away, almost near the pier.*
You: "Whatever!"
*I shouted and walked along the shore.*
*...*
*I got back relatively quickly and without much trouble.*
*However, my hands still ached terribly, and my eyes were closing themselves.*
*Probably such a physical and, more importantly, emotional load is too much for one person.*
*I walked slowly toward the camp leader's cabin, staring down at my feet and thinking about nothing.*
*Someone called to me at the square.*
Alisa: "Hey!"
*Alisa ran up to me.*
Alisa: "Have you been to the island."
You: "Yes..."
*To tell the truth, I didn't want to talk to her about anything, but I already didn't have the strength to lie to her.*
Alisa: "And how did it go?"
You: "Doesn't matter... I'm very tired and I'm going to sleep."
Alisa: "Come on, tell me!"
*Her face had such a nasty grimace that I shuddered with rage.*
You: "Why should you care?!"
Alisa: "Well, I just..."
*She murmured in dismay.*
You: "Mind your own business!"
*I snapped, and quickened my pace toward the cabins.*
*Alisa did not try to stop me.*
*Annoyingly, Olga Dmitrievna had not returned yet, and I could not find my key.*
You: "What if I lost it?"
*The only thing I could do was wait.*
*I plopped down into the deck chair and closed my eyes.*
*My heart was heavy and my soul was being torn apart by vague expectations.*
*From time to time I had a feeling that I was already dead (just without realizing it) and had been thrown into hell.*
You: "But really, instead of trying to get out of here, I'm spinning on a diabolic roundabout and it goes faster and faster. I'm becoming more and more involved in the life of this world, of this camp."
*As if I had no past life – the real one*
*As if I was always interested in the opinions of others...*
You: "Damn it! I never cared about it!"
You: "Why right here? Why right now?"
*I recalled the face of Lena, in tears.*
You: "Yeah, probably not the opinions of others, but her opinion was the one I cared about... "
*I heard far footsteps and after a while Olga Dmitrievna appeared.*
*She looked at me for a few seconds. Seemed like she was about to say something, but then just sighed, opened the door with her key and went in.*
*I followed her.*
*Shapeless shadows, blurry memories, fragments of feelings and emotions swirled in my head for a long time.*
*For so long that after a while I couldn't tell where I was or what's happening to me.*
*The only salvation was sleep...*
*I don't know what time it was when Olga Dmitrievna woke me up, but even before opening my eyes I felt the imminence of death.*
*My whole body ached, I felt dizzy, my mind was clouded by haze.*
Olga: "Semyon! Wake up immediately or you'll miss breakfast and, more importantly, the lineup!"
*Looks like the camp leader intends to exploit me to the fullest today, the same as any other day.*
*I garbled something, covered my head with the blanket and turned to the wall.*
You: "In the end, Olga Dmitrievna's anger will never go beyond words."
*At least I really wanted to believe so then.*
Olga: "Stand up right now or..."
*'Or what?' – I was going to say triumphantly, but kept silent.*
*Not because of fear, just because I felt too lazy to open my mouth.*
You: "Really, what could she do to me?"
You: "Lecture me at the lineup? Hang my photo on the wall of shame?"
You: "Or use me for inhuman alien experiments?"
You: "Well, I'm ready for that too, just let me sleep a couple of hours."
Olga: "Ok... But if you miss the lineup...!"
*The door slammed behind the camp leader, and the sleep which had been about to fade claimed my mind again.*
*...*
*I woke up dazzled by sunlight.*
*It was 1 P.M. according to my cell phone, which was squeezing the last drops of charge out of its battery.*
*Strangely enough, my body didn't ache, my head felt clearer, and, all in all, it was a good beginning to the day.*
*After waving my arms, pretending to do early exercises, I sprang out of the cabin and headed to the washstands.*
You: "Yeah, I slept through breakfast, but we'll be served lunch soon, so I shouldn't worry that I'll have to stay hungry like I did yesterday."
*Along the way, I met a pioneer whose face somehow looked strangely familiar.*
*But I was going so fast I couldn't really see him. And when I turned around he was already gone around the corner.*
*There was nobody near the washstands.*
*Everyone is probably busy with Olga Dmitrievna's tasks and God knows what else.*
*I quickly brushed my teeth, washed my face and was already going to leave when I suddenly heard the sound of water flowing from the opposite tap.*
*A pioneer leaned against a washstand over there.*
*I couldn't see his face, but judging by his figure he looked like the one I saw a couple of minutes ago.*
Pioneer: "How are you doing? The sun's so bright today!"
*I looked up into the sky, shielding my eyes with my palm.*
You: "Yeah, nothing special..."
*It wasn't easy to get a better look at the pioneer – given the way he stood, the bright sunlight that reflected from the water and shiny metal surfaces of the washstands heavily obscured his face and I wasn't able to distinguish any single feature.*
Pioneer: "The camp leader is angry today... so angry!"
*His voice sounded painfully familiar too.*
You: "Well, she's always like that..."
Pioneer: "Well, you'd know better, yeah..."
*I tried to remember if I've ever heard this voice or seen this pioneer before.*
Pioneer: "Well, see ya..."
*He turned the water off and quickly marched towards the forest path.*
*For a second I thought of following him, stopping him, but I quickly fought it off as I decided that it's not worth spoiling such a great morning with suspicions and burdensome speculations.*
*Nature was glowing with the bright light of life: lush treetops were rhythmically swaying in the wind, whispering to each other; the breeze gently stroked the high emerald grass; birds were cooing in the shade, escaping the midday heat; the woods and fields, stretching beneath the horizon, were dissolving in warm sunlight.*
You: "I don't know which month is it now but it looks like midsummer."
*I distinctly remembered the summer vacations of my childhood and youth – times of fun leisure and carefree joy.*
You: "Childhood games, how many there were..."
You: "I wouldn't say no to playing war games or hide and seek now. Or swinging on a bungee."
You: "Or maybe building a sand castle and inhabiting it with toy soldiers, ready to defend their master to the last drop of their plastic blood."
*...*
*I went to the square and sat on the bench, waiting for lunch. It looked like there wasn't much time left before it.*
*From time to time pioneers passed by me, sometimes alone, sometimes in pairs or groups of three.*
*But always someone I didn't know – Alisa, Ulyana, Lena, or Slavya were nowhere to be seen.*
*Thoughts about the meaninglessness of existence were circling in my brain, but this didn't worry me on such a beautiful day.*
You: "Just think about it, who could think of grieving for his life lived in vain or lost early while basking in the rays of such a friendly Sun?"
You: "Certainly not me!"
*I looked upon Genda.*
*He was meditating, as always.*
You: "Now he definitely never gets any unnecessary doubts."
*I remembered my first hours in this camp and the day before, the anguish, the anxiety and fear.*
You: "That all seems so far away now, although so little time has passed."
You: "Will I get out of here or not...?"
*It didn't concern me as much as before.*
You: "Maybe I'm already dead. Then this is the last stop, please get off the train..."
Pioneer: "What are you thinking about?"
*I looked up and saw that pioneer I'd seen before.*
*I couldn't see his face again, as the sun was shining in my eyes.*
You: "You know, life..."
*It seemed he would sit down next to me, but the pioneer stayed in the same place, only half-turned, which completely killed any hope of seeing his face.*
You: "Listen, have we met earlier? I don't think I remember you..."
Pioneer: "Well, let's say that you know who I am."
You: "But I don't."
*I laughed sincerely.*
Pioneer: "Here – you don't."
*He answered short.*
You: "I see..."
*Honestly, it's not like I didn't want to talk, I just didn't know what to talk about.*
*And my soul was so calm this didn't bother me.*
Pioneer: "Your first time here?"
*He asked a question but his tone implied he was only expecting a confirmation.*
You: "Yes... And you?"
Pioneer: "Me?"
*He paused for a few seconds.*
Pioneer: "Nah, it's not my first time here... One might say that I've visited this camp every year since my early childhood."
*Such an answer got me interested.*
You: "Well... And what was it like... before...?"
Pioneer: "It's always the same... Olga Dmitrievna being the camp leader, all the same pioneers around, all the same lineups at the morning and all these wicked accidents."
*For a moment I thought that it was me speaking, not him.*
You: "Interesting..."
Pioneer: "It's just that with every new..."
*He hesitated.*
Pioneer: "Year... More and more interesting things happen and one gets to understand better what's going on."
You: "What are you talking about?"
*This conversation positively triggered my curiosity.*
You: "It's a pity that I can't distinguish the face of this pioneer at all."
Pioneer: "Well, every session in the pioneer camp reminds of the previous one."
*He said calmly.*
You: "Probably... This is my first."
Pioneer: "It shows."
*The pioneer grinned.*
Pioneer: "But it looks like it won't be the last."
You: "Well, it's fun here and all, but... You know how they say, there's no place like..."
Pioneer: "Home, but you still have to get back there!"
*Now I was absolutely sure that this guy was hiding something from me.*
*To be precise, he stood out too much from the camp's usual ordinariness and was too different from the local inhabitants.*
You: "What do you mean? You think I'm stuck here forever or something?"
*I said, enunciating every word.*
*The pioneer had no time to answer as the lunch bell sounded.*
*I turned my head towards the loudspeaker, and by the time I looked back, the guy was already gone.*
*Thousands of theories and speculations instantly appeared in my mind, but I stopped myself, remembering all the apparent normality of this camp.*
*After all, nothing supernatural has happened in these five days.*
*Moreover, everything here seemed too natural, sometimes even boring.*
You: "Maybe this pioneer didn't mean anything by that and I just misunderstood him?"
*Thinking that, I went to the canteen, intending to feast.*
*Sometimes it seemed to me that lunch here is akin to the crowds around the soup kitchens during a famine.*
*Pioneers were running around, pushing each other, trying to crawl through for the first meal and take the most comfortable table.*
*I was calmly standing and patiently waiting for the cook to get me my assigned food rations.*
*For lunch today we had Okroshka (which I didn't really like) and cutlets with potatoes.*
*I sat in a corner and mentally rejoiced that I will be able to eat in peace.*
*My table was the farthest from the kitchen. I could reasonably hope that the pioneers who were looking for a free place wouldn't reach it.*
*Or would reach it last.*
*However, when I moved on to the main course, Slavya, Shurik and Electronik appeared from the crowd.*
Slavya: "Can we?"
*I had nothing against their company.*
You: "Of course."
*Lunch was going surprisingly calmly, even Electrnonik wasn't jabbering as he usually does.*
*I finally finished the meal, sprawled in my chair and, satisfied, clicked my tongue.*
You: "Listen, do you know this pioneer... I saw him today… You know, he's so…"
*I suddenly realised that I don't really know how to describe him.*
You: "Well, about my height, same constitution..."
Slavya: "Hard to say from such a description."
*Slavya smiled.*
Sergei: "Well, we have half a camp of such guys, if it comes to that."
*All in all they were right.*
Shurik: "Why are you asking?"
You: "It's just that I met him today. And it seemed like I haven't seen him here before."
Sergei: "Look in the canteen! I don't think he'll miss lunch!"
You: "Why didn't I think of that?!"
You: "That's it! Okay guys, enjoy your meal!"
*I got up and started to slowly walk along the rows of tables.*
You: "Lena and Zhenya are sitting over there. I gave them a friendly smile."
You: "Alisa and Ulyana are laughing and arguing about something."
You: "Olga Dmitrievna, surrounded by pioneers... Good thing she didn't notice me."
You: "There are hardly any free seats, but the guy from this morning is nowhere to be seen."
You: "The situation is getting more and more interesting..."
You: "Looks like I won't find him here."
You: "Maybe he already had lunch?"
*I headed to the exit.*
*It was so hot outside that it seemed like you would instantly melt after coming out of the shade.*
*I suddenly felt like sleeping*
*I yawned and headed to the camp leader's cabin in order to follow the domestic interpretation of the Archimedes principle.*
*In the end, Olga Dmitrievna is unlikely to return any time soon (at least I think so), and I will definitely have a couple of hours to rest.*
You: "Anyways, I really don't expect any other options to arise. Especially in this heat."
*The heavenly coolness in the cabin became my salvation.*
*I took my clothes off and jumped into bed.*
*Сrickets were lazily chirping outside, the wind was shaking the curtains on the window, and I sank into a dream...*
*...*
*Knocking on the door woke me up. The knocks were soft but insistent.*
*I reluctantly got up and went to open it.*
*Strangely, there was nobody on the doorstep.*
*I rubbed my eyes and stepped out to look around. All the same, no one around.*
You: "A dream, maybe?"
*It was already four o'clock.*
*I felt jaded.*
You: "I probably shouldn't have slept in the afternoon. After all, I knew what was going to happen!"
*I put on my boots, left the cabin and locked the door.*
You: "But where shall I go? All in all there is not much time till dinner"
*A sudden thought came to me that it would be nice to refresh myself, so I went towards the beach.*
*The Sun has passed the midday mark a while ago. It gets dark early here, in the South.*
*I squinted and looked up at the flaming disc.*
Pioneer: "Who was that just now?"
*I flinched.*
*The same mysterious guy was standing in front of me. And once again his face was hard to see due to the bright light.*
*For a moment the sun blinded me so I could not see anything besides the faint contours of objects.*
You: "Are you stalking me?"
Pioneer: "Nope, I was just passing by."
*He answered calmly.*
You: "Then you should know better!"
Pioneer: "So you haven't seen anyone?"
You: "Correct."
*I rubbed my eyes but it did not help.*
You: "Why didn't I see you at lunch?"
*I asked bluntly.*
Pioneer: "I wasn't hungry."
*He laughed.*
*I blinked a few times and my vision came back. But the pioneer had miraculously disappeared once again.*
You: "What the hell is going on here?!"
*Now I was absolutely sure that there was something strange about that guy.*
You: "He must be directly related to everything happening around here!"
You: "I will have to find out."
You: "But for starters it's good to confirm that I am not mistaken, and that he is not just a local pioneer."
*It was quite crowded at the beach. It looked like everyone from the camp was here.*
You: "Well, no wonder, it's so hot outside."
*Olga Dmitrievna was standing just a bit further apart from everyone, keeping an eye on her army of pioneers.*
*As soon as I thought that coming here might not have been the best idea, she noticed me.*
Olga: "Hey Semyon!"
Olga: "You weren't at the lineup! And in general you are just lounging around all day!"
*I did not know how to answer.*
Olga: "And just how are you planning on becoming a proper pioneer...?"
*She continued more softly.*
You: "Olga Dmitrievna, in the camp... Is there a pioneer who... looks a lot like me?"
*She looked surprised.*
Olga: "Maybe, I don't know... Why do you ask?"
You: "Oh, I am just curious..."
Olga: "Well we have a lot of boys here."
You: "Alright, never mind..."
*Someone's yell came from the river side and Olga Dmitrievna rushed in its direction.*
You: "Well, it looks like I will be spared a lecture."
*I lowered myself onto the sand and stared at the pioneers playing in the water.*
*After a few minutes of sitting here, Ulyana approached me.*
Ulyana: "Why so sad?"
You: "I'm not sad."
Ulyana: "Well why are you here sitting all alone?"
You: "Just thinking..."
Ulyana: "About what?"
*I decided to spare her my story about the mysterious pioneer.*
You: "Well imagine that you are chatting with a weird person... And you have to figure out what exactly is so weird about them."
Ulyana: "Simple! I would just ask them!"
*She laughed.*
You: "Too simple... But he won't answer."
Ulyana: "How do you know? Have you tried asking?"
You: "No, but it's obvious..."
*Ulyana did not answer, just sat down next to me and let out a tired sigh.*
Ulyana: "I'm all swimmed out."
You: "And what if they know something, but won't tell you?"
Ulyana: "Make them!"
You: "But how...?"
*For a bit longer we sat together talking about random things and then I got up, said goodbye and went away.*
You: "It's time to find the mysterious stranger and get all the answers."
*The first place to visit was the bus stop.*
You: "After all, this is where it all began!"
*The road was empty, as always. Only small dust tornados were occasionally visible on it.*
*I was ready to turn around and go back to the camp, but then I heard someone whisper.*
Pioneer: "Don't trust him!"
*Someone was hiding behind the monument.*
*A pioneer was sitting there with his back to me.*
*And once again, the voice seemed strangely familiar.*
You: "Who are you?!"
*I took a few steps towards him.*
Pioneer: "Stop! Don't come any closer!"
*For some reason I froze in my tracks.*
*From somewhere deep inside an assurance came to me and I understood that I shouldn't argue with him.*
You: "Alright, I'll stay here..."
Pioneer: "Have you seen him? Talked to him?"
*He asked nervously.*
You: "Who are you even talking about?"
*He was dressed in a pioneer uniform.*
Pioneer: "You know who..."
*And I definitely did know! He was talking about the weird pioneer I saw earlier.*
You: "Yes…"
*I answered after a few moments of silence.*
Pioneer: "What did he tell you?"
*The pioneer asked in a pleading tone.*
You: "Nothing, really..."
Pioneer: "Did he give you advice? Did he tell you what to do? Threaten you?"
You: "No, nothing like that... Of course he seemed pretty weird, but nothing more than that..."
Pioneer: "Remember he may not be alone! Or more likely, he is alone but you may meet many pioneers here who look like him."
You: "And what about you? Who are you? Who are you hiding from?"
Pioneer: "You will understand... In time... Just remember, the most important thing is to find the exit!"
*All of a sudden a strong gust of wind came through, ripping leaves from the trees and throwing an old paper bag into my face. Shielding myself, I averted my eyes.*
*When I looked back at the monument, the pioneer was already gone.*
*At that moment I was overwhelmed by fear. Real, almost tangible fear.*
*I remember being scared during my first hours at this camp.*
*But back then everything around me seemed kind and friendly. Now Sovyonok revealed its fangs, getting ready to eat me.*
*And ahead – the unknown...*
*My body was covered in goosebumps, my throat was dry and my hands were shaking. I tried to ignore it all and headed back to camp.*
*It was already dinner time but I had no desire to go to the canteen.*
*After meeting the second mysterious pioneer, just thinking about the locals made me, if not afraid, then at least creeped out.*
You: "I don't even know who, or what, they all are."
You: "And even though nothing had happened yet, it does not mean I can trust them!"
*I stopped in front of the club house, but then realised that this is not the best spot to be at – I could run into someone, which was not something I wanted to do at the moment.*
*Almost running, I hurried towards the forest and walked a few metres along the path before finally stopping.*
You: "On one side – the mysterious pioneer... Well, two of them to be precise."
You: "On the other – all the other inhabitants of this camp, who seemed absolutely normal."
*Either way, my decision to stand back and let everything resolve itself was under some serious pressure.*
*At this point it was clear to me – I had to do something on my own.*
You: "But what exactly...?"
*Everyone is probably having a dinner, so I have a good chance to make it to Olga Dmitrievna's place without being noticed.*
*I decided to first take my clothes that I wore when I arrived here along with my cell phone.*
You: "I won't be able to come up with a solid plan right off the bat, so for the time being I might as well hide in the forest."
*I leaped up the steps and entered the building.*
*My clothes were right where I left them and my phone was where it was supposed to be – under my pillow.*
*I quickly grabbed it and was ready to stuff it into my pocket but then I noticed something on the screen.*
*The message window was open.*
*The text read:*
*'You're wrong, Semyon! You are so wrong!'*
*It felt like my soul had left my body.*
*I froze on the spot.*
*I was shaking and my blood was pumping so hard, it felt like my skull was going to burst open from the pressure.*
*It took at least a full minute for me to come back to senses.*
You: "Olga Dmitrievna could have typed in the message... Or one of the pioneers."
You: "It's easy to figure out how to do it, even if they are not familiar with this technology."
You: "But no one besides me should know where I keep the phone!"
*This event was the straw that broke the camel's back.*
*I rushed out of the house, determined never to come back here.*
*…*
*Night fell on the camp grounds.*
*I had been sitting in the woods for a few hours, trembling at every noise.*
*The spot that I chose was far away from the path, so it would be hard to find me.*
*I was keeping a few plans in my head for the time being. To try and run, to kill every single person in the camp...*
*However on the other hand, one thought chased me and I realised that I shouldn't behave like this because of some strange pioneer. Or even because of that message on the phone...*
You: "All of this was reinforcing the thought that everything happening here was far from normal, however there was no proof that anyone in the camp had anything to do with it."
*I could have stayed here until morning, lost in my own thoughts, but I heard footsteps coming from somewhere nearby...*
Pioneer: "So you decided to escape after all?"
*I turned around but couldn't see the pioneer's face in the dark.*
*Nevertheless, I was pretty sure that it was him.*
*I wasn't afraid then.*
*More precisely, I was so physically exhausted that I was prepared for any possible course of events and somehow managed to reason appropriately and to maintain the conversation.*
You: "I wouldn't call this an escape."
*...I answered slowly, stretching every word.*
Pioneer: "Huh? Then what is it?"
You: "A tactical retreat..."
Pioneer: "Brilliant!"
*He burst into laughter.*
You: "Listen, why don’t you tell me what's going on, who are you and what you want from me?"
Pioneer: "What did that guy tell you at the gate?"
*It seemed that he didn't even hear my question.*
You: "He told me not to trust you."
*I lied.*
*But on the other hand, I thought that it was what he meant.*
Pioneer: "Well, that's always the way for him... Running away, hiding..."
*I could hear irritation in his voice.*
You: "I am not sure what kind of circus you are running here, but I’m not going to be a part of it!"
Pioneer: "Oh, why not… You're the star, after all!"
*I couldn't see his face but I bet he was smiling.*
You: "Explain my part to me then!"
Pioneer: "You know, I was like you in the beginning... The first time everything went peacefully."
Pioneer: "Then I escaped, I tried to understand what was going on, got mad and even... tortured them to get the truth!"
*He laughed crazily.*
*I shivered.*
Pioneer: "But it was pointless!"
*...continued the pioneer after calming down a bit.*
Pioneer: "Pointless... And then I began to notice the lapses..."
Pioneer: "At first I just heard their voices – from a distance and sometimes in my head."
Pioneer: "Then vague silhouettes appeared. Then they slowly took on physical form."
Pioneer: "And finally, they stepped into my world! I could touch them, introduce them to other pioneers..."
Pioneer: "And they all were different! Different! Do you get it? Different!"
*He started shouting.*
Pioneer: "And it recurred again and again. You can get used to the loops, but..."
Pioneer: "Then I learned how to get into their worlds by myself, to interact with the others. But it turned out that I'm not alone. There are lots of us!"
Pioneer: "Today you saw at least one more."
*He fell silent.*
*I didn't know what question to ask and didn't want to interrupt his story, so I simply waited.*
*After a minute he continued.*
Pioneer: "It's not that simple, of course... And it's not always possible."
Pioneer: "Only under certain circumstances... When you feel strong emotions, for example."
*I instantly remembered how I saw him the first time, the time when I didn’t feel any emotions at all.*
Pioneer: "Including the moments when you feel happy..."
*As if he was reading my thoughts.*
You: "I see..."
You: "So, you’re trying to say that there are several parallel worlds including the same camp with its inhabitants where I am replaced by you or that guy I met at the bus stop...?"
Pioneer: "Yeah, something like that..."
*His answer didn't surprise me at all.*
*In the end, it's clear that whatever happens here is beyond the limits of human understanding, and this theory didn't even seem all that unusual.*
You: "But you've said that everything recurs..."
Pioneer: "Yes, it recurs."
You: "And what will happen... afterwards?"
Pioneer: "You'll start from the very beginning – you'll wake in the bus, come to the camp, meet Olga Dmitrievna, the girls, Elektronik..."
You: "But if it happened to you, then why should it happen to me as well?"
Pioneer: "It happens to everyone!"
*Once again, he laughed hysterically.*
You: "And how many 'loops' have you experienced so far?"
Pioneer: "I stopped counting them already... At first I tried to remember them though. Maybe a few hundred..."
*No wonder, it was very clear to me that this guy was suffering from a progressing mental dysfunction.*
You: "But you searched for a way out, didn't you?"
*He didn't answer.*
You: "That's what that guy at the bus stop was talking about."
Pioneer: "Because he understands nothing, damn it!"
*...he shouted.*
Pioneer: "Because he's just like you! Constantly running away, hiding!"
You: "What would you suggest then?"
Pioneer: "If I had any suggestions, I wouldn't be standing here talking to you."
You: "Alright, but you were trying, weren't you?"
Pioneer: "Are you trying to understand what I know, since I've been around here for a long time?"
*...he asked cheerfully.*
You: "Well, that's evident..."
Pioneer: "Yes, I did try to run away from here."
Pioneer: "There..."
*He waved towards the forest.*
Pioneer: "...is nothing there. Nothing but trees. When I had been walking there for several days and finally passed out, I found myself in the bus again."
Pioneer: "Same for walking along the road – it's endless."
Pioneer: "Talking to somebody about that is pointless. You probably already understood that by yourself."
You: "I did."
*...I interjected.*
Pioneer: "Even if you try to explain your situation directly, at best you'd just be considered an idiot."
You: "What if you try to not leave the bus?"
Pioneer: "It's pointless. Sooner or later, you'll be found."
Pioneer: "I even tried to spend the entire time there. In the end I fell asleep, and everything started from the beginning."
You: "And what if you start it by yourself and leave?"
Pioneer: "No keys. And I don't have any carjacking skills."
You: "A cursed cycle..."
Pioneer: "Exactly!"
*A long silence fell.*
*Finally, I asked:*
You: "And what about the people around here? Don't they raise absolutely reasonable suspicions?!"
Pioneer: "Suspicions?"
*Laughter again.*
Pioneer: "The only thing that is suspicious about them is that no matter how much you tell them, they stare at you with their eyes out on stalks!"
Pioneer: "The people... I feared them at first, too."
Pioneer: "Then I used them for different experiments... And now I don't consider them humans. They're all dolls, puppets!"
Pioneer: "You can easily predict any reaction, any word or action!"
You: "So they aren't worth fearing, are they?"
Pioneer: "The one worth fearing is yourself..."
*...he said softly.*
Pioneer: "Do you know how funny it is when human bones crack as they slowly break from distension...?"
You: "Looks like he has finally lost his marbles."
You: "Listen, I understand everything, but..."
Pioneer: "The other one thinks that's a bit much, too..."
Pioneer: "But it doesn't matter. Nobody but you is real here!"
*The pioneer suddenly fell silent.*
You: "Well, no, I don't agree with you."
Pioneer: "You're probably thinking 'why I didn't check this all by myself?', aren't you? 'Why I didn't try to reach the nearest village or town?'."
You: "Yes, I did have such thoughts."
Pioneer: "'Why wasn't I suspicious? Why was I doing different stuff instead of searching for answers?'"
You: "Well... Yes..."
Pioneer: "Forget about it! That's normal. We all behave like this for the first time here."
You: "But how many others have you seen so far?"
Pioneer: "Not that many."
*The pioneer was lost in thought.*
Pioneer: "About ten people, maybe... But I'm sure there're many more of them!"
You: "And... is everyone... like this?"
Pioneer: "In fact, yes. Only the details are different, but the main thing is invariable – there's no way out of here!"
Pioneer: "And, by the way, you're just like the majority of them!"
Pioneer: "The only thing that differs is that you have heard everything from me instead of experiencing it for yourself."
*I don't know if I should thank him for that...*
You: "Well, and what now?"
Pioneer: "Nothing."
*...he said shortly.*
*I closed my eyes and lost myself in thought. That was a critical mistake.*
*When I opened the eyes, I didn't see anybody, just like the previous times.*
You: "So it's clear what's going on now... But, in fact, how could everything he said guide me to an answer?"
You: "Yes, I'm not alone. Yes, everything recurs. But what's the reason for all this?"
You: "And, what is more important – where's the way out...?"
*The only useful thing that I extracted from the conversation was that the local inhabitants were not worth fearing.*
*And that was quite significant to me for now, since it was much better to sleep in a warm cabin instead of the forest.*
*I sighed, took my things and headed towards the camp.*
*As I was walking, the conversation with my fellow sufferer popped up in my mind every now and then.*
You: "Why did I not ask him about the message on my phone? And some other stuff... There were hints, after all..."
You: "Maybe if I had found some details out, I could have drawn some conclusions."
*However, it didn't seem like our meeting would be the last one.*
*The lights were on in Olga Dmitrievna's cabin.*
*I opened the door gently and went in.*
Olga: "Speak of the devil, here you are!"
*...the camp leader said angrily.*
You: "Olga Dmitrievna, I'm so tired now, so let's put off the lecture."
Olga: "Tired from what, I wonder?"
You: "From everything!"
*...I snapped rudely.*
*The camp leader looked at me with surprise.*
*I fell into bed without undressing.*
Olga: "Semyon, a role model pioneer shouldn't behave like that!"
You: "And how should he behave then?"
Olga: "Well, not like that..."
*The camp leader stumbled for a moment, as if struggling to pick the right words.*
Olga: "He should respect his seniors!"
You: "I respect you immensely, for sure..."
Olga: "Semyon!"
*The sarcasm in my voice didn't go unnoticed.*
You: "And now I'd like to sleep."
Olga: "Wait, I..."
You: "By the way, how far is the nearest town? When does the bus arrive? How can I even get out of here?"
*...I asked in a surprisingly calm voice.*
*There was no answer, and there shouldn't have been any.*
*I said all this just in order to get rid of her.*
You: "Why are you silent?"
Olga: "I'm tired, let's talk about that tomorrow."
*The camp leader got up and turned off the light.*
You: "Yes, it's all just like that guy said."
You: "Why did I speak to him so calmly and properly, I wonder?"
You: "I should have been shivering from horror..."
*That pioneer didn't have much credibility, but I had a feeling that he's unable to harm me.*
*As soon as I thought that it would be a good idea to ask something else, fatigue overtook me and I passed out.*
*I woke up because somebody was shaking my shoulders*
*It was too hard for me to open my eyes, so I just whined pathetically.*
Olga: "Get up already! You're going to miss the lineup!"
*Once I realised what Olga Dmitrievna wanted from me and what time it was, I rolled over to face the wall.*
*I was so tired that I wanted to choke the camp leader just so she would quit disturbing my recovery from a hellish yesterday.*
Olga: "Semyon! Get up immediately!"
*I mustered up my strength, opened my eyes and sat up.*
You: "Olga Dmitrievna... I understand, but I had a hard day yesterday..."
You: "Can I sleep in at least today?"
*I started pleading.*
Olga: "It's out of the question! Lineup is mandatory for every pioneer! And you've already missed it a few times."
*My head went completely numb so I just couldn't find any arguments against that.*
*In a couple of minutes we were already standing at the square.*
*I dozed off, taking great pains to not fall asleep on my feet, so I missed everything that Olga Dmitrievna announced.*
*The majority of the pioneers seemed to feel the same.*
*Electronik yawned constantly, Alisa had huge baggy eyes, only Ulyana seemed to be full of health and energy, as always.*
*I swept my eyes over the lineup yet again and couldn't find Lena.*
You: "That's odd. Generally, she's a diligent and committed girl, it's unlike her to miss such events."
You: "On the other hand, that was too much for her yesterday. Such stress. She's probably depressed..."
*Although such behavior from her was very surprising.*
*I mean, I'd suspected that she was not the kind of person she wanted others to see her as, but I never expected such a drastic change.*
*Lena – amazingly! – somehow reminded me of Alisa, even more harsh and brutal at times.*
*And now I was not sure how to behave around her – I was simply afraid of her.*
*Finally, lineup was over and the pioneers dragged themselves off to breakfast.*
*Miku caught up with me near the canteen.*
Miku: "Semyon, good morning! How did you sleep? Any dreams? How are you? Ready for breakfast?"
*She, as always, blabbered without a break, adding a cute smile at the same time.*
You: "I'm ok."
*I answered lazily.*
Miku: "Today is quite gloomy... Maybe because of the weather – it's quite dark, it may even rain... So yeah! Everyone is sad and gloomy! I thought, maybe something happened but no one told me what."
Miku: "Can you imagine that! Something happened and everyone knows about it apart from me. I was sad about it, but then..."
You: "Don't worry, you won't miss the end of the world."
*I delivered a snarky remark.*
Miku: "Huh?"
*It looked like she was so into her monologue that she was completely oblivious to everything around her.*
You: "And if you are going to miss it somehow – I will make sure to let you know..."
You: "Nothing. Enjoy your meal."
*I marched to the canteen with a firm step to get my daily portion of fats, proteins and carbohydrates.*
*To my surprise, a seat in the far corner was free.*
*I sat down and tried really hard to make a face that would let everyone know that there is really no need to come anywhere near me, unless there was an emergency.*
*I just wanted to sit alone and think. Moreover, keeping my mind off other things was making me less sleepy.*
Slavya: "Hi, mind if I join you?"
*I did not notice Slavya standing there.*
You: "Strange..."
You: "Sure..."
*I answered after hesitating for a second.*
Slavya: "Bad mood?"
You: "A bit."
Slavya: "Did something happen?"
You: "Not really..."
Slavya: "You don't have to tell me if you don't want to."
You: "There's nothing to tell you about."
*We kept eating in silence until I asked:*
You: "Where did you go last night?"
Slavya: "Me? Oh I just wanted to be alone for a while."
You: "That's not like you."
*I felt a bit more lively.*
Slavya: "Really? Well maybe... It's also not often that you're seen so gloomy."
You: "She might be right."
*Even in the most unfavorable circumstances I've always tried to have a positive outlook on things.*
*Not that I was an optimist, I just always tried not to feel too down.*
*Keeping my previous life in mind, it's only natural – as soon as you let depression get a hold on you, the noose will start to look very appealing.*
You: "Perhaps."
*When Slavya was done with her meal I was still poking the porridge with my spoon.*
Slavya: "I'll be going."
You: "By the way, have you seen Lena?"
Slavya: "Nope, why do you ask?"
You: "I didn't see her at the morning lineup. That's odd... That's not like her."
Slavya: "Maybe you are right. I don't think it's a big deal to be honest."
You: "Yes, of course, I was just wondering..."
*I sat for a few more minutes in place and then headed outside without finishing my breakfast.*
You: "Today was quite gloomy. The first gloomy day during my time here. I'd kind of gotten used to the bright and burning sun."
*The heat that would only subside by the evening seemed to be an irreplaceable component of this place.*
*It looks like even here the weather changes after all.*
You: "Almost like it's matching my mood..."
You: "It looks like just more proof that this place or it's creators are sentient and have great storytelling skills."
*Sometimes I really wanted to focus on a single theory of mine, concentrate on it and forget about all others.*
*Just to decide for myself that it's all done by aliens, or I am in a parallel universe. Or witchcraft, or military experiments...*
*Just to pick one and be done with it!*
*To stop thinking about all possible explanations to this situation, constantly jumping from one to the other. Just to focus on a single one.*
You: "But it's impossible."
You: "I have (almost) no facts about anything. Nothing extraordinary has happened to me here yet."
*Yes, some odd things took place. But they can and do happen in the real world too.*
*After yet another cycle of similar thoughts I found myself at the bus stop of route 410 and the gates of the camp Sovyonok.*
You: "No answers, no hints, no clues..."
*I was walking wherever my legs were taking me.*
*It was quiet in the residential area. Not a single person there, to be precise.*
*My astonishment grew even more when Electronik appeared around the next turn.*
*I wanted to call out to him but stopped, because he was going a little too confidently in an unknown direction.*
You: "It's strange, that goes against his nature."
You: "Anyway, what can I talk with Electronik about? And yeah, I'd have to start the conversation first..."
You: "Seems like I was completely in despair."
*However, it would be interesting to follow him and to find out where he is rushing to.*
*As a child I liked games of spies and here is a chance to put myself into a real spy's shoes!*
*I decided not to sneak and hide in a special way and just tailed him quietly at a distance.*
*Soon we came to the library. Electronik knocked and went inside.*
*I stood behind a big tree so nobody could see me and began to wait.*
*…*
*He was absent for quite a long time.*
You: "Perhaps this is a stupid idea, because in fact, what’s difference does it make if he went to the library? Maybe just decided to get something to read?"
You: "He was walking fast? So what?"
You: "Perhaps he has some business afterwards..."
*My thoughts were disturbed by a loud door slam.*
*I looked towards the library and saw Electronik, running away from there, and Zhenya, who ran after him, shouting along the way:*
Zhenya: "I don't want to hear it anymore! Or to see you either!"
*They ran past me, but naturally they were so involved in chasing that they didn't notice me.*
*The whole situation seemed very funny, and I decided that I needed to find out what the matter was.*
You: "I wonder, where could Electronik be running to like that?"
*Perhaps he ran to the infirmary?*
You: "No, that's obviously a silly idea..."
*Hiding in the canteen wouldn't be a bad decision.*
*However, he wasn't here either.*
You: "Yes, it is quite obvious that he ran straight to his native cybernetics club."
*I entered without knocking but didn't find anyone inside.*
You: "Electronik, it's me!"
*The sound of footsteps came from the next room and soon Electronik himself appeared.*
Sergei: "Hi Semyon! I am just..."
*His eyes ran guiltily and his shirt had visible traces of sweat.*
You: "Going in for sports, I see. Sprinting."
Sergei: "I... You saw that?"
*He asked, doomed.*
You: "Yes, purely by chance. So I decided to stop by and to ask how you were doing and what happened?"
Sergei: "Nothing special, really..."
You: "Indeed, fleeing from an angry librarian – it's nothing..."
You: "You can tell me."
*I smiled disarmingly.*
Sergei: "Really? And won't you tell..."
You: "Of course! Silent as the dead! Cross my heart!"
*It seems I exaggerated there a bit, but looks like it had convinced him.*
Sergei: "Okay."
*He took a deep breath, gathering strength.*
Sergei: "You know, I've liked Zhenya since the first day..."
*At those words I wanted to fall to the floor and start rolling around, shaken by violent attacks of laughter, but out of respect for him I refrained. Still, his next few words flew past my ears.*
Sergei: "...and so I just decided. Well, and you saw what happened next..."
You: "A brave fellow, indeed."
You: "Well, you... Try harder I guess and you will succeed!"
*I patted him on the shoulder, trying really hard not to laugh.*
Sergei: "Thank you for the support."
*He smiled sadly.*
You: "Okay, I have to go, I have some work to do."
*I shot out of the clubhouse like a bullet and finally laughed out loud.*
You: "However, if you think about it, Electronik and Zhenya would make a wonderful couple."
You: "They are actually a perfect match. It is strange then that Zhenya rejected him..."
*I was going towards the square thinking further about this episode.*
You: "At the end of the day Electronik is not such a simpleton..."
You: "Just like that, he declared his love, even realizing that refusal will follow. Or on the contrary, is it because he's just as simple as an apple pie?"
You: "Either way, you can feel the honesty and sincerity in his behaviour."
You: "More complicated people would spend hours, days, months, years thinking about how to present this in a better way, what consequences it could have and whether you should even bother. I would do so myself."
You: "No, rather, I have done so."
You: "But he just said it. Unsuccessfully of course, but it could have also gone differently..."
*These thoughts made me completely melancholy, so much so that the lunch signal, usually so anticipated, didn't trigger any emotions at all.*
*The canteen was chock-full. It seems that the camp was slowly emerging from the morning depression.*
*Maybe the sun that had come out from the clouds contributed to that, or maybe something else that I'd missed while running after Electronik.*
*Only the places next to Ulyana and Alisa turned out to be free.*
*I braced myself and started walking towards them – eating was still a necessity.*
You: "Can I sit with you?"
Alisa: "Oh just sit down."
Ulyana: "Why are you so gloomy?"
You: "It’s just that you are too cheerful. I'm trying to maintain the energy balance in the universe."
*Ulyana giggled.*
*Oddly enough, the girls did not pay any attention to me and talked about their own concerns.*
*At first I thought it was good, but then I started to think that they were just taking no notice of me.*
You: "By the way, where is Lena?"
*Because of all my thinking I'd completely forgotten about her.*
Alisa: "I don't know."
*Alisa answered absently.*
You: "Has she still not appeared?"
Alisa: "As you can see..."
*I took a look around the canteen but didn't see her anywhere.*
You: "And nobody's heard anything about her?"
Alisa: "No."
You: "Don't you find it strange?"
Ulyana: "What’s so strange? Maybe she is reading, maybe sleeping or something."
You: "Seems more like you’re talking about yourself."
Alisa: "It's none of your business, is it?"
*Alisa interjected angrily.*
You: "Well, if a person is missing..."
Alisa: "You weren’t so worried when Shurik disappeared!"
You: "That's quite different.."
Alisa: "Yes? And why, I wonder?"
*I had no answer and just blankly looked at Alisa before going back to my food.*
*She did not insist on continuing the conversation.*
*…*
*Lunch was over. I silently stood up and went out of the canteen without a goodbye.*
You: "So, Lena disappeared... What should I do now?"
You: "On the other hand, why should I do anything? Why me? Where am I and why am I here, who are all these people?"
You: "One can not be absolutely sure whether Lena is what she seems."
You: "Perhaps all this doesn't even exist, so why should I worry...?"
You: "However, for me now Lena is still the same Lena. The modest, quiet girl I met on the first day."
You: "And even her strange behavior could not affect my attitude towards her."
You: "In the end, it’s not certain that I still exist. So while the world is logical (at least to some extent), I have to play by its rules!"
*I quickly went to the camp leader's cabin.*
*Once inside, I saw Olga Dmitrievna lying on the bed and reading a book.*
You: "Do you know where Lena is?"
Olga: "No, why are you asking?"
You: "She's nowhere to be found. She missed both breakfast and lunch!"
Olga: "So what?"
*She looked at me blankly.*
You: "What do you mean ‘so what’? When Shurik was gone the whole camp was searching him from the early morning."
Olga: "I don't understand you."
*There is something strange happening to the camp leader again. She was behaving absolutely incomprehensibly, illogically.*
You: "Do you think it’s normal? So where is she now?"
Olga: "I don't know."
*Olga Dmitrievna replied calmly.*
You: "This is too much!"
*I started to lose my temper.*
Olga: "Ask Miku – she is her roommate after all."
You: "That was a good idea, because obviously I would get no more answers here."
*I went outside, slammed the door and went to look for Miku's and Lena's cabin.*
*It was nice that the orchestra-girl had told me before where she lives, which is why I was at the door of their cabin a minute later.*
*I should have knocked, but for some reason I couldn't.*
*After a few deep breaths I knocked on the door several times.*
Miku: "Come in!"
*I heard a familiar voice*
You: "Hi... Do you know where Lena is?"
Miku: "No... I haven't seen her today. You're looking for her, right?"
You: "Don't you think it's strange?"
*By that time I'd started suspecting everybody of hiding information about Lena's location, of conspiracy, of involvement in me being here, of Kennedy's assassination and of hundreds of other terrible things.*
Miku: "Well... You know, maybe... I thought she went somewhere and then I just got lost in doing things – breakfast, music club, helping to clean, and then lunch, and then, and then..."
You: "Okay, I see... And what about yesterday? Was everything normal?"
Miku: "Well... She came late and immediately went to bed, I didn’t even notice anything wrong."
*No chance of finding out anything here either.*
You: "Thanks."
*I said abruptly and left.*
*At that moment it seemed to me that the missing Lena was the only living person in this pack of talking dummies, and I had to find her!*
*However, it seemed almost impossible to do this alone, so I went for help.*
You: "Who would be most willing to help me? Of course, Slavya!"
*I decided that at this time she would be engaged in cleaning something. For example, the square.*
*So I went there.*
*My sixth sense didn’t let me down.*
You: "Hi!"
Slavya: "Hey!"
You: "Have you seen Lena?"
Slavya: "No. Why are you asking?"
You: "Nobody's seen her since this morning, She was absent during breakfast, as well as during lunch."
Slavya: "Strange."
You: "I also think this is, to put it mildly, strange. Can you help me find her?"
Slavya: "Oh, sorry. Maybe later? I've got cleaning here to finish..."
*It was like a lightning strike.*
*I took a few awkward steps back and ran away from this place.*
You: "No, that was not her! It was as if somebody had replaced her! Not only her but also the other inhabitants of this camp."
You: "What is happening? The strangest thing is that it doesn’t have anything to do with me, but with Lena!"
You: "Maybe she came here the same way as I did?"
You: "Exactly! That could be the reason why she behaves quietly most of the time."
You: "No, wait... But what about her knowing Alisa...?"
You: "No, something does not add up."
*My head was going to explode, and I started to choke.*
*After catching the breath I looked around and found myself at the bus stop. I sat on the kerb and covered my face with hands.*
You: "If before nothing had really been up to me, but was going relatively smoothly, then now I was, as always, helpless, but the situation was totally different."
You: "Watching the battle fought from the side with no threat to your life and being on the hot spot without being able to help the ones you care about are two different things."
*…*
*I was just sitting.*
*Time passed and the sun began to fall.*
You: "Probably dinner has already started."
You: "Although what's the difference, I still don't want to eat."
*I stood up and trudged back to the camp on rubber legs.*
You: "As always, the only thing left is to wait."
*I decided to go to the beach.*
You: "While everybody was at dinner I could sit quietly and think there."
You: "Though what could I think about? Enough maybe?"
*However, my expectations were ruined.*
*On the beach I met Zhenya, which greatly surprised me.*
You: "You also come here?"
*She looked at me from behind her glasses.*
Zhenya: "Do you think I'm not a human being?"
You: "No, I don't mean that."
Zhenya: "Then what do you mean?"
You: "Nothing... By the way have you seen Lena?"
Zhenya: "No."
You: "I see..."
Zhenya: "What do you want from her?"
You: "Well... Nobody's seen her since yesterday evening."
Zhenya: "Do you think that somebody could get lost in this camp?"
*She laughed loudly.*
You: "Shurik succeeded..."
Zhenya: "That was a special case... Those guys are two peas in a pod and you never know what to expect from them."
*I immediately remembered the morning incident.*
You: "Tell me... Why were you chasing Electronik this morning?"
*Zhenya got uncomfortable.*
Zhenya: "It's none of your business."
You: "Just asking."
Zhenya: "Because he is a fool!"
*She turned away after these words.*
You: "Maybe you shouldn't be so strict towards him."
*Even to me it wasn't clear whether I’m defending Electronik or just keeping the conversation going.*
Zhenya: "Then how else should I treat him?"
You: "Well, give him a chance... You know, such an act requires lots of courage."
Zhenya: "You say it... as if it is something special, some kind of achievement. Would you be able to do that yourself?"
*I thought and answered after a while.*
You: "I don’t know... Haven't had the right moment yet."
Zhenya: "I hope you'll have it soon."
*Zhenya said rudely and walked towards the canteen.*
*I sat down on the sand and thought.*
You: "True that, Electronik was able say it, but can I do the same thing? That is the question, a big question."
You: "If I got the right moment... But which and when?"
You: "It's always easier to think about something ephemeral, to get ready for dozens of possible situations, to predict the following events for many steps ahead."
You: "But most of the time it all goes differently."
You: "Even a small event is enough to ruin all your plans."
You: "And if you're not ready to do it at any time, whenever, under any circumstances, if you are ready only when everything is exactly as you had expected, it is unlikely you'd ever get anything worthwhile."
You: "Therefore, the only correct answer to Zhenya's question was 'no'."
You: " Not an ambiguous, uncertain, half-hearted, or forced answer. Just 'no'."
You: "There is only a simple 'yes' and a simple 'no'."
*It's always been hard for me to understand that.*
*Between these two extremes I always worked in a great number of different answers like “maybe”, “perhaps”, “probably if”, and “not sure but I will try”...*
*…*
*I was so absorbed with my thoughts that I did not notice how the darkness stole across the camp.*
*Under other circumstances I would have gone to sleep now... But looking for Lena at night was not a good idea.*
*I got up and slowly wandered aimlessly.*
*Soon, the path led me to the sports ground.*
*I stood there for a moment and was about to leave when I heard noises.*
You: "Clap, another clap... Something painfully familiar!"
*I ran towards the volleyball court and saw Lena, who was unsuccessfully trying to hit the shuttlecock with the racket.*
*I stood in shock for a long time.*
*My head was completely empty, I just looked at her and felt a sense of joy. Joy at finding her, joy at seeing her again.*
*Finally I came to my senses and decided to approach...*
*But after a couple of steps I stopped.*
You: "And what do I say now? “Glad I found you”? “Where have you been, I was worried”?"
You: "After yesterday's conversation it's very unlikely she wants to see me."
You: "And what if Lena asked me why I was looking for her? Why I was worrying?"
You: "I did not know why myself... Probably it's because she was absent for too long."
You: "Maybe if it wasn't her but some other person who I know I'd have been worried the same way."
You: "Maybe if I'd behaved differently yesterday she would not have disappeared today."
You: "I'm not sure, but I'll try to come up with something adequate..."
*I took another step and stopped again.*
You: "Probably, maybe, perhaps, not sure..."
You: "Again and again, these words appeared in my mind, in my life..."
You: "Unconsciously, without my will!"
You: "But why? For what purpose?"
You: "I have to make a decision! Once and for all!"
You: "Although ... There are two simple words – “yes” and “no”."
*Finally it's all clear!*
*I went to the court, approached Lena, smiled and said:*
You: "Hey!"
*She turned and looked at me.*
Lena: "Hi..."
You: "You were absent all day."
Lena: "Yes... I was walking around."
*Everything she said was quiet and calm with no trace of embarassment or shyness. With no emotions at all, in fact.*
You: "We worried about you."
*Though the only one who worried was me.*
Lena: "You shouldn't have."
You: "But you can't.... You can't just disappear like that!"
*I tried to smile to make my words not sound like a reproach.*
Lena: "I don't think that anybody cares about that."
You: "I care, for one."
Lena: "Why?"
*I read surprise in her eyes.*
You: "Because... Because it's not right!"
*No matter how I tried to be perfectly honest, it came out wrong.*
Lena: "Ah! I see... Ok, I won’t do this again."
*It seemed like this conversation was not interesting to her.*
*Silence followed.*
*I just didn't know what else to say, and Lena seemed to be quite content with the silence.*
You: "Are you any good?"
*I finally said, pointing at the racket.*
Lena: "Not very..."
You: "If you want, I..."
Lena: "No, I don't."
*She walked to the bench and put down her racket and birdie.*
You: "Okay..."
*To tell the truth, I did not expect that response.*
Lena: "Want to look at the stars together?"
You: "Yes, of course..."
*I sat down beside her.*
*Lena intently studied the sky.*
*Lots of small lights shined above me. Some of them were brighter, some were barely visible.*
*I never really understood what people see in just sitting back and looking at the stars.*
*After all, here on Earth they're just small dots of light and it's unlikely that many people know what kind of celestial bodies they are, as well as their size and how far they are from us.*
*Of course, it's so romantic to just enjoy the light of distant stars, but for me it was like staring at a brick wall. It also has its potholes, unevenness in the brickwork, patterns on the stone.*
*A stellar sky in miniature.*
You: "So what do you see there?"
Lena: "Stars..."
*She said mysteriously with her head up.*
You: "Yes I know, I see them too. But what’s so special about them?"
Lena: "I don't know... It seems that they talk to me. There are other people there. They have their own life, probably much better than ours, and they too look at the sky and see the Earth, me and you."
You: "Voices of the distant stars..."
You: "I had already heard that somewhere else."
Lena: "You can call it that."
You: "Interesting theory."
Lena: "No no, the theory is quiet common."
*Lena looked at me.*
*In the dim moonlight, I noticed a small tear rolling down her cheek. Or at least I thought I did...*
You: "I guess I'm just a more, let's say, practical person."
*She said nothing, just stared at the sky again.*
You: "But if you think about it, of course, there's endless interstellar space, millions of planets, hundreds of galaxies... It's fascinating!"
*My voice sounded unnaturally excited.*
Lena: "You don't need to talk about all these things."
You: "About what?"
Lena: "About this... About everything..."
You: "No, the stars are... are really beautiful..."
Lena: "Why did you come?"
*Now she was crying for sure.*
You: "I...I... was looking for you."
Lena: "Why?"
You: "I don't know why! I just was!"
Lena: "You found me, happy now?"
You: "Well..."
*I mumbled.*
Lena: "Why didn't you go to Alisa?"
You: "What does she have to do with it?"
Lena: "Are you trying to say that it’s not about her?"
You: "Yes, that is exactly what I am saying! Why did you bring this topic up again? I thought we already cleared everything up."
*Of course, we didn't clear anything up. To be precise, we didn't even start to.*
*However, I don't understand why all this is necessary.*
Lena: "You think I really want to talk about it myself?"
You: "If you don't then why?"
Lena: "Because... Because... It's because of you!"
You: "Because of me what?"
Lena: "You and Alisa..."
You: "Me and Alisa what? We don’t have a relationship… we don’t have anything at all!"
Lena: "Don't lie to me..."
*Lena turned away sobbing quietly.*
You: "Why is this so important to her?"
You: "What else can I say if you don't believe me?"
Lena: "Tell me the truth!"
You: "I've already told you!"
Lena: "Then go to her!"
You: "Why should I go to her? I don't want to go anywhere!"
Lena: "Why are you sitting here and torturing me?"
You: "Oh Lord! How am I torturing you?"
*Lena didn't answer.*
You: "I've been looking for you for the entire day, because I was worried! I came here because you're here! I'm sitting here because I want to be here! What don't you understand?"
*She stopped crying for a moment.*
Lena: "Is that true?"
You: "Of course!"
Lena: "I mean something to you?"
*Even taking into account all the things I’ve just said, this question came at me unexpectedly.*
You: "Well.. Yes..."
Lena: "If only you could hear yourself now!"
*She cried, got up and walked briskly towards the exit of the sports ground.*
You: "Wait!"
*I caught up with her and grabbed her arm, but she pulled out of my grip.*
Lena: "Don't touch me!"
*Now Lena was a totally different person.*
*And I couldn't say that she was aggressive, assertive or super strong-willed. She just had no doubts about what she was doing.*
You: "Wait! What did I say? That's all true!"
Lena: "Save all this nonsense for her!"
*I tried to stop Lena once again, but she glared at me so strongly that I did not dare to argue.*
You: "Just imagine how I feel! You make up a bunch of stupid things, and now you think that I'm guilty of all mortal sins!"
Lena: "Why should you care?"
You: "I should!"
*She stopped for a moment and looked at me.*
Lena: "It's all lies!"
*In my anger I banged my forehead on an iron post.*
Lena: "You can just beat yourself up here!"
*I had seen Lena be many things, but not ruthless and indifferent.*
You: "Wait, let's talk calmly!"
Lena: "We have nothing to talk about!"
*She crossed the football ground and I trailed behind, trying in vain to persuade her to listen to me.*
You: "I don't know why I'm doing all this. To prove that I'm right?"
You: "So I won’t be misunderstood? So I will look better in her eyes?"
You: "Or is there some other reason?"
*In any case, at that moment I just felt that it was necessary.*
*We came to the square.*
*Lena was pretty fast, I could barely keep up with her.*
*I had to say something. My head was filled with different options, but nothing suitable.*
You: "Wait!"
*No answer.*
You: "Listen..."
*No answer.*
You: "Will you stop it!?"
*No answer.*
You: "We’ll wake the whole camp!"
Lena: "So what? What's the difference?"
*Strange, but at that moment I was more worried about our behavior than Lena.*
*She stopped.*
Lena: "Thanks for accompanying me, I’ll go alone now."
*Lena said bitterly.*
You: "You haven't listened to me yet!"
Lena: "To me, it seems like I've already listened, several times even!"
You: "So what do you want from me?"
Lena: "Me? From you? Nothing at all!"
*She sounded much more confident than me, there was no trace of doubt in her eyes.*
You: "What can I say...? What can I do...? Damn it!"
*I was ready to burst into tears.*
Lena: "Don't get so emotional. Nothing happened."
You: "Nothing happened?! Something definitely happened!"
Lena: "You won't lose anything if you pay no attention to me."
You: "Let me decide that!"
Lena: "No, seriously, why? There are many pleasant activities you could choose to do. Well, to be honest, I don't need it anyway."
You: "If you don't need it, why do you constantly mention Alisa?"
*Lena's face changed.*
Lena: "This is none of your business, get it!?"
You: "No, now it's my business!"
*She looked at me as if she was ready to kill.*
Lena: "Why are you bothering me? You have her? So go to her! She won't refuse, I assure you."
*Lena started screaming, her hair disheveled, her face flushed and her eyes bloodshot.*
You: "Calm down! I won't go to her. Why would you even think so? Just see – I'm here now and I’m not going anywhere."
*She seemed to calm down a bit.*
Alisa: "What's going on here?"
*I turned around and saw Alisa lazily chewing a bun.*
You: "In the wrong place at the wrong time. This situation is a perfect example."
*I just froze in surprise, not knowing what to say.*
*But Lena was smarter.*
Lena: "Time to pass him on. Catch!"
*Alisa looked surprised. No wonder, she hadn't heard the entire conversation.*
Alisa: "What?"
Lena: "I said catch."
*Within a moment Lena became like she was before – calm and unruffled.*
Alisa: "What should I catch?"
Lena: "Him!"

*Right then, what I should do was completely unclear.*

*I had no idea what the logic behind her actions was. What the meaning and motivation was.*

*She was lying with her eyes wide open, staring at the ceiling.*

Olga: "Wake up already!"

*Though I've already started to think that it's not entirely wrong.*
*The entire lineup consisted of a roll-call and announcement that the shower room is closed today for repair.*

*Frankly speaking, I wasn't in the mood for eating at all.*

*I guess her exact words flew over me.*
*Just the melody of her voice was enough for me – it hypnotized and carried me away from this sick woman and stupid pioneer camp while calming and healing the wounds in my soul.*

*Olga Dmitrievna calmed down a bit.*

*I expected a storm of applause like in American movies but crowd started to dissolve quickly as the show came to its end.*
*And Ulyana just winked at me slyly.*

Slavya: "Oh, come on…"
You: "What? That's the simple truth, not a trace of lies or flattery!"

*Slavya looked at me with surprise.*
You: "Well, you know, it's just sometimes..."
Slavya: "Ok, let's go!"
