*I was just going to tell her about a feeling I get sometimes – when you want to go somewhere outside of your comfort zone. At least for a while, at least for a couple of hours.*
*I used to do this before quite often – visiting foreign districts or even neighbouring cities.*
*New places and sceneries calm my heart and help to realise that the world is not limited by my apartment walls, or the daily route to university or the workplace.*

*Right now I was definitely sure that there was nothing interesting in my life at all.*

You: "When I was a kid – like 5 or 6 years old I guess – there was a small hut near my family's country house."

Slavya: "Oh, come on!"

*I've mumbled slowly.*

*My survivalist thoughts were interrupted by Slavya who suddenly appeared right above me.*

*…*

*I woke up early, when Olga Dmitrievna was still asleep. I stretched and sat up in the bed.*

Shurik: "Just be careful."

*I took the package. If the pioneers weren't passing me the key to the Pearly Gates, it still looked like they were at least giving me the Olympic Torch.*
You: "Can I go?"
Sergei: "Of course."
*Electronik said threateningly.*
Shurik: "Just be careful!"
*Shurik pleaded.*
*Outside, I took a good look at the package.*
*They never told me not to open it.*
You: "Although it would make sense to go further on."
*I quickly walked to the square and, making sure nobody was following, slipped into the forest.*
*I just stood there for a while, indecisive, looking at the package.*

*I had a lot of questions.*
*I opened the package and saw a bottle of 'Stolichnaya' vodka.*

*I wrapped the bottle back up and scratched my head.*
You: "This isn't weird anymore, this is just stupid."
You: "So stupid I couldn't think of one intelligent theory."
*I stood there for a while longer and thought I shouldn't let such a wonderful chance slip away. I quickly walked to the camp leader's cabin.*
*Thank God, Olga Dmitrievna was not there. I snuck inside and began to rifle through the contents of the table drawer.*
*Soon, the vodka was in a soda bottle, while in its place was some water for the plants.*
*Happy with my clever plan, I went out and skipped along the way to the infirmary.*
You: "Seriously, what is so wrong about that? They almost got me into a trap! If the camp leader had seen me..."
You: "If anyone else had?"
You: "I could have managed myself..."
You: "So it was absolutely nothing!"
*I gathered all my strength and knocked on the infirmary door.*
Violetta: "Hello... pioneer!"
You: "Hello! I have a package for you – a bottle for your armpit... I mean a package for your cabinet."
*I was so euphoric I began to talk nonsense.*
Violetta: "Ahh..."
*She said.*
Violetta: "Hand it over."
*I handed her the package.*
*The nurse stuffed it into the desk drawer without looking.*
Violetta: "You didnt open it, did you?"
You: "Of course not!"
*I blurted out.*
Violetta: "Good boy."

Violetta: "Go, go... pioneer."
*I closed the door behind me and let out a sigh.*
You: "I could always pin this on the crazy inventors, and in my situation I could really use even the most basic form of stress relief!"
*I came to the square. The clock showed noon. That meant dinner was coming.*
*I sat on the bench with the solid intention of not moving from here until the come-and-get-it bell sound comes.*
*Pioneers were running by. They were smiling and shouting merrily.*
You: "Yes, the day was definitely a wonderful one."
*I glanced over the square and saw Lena approaching.*
Lena: "Relaxing?"

*She sat by me and looked at the sky.*
Lena: "Nice day, huh?"

Lena: "I told you everything already."

Lena: "Just forget it."
You: "If you say so..."
*We sat for a little longer in silence.*
You: "I just can't, not like that."
Lena: "So what do you think about Alisa?"
*She said, ignoring my inquiry.*
You: "What do I think about Alisa?"
*I repeated, lost in thought.*
You: "I don’t really know... Why?"
Lena: "You're just so worried about yesterday."
You: "Well of course... But what does that have to do with it?"
Lena: "There's a direct connection there!"
*She laughed.*
You: "Let's assume..."
Lena: "So what?"
You: "Well she..."
*And again I started thinking.*
You: "Really, what do I think of her?"
You: "Well she... She can be arrogant sometimes."
Lena: "That's right."
You: "What else can I say? Now that I think of it, I don't know Alisa at all. The way she acts does annoy me sometimes."
You: "If you were wondering if I had any negative feelings about her, then no."
You: "I mean, she gets carried away, but everyone has their quirks..."
*Lena stared at me.*
Lena: "Really?"
You: "Did I say something wrong?"
Lena: "No, not really..."
*She laughed out loud one more time, just before the lunch bell sound came.*
Lena: "Alright, see you!"
*I didn't stop her, although I had a lot of questions left.*
You: "But how do I ask them? And should I?"
*I got up and slowly shuffled to the canteen.*
*There were only few spots left, so I had to sit with Electronik and Shurik.*
Sergei: "Did you deliver it?"
You: "Yeah..."
*I answered lazily, poking my fork at the buckwheat kasha.*
Sergei: "No incidents?"
You: "No incidents... What was in there anyway?"
Sergei: "You didn't open it did you?"
*He stared.*
You: "No..."
Sergei: "Great!"
*Finishing my meal, I went out.*
*I was struck by a sudden yawn.*
You: "Taking a nap wouldn’t be a bad idea."
*I headed to the camp leader's cabin.*
*It felt like the summer sun was going to melt the whole planet, together with all its inhabitants.*
*There was nowhere to hide – the sunlight seemed to reflect from every surface. Looking up, you risked going blind.*
*Using my last bit of strength, I pulled the doorhandle, entered the room and fell onto the bed.*
*Of course I wouldn’t expect the cabin to be really cool, but it was much better than outside.*
*Blissfully, I stretched out on the bed and closed my eyes.*
*Strangely, sleep deserted me. I was overwhelmed with thoughts, teeming in my head.*
*Here is another theory, a solution to the problem of how I got here. Here is an explanation of what's going on here. And here is the true form of all those inhabiting this place.*
*I remembered Lena saying, 'What do you think about Alisa?'*
You: "Seriously, what do I think of her? What can I think of a person I've only known for a few days? Can I just draw conclusions based on a couple of words and deeds?"
You: "Although her deeds..."
*I laughed a bit.*
*Any relevant organization would draw the right conclusion based on the monument bombing.*
You: "Still though, I... don't care?"
You: "Maybe I really don't think anything of her?"
You: "Can one be interested in a person who's not interesting?"
You: "No, that's some sort of a absurdity..."
*A knock on the door.*
You: "Come in!"
*I was too lazy to get up so I just sat up a little bit.*
*The door opened and I saw Alisa. What a coincidence...*
*She stopped, unsure, and stared at me for a couple of seconds.*
You: "I guess you were looking for the camp leader?"
You: "Why would she though?"
Alisa: "No."
You: "What's up then?"
Alisa: "I was looking for you."
*She sounded calm and not aggressive at all.*
*I caught myself, thinking I was not afraid of her and had no concerns when she behaved like that – normally.*
You: "What for?"
Alisa: "I want to make everything clear."
*She sat on the bed across from me.*
You: "What exactly?"
Alisa: "I want to clean up any misunderstandings or miscommunications."
You: "Alright, I’m up for that!"
Alisa: "Have you spoken with Lena today?"
You: "Yes."
Alisa: "About what?"
You: "Nothing really..."
Alisa: "You're lying."
*Alisa looked stiff and worried. She crossed her legs and bit her lip.*
Alisa: "You do understand I... I'm always assumed to be guilty whenever anything happens?"
You: "Well you always are guilty."
*I said thoughtlessly.*
*A spark flashed in her eyes but she kept talking calmly:*
Alisa: "Maybe... But in this case... Me and Lena, we're always like that – even if she starts something, she's all innocent and I take all the blame!"
You: "So you're saying that Lena... Actually, I don't really know what you're saying."
Alisa: "You never understand anything, do you!?"
*She fumed.*

You: "No..."

Alisa: "Well, now you do..."
You: "Now I do..."
*An uncomfortable silence overtook the room.*
*I was processing what she said, and Alisa seemed unsure of how to continue the conversation.*
You: "Lena likes me... Could I ever have guessed? Unlikely."
*My intuition is usually good but when it's about me and my feelings it does not work at all.*
*The weirdest thing was, I accepted the news with almost no worries.*
*Right at the moment, I was listening to Alisa, I was focused only on her. I could think about the rest later.*
Alisa: "And she thinks I'm gonna steal you away from her! She thinks that all the time, understand? Even though it's always the other way around! Everyone looks at her cause she's such an angel, and nobody pays any attention to me!"
Alisa: "To them I'm just a shoulder to cry on..."
*Alisa started screaming.*
You: "Look, I... Please don't get so upset! I don't think of you like that!"
Alisa: "Of course..."
*I still had no idea what forced her to be so honest. And I didn't know how to react. Moreover, I was not worried at all.*
*It was like I was watching another episode of some TV series, and what was going on in the room was on the other side of the screen.*
You: "I understand, I was the reason for all of it... But today Lena said it was okay."
Alisa: "That's just like her! You've probably realised that she's not as quiet as she wants to seem!"
You: "I'd started to guess."
You: "If I can do anything..."
Alisa: "Tell me..."
*Alisa raised her eyes. Only then did I see she's been crying.*
*Some sort of worry stirred inside of me. I could not treat this conversation like I was an outsider anymore.*
Alisa: "Do you like Lena? Or do you like me?"
*I guess I should have expected a question like that, but I just wasn't ready.*
You: "Just like that..."
You: "Lena is nice of course... But Alisa has her good points as well."
*Besides, the way she was at the moment, she could seriously compete with Lena.*
You: "I don't really know you two at all... A question like that... It's difficult to answer directly."
*If I could say no, I would have, at that very moment.*
*But I only had one chance for the other answer as well.*
*And I didn't know what to choose.*
Alisa: "You did want the situation to resolve itself."
You: "Of course, but..."
Alisa: "Why 'but' again?"
You: "Why 'again'?"
Alisa: "Why 'why'?"
You: "Look, we're going nowhere with this."
Alisa: "Well, answer then!"
*Her face fell back into its usual bold arrogance.*
You: "I need time to think..."
Alisa: "Well go ahead and think!"
*Alisa stood up abruptly and headed out.*
Alisa: "Don't forget we have plans for tonight!"
*She said on the threshold, smiling.*
*The door closed behind her before I could say anything.*
You: "Plans? What kind of plans?"
*The talk with Alisa left a heavy impression on me.*
You: "So, Lena likes me..."
You: "On its own, the news could shock and startle. And I, above that, was also forced to make a choice. A difficult one, to put it mildly. And any choice I make would be a mistake for someone."
You: "If only I could refuse them both..."
*Although I didn't like the word 'refuse' itself.*
You: "If I could just answer her question with a 'no' it would be easier."
*But I knew it couldn't work like that.*
You: "After I talked to Alisa, I realised nothing would ever be the same again."
*It can't be, no matter what happens. And I'll have to make a decision...*
You: "Since I rejected the “no” scenario, I needed to pick a positive solution. If, of course, I could live with it."
*But I was sure that out of all the possible outcomes, there's one that won't just satisfy everyone, but would also be one that I would want to strive for.*
*And the choice seems obvious: Lena. She's pretty, she's cute, she's kind.*
*But then again, there was something about Alisa that attracted me.*
*Suddenly the door flew open, and Olga Dmitrievna came in.*
Olga: "Lounging around again, huh."
You: "Just resting... It's so hot out there..."
Olga: "Go and help Slavya. She was asking around."
You: "Where?"
*I asked lazily.*
Olga: "On the sports field."
*Reluctantly, I got up and headed out.*
*I should really air my brain out anyway.*
*There were a lot of people at the sports grounds. Some were playing football, others were playing badminton. Younger kids were just chasing each other.*
Slavya: "Semyon!"
*Slavya walked up to me.*
You: "You require my assistance?"
*I asked, all official-like.*
Slavya: "Yeah... Listen, did you take the infirmary key?"

Slavya: "Well you were there a lot recently."
You: "I guess she is right..."
You: "No..."
Slavya: "Maybe you know who did?"

Slavya: "The nurse came up to me to ask for my key – you know that I have a key to every building in the camp. She said hers went missing."

*I shrugged.*
Slavya: "No, she says she couldn't have."
You: "I don't know, okay?"
Slavya: "Okay."
*She smiled and ran off.*
*I headed to the camp leader's house, determined to get some sleep after all.*
*Olga Dmitrievna wasn't there, thank God, so I fell on the bed and lost consciousness.*
*...*
*I don't exactly remember what I dreamt of but it left a heavy impression, as afternoon naps often do.*
*I put some effort into getting off the bed and looked at the clock. It was just after seven.*
You: "Not surprising if you think about it – I should have expected to sleep through the day."
You: "Although, as it turns out, I missed dinner as well..."
*That thought made me uncomfortable, and I headed to the exit.*
*I stopped on the threshold and thought of what to do next.*
*I don't know how long I would have stood there – my head was still heavy after sleep – if someone hadn't called out to me.*
*Slavya was quickly walking towards the cabin.*
Slavya: "Semyon..."
*She started, breathless.*
Slavya: "Are you sure you don't have the infirmary key?"
You: "Of course not, why would I need it?"
Slavya: "Well do you know who took it?"
You: "No I don't. Why?"
Slavya: "Well... Something has gone missing."
You: "What?"
Slavya: "Something important..."
*Slavya hesitated.*
Slavya: "Some medication."
You: "So all this disturbance was started because of some medicine? Although..."
*I pondered.*
You: "I mean, I have the bottle in my cabin... Did she mean that?"
*I tried to keep my face still as stone, without doing anything to give myself away.*
You: "Okay. I don't know, I'm sorry..."
Slavya: "Okay..."
*Slavya said in frustration.*
*I looked at her and tried to figure out how bad the situation was for me, or whether I was in trouble at all.*
You: "On the one had, the vodka... I did... steal it."
You: "Then again, she's saying it's 'gone', as in disappeared, all by itself, with no external influence."
You: "Although it’s highly unlikely that she would say that a bottle of trophy vodka was stolen from the infirmary."
You: "So the way it was said was okay. The problem was different."
*I suddenly got really scared.*
You: "What if they find out that was me?"
You: "Even if it wasn't about the bottle, they'd still find it while looking for what was gone."
*Basically, I had to get a move on! And the main thing to do right now was to get rid of all the evidence!*
*I jumped into the cabin, shoved the bottle under my belt and raced to the forest. Burying it somewhere was the best decision at the moment.*
*I took my time looking for a spot, never noticing night falling on the camp.*
*A familiar voice surprised me.*
Alisa: "Hey!"
*I struggled to turn back, making my face look as casual as possible.*
Alisa: "So. What's going on here?"
You: "Oh I'm just having a walk."
*My voice sounded calm but I already understood – I couldn't fool Alisa.*
Alisa: "Alone? At night? In the woods?"
You: "Well yeah... What’s wrong?"
Alisa: "Nothing. Nothing at all."
*She stared at me.*
You: "Okay, then I'll..."
Alisa: "Hold on! Aren't you forgetting something?"
You: "Don't think so."
Alisa: "We had an agreement!"

Alisa: "About tonight!"
*I think she's right. There was something like that.*

Alisa: "No I don't! Let's go!"
*She turned around and gestured me to follow.*
*I thought there was no point in arguing – any word or action could give me away.*
You: "And then..."

*It was a couple of minutes before we reached her cabin.*
*While we were walking, I was busy trying to find the best time and place to ditch the vodka, but Alisa stayed so close that I couldn’t manage anything.*
Alisa: "Well?"
*She stared at me.*
You: "Well what?"
*I was so nervous that my hair was wet with sweat.*
*The only thing on my mind at the moment was how to adjust the bottle so she wouldn't notice.*
Alisa: "What do you say?"
You: "About what?"
*Alisa pondered.*

Alisa: "So?"
*Alisa looked at me teasingly.*
You: "What?"
Alisa: "Wanna take a shot?"
*I didn't even know what to say to that.*
You: "What she had was just rotten water. The real vodka was in the bottle under my belt."
You: "Well, I kind of..."
Alisa: "Don't tell me you don't drink!"
*Alisa pouted.*
You: "I don't know... No, I just..."
Alisa: "Alright then! Just a second!"
*In just an instant Alisa got two glasses and filled them to the brim.*
Alisa: "Let's do this!"
*She said, giving me one of the glasses and downed hers before I could answer.*
Alisa: "Eugh!"
*She gasped.*
*In a moment she realised...*
Alisa: "What on Earth is that?!"
*She started spitting.*
Alisa: "They call this vodka?!"
*Despite my difficulty, I couldn't help laughing.*
Alisa: "What are you laughing at?"
*Alisa shouted, red in the face.*
Alisa: "I'm asking you, what's so funny?!"
You: "It actually is funny."
Alisa: "So you're having fun? Drink yours, we'll see how you laugh then!"
*I had no desire to try the stale water, but just to avoid making her suspicious I asked:*
You: "So, how does it taste?"
Alisa: "Like rotten water."
*Alisa said, upset.*
Alisa: "I was just going to relax a bit, have a cultured time-out, and then it..."
You: "A cultured time-out..."
*I repeated, as a new bout of laughter bent me in half.*
Alisa: "Hey, stop it!"
*Alisa shouted and jumped at me.*
*She was trying to hit me, or bite me or something. Maybe her plan was to crush me to death with her authority. I just grabbed her hands, and all she could do was gasp in powerless anger.*
*All was going fine but then Alisa's legs slid and she began to fall.*
*I let go of her hands, so she fell right on top of me, painfully headbutting me in the nose.*
*I moaned in pain, threw her off and turned to the side.*
Alisa: "What do we have here?"
*When I realised she had taken the bottle, all the pain disappeared.*
You: "Give that back!"
*I tried to get the bottle back but Alisa nimbly jumped off the bed and ran to the far corner of the room.*
Alisa: "Let's see, huh!"

Alisa: "What... what is this?"
*She rasped, while coming back to her senses.*

*I seemed to have come to terms with my defeat.*
Alisa: "But where did you get it...?"
You: "You really thought you had stolen the right one from the infirmary?"
*She nodded.*
You: "Well, it was the right bottle, sure, but the contents..."
Alisa: "Man, you're clever!"
*She was already starting to slur her words.*

Alisa: "Come on!"
You: "I don't want it!"
You: "Really, this is not the right time or place."

Alisa: "Well, you have the vodka!"

Alisa: "Well, how was it?"

Alisa: "No way!"

*The alcohol was starting its work. Without a second thought, I gulped down the vodka.*
*Alisa was definitely less experienced – she was having some trouble with her second glass.*
Alisa: "Ugh... How does it..."
*She seemed really drunk already.*

Alisa: "How about me?"
*Alisa was outraged.*
You: "Haven't you had enough?"
Alisa: "No way!"
*She grabbed the bottle from my hand and started to drink straight from it.*

Alisa: "This is so cool!"
*She said, catching her breath.*

Alisa: "That's all!"

Alisa: "Oh who cares!"

Alisa: "And for all the gentlemen!"

Alisa: "I'm getting dizzy..."
*She undid a few buttons on her shirt.*
*I carefully looked at her.*
You: "Had she always been this beautiful? Or is everyone beautiful to me at this point...?"
*Whichever it was, I could not force myself to look away.*
Alisa: "You're gonna stare a hole through me if you keep going like that!"
*Alisa laughed.*
You: "Sorry..."
*Embarrassed, I stared at my feet.*
Alisa: "You can look if you're so interested."
*With some effort, I opened an eye and saw her continuing to unbutton her shirt.*
*No words could escape my mouth. Besides, who needs words at a moment like this?*
*...*
*What happened then was what was supposed to happen.*
*At the time I was unable to think of what was right to do.*
*And I didn't want to – I just felt good.*
*...*
*The lightbulb burned out, or one of us turned off the light, but either way the room went dark.*
*I looked around her cabin and thought of something.*
You: "Where's Ulyana?"
Alisa: "What, you're afraid someone will come in and see us?"

Alisa: "Well, not something like this of course..."
*She looked at me intently, smiled and closed her eyes.*

*My head ached suddenly – the alcohol seemed to be wearing off.*
*Best thing to do in this case is to follow her lead and get some sleep as well. Before I finished the thought I was already fast asleep.*
*The bright sunlight was striking my eyes even through my eyelids.*
*I stretched out lazily and quickly got myself out of the bed.*
*It was 2 PM.*
You: "Looks like yesterday really finished me off and my body required much more time to recover than usual."
*I had a stroll around the room, thinking of what I should do today.*
*Obviously my life in the camp would never be the same again after everything that I'd heard from that strange pioneer.*
You: "And if everything's just as he said, I have plenty of time ahead."
*I grabbed my hygiene kit and went outside.*
*I managed to take only a couple of steps, as somebody ran into my back.*
*I turned around and saw Alisa.*
Alisa: "Hey, be careful!"
*Said she indifferently and ran on her way.*
*She held some kind of a bag in her hands...*
You: "Ah, whatever, yet another ordinary day in this crazy place."
*I finished brushing my teeth and then spent an eternity washing my face with ice-cold water to bring myself to my senses and refresh my head at least a bit.*
*I felt a bit better after that.*
*Suddenly, hope struck me from nowhere. It wasn't a hope that I'd be likely to leave this place safely...*
*Rather, I just didn't want to believe that everything is as bad as that guy told me.*
Pioneer: "Good morning..."
*I heard a faint voice coming from the woods.*
*Someone stood behind a tree.*
You: "Morning..."
Pioneer: "Are you ready?"
You: "Ready for what?"
*I looked again and it seemed like it was the pioneer from the bus stop yesterday.*
*Indeed, I was prepared for such weirdness today, so I wasn't really surprised and started this conversation quite clear-headed.*
Pioneer: "You didn't believe him, did you?"
You: "What are you talking about?"
Pioneer: "Everything that he said..."
You: "Alright, but what is your opinion on what is happening?"
*I'd already distanced myself from the outside world and decided to treat everything happening to me just like a fictional film, not reality.*
You: "Hopefully, it would give me more room to move around in terms of situational logic analysis."
Pioneer: "There is an exit. There has to be!"
*He said excitedly.*
You: "I don't know... But I'd like to believe that too."
Pioneer: "If you'd just..."
Slavya: "Semyon!"
*I turned around.*
*Slavya was standing right next to me.*
Slavya: "Who were you talking to?"
You: "Ahem... No one... Just talking to myself."
*I hardly think it's worth telling her about aliens from parallel worlds.*
You: "She probably can’t even see them anyway..."
Slavya: "Have you prepared already?"
You: "Prepared? For another hike?"
Slavya: "No! Today's the last day of the session."
You: "What...?"
*A stupid smile settled on my face.*
Slavya: "There will be a bus this evening. We're leaving."
You: "Holy cow..."
You: "I was ready for even the most incredible of twists, but..."
*Was this what that mysterious pioneer was talking about?*

*It was probably very hard for her to discuss it indeed.*

*Lena smiled slyly.*
*It was just now that I realised that I'm playing a high-stakes game.*

*I assured myself that this is it – the real Lena is in front of me.*

*...*
*I desperately tried not to fall asleep. It's unknown what's awaiting there – after the buses' next turn. It might be a new life waiting for me, or it might be the end of this fairytale – and I'll be buried in the coffin of the peeling walls and ceiling of my old apartment.*
*But it was a losing battle – Morpheus has summoned legions of monsters under the command of Fatigue, Exhaustion, Desolation and Uncertainty.*
*I had no chance to win the battle against these Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse – and I drifted off to sleep.*

*It looks like our two amped-up cyberneticists are paying a visit to the clubhouse before the break of dawn today.*

Ulyana: "And what's the..."

*And one of these conditions was sitting right in front of me, smiling broadly.*

Ulyana: "You and your jokes…"

Ulyana: "Let's go."
*Ulyana said happily and pointed at the bag.*

*I shouldered her belongings. The weight almost made me bend in half.*
*I was thankful for the fact that the bus stop was just a few hundred metres away.*
*I shoved her stuff onto the bus, and then hurried to get my own humble luggage.*
*After some time all the pioneers were here.*
Olga: "Everyone is here?"
*Began Olga Dmitrievna.*
Olga: "You're leaving our camp today and I'd like to tell you something in parting."

Olga: "I hope that you'll remember the time you've spent here for a lifetime and that you'll retain only pleasant memories about Sovyonok."
Olga: "I also hope that you became at least a little bit better, managed to learn something and found new friends... Just... come back next year."

*I wasn't expecting her to get so emotional but I completely agreed with everything she said.*

*I always felt more comfortable thinking about abstract stuff, distant perspectives and global matters than of simple, ordinary issues.*

*Some people were chasing me...*

You: "It’s just, today we're leaving, right?"
Slavya: "Right."
You: "And we will move back to our cities."
Slavya: "Well, yeah."
You: "And when will I see you again?"
*Slavya grew thoughtful.*
Slavya: "I don't know..."
You: "And I don't know either."
Slavya: "But you could write me letters!"
*She smiled, but her smile didn't bring me peace of mind.*
You: "Yes, of course, but you know, that's not the same."
Slavya: "What is it then?"
You: "Can I go with you?"
*I decided to take a chance and speak plainly.*
Slavya: "And what will you do there?"
*Slavya seemed to not be surprised, but a bit vexed.*
Slavya: "Studying, my parents... And what will people say?"
*I wasn’t thinking about the opinions of other people. And to be honest, they didn't worry me much.*
You: "Well, we can always find a way!"
Slavya: "What way?"
You: "We'll think of something!"
Slavya: "Semyon, we are too young for this..."
You: "In fact, I'm not."
You: "So what?"
Slavya: "Maybe after some time..."
You: "How much time do you need? A year? Two years? Five?"
Slavya: "You say it as if... I don't know..."
*She seemed confused.*
You: "So everything that happened here was just a holiday romance?"
*I started getting angry.*
Slavya: "No! Of course not! Just..."
You: "What?"
Slavya: "I'm not ready to discuss it right now. Let's talk about it later."
You: "When later? We have only a couple hours left till departure."
*Slavya said nothing and continued to pack her things.*
*I'd expected almost any kind of reaction from her, but not this.*
*In fact, she just pushed me away.*
You: "It turns out she doesn’t need to continue our relationship. So, I'm not that important to her."
You: "Look, I still don't understand."
Slavya: "What?"
*Asked Slavya without turning.*
You: "Why don't you want..."
Slavya: "And how did you expect it to be?"
You: "Well, I can find a job, rent an apartment."
Slavya: "And what can you do? Do you at least have a school leaving certificate?"
You: "In fact yes. It's lying somewhere in the closet..."
You: "That's not important here!"
Slavya: "Why not?"
You: "If you have a goal you can overcome any obstacles! Moreover, they are not that big."
Slavya: "That’s what you think."
You: "Maybe you are right. But anyway, I can't understand your reaction! After all, if we just leave, that's all, that's the end..."
Slavya: "I didn't say that."
You: "But it's obvious."
Slavya: "Where did you get that idea from!?"
*She shouted.*
*Perhaps it was the first time I had seen Slavya like this.*
You: "Well, let me put it differently. I don't just want to go back to the place where I live... and to communicate with you only by letters or phone, hoping for a chance to meet."
Slavya: "It will be hard for me too."
You: "Well, what's the problem then?"
Slavya: "You know, not everything is up to us..."
You: "Who is it up to, then?!"
You: "Although, no-one would know how right she is better than I. If it was all up to me, I would have never found myself here."
Slavya: "There are norms of society, laws, morality, ethics after all."
You: "What do those have to do with anything? Are all those that important?!"
Slavya: "If they are not so important to you, they are important to me."
You: "Okay. I'm even ready to behave according to your standards, but there is something more important."
Slavya: "Maybe... But I can't so suddenly..."
You: "You don't have much time to think."
*I paused for a moment to gather my thoughts.*
You: "I can only offer myself... Because it's the only thing I've got."
You: "Moreover, I don't know what might happen to me in an hour, but I’m sure that, whatever happens, if I have to start from scratch I want to start with you."
Slavya: "You’re speaking so beautifully, but imagine how I feel! For you it's all so simple, but I have my own life that I’m used to, and to change everything just like that..."
You: "I had one before too."
*I said softly.*
Slavya: "What?"
You: "I’m saying that it's inevitable. Changes are part of life, you cannot live without facing them."
*Slavya looked thoughtful, stood still for some time holding her bag in her hands, then came up to me, sat beside and put her head on my shoulder.*
Slavya: "Okay, I believe you. If you say so, then let it be!"
*At that moment I felt perfect happiness.*
You: "It doesn't matter that a week ago I was in a completely different world, living another life. All of that is gone and now it seemed to me like something wild or alien."
*I don't even understand how I could consider that normal.*
You: "Now I am less concerned about how and by whose will all this happened."
You: "Now I'm not looking for answers. Why would I, when they are all right here in front of me?"
You: "Now I have a long road ahead, hand in hand with the person I love. And looking back makes no sense."
*I could sit here forever, not noticing the time, but Slavya finally looked at the clock and gently whispered in my ear:*
Slavya: "It's time."
You: "Yes, exactly. You go to the bus stop, and I'll run to the camp leader’s cabin to get my things."
Slavya: "You are so disorganised! You'd should have gathered them in advance."
*Laughed Slavya.*
You: "I don’t have much to pack anyway..."
*I leaped out of the house and ran towards Olga Dmitrievna’s cabin.*
*The camp leader stood on the threshold, apparently waiting for me.*
Olga: "I thought you wouldn't come..."
*I didn't reply, just bounded inside, packed my winter clothes into a bag and ran out.*
Olga: "Come on already, it's time."
*In a minute we stood at the bus stop, together with the other pioneers.*
Olga: "Everyone's here?"
*Began Olga Dmitrievna.*
Olga: "You're leaving our camp today and I'd like to tell you something in parting."
*She was visibly nervous and desperately lost for words.*
Olga: "I hope that you'll remember the time you've spent here for a lifetime and that you'll retain only pleasant memories about Sovyonok."
Olga: "I also hope that you became at least a little bit better, managed to learn something and found new friends... Just... come back next year."
*The camp leader turned away. It seems she was trying to hold back her tears.*
*I didn't expect her to get so emotional but I completely agreed with everything she said.*
*Perhaps it was the first time that I didn't turn a deaf ear to her.*
*I think I'll miss this camp. And even Olga Dmitrievna.*
You: "Although, if this is the start of a new life, then why not come back here one more time?"
*Sovyonok was far behind. The week had passed like an instant, and come to an end, but that was the beginning of something new. My new life in a new world. Together with Slavya.*
*The moon was shining, making everything as bright as day. Beyond the bus windows endless fields were passing, on occasion dressed up in gray but no less cheerful outfits, decorated in the distance with the dark green of the mighty forests.*
*Anyway, the surroundings were the least of my concerns now – I was enjoying the moment.*
*Slavya and I were sitting in the last row, looking at the other pioneers.*
*Ahead, Ulyana was going wild. She was running through the cabin and shouting. Lena was reading a book and Alisa was sleeping.*
You: "Seems like this world is absolutely normal."
You: "And it doesn't really matter how I got here, if everything turned out so wonderfully. I became a different person, met Slavya."
Slavya: "What are you thinking about?"
You: "Life."
Slavya: "And how is it going?"
You: "Just great!"
*She laughed softly.*
You: "You know..."
Slavya: "Let it wait a little. The bus is rocking me to sleep. I will take a nap if you don't mind."
You: "Sure, go ahead!"
*She rested her head on my shoulder and soon fell asleep.*
*...*
*The imminent arrival at the district centre – and a new chapter in my life - didn't worry me at all.*
*When you are on the top of the world, small things don't bother you.*
*Therefore, I fell asleep as soon as I felt tired, with no fear of anything.*
You: "You think it's only complicated for you!"
Slavya: "It seems to me that it's hard for you too. But for some reason you don't think so."
You: "And what if I told you that I don't have a place to go back to, that since last Monday there is no more life for me and I have to start from scratch?"
Slavya: "I don’t know... That doesn't sound very reasonable."
You: "And it shouldn't! But it's true."
Slavya: "And then what... Please, explain."
You: "I came to this camp by accident! Actually, I'm from another time, perhaps from another world."
You: "From the beginning of the 21st century."
You: "And I'm older than I seem."
You: "I don't really know how I got here."
*Slavya stared at me, but said nothing.*
*The moments dragged on endlessly.*
*I waited for her to laugh at me, to call me sick, or something even worse.*
Slavya: "And why are you telling me all this?"
*She finally asked quietly.*
You: "I want you to understand my situation."
Slavya: "But it... It just sounds stupid."
You: "Of course! If I were you, I would react the same way."
Slavya: "And what do you expect from me?"
You: "I don't know... I just felt that I needed to confess."
Slavya: "I’m not saying that you're lying and I don't think you're crazy, but you have to understand, I can't just accept it."
You: "Yes, I understand... I just thought that it would help you to understand my situation and my motivation for my actions."
Slavya: "It didn't, to be honest."
*I sighed in frustration.*
Slavya: "And my opinion hasn't changed."
You: "But..."
Slavya: "You'd better be off, you need to pack your stuff or you'll be late."
You: "There's..."
Slavya: "Let's talk later."
*I wasn't going to argue.*
You: "If Slavya hasn't changed her mind after my confession then it's pointless to press on right now."
*Distressed, I shuffled off to Olga Dmitrievna’s cabin.*
*The camp leader stood at the doorstep and looked like she was waiting for me.*
Olga: "Why are you so gloomy? Did something happen?"
You: "No, nothing. Just came to pack my things."
Olga: "Oh, come on, let it out. You might feel better."
You: "Well... How do you think I can prove that I'm telling the truth to somebody who doesn't believe me?"
Olga: "Are you absolutely sure that you're telling the truth?"
You: "Absolutely!"
Olga: "Then perhaps they might just need time to consider."
You: "Except there's no time left."
Olga: "Then I don't know."
*She shrugged her shoulders in dismay.*
You: "Well, it's something at least."
*I tossed my winter clothing into a bag and headed to the bus stop.*
*If a couple of days ago I'd seen the Icarus standing at the gate of the camp and waiting for pioneers, I would've been the happiest person in this reality.*
*But right now I wasn't in the mood to rejoice.*
*There was still plenty of time left until the bus departure time.*
*I sat down on the kerb and buried my head in hands.*
Lena: "Why so sad?"
*A familiar voice pulled me out of my thoughts.*
You: "Just..."
Lena: "Had a fight with Slavya?"
You: "You could say that."
Lena: "And what's the reason?"
You: "She doesn't believe that I'm an alien from the future."
*I smiled ironically.*
Lena: "I wouldn’t believe it either."
*Said Lena seriously.*
You: "If I were in your shoes, neither would I."
Lena: "It's not a big deal, you’ll make up from a quarrel!"
You: "Yeah, but there's not much time left to..."
Lena: "Left to what?"
You: "To make the right choice..."
*...*
*After a while the whole camp assembled together at the bus stop.*
Olga: "Everyone's here?"
*Began Olga Dmitrievna.*
Olga: "You're leaving our camp today and I'd like to tell you something in parting."
*She was visibly nervous and desperately lost for words.*
Olga: "I hope that you'll remember the time you've spent here for a lifetime and that you'll retain only pleasant memories about Sovyonok."
Olga: "I also hope that you became at least a little bit better, managed to learn something and found new friends... Just... come back next year."
*The camp leader turned away. It seems she was trying to hold back her tears.*
*I didn't expect her to get so emotional.*
*Although her speech sounded like a complete nonsense to me. As usual.*
You: "Of course, this is where I met Slavya. But now we were going through a tough time. And what will happen next is absolutely unclear."
*So I didn't care about whether I'll miss this place and Olga Dmitrievna or not. Unlikely...*
*When the pioneers started to get on the bus, I pushed through the crowd to Slavya.*
You: "Let's sit together."
Slavya: "Okay."
*She said quietly.*
*I even thought that I saw the shadow of a smile on her face.*
*The bus flew across the expanses of my new world. Outside, fields followed forests, and then calm rivers and highlands..*
*I felt as familiar with all this as if it was my own homeland.*
*Anyway, the surroundings were the least of my concerns now – I was trying hard to find the right words to start a conversation.*
*We'd just been sitting there, probably for a couple of hours. But all attempts to strike up a conversation had ended with one-word answers.*
You: "Forget about what I said before! I don't want to make excuses or say that it's not true. It's just now – the most important thing to me is you."
Slavya: "I understand."
*She looked at me carefully.*
You: "Even if I sometimes act the wrong way and talk nonsense… Regardless, the main thing for me now is to be with you! And it always will be."
You: "I understand that I acted too recklessly and planned stupid ventures. But we can try to make everything right. Together! You and me!"
*Slavya was still gazing at me.*
Slavya: "Do you realise that it will be difficult? That you can’t just run blindly into the dark? Because then there will be so many problems that we won't be able to solve."
You: "Yes, I understand that now! But for you, I am prepared for anything."
*She didn't say a word but just kissed me gently and put her head on my shoulder.*
*It definitely meant 'yes'!*
*I didn't want to bother her anymore – let her sleep.*
*The point is that Slavya finally understood me, understood what she means to me. She realised that I'll do anything for the her sake.*
*And even if I'm overreacting or deciding too early, she's ready to put me on the right path. The path that we'll walk together!*
*...*
*Night started to claim its rights and the bus settled down to sleep.*
*At first I tried to fight it, but is there any use in enduring and wasting my efforts when the future had finally become crystal clear for me?*
*My eyes shut just for a moment...*
*A sharp pain throbbed through my entire body.*
*I felt it especially sharply in my temples.*
*It feels like they're ready to shatter into a thousand little pieces, giving the wind free access to my empty head.*
*Probably I would not have been able to stand even five minutes of such torture if I hadn't opened my eyes in time.*
*I was somewhere, it was impossible to tell precisely where.*
*My mind was clouded in mist, my thoughts were confused.*
*The moment between the unconscious and conscious states when you vividly remember your dreams.*
*I was going somewhere by bus and was about to doze off when suddenly a girl came up to me and began to speak quickly.*
*I couldn't understand a word, but the girl looked very upset.*
*I failed to understand what she needed from me.*
*Time passed, and she kept talking on and on.*
*It was getting really annoying.*
*I wanted to ask her to cut it out or at least calm down a bit, but I failed – either because I didn't manage to say anything or because my words didn't reach her.*
*I couldn't even see her face. I was simply listening and staring, staring and listening...*
*Perhaps it wasn't important for me then.*
*Surely you would not try to remember what a mosquito disturbing your sleep looks like.*
*Surely you wouldn’t manage to recall the frequency of its flapping wings or the inclination of its proboscis after that.*
*And this girl is just one of millions of voices that disturb you from concentrating, from thinking, from falling asleep...*
*The louder her voice grew, the harder it got for me to catch her words.*
*The bus cabin, the seats worn by time, the uneven floor, the rusty ceiling, the cracked glass of the windscreen – everything was floating away. Along with her.*
*And then I felt unique sense of relief.*
*It didn't matter how real the bus and the girl had been – it was nothing but a bug to me.*
*And here I am, hanging in total emptiness and falling inside a dream...*
*Wow, dreams can be really something... Not quite a nightmare, yet definitely not something pleasant.*
*I got up, rubbed my face to get back to reality, gave a loud yawn and prepared to clean myself up.*
*It was a really grey morning.*
*Unable to find my hygiene kit on the night stand, I concluded that I could manage without it.*
*It was hard to get dressed – my hands were trembling like hell.*
*I looked at my reflection in the mirror and checked out my two-week stubble.*
*Well, perhaps Olga Dmitrievna has a razor...*
*It was only when I went outside that I suddenly understood that I'm not in a pioneer camp!*
*I'm back in my apartment!*
*And I've just come out of my room into a passageway, not out of the cabin!*
*I was overwhelmed with surprise, with dismay, with fear, even with terror.*
*But how?!*
*I sat down on the bed and buried my face into my hands, trying to remember the chain of yesterday's events.*
*Yeah, the bus, the last day of the term.*
*Yeah, I fell asleep... and woke up back 'home'.*
*Well, to some degree, it might even seem quite logical.*
*It seemed that the initial astonishment has worn off during the first few seconds.*
*After all, the fact that I came back like this after a week-long absence is no stranger than my sudden appearance at some pioneer camp of the eighties in the first place.*
*The events of the last two days flashed before my eyes in an instant.*
*That mysterious pioneer, his words...*
*But how did I manage to get back to reality then?*
*According to him, I was going to be stuck there forever, as there's no exit!*
*On the other hand, I wasn't alone.*
*That pioneer at the bus stop and the mystery voice emphasized the contrary – that the exit exists.*
*Does that mean I found it, I managed to get out of the endless loop? But how?*
*Nevertheless, I wasn't sure whether I should rejoice or grieve – over the last week I'd kind of gotten used to the everlasting inner monologue, the search for answers and the in-depth analysis of everything, so I simply couldn't accept this fact as it was, without figuring out what exactly happened to me.*
*Sure, he told me that I'm the only one who has observed the existance of other guys like me during their very first loop, but does that mean anything?*
*Anyway, all his theories and ideas instantly collapsed like a house of cards!*
*Now I had to decide how I should react.*
*Of course, I should rejoice! After all, I'm back to the real world.*
*Maybe the last seven days were just a dream.*
*Indeed, there's absolutely no evidence that I really was there.*
*I don't see my pioneer uniform anywhere, I look my age, just like I did before. My phone is on the table, fully charged.*
*But one can't deceive one's own memory. One can't live through such terrifically real experiences in a dream.*
*I still remember the events of the whole week in great detail.*
*Perhaps I was in a coma all this time?*
*An ironic laugh escaped my lips.*
*Nah, that's not an option either.*
*Then... all's well that ends well?*
*The last few hours in the camp flashed through my mind.*
*Indeed, I wasn’t hoping to get out – either from that camp or from that reality – and I was pretty much ready to another week. And another, and another one...*
*I'd accepted my role, I'd reconciled with my destiny.*
*And what was I supposed to do after all the stuff that happened?*
*I heaved a doomed sigh, got up from my bed with considerable effort, and went to my computer.*
*That's weird, but according to it, only 14 hours have passed since my disappearance from this world, not a whole week.*
*A new message in the instant messenger...*
*Hi Semyon! Yesterday... It was legendary! CU L8R! :)))*
*My college friend. It was him who invited me to that party with the rest of his college friends that I was going to attend.*
*Suddenly, all my senses came back to me: the headache, the dizziness, all the symptoms of a hangover.*
*It looks like I indeed attended that party yesterday. And I was partying hard... So, there was no pioneer camp? But then, where did all these memories, emotions and feelings come from?*
*All of this was so incomprehensible that I became enraged. I began cursing foully, trying to tear my hair out and hammering on the keyboard with my fists. I didn't return to a normal state until there were no keys left on it.*
*Why should I care so much? Nobody worries when a dream or a hallucination ends. Moreover, people are usually glad that it happens. Was I really that prepared to stay there that my return to reality became so undesirable for me?*
*And then a simple and obvious thought crossed my mind. Perhaps I'm just going insane...*
*Indeed, madmen frequently have visions which they perceive as reality. Besides, I had all the symptons of insanity: I never leave the four walls of my prison, I never socialise, I have lots of psychological problems. Well, that explains a lot!*
*My dark, nervous laughter echoed in the room.*
*Guess it’s the right time for me to visit a therapist. Or rather a psychiatrist. Or should I just surrender myself at the asylum?*
You: "A horse! A horse! Half my kingdom for a horse!"
*I cried at the top of my lungs between bouts of my manic laughter.*
You: "Dispute not with her! She is a lunatic!"
*The racket my neighbours made on the wall calmed me down somehow.*
*If I'm tripping that bad, it looks like only a lobotomy could help me.*
*...*
*I just sat completely freaked out for several hours. Doing nothing, thinking nothing, just staring at the monitor, long since gone into sleep mode. Finally I moved the mouse and opened a few tabs in the browser. So, what's new? F5, F5!*
*As if the events of the past week had never happened. Come on, do you have to grieve for a hallucination? Was it real? Sure. Lots of memories? Sure. Looks true enough? By all means, yes! Any proof? Nope.*
*The verdict is clear, as is my future course. I have long suspected that my current lifestyle wasn't doing me any good. I wasn't ready for such an unusual event, but so what? I'll have to be more prepared for my next trip.*

Message: "Hi, how are you doing?"
*Sure, quite an original way to start a conversation.*
You: "Doing fine."
*The contact's profile was completely empty. Not even a nickname – just a nine-digit number. You can't guess what kind of person is on the other end by just looking at a number, can you? Sure, someday it will be all different. Unified digital identifiers instead of names, a couple of symbols for a biography, several bytes of personality and three and a half bits of feelings...*
Message: "Get home safely?"
*Probably someone from yesterday's party.*
You: "Seems like it."
Message: "You do remember everything I told you yesterday, right?"

Message: "I see."
