*My whole body was covered in bruises and scratches, but I could still walk.*
Lena: "Ouch..."
*Lena cried out behind me.*
You: "What is it?"
Lena: "I think I sprained my ankle..."
*I was honestly expecting the next line to be something clichéd like 'leave me behind, I'll only be a burden', but of course she could never say that.*
You: "Okay, lean on me."
*I went over to Lena and offered her my shoulder.*
*Soon enough the stone walls gave way to wooden ones and we ended up in some sort of a mine.*
Masha: "Let's have a break!"
*Masha begged.*
*I carefully lowered Lena to the ground and sat down nearby.*
You: "Well, at least those monsters are nowhere to be seen..."
Masha: "But for how long...?"
*I sighed heavily and closed my eyes.*
Masha: "What do you think is going on here?"
*Masha's voice was trembling but she still sounded more or less confident.*
*Looks like she's so exhausted and devastated that there's just no strength left for fear.*
You: "I don't know... And honestly, I don't want to know!"
Masha: "But we're... gonna get out?"
You: "Definitely!"
*I couldn't see her face but I was sure that she's smiling.*
*Suddenly the flashlight blinked and went out.*
*I hit it with my palm several times, the mine's walls lit up with a dim light once again, and I immediately realised that something was wrong!*
*Lena was nowhere to be found!*
You: "Lena's disappeared..."
*I whispered.*
Masha: "What?"
*Masha grabbed me by the sleeve and stared at the spot where Lena had been sitting a moment ago.*
Masha: "How? But how?"
*She started to cry quietly.*
Masha: "We will die... We will definitely die!"
*I also very much wanted to burst into tears.*
*Darkness surrounded us all around, closing in.*
*The flashlight was gradually dying - and with it, our chances of survival.*
You: "Get up, time to go. The battery will die soon."
*A couple of minutes later we came to a fork.*
You: "What the hell, is this some kind of labyrinth too?"
*I hissed under my breath.*
Masha: "Let's go back, maybe?"
You: "No. No way."
*Masha pressed against me even harder*
Masha: "Where to, then?"
You: "I don't know..."
*But we had to choose anyway.*
*And I decided to go right.*
*Soon we came to another fork.*
Masha: "Where to now?"
You: "Let's stick to the direction we chose before..."
*We had been wandering for too long, we had neither strength nor will left to move on.*
*I was so terribly thirsty I was ready to lick the moisture from off the walls.*
Masha: "Let's sit... just a little... a bit..."
You: "We can't! We must keep going!"
Masha: "But just a minute..."
*Masha begged in anguish.*
You: "Fine..."
*She lowered her head onto my shoulder.*
*The flashlight was blinking more and more often, so I decided to turn it off for now, to save the battery.*
Masha: "This is it..."
*...*
*I don't know how much time passed.*
*I desperately wanted to sleep. My eyes were closing by themselves.*
*How did we first meet...*
*That was so long way ago...*
You: "Do you remember...?"
*I asked in a whisper.*
Masha: "What...?"
*Masha's voice was trembling.*
You: "How we met..."
Masha: "Yes..."
*She tried to laugh but immediately began to cough*
Masha: "I will sleep for a while, okay?"
You: "Just for a while or you will sleep through the whole day again..."
Masha: "Well, but you will wake me up...?"
You: "Of course..."
*I kissed her and closed my eyes.*
*Oblivion was getting closer but I didn't care – I was transported back in time to that very day...*
*...*
*...*
*My whole body was aching...*
*Perhaps my brain couldn't rest peacefully because it was distracted by thousands of signals from my nerve endings.*
*Somehow I rose and woke up Masha.*
*After all, we were planning to survive...*
*How long have I been in this mine...?*
*Fork after fork, tunnel after tunnel.*
*Masha was whispering something all the time.*
*'To the left'… 'To the right'… 'To the left'… 'To the right'…*
*It seems that I won't be able to handle even one more turn...*
*But suddenly the flashlight highlighted a tight passage in the darkness and soon we found ourselves in an open chamber.*
Masha: "Look!"
*Masha was pointing somewhere into the darkness.*
*I flashed the light there and saw a neckerchief lying on the ground.*
Masha: "This is not..."
You: "No! Let's go!"
*At last we got out of the labyrinth and found ourselves in a small room.*
*There were broken bottles all over the floor, pipes stretched along the walls and at the end of them were rusted valves. A mess of graffiti was scrawled all over the walls.*
You: "At least it's a change of scenery."
*I sighed.*
*The flashlight had almost died and I had to shake it up every 10 seconds to slightly recover the battery.*
*Exhausted, Masha dropped to the floor.*
You: "We can't stop. I'm sure there is the exit somewhere here!"
Masha: "How do you know...?"
*I looked at her.*
*She obviously had no energy anymore – Masha was struggling with her exhaustion and could lose consciousness any second.*
You: "I just know it!"
*I smiled, trying to look encouraging.*
Masha: "Well... If so..."
*She leaned against the wall and stood up hardly.*
You: "Sit here for now, I will see what is further on..."
Masha: "I'm afraid..."
*Masha trembled.*
You: "I'm not going far!"
*She raised her eyes to me, full of hope, and nodded almost imperceptibly.*
*I looked around and noticed a heavy iron door.*
*My attempts to open it came to nothing – it was completely rusted shut.*
*Ugh, I wish that pipe was here now...*
*But there was no other choice!*
*I braced my leg on the wall and threw all my weight against the handle. My muscles bulged, my forehead was awash with sweat, my vision darkened...*
*But the door didn't budge, just gave off a hollow rattle.*
You: "It's alright, wait a second..."
*I shouted over to Masha, gasping for breath.*
You: "I need to find some kind of stick."
*I ran over to Masha, bent down and smiled.*
You: "There is definitely an exit behind this door!"
Masha: "Huh..."
*She looked at me wearily.*
*I ran out of room and began to scour the mine in search of something suitable.*
*The flashlight was about to die and, having blinked its last, it finally went out...*
*I panicked and began to blunder around, trying to find the way back.*
*However I kept running into walls and couldn't remember at all how I got here.*
You: "Masha! Masha!"
*I screamed, hoping that she would hear me.*
*Suddenly a sound came out from behind me, a light appeared and my shadow appeared on the ground, stretching far off into the darkness.*
*I was rooted to the spot by fear.*
*I heard a seemingly familiar voice.*
Lena: "What’s wrong Semyon, got lost?"
*I slowly turned around and saw Lena holding a flaming torch in her hand.*
*Her face was disfigured by an inhuman grin.*
Lena: "I've come for you!"
*This was the same Lena that I saw at the square last evening.*
*The same as in Olga Dmitrievna's cabin.*
*That was Lena, and at the same time, not Lena...*
*This creature was more like those 'Ulyanas'...*
Lena: "I am coming for you!"
You: "You... you... who are you?"
*I squeezed out.*
Lena: "It's Lena! Don’t you recognise me?"
*She burst into devilish laughter.*
Lena: "You completely forgot about me while having fun with them?"
You: "I...I..."
*Words stuck in my throat.*
Lena: "It's alright! There is nobody left now! Just the two of us!"
You: "So you... you did everything...?"
Lena: "Bingo! Not everything of course..."
*For a second her face became guilty, but then she grinned again.*
Lena: "Slavya was first! She was always so annoying! She was Ms. Reliability! Diligent, hard-working, always everywhere, agreeing with everyone! Yuck! Boy did she scream when I was tearing off her arms, huh? It's a pity you didn't get to see it all!"
*Her mouth began to tremble, her saliva dripped out of it and her eyes rolled up.*
Lena: "And then Alisa... 'Everybody is annoying me, I don't need anyone'! Now she's hanging peacefully alone on a tree! However, it wasn't easy to lift her up there, but it had a much greater effect! How you all screamed, huh? Like pigs in a slaughterhouse!"
*Lena's face was twisted by a grin of sick pleasure.*
Lena: "Alright, just that bitch Miku left to deal with – and then it's over!"
*She produced a giant cleaver covered with blood from behind her back.*
Lena: "Well, actually..."
*It seemed to me that she was lost in thought.*
Lena: "I don't know what that crap in the form of Ulyana was... Her and the other pioneers weren't killed by me... But does it really matter now?"
*She shook the torch and it flared out in a second.*
Lena: "Wait here, I will be quick!"
*Her devilish laughter came from behind me.*
*That means she went after Masha!*
*I must do something quickly!*
*But I have absolutely no idea which way to run – the darkness completely disoriented me.*
*Screw it!*
*I ran the way I assumed Lena went.*
*After only a short way I painfully smashed into a wall. I turned around, trying to move slowly, but I stumbled over another obstacle, fell down and screamed in pain.*
*Trying to rise, I realised that I couldn't put any weight on my left leg. Seems like I twisted it...*
*I tried to crawl but it worked out badly – the whole mine floor was covered with sharp stones, rusty rails and broken boards.*
*After only a short way my arms were torn to bleeding pieces of meat and my eyes couldn't be opened because of the dust and sand.*
*I fumbled in my pockets and pulled out the matchbox.*
*I tried to light a match with my shaking hands, but couldn't get them to light.*
You: "Calm down... Calm down..."
*I muttered.*
*At last, after the fifth try, the mine was lightened by a dim light.*
*I quickly oriented myself and worked out which way I have to run.*
*It seemed to me that only few seconds passed before I found myself in the room where I'd left Masha.*
*The last match went out, but I just had enough time to see Lena, raising her cleaver above Masha.*
*I rushed towards them, screaming, and dived forward.*
*My hands suddenly collided with something. I fell to the ground and began smashing everything around me.*
*Most of my punches didn't hit the mark but then my hands met something soft. I heard a moan and dead silence set in.*
*I rolled onto my back and started breathing heavily, inhaling the dry air greedily.*
You: "Masha?"
*I called.*
*I heard quiet sobs.*
You: "Are you still alive?"
Masha: "Yes..."
*She whispered.*
You: "Did she get you?"
Masha: "No..."
*I began to fumble in the darkness and soon found the torch and a lighter.*
*Shapeless shadows began to dance on the walls and I saw Lena's body sprawled on the floor. She seemed to be alive.*
*I was going to finish her.*
Masha: "Don't..."
*Masha crawled right over to me and grabbed my leg.*
You: "But we can’t just..."
Masha: "You don't need to..."
*Of course Lena wasn't to blame for everything...*
*But she's the devil incarnate!*
*There's no way we can let a human like her (if she can still be called a human) live.*
*But when I looked at Masha I realised that I can't... I just can't...*
*I took up the cleaver from the floor, and twisting it in my hands, I decided that it would make a perfect crowbar.*
*Going over to the door, I jammed it into the wheel and pulled on it as hard as I could.*
*The door creaked and opened. Fresh air streamed into the room.*
You: "We're saved..."
*I returned to Masha, helped her to get up and we left the room, leaving Lena lying unconscious.*
*Beyond the door there was a short corridor with a ladder at the end of it, which led up to a grating.*
*I climbed up and pulled on it with all my strength.*
*The grating fell down with a crash and we climbed out.*
*I fell to the grass, exhausted, and looked around.*
*Again this square, again this camp...*
*The bright red dawn was breaking in the east, burning the tops of a distant forest.*
*The last stars winked at me, unaware of everything that had happened here, in this hell.*
*Masha rested her head on my shoulder and pointed up to the sky with a trembling hand.*
Masha: "I wish we were there..."
*Though we got out of dungeon, nothing is over – crowds of zombie Ulyanas are wandering through the camp, an insane Lena is lying underneath and heaven knows how much more devilry we will encounter here.*
Masha: "I really want to sleep..."
*I didn't know how to answer her.*
*Because I don't know where to run, don't know where can we be safe.*
*Don't know how to return to our world...*
You: "Sleep..."
*I patted Masha's head.*
Masha: "Listen, this would make a great script for a film!"
*She laughed out loud.*
*I looked at her in horror.*
*Masha was smiling.*
*But her smile wasn't diabolical like that one of Lena's. It was pure, honest, maybe even childish.*
*All her exhaustion had gone away and her eyes were shining with a cheerful spark.*
You: "What... happened to you?"
*I could hardly speak.*
Masha: "Everything is fine!"
*She lay down on my shoulder again.*
Masha: "That was the last scene!"
*Suddenly I felt my strength leaving me.*
*My vision darkened, my consciousness began to float away somewhere.*
*I was lying in silence and only the sound of Masha's breath could be heard.*
*Not the grasshoppers' chirping – like all of them had died at last – but only Masha's steady breathing.*
*And her smile...*
*...*
*...*
*I struggled to open my eyes.*
*Bright moonlight reflected on the water, cheerfully skipping on the waves, a light night breeze was blowing and somewhere far away an owl was hooting.*
*I looked at Masha who peacefully slept nearby, covered by my shirt.*
*What a dream...*
*My mobile phone dimly showed the time – 3 a.m.!*
*We'd better go to bed, or tomorrow Olga Dmitrievna will make us...*
*I'd just decided to wake Masha up, but I suddenly noticed an opened script and a pen next to her.*
*I quickly went through several pages and was horrified – it was completely identical to what happened in my dream!*
*Bile rose in my throat and my eyes darkened.*
*Masha rolled over, opened her eyes and looked at me.*
Masha: "You awake?"
You: "Did you… write this?"
*I asked, thick-tongued.*
Masha: "Yes, what’s wrong?"
*I didn't know how to answer. I just couldn’t understand what was going on.*
Masha: "You were sleeping so cutely that I didn't want to wake you. And the grasshoppers were chirping so loudly... So I..."
*She smiled.*
You: "Wait, but we are here now?! I mean, we're not pioneers, we are filming here and all that kind of stuff, aren't we?"
Masha: "Yes, of course we are."
*Masha looked at me uncomprehendingly.*
*Maybe I woke up, read what she wrote and then fell asleep again...?*
Masha: "You're drenched with sweat!"
*She fumbled in the pockets of the pioneer uniform lying next to her and gave me a handkerchief. A typical Russian handkerchief embroidered with colorful flowers.*
*I took it and suddenly felt a surge of warmth. The same warmth you feel when someone dear to your heart gives you a present.*
Masha: "Shall we go?"
*Masha started getting dressed.*
You: "Yes... let's go..."
*I barely stood up and went down to the river.*
*Cold water revived me and that dream stopped seeming so real.*
*After all, it was just a dream, wasn't it?*
*On our way back Masha held my hand and chattered about everything non-stop.*
*We came to the square.*
Masha: "I hope those creatures will let me sleep at least tonight..."
*She said thoughtfully.*
You: "Who?"
Masha: "The grasshoppers!"
You: "Ah... yes, that’d be great..."
Masha: "Well, I'll go..."
*She looked at me keenly, turned around and was about to leave.*
You: "Wait!"
*I grabbed her hand, pulled her towards me and kissed her hard.*
*Because sometimes, a dream is just a dream...*
*And reality is reality...*
*It's interesting, how seemingly simple events can affect a person.*
*For example, there are such widespread occurences of OCD (obsessive compulsive disorder) among children, where when you walk on the road you have to step on the tiles precisely, avoiding the cracks.*
*It seems like nothing special, but if one doesn’t get rid of it in time – just forgetting, or forcing oneself to step over the tiles – it could become a really big problem in the future. For instance, one will only stare down and will get hit by a car…*
*I never had anything like OCD, but minor events in my life often led to major troubles.*
*Really, what's wrong with meeting a strange girl with cat's ears in a pioneer camp on the edge of time and space, or possibly even between the worlds...?*
*Doesn’t seem like a big deal.*
*Although, perhaps I just got used to thinking that nothing really existed for me before this week. There was only this camp and this life.*
*That's why something like a cat-girl was just par for the course in this wonderland.*
*She's just another character in this play, neither better nor worse than any other.*
*But somewhere deep in my soul I knew that wasn’t so.*
*All the camp inhabitants seemed normal, sometimes even too normal, with absolutely nothing remarkable about them.*
*Geez! You could even say that my life here was simply boring.*
*And now…*
*My head was about to burst with thoughts, so I opened my eyes and jumped out of bed.*
*The camp leader's cabin was the same as usual.*
*Outside the window a bird monotonously cheeped, trying to burst the capillaries in my eyes with her singing.*
*The clock showed 11 a.m.*
*Why didn't Olga Dmitrievna wake me up? Though who cares…*
*I slept enough at least.*
*However I didn't feel like I'd fully recovered.*
*The whole world was seemingly laughing at me – the bright sun outside, the lightly-blowing breeze, gently whispering to the crowns of the trees, and this nasty bird had brought some fellows with her, obviously trying to ruin my mental stability.*
*The water from the washstands was ice-cold as usual.*
*While washing my face, I realised that I forgot my toothbrush, tooth powder and towel in the cabin…*
*Strange I didn't forget my head…*
*I couldn’t imagine a worse start to the day.*
*At that moment I thought it was the worst day of all that I have spent in this camp.*
*Although there weren't a lot of choices: little more than a hundred hours, not enough time to get the full image of a new home.*
*Home… This word struck my mind painfully.*
*Do I have to stay here forever?! But why, how, what for...?*
*I helplessly sat on the grass and buried my face in hands.*
*Suddenly I remembered that girl. I wonder how many more fantastic characters I will meet here?*
Pioneer: "A wonderful day, isn't it?"
*I couldn't even be bothered to raise my head.*
You: "Yeah, couldn’t be any better…"
*I answered, keeping the same pose.*
Pioneer: "Why so sarcastic?"
You: "Sarcastic?"
*I was surprised and looked up, but there was nobody nearby.*
*Is it my imagination? No, I heard that for sure…*
*Maybe I'm losing my mind?*
*That underground mine, Shurik, voices, the cat-girl, more voices… Is there anything here I can be sure about?!*
*I punched the washstand painfully hard and immediately jumped up, holding my hand and cursing.*
You: "Damn it!"
*Suddenly, somebody walked out of the bushes in front of me. Or something…*
Yulya: "Hi!"
*It was the girl from yesterday.*
You: "Hi…"
*I didn't know what to say.*
You: "I didn't know what to expect from her."
*She's probably a hell beast and came here to end my life. That is, of course, only if it hasn't ended already…*
*The cat-girl stared at me.*
Yulya: "It hurts?"
*She looked at my hand.*
You: "Yes…"
*I answered timidly.*
Yulya: "Then why?"
You: "Why what?"
Yulya: "Why did you punch it?"
You: "Cause I was angry…"
*I was completely unsure how I should talk to her.*
*Perhaps one wrong word, phrase, or gesture could be fatal for me.*
Yulya: "Angry at who?"
*But the girl wasn't showing any signs of aggression – it seemed that she was just wondering what is happening.*
You: "At myself."
Yulya: "I see."
*She smiled faintly.*
You: "Listen… I don't know how should I put it, but I must ask…"
*I kept silent for a moment, gathering myself.*
You: "Who are you...?"
*The girl looked at me blankly.*
Yulya: "I am me, of course!"
*She said confidently.*
You: "No, no doubt about that, but… How should I say it…? You just don't meet a human with cat ears and a tail every day, you know."
*The cat-girl carefully examined the aforementioned parts of the body and asked:*
Yulya: "Why?"
*I was totally confused.*
*If in the first few minutes I thought it was necessary to be afraid, to be very careful, now she seems more like a good spirit being than a hostile monster.*
You: "Because in my world…"
*I was absolutely convinced that I shouldn't hide anything from her.*
You: "In my world, this only happens in fairy tales."
Yulya: "What is a fairy tale?"
You: "Well… It’s a story which cannot happen in reality."
Yulya: "So I don't really exist?"
*The girl laughed.*
You: "I'm not even sure that I exist…"
Yulya: "But I can touch you – so you exist."
*Just thinking about the fact that she will touch me, I felt uncomfortable.*
You: "Well, let's say I exist, yes…"
*I stepped back.*
Yulya: "Goody-goody!"
*The girl smiled and waved her tail.*
*There was an awkward silence.*
*All the time I'd spent in this camp, I lived as if in a dream.*
*Sometimes when you sleep you realise that everything that happens in your brain is just a figment of your imagination, and you need just to wish…*
*I'd thought so for the last five days, this thought constantly existed somewhere deep in my soul.*
*However, it seems that everything is happening in reality. At least, I couldn't just wake up…*
You: "I just want to understand…"
Yulya: "What?"
*The girl was still smiling.*
You: "How I got here... And how to get out of here."
*Suddenly, I heard voices by the road side, so I turned around.*
*Slavya and Zhenya were slowly approaching the washstands.*
You: "And you…"
*But the girl had disappeared.*
You: "Did you see, did you see it?!"
*Like I just needed someone to confirm the existence of this creature. Then I can convince myself that I'm not going crazy.*
*What an irony – to go mad while in the Land of Oz... Though just arriving here is already a ticket to the loony bin.*
*And even if I wake up right now, I still wouldn’t be sure that it was all a dream.*
Slavya: "See what?"
*The girls looked at me blankly.*
You: "Anyone beside me…"
*I could hardly speak.*
*So, an illusion, huh? So I’m actually…*
Zhenya: "You should get your head examined, seriously!"
*Zhenya snorted and passed by. Slavya smiled apologetically and hurried after her.*
*So it’s all that simple...?*
*I wanted just one thing now – for someone in this nightmare to believe that I'm still sane!*
*This whole camp and its pioneers did not seem as real as yesterday.*
*In the end, less than a week ago I lived the completely normal life of an ordinary man of his time, and now…*
*Maybe everything that happened made me think that all is going the way it should? That it's normal – just to be, to exist here.*
*And now the last leftovers of my common sense desperately clung to this catlike girl with the ears, trying to prove to the locals that I'm not crazy.*
*See – you don't exist, you! It's me in your tale, not you in mine…*
*My head was about to explode.*
*If not for the signal for dinner, perhaps I would have run to the library, searching for medical books with lobotomy instructions.*
*The canteen was crowded as usual. Some things never change.*
*For the first time I looked at all the local pioneers from a slightly different angle.*
*Indeed, why is everything so... correct?*
*As if someone created this pioneer camp by carefully compiling material from the internet, without bothering to visit such a place himself.*
*It was just like an old Soviet movie – the strict camp leader, the exemplary pioneers. Even Ulyana. And even Alisa…*
*All within the normal range.*
*So where does that strange girl come from?*
*She seemed like a smear of paint that just happened to be on the picture due to the shaky hands of a sloppy restorer.*
*Electronik suddenly sat beside me.*
Sergei: "Hey there!"
*He smirked.*
You: "Hey…"
Sergei: "What are you thinking about?"
You: "Just…"
*There was absolutely nothing wrong with speaking openly to anyone. Not any more…*
You: "Did you happen to see anyone strange here?"
Sergei: "Strange?"
You: "Well… Not quite human."
Sergei: "I don't really understand."
*Electronik laughed.*
You: "A girl with cat's ears and a tail."
*I said shortly.*
Sergei: "A girl with ears and a tail..?"
*He began to think.*
Sergei: "How do you know about her?"
You: "Well, let’s assume I saw her."
*This conversation was starting to get interesting.*
Sergei: "Let’s assume, or you actually did?"
You: "Is it really so important?"
*Elektronik stared at me seriously.*
Sergei: "There is a legend here about a cat-girl. She steals food, small bits and pieces of stuff and avoids people."
You: "Really. A legend?"
You: "So what does this girl look like?"
Sergei: "I never saw her myself. They say that she has a tail and ears, as you described."
You: "What else?"
Sergei: "Well, this legend is old, and I don't know much about it."
You: "Who do you think knows more?"
Sergei: "Ask Olga Dmitrievna – she’s been in this camp many times, even before she became a camp leader."
You: "Alright, thanks."
*I stood up and went to find the camp leader.*
*I bet she decided to take a nap after lunch.*
*Perhaps Olga Dmitrievna was the only element that was somewhat out of place in the picture of an ideal camp – she certainly was not a role model camp leader.*
*I opened the door and confidently entered the cabin.*
*And indeed, she was lying on the bed and reading a book, as expected.*
Olga: "Semyon… Slacking again?"
You: "Actually, yes, but anyway. I wanted to ask you something."
*She stared at me, and I hesitated a little.*
*Maybe I shouldn't be so straightforward about everything?*
*It was like my internal firewall had triggered, and I just could not tell the camp leader that I had seen the cat-girl today.*
*Maybe I got quite used to hinting at something, avoiding straight questions, lying and keeping words back.*
*In just four days! Although, I guess I'd been doing that my whole life…*
You: "Olga Dmitrievna, I was at the dinner… spoke with Elektronik. And he told me a legend about a cat-girl, that supposedly lives here."
You: "He also said that you would know more…"
Olga: "Why do you need to know that?"
*The camp leader gave me a piercing look and stood up.*
You: "Just curious! I like stuff like this!"
*I tried to smile, but it didn't seem to make things any better.*
Olga: "We have a completely normal camp."
*Sure you do! Completely normal! Don't even want to imagine what you'd call 'unusual' – I suppose something with zombies and maniacs.*
*'A Nightmare on Sovyonok Street'…*
You: "Yes, I understand, but... Electronik said that you visited this place before."
Olga: "Yes…"
*The camp leader was thinking about something.*
Olga: "However, there is indeed a legend. That somewhere in the surrounding woods a strange cat-girl lives, sometimes stealing food and small items from cabins. She is afraid of people, and if someone accidentally sees her, she runs away."
*That was quite different from what I saw this morning.*
*That girl was more like watching me, studying, trying to understand, but not afraid at all.*
You: "And you..."
Olga: "Have I seen her?"
*Olga Dmitrievna interrupted me.*
Olga: "No, I haven't, but I was quite close to doing so several times. Bottles, milk, tooth powder, and plenty of other things disappeared from my cabin sometimes. Mysteriously disappeared without a trace."
*I'd completely forgotten about the fact that all the pioneers here do not actually exist, and just listened attentively to the camp leader.*
Olga: "I was curious where this stuff disappeared to before. But in the end, there is no evidence of her existence…"
*She smiled, as if implying that this conversation is over.*
You: "And if there was?"
Olga: "Why are you so interested in this?"
You: "Who wouldn't be interested in stuff like this…?"
*Though I still had many things to rack my brains for.*
Olga: "I don't know..."
*The camp leader thought about something for a second and then returned to her usual Mother-of-all-camps state.*
Olga: "Well, seems like you've decided to become completely laid back! Do something already..."
*She paused and stretched herself in such a way that wrinkles that shouldn’t even be there at her age came out.*
Olga: "Go on... Get down to business!"
*I just sighed and went out.*
*All in all, no-one from among the pioneers has ever seen a cat-eared girl, they'd only heard “legends”.*
*Well, I should probably find her!*
*I'd already recovered from this morning's shock events, and existential thoughts have by now stopped pressuring my brain, so it was possible for me to take a reasonable position, more or less.*
*It was necessary because I still had a lot of questions: how did I get here? For what reason? Why? And where is this 'here'?*
*And the cat girl is the catalyst for it all.*
*But I didn't want to start theorising about parallel worlds, aliens, experiments, and the afterlife again.*
*I was fed up with this after just my first few hours in this camp.*
*Perhaps I just need to put aside the theories and look at the physical reality.*
*Even if I assume that this world exists regardless of my will and I have to live here, my arrival here is inexplicable. It's more worthwhile to concentrate on studying this world and on analysing possible events which may happen to me here.*
*I'll do that until the opposite is proven. Until then let's assume that I'm stuck here. For the long haul, if not forever.*
*The deckchair melodiously squeaked with my every movement, lilac branches tried to strike me in the face and the vile morning birds were silent for a long time, apparently tired of the summer heat.*
*The tree tops seemed like sharp peaks of the high walls of a medieval castle, lost in the boundless woods.*
*And these cabins, the square, Genda's monument, the clubhouse building are just a little village of peasants, huddling near the millennial walls of a grim fortress, hidden in a grove.*
*And all of us here – either people like me or catgirls – are just servants of an evil genius hiding somewhere out there...*
*It would be much easier if the camp was on top of a hill.*
*Because a thousand years ago the best place for a fortification was always somewhere up high.*
*Probably that someone just has nothing to be afraid of. But in that case he would not hide so carefully behind the treetops.*
*I sighed and closed my eyes.*
*My consciousness slowly started to desert me, and soon the whole world faded into darkness.*
*…*
*And again, before my eyes, like an endless carpet – the road, surrounded by woods and fields goes ever on.*
*The bus is going somewhere, leaving behind everything I knew, loved, and hated.*
*An unfamiliar girl is leaning over me and gently whispering something in my ear.*
*I'm actually interested in what she's saying.*
*But I can't hear her – I'm just watching everything from the side and can see everything except her face.*
*And hear everything except her words.*
*And feel everything except my own life...*
*I woke up feeling like I was suffocating and began greedily sucking in air.*
*My breath soon went back to normal and an intolerable thirst came upon me.*
*But... What was that dream all about? And who was that girl?*
*These questions again...*
*Maybe I've already died and gone to hell.*
*Can a human being feel that his life is now over and that he can just move on to the next stage of existance?*
*My head was about to explode due to such cosmic thoughts.*
*What did I do to deserve this? I'm just an ordinary guy, not a philosopher, not a theologist, not a scientist.*
*And I don't want to understand the substance of things, the way of the universe. I'm not asking for any more than just to live my life peacefully, and then doze off into an eternal sleep when everything is over.*
*But no – I'm just trapped here!*
*Tears of frustration welled in my eyes.*
*And why is it always like this?!*
*I started to think that if I give it any more thought I would either understand the Substance of All Things or go insane for good.*
*Ultimately, it all started with a bus – I got in, went to sleep and...*
*There was a girl. Perhaps one of the local pioneers, maybe even that cat-eared one!*
*Well, why not? I can’t rule a single idea out. So I'm here now...*
*My thoughts stopped. Tumbleweed rolled back and forth in my brain, bouncing around the organ which kept my ears from falling off.*
*And... that's all.*
*Now I'm here – in hell, heaven, purgatory, or wherever. Looks like I'm going to spend the rest of eternity in this place...*
*For some reason I fixated on this exact theory.*
*It's strange that I didn`t care about the fact that a spiritual being doesn't have basic human senses – sight, hearing, touch.*
*All in all, at first glance there was nothing different about me from my condition a week ago. Well, except for being a couple of years younger.*
*Then what's so bad about what happened?*
*I might even consider this a second chance!*
*After all, it's not that hard to get a job, I could rent a room in a hostel...*
*I'm seventeen now – I'm still healthy, my brain is in an excellent state, my energy is at its peak. I might try to achieve something...*
*But what had prevented me from doing so before? Was I really that old back then?*
*I jammed like an old rifle, and without outside help I wouldn't have escaped this cycle of self-reflection.*
*Fortunately, Lena soon appeared by the camp leader's cabin.*
Lena: "Hi."
*I raised my eyes reluctantly and stared through her for a few seconds.*
You: "Hello..."
Lena: "Um... I..."
*She stopped, looked away and blushed.*
Lena: "Well, never mind. May I have a seat?"
You: "Sure."
*Lena perched herself on the edge of a deck chair.*
Lena: "What are you thinking about?"
You: "Trying to understand the laws of this world."
Lena: "And how's it going?"
*She asked seriously.*
You: "Not too good... Perhaps they're beyond human comprehension."
Lena: "Then, maybe you shouldn't bother?"
You: "But what should I do? I just have to."
Lena: "Why?"
*And really – why?*
*Does it happen to be of some vital urgency?*
*I didn't really bother thinking about things like that in the past and lived in relative peace.*
*And what has changed so drastically now? I won't think about it now either and will be living in somewhat different conditions, but what's wrong with that?*
*If there is no choice...*
You: "I don't know. It seems that nothing is up to me."
*It looked like Lena wanted to say something, but she didn't.*
You: "And you probably came to see Olga Dmitrievna?"
Lena: "Yes... I mean... no. But, to be honest..."
You: "What is it?"
Lena: "Sometimes I feel that way too."
You: "What do you mean?"
Lena: "That nothing is up to me."
*I looked at her attentively.*
*She was sitting with downcast eyes, nervously toying with a handful of field flowers – they were yellow like the fervent rays of the summer sun.*
Lena: "Well, you know... These flowers, for instance – they were growing just for the sake of it, and then I ripped them out of the ground, and that's all!"
*She was literally about to start crying. It didn't really fit my picture of Lena.*
You: "Well, yeah... To be honest, I really don't know what to say."
Lena: "Well, so are we – we are ripped out, and then..."
*She got up abruptly and rushed in the direction of the square, without saying goodbye.*
*Indeed Lena, like all the other pioneers, seemed to be real. Not a figment of my imagination, not a doll, not an NPC.*
*A few hours ago I was sure that I am the only one who exists here. And possibly that cat-eared girl.*
*I wish I could find her…*
*I'm in a state of something like spiritual deprivation – all my senses are working properly, but I still have a painful need to know why I am here.*
*As if the need for identity, to find my place in this world, to determine its nature, laws and mechanisms had become vital, just like the need for food and rest.*
*It is probably the worst punishment for a human – to have the desire to understand something, but not the ability. To wish to change something but to not have the opportunity. To strive for something, but to be unable to achieve it.*
*I never seriously thought before – why am I in the world, how much time will I spend here, what do I have to do, and what will come next?*
*Now, after encountering this other world, I have nothing left but to think about these.*
*I guess that if it is possible to escape from here, I will return to my quiet life where I don’t have such troubles.*
*But I won’t return...*
*It's so hard to face a task which cannot be completed.*
*If I could choose my fate, I would never agree to this bus, this camp, these girls – I would stay there, in my appartment, in front of the monitor.*
*You can’t demand anything more from a person than he can do.*
*It's better to spend the rest of your life working in the mine than trying to understand something that just won't fit into your head!*
*After all, there is no other way.*
*Of course, it is possible to make a valiant effort, to try not to think, try to accept this reality and to start a new life.*
*But it’s not part of human nature to neglect everything that happens around you.*
*If I was accused of a crime which I had not committed, of course I would try to resist, to prove my innocence.*
*No one would agree to live in jail instead of at home, whatever their home is like.*
*And now it’s me who was thrown from the world I was used to into this 'jail'.*
*Though it is boundless, though there are no walls or bars on the windows, it is still a jail – I did not ask for this, and my only desire for now is to return back home.*
*And the only key out of here is hung just a bit higher than I can reach with a jump.*
*And there is nothing helpful around – no chair, no stool, not even a small stone that could be put under my feet. And no one to help me.*
*A few centimetres. Just a few centimetres separating me from freedom, from realising everything…*
*Maybe it's impossible to return back home, but at least I'll be able to escape from this jail!*
*That is exactly what I've wanted for the last five days…*
*…*
*Night slowly descended onto the camp.*
*Dinner went by without me, and the camp leader stopped several times by the deck chair, trying to tell me something.*
*But I was already in another world – the world of my cage with a key, bound by a Gordian knot to Ariadne's thread.*
*It was not long before the light in the cabin was turned off and crickets started their lamentable whining all around.*
*Somewhere in the distance an owlet was hooting at a speed of 37 hoots per minute*
*I was sitting and rhythmically knocking, trying to accompany him.*
*Suddenly bushes rustled around me, and a squirrel with a nut in its teeth climbed on a tree. It must be hurrying to meet its family…*
*The summer night's charm was as rich as always, but it didn't affect me in any way at all.*
*The mechanisms of my brain and probably my soul were in need of serious maintenance, not just a slapdash repair of the bodywork and a new paint job.*
*I decided to take a walk.*
*Because thinking about it, I've been sitting in this deck chair for almost the whole day. I even took a small nap...*
*Everyone in the camp was tired. The camp was sleeping.*
*The walk between pioneers' cabins, the square with the statue of Genda, the forest path, all that was changing like pictures in a kids’ book. The whole world looked like a picture too.*
*And that is not what I was thinking just yesterday...*
*And the reason for that was a strange girl with animal ears, a cat-girl (though she could just as likely be another animal).*
*It was like there's a defence mechanism that activated just after I appeared here, which didn't let me 'look for answers', or 'get a hold of the situation'.*
*There were always more important things, such as missing the lineup, getting a comfortable seat during lunch, or sneaking away from the camp leader.*
*Anything other than thinking about why am I here and how I can get out. Anything...*
*I sat on a stump and closed my eyes.*
*A million images appeared in my brain at once, and among them was a road, a bus, and that girl. Yes, the girl with animal ears. It was her who was in the bus!*
*I quickly opened my eyes and saw her in front of me.*
*At first it looked like a dream or a hallucination, but a sudden gust of cold wind brought me back to reality.*
*The strange girl was sitting and sprinkling sugar on a mushroom.*
You: "…"
Yulya: "They grow better this way."
*She said with a serious face.*
You: "Who?"
*I uttered with difficulty.*
Yulya: "The mushrooms, who else!"
You: "Mushrooms...?"
Yulya: "Yes, mushrooms."
You: "Why do you need those mushrooms?"
Yulya: "To eat of course! Why else would you need mushrooms!"
*The girl pouted.*
*I just didn't know how to start a conversation with her, because I was sure that the thing which looked like a strange girl with animal ears had brought me here, and making friends with a higher being wouldn't do much good.*
Yulya: "Do you have more sugar?"
*She asked suddenly.*
You: "I don't know... No. Why do you need it?"
Yulya: "What do you mean 'why'!? I told you – for the mushrooms! They grow better that way."
*Despite everything, the girl looked totally normal.*
*Of course, you don't often see a human with animal ears and a tail (and they actually looked real), but apart from that...*
You: "I can bring some..."
*I don't know why I said that, maybe I just wanted to earn her trust.*
*As long as mind-reading wasn't one of her abilities.*
Yulya: "That's alright, no need. There is enough."
You: "Good…"
Yulya: "And?"
You: "What?"
Yulya: "Why did you come?"
*What does she mean? Come to this glade or come to this camp? Or into this life...?*
*My head was about to explode from existential thoughts.*
*Just a little bit more... and everything would become crystal clear.*
*No, 'the answers' and 'the understanding' didn't appear from thin air. The safety device just cut in – caution, doors are closing, no more people will fit in the train, the next stop is...*
*The train was gone and I stayed on the platform without my luggage, wearing a light jacket in the minus-twenty degrees celsius frost.*
You: "I was just having a walk!"
*The words echoed hollowly in my head.*
*I felt like a viking from the middle-ages who stands alone against a hundred enemies. No doubts, no regrets, only an iron will to die hard!*
Yulya: "I see..."
*The girl answered without much interest and went back to her work.*
You: "It was you? Back there in the bus?"
Yulya: "Me..."
*She replied lazily, without tearing herself away from the mushrooms.*
You: "Why did you bring me here?"
Yulya: "I didn't bring you."
You: "Then who?"
Yulya: "I don't know."
You: "But were you in the bus?"
Yulya: "I was."
You: "And?"
Yulya: "What?"
*Yelling at her was dangerous, but I couldn't help it.*
You: "What what?! Answer me!"
Yulya: "Did you ask something?"
*It looks like this conversation doesn't bother her at all.*
You: "Who are you?"
*She looked at me in surprise.*
Yulya: "I am me!"
You: "Okay... Where are you from?"
Yulya: "I don't know... I've always been here."
You: "What do you mean – always? You must have come from somewhere, no?"
Yulya: "I don’t know..."
*I doubted for a moment that this is an omnipotent being before me.*
*Of course this girl is a little extraordinary (to be precise, absolutely extraordinary) and she was with me in the bus then, but maybe she has nothing to do with my arrival here. Anything is possible...*
You: "What do you know?"
Yulya: "I know how to make supplies for winter."
*She smiled with sweetness and ease.*
You: "What supplies?"
Yulya: "Well, you know! For the winter! It could get cold..."
Yulya: "I've never seen the local winters though."
You: "How come you've never seen them, if you've always been here?"
Yulya: "I don’t know."
*She looked at me intently.*
Yulya: "Anyway! You're boring as hell!"
You: "Me!?"
Yulya: "Yes, you."
You: "How do I bore you?"
Yulya: "Your stupid questions."
You: "Stupid...? Well, I was dragged out of my usual world, brought here, and now my questions are stupid?!"
Yulya: "Yes."
*She calmly replied.*
You: "So, what questions would you consider not stupid?"
Yulya: "Where one can get sugar, for example."
You: "In the canteen, where else?! Plenty for you to steal, you're well known for doing that, I've heard."
Yulya: "I do not steal!"
*The animal-eared girl was outraged.*
Yulya: "I am borrowing it! It comes back anyway!"
You: "Comes back or not... I don't care! I want to understand how and why I am here! I want to go back!"
Yulya: "I'm not interested in that."
*The girl stood up and shook herself.*
You: "But I'm interested! If you're not the one to blame for everything, then you must know the answers!"
You: "Someone should know them after all..."
*She looked at me intently and laughed.*
Yulya: "You're funny!"
*I completely lost my temper.*
You: "Stop mocking me! You! I am fed up with you! Why me exactly?! How am I worse than anyone else?! I never asked for anything as “fun” as all this! Leave me alone! I didn’t bother anyone! I didn’t hurt anyone! What did I ever do to you?! Get lost! Let me live in peace!"
*My whole body shivered, the blood pounded in my head like a cannon, everything went dark before my eyes.*
Yulya: "Have you blown off all your steam?"
*She asked quietly.*
*I was about to smash her. At least I'll check if she is flesh and blood.*
Yulya: "Alright, let's go."
You: "Where?"
Yulya: "You'll see."
*The girl gestured me to follow her and went into the depths of the forest.*
*…*
*After some time I started to suspect that we were walking in circles.*
*Finally, I decided to check it out and put a candy wrapper in a noticeable spot.*
*Indeed, we soon passed it again.*
You: "Wait."
*I didn't dare to grab her hand, so I tried to stop her verbally.*
Yulya: "What?"
You: "Where are you taking me?"
Yulya: "I said that you'll see!"
You: "But we're walking in circles."
Yulya: "So what?"
You: "What do you mean 'so what'? You won't get anywhere by walking in circles!"
Yulya: "But you said it yourself, that you were just having a walk..."
*The girl seemed strange, illogical, even arrogant, as if she takes pleasure in mocking me.*
You: "I’m not moving an inch until you explain what is going on."
Yulya: "Okay..."
*She stopped and leaned back against a large tree.*
Yulya: "I was just bored! It's the same old stuff all the time, all the time... But recently lots of new stuff happened and now..."
You: "Now what?"
Yulya: "Now I can talk to you."
*She smiled.*
You: "And you couldn't do it before?"
Yulya: "Well, I certainly could. Maybe..."
You: "So what happened?"
Yulya: "I don’t know."
You: "Then why do you think that something has happened in the first place?"
Yulya: "I've got a feeling."
You: "A feeling, eh...?"
*I gave a helpless sigh.*
*Maybe she's just a lunatic that escaped a local asylum and not an omnipotent being?*
You: "Come on, let's get serious."
Yulya: "Ok, fine!"
*The girl looked at me intently.*
You: "Who are you and what's happening here?"
Yulya: "I don’t know!"
*She answered with the same expression on her face.*
You: "And who knows?"
Yulya: "I don’t know!"
You: "Alright. I'm going to sleep."
*I had no strength to talk about it, to listen to her nonsense, to walk in circles in the forest.*
*Even if she knows the answers and she can return me to the usual world and all, not today. Just enough for today!*
*If I stay here one more second, there won’t be anyone left to return.*
Yulya: "Good night."
*The girl said nicely.*
You: "That's all?"
Yulya: "What else do you want? You're going to sleep."
*She's right...*
You: "Okay. Do you at least have a name?"
Yulya: "Name?"
You: "Yes, a name!"
Yulya: "I don’t know…"
You: "And who knows?"
Yulya: "I don't know!"
You: "Okay. And what should I call you then?"
Yulya: "I don’t know…"
You: "But a person... every single thing in the world should have a name, there's no other way..."
*She looked at me uncomprehendingly.*
You: "Alright then, you will be Yulya!"
Yulya: "Yulya..."
*I don't know why I chose that name. Maybe it was just the first thing that came to my mind.*
Yulya: "Fine."
*She smiled merrily.*
Yulya: "And now I have to go!"
*The girl flicked her ears and disappeared into the forest.*
*I slowly dragged my feet back to the camp.*
*Now it looked like I was in some sort of tragicomedy.*
*The higher beings cannot be idiots with the developmental level of a kindergartener, can they?*
*Though it is possible they don't perceive the world the same way we do...*
*I was so exhausted. I couldn't fully comprehend everything that had happend to me recently.*
*The answers could be right before me, I just need to stretch out my arm. It could be that saving stool, which would help me to reach the key.*
*And how could I be so calm in such a situation?*
*Maybe I’m just tired... Dead tired.*
*Olga Dmitrievna waited for me on the doorstep of her cabin.*
Olga: "At last! And where were you wandering in the dead of night?"
*I looked hard at the camp leader.*
*I wonder, is she real? I don’t have a single doubt about that girl, Yulya. She may not be a human, but she exists.*
*And what about Olga Dmitrievna, the other pioneers?*
You: "You know, I saw that cat-girl."
Olga: "Sure, of course..."
*She chuckled.*
You: "Well, you don't have to believe me if you dont want to."
Olga: "I don't want to and I don't believe you!"
You: "It's your choice."
*I said in a tired voice and pushed my way into the cabin.*
Olga: "Semyon, tomorrow..."
*I didn't hear the rest of her words.*
*There was only one thing to understand – whether anything is up to me or not.*
*Should I keep desperately reaching for that key, or is the cat-girl the answer I've been looking for?*
*Maybe the only thing left to do is to understand?*
*No one ever said that the clue will be written straightforwardly in your own language!*
*Though maybe I always knew those 'answers' and I just had to comprehend their meaning...?*
*What if everything is not real and I am just dreaming?*
*What if I just imagined everything about 'finding the answers', about 'understanding them'?*
*Maybe there is no cage, no jail, and the key has already been hung up from the burned-out lamp in my room, which has turned into a pioneer camp, inhabited by unreal but very alive people, who seem so understandable and so precious.*
*Well, no... I am not a wizard, not an oracle, not a God...*
*Voltaire once said: 'Illusion is the first of all pleasures'. Maybe my most successful skill was my illusions.*
*Lines of thoughts connected one by one, ready to keep it going until morning, but the safety device worked again and unplugged the whole system, instead of reformatting my brain like last time.*
*I was woken up by a hellish noise in my head. It turned out to be the alarm clock.*
*Having found its button with difficulty, I turned it off.*
You: "Olga Dmitrievna, it's 7 o'clock in the morning, why so early?"
*I said in the direction of the other bed, opening my eyes.*
*But there was no one there. The camp leader must have gone somewhere already.*
*I rose with difficulty and looked myself over in the mirror. A common pioneer, nothing more.*
*If someone showed me photos of the local residents with me among them, I'd never recognise myself.*
*The sun shined brightly outside, nature seemed to laugh at me.*
*I slowly walked to the washstands.*
*I met only a few pioneers on my way, who were obviously in a hurry.*
*Strange. Where are they going at such an early hour...?*
*The cold water refreshed me a bit and all the memories of the last few days poured into my head.*
*Well, I should find Yulya and try to be very polite and proper this time.*
*After all, if you can’t even understand a fellow human being when judging him by your own worldview and ideas, then how can you talk to something completely alien?*
*Why should aliens or cat-girls follow the same moral laws and draw the same logical conclusions as I do?*
*They may percieve the universe in a completely different way, and humans are just ants to them.*
*We don't think anything of killing a troublesome mosquito, so why should they pay any attention to me and my small problems?*
*Though it could all be totally the other way around... And Yulya may not be guilty in this...*
*There was a rustle in the nearby bushes and I saw a familiar pair of ears.*
You: "I see you."
*Yulya reluctantly left her hiding place.*
Yulya: "Come on..."
*She snorted, pouting.*
You: "Are you watching me?"
Yulya: "Yes. Is that not allowed?"
You: "Well, it's probably allowed. I wanted to talk to you anyway."
Yulya: "Really? Me too."
You: "What about?"
*I wondered.*
Yulya: "Something strange is happening here..."
You: "Strange? What?"
Yulya: "I don't know... It's just... everyone's behaving differently than usual. Something has happened. First you, then all the others..."
You: "What are you talking about? I don't understand."
Yulya: "I don't know, I just feel it and... when I feel something, it always happens!"
*Yulya looked downcast and even a little afraid.*
*At this time, she totally doesn't look like any kind of higher being.*
You: "Okay, let's investigate it together."
Yulya: "No, no one should see me! Come here in an hour, until then..."
*The sound of heavy steps sounded from the road, someone running.*
*I turned around and saw Slavya approaching.*
*Yulya disappeared into the forest, as expected.*
You: "Hi."
*I smiled.*
Slavya: "Yeah, hi..."
*She looked really nervous, with her cheeks blushing, eyes sparkling and braids all messy.*
Slavya: "Semyon, it's... Come with me, you'll see for yourself!"
You: "What happened?!"
*Slavya's face wore such a pleading expression that I decided not to argue.*
*She grasped my hand and dragged me to the square, the entire camp was probably there.*
*As we turned the last corner, I looked past the crowd of pioneers who were staring in the direction of Genda and there was...*
*In a distance, where before there were fields and forests, a city slowly started to appear!*
*At first it was faded, like it was made of smoke, but then it became more solid, as if emerging from a fog.*
*Sky City – I thought at once.*
*But, strange or not, there was nothing special about it, just a normal city – plenty of those in the territory of our vast country.*
*You could call it too normal, almost boring.*
*A city you would never pay attention to when passing by it in a car or flying over it in a plane.*
*But to see such a thing here and now, in the camp, lost in the vast fields and forests of another dimension, where the only life consists of the local pioneers, squirrels and mosquitoes...*
*Even a cat-girl is not that strange compared to this!*
*Slavya kept squeezing my hand tightly.*
*Pioneers whispered around us, as if afraid to speak in a loud voice, afraid that that illusion would disappear, or even the opposite – it would become more real, crushing the little camp Sovyonok beneath it.*
*But the city stayed in place, like a white cliff rising above a valley.*
*There was nothing special about it, neither gigantic skyscrapers nor significant architectural constructs, only houses of different colors and different numbers of floors, industrial buildings and a hospital or something like it.*
*You couldn't make out people or cars from that distance, but I was sure that the city is teeming with its own life, independent from our camp.*
*I wonder if someone there got up on a roof and is looking at us through binoculars, trying to make out the pioneers crowding in the square?*
*Indeed, it seemed like something flashed on one of the tallest buildings in the distance.*
*But wait a minute... Binoculars!*
*According to my estimations, there were about two or three kilometres to the city, so if I want to understand something right now then I need binoculars or a spyglass.*
*I ran to Olga Dmitrievna.*
You: "Do you see that too?"
Olga: "Yes, of course."
*She replied as if strained.*
You: "I need binoculars! Or a spyglass!"
*The camp leader stopped watching the faraway city for a moment and looked at me uncomprehendingly.*
Olga: "Binoculars... Yes. Go to the Cybernetics club. There should be some."
*I darted off and rushed in the direction of clubs' building.*
*Electronik and Shurik were tinkering with something as usual and looked like they knew nothing about the weird stuff happening in the camp.*
You: "Binoculars! Quick!"
*I shouted trying not to lose my breath.*
Sergei: "What is it?"
You: "Haven't you seen it? Ah damn, you are sitting here with your robots like owls! Do you have binoculars or a spyglass?!"
*I pronounced each word slowly like a caveman who had just learned how to speak.*
Shurik: "Can you calmly explain what this is all about?"
You: "No time to explain, give me the binoculars and hurry to the square!"
*The young cyberneticists didn't keep arguing with me, and in a minute we were standing with the rest of the pioneers as I used the binoculars to carefully examine the city which appeared from God knows where.*
*At first glance there was nothing special about it and it gave me an impression of being from my time, the beginning of the 21st century: ad boards, satellite dishes, pompous shop signs, modern cars...*
Olga: "Give those to me!"
*The camp leader snatched the binoculars from my hands.*
Yulya: "So, is that your world?"
*I turned around and saw Yulya standing next to me.*
You: "You said no-one should see you..."
Yulya: "Yes, but..."
*She was lost in thought.*
Yulya: "No-one sees me right now."
*The pioneers didn't pay any attention to the strange girl with cat ears, too occupied by watching the far-off city.*
You: "Do you know what it is ... and why?"
Yulya: "N-no."
*She answered after a short pause.*
Yulya: "There was nothing like this before! Nothing at all."
You: "And what was there?"
Yulya: "Well. You came, then left, then came again..."
You: "And what did you do all that time?"
Yulya: "I told you before, I was preparing supplies for the winter!"
*I totally couldn't understand, does Yulya really not consider this situation even a little bit strange, or is she just good at role-playing?*
*However, who would need to put on such a show for my benefit alone? I'm nothing but a guinea pig in a cage!*
You: "I don't believe you. You should know something..."
Olga: "Semyon."
*I turned to the camp leader.*
Olga: "I have no idea what all that is about, but it looks very strange. We should call the police!"
*Olga Dmitrievna reacted in the usual way, like a normal person would in such a situation.*
*I turned back to Yulya to triumphantly inform her about it, but the cat-girl had already disappeared.*
Olga: "What can it be?"
*The camp leader said quietly, not addressing anyone.*
*I didn't know if I should tell her about myself, about the future, about traveling to the past...*
*How do I know that that city really is from my time?*
*Could it be just another illusion and the behavior of pioneers is just a part of it? And what if it isn't...?*
You: "This..."
*I didn't manage to say any more.*
Ulyana: "Cool! Cool!"
*Ulyana shouted, appearing from nowhere.*
Ulyana: "Let's go and check it out!"
Alisa: "Oh, yeah. They must be expecting us!"
Slavya: "Wait a moment. We should think it over first!"
*Lena came up to us, but didn't say anything.*
Slavya: "What do you think, Semyon?"
*Slavya asked and stared at me, as if expecting an immediate answer.*
*And actually, why should what I think about it matter?*
*What is the difference between me and them which makes me all-knowing?*
*What does it matter that I am new to this world? The things that are happening are as obscure to me as for any other local.*
You: "I have no idea! Indeed, let's go and see for ourselves... It doesn't seem to be too far."
Olga: "But it's dangerous!"
Lena: "Isn't sitting here dangerous too?"
*Lena said shyly. All the pioneers and the camp leader looked at her uncomprehendingly.*
Lena: "Well, I mean... If that city has appeared so suddenly, then something else could happen too, and we..."
*She seemed to be getting completely confused and so she stopped talking.*
Alisa: "Well, she is right."
*Alisa said in a lazy voice.*
Alisa: "I certainly don't understand what this is all about, but I am not going to just sit and wait till something else happens! So, if no one else is going to..."
Ulyana: "And me, and me!"
*Ulyana interrupted her.*
Slavya: "Well, what then? What if it is just an illusion?"
You: "Then we don't lose anything."
*I was a bit surprised by the locals' urge to find out the nature of this phenomenon, because before they had avoided any conversation related to my appearance in this world.*
*Maybe it's a riddle inside a riddle? Like two enclosed spheres, we are within the shell of the outer one, where everything is clear for them but alien to me, and that city is just the intersection of the two spheres.*
*However, if it is true, then I should be located on the boundary, not knowing anything about one or the other.*
*Olga Dmitrievna was doubtful.*
*Everyone else waited for her approval or strict prohibition.*
*Nothing surprising about that: in the life of the camp, organised as Swiss watch, she was a tyrant and despot, but when the boundaries of Sovyonok expanded and a mysterious opponent appeared from beyond them, she couldn't keep the reins of power in her hands, started to panic, to feel restless on the throne which was losing its appeal.*
*This may be the right time to start acting with confidence!*
You: "I think we should go and check it out!"
*How long should I sit here, trying to look for some answers?! Where do I find them? In the canteen? In the camp leader's cabin? Near the Genda statue?*
*I have nothing to do here, especially when such an opportunity comes across!*
Olga: "But..."
*Olga Dmitrievna shyly objected.*
You: "What if we are already dead or something...?"
*I had to motivate the others in some way, but I hadn't decided to tell them about myself.*
Lena: "How's that... dead?"
*An expression of terror filled Lena's face.*
You: "I am not talking literally, but anything could happen! We can't tell for sure what is going on here, so any theory has to be considered!"
*Lena started crying and Slavya tried to comfort her.*
Ulyana: "It's even more fun that way!"
*And here is Ulyana, for whom even death itself may not be a good reason to act calmly.*
Alisa: "We should go in any case!"
*Alisa said cheerfully.*
*I turned around and looked at Shurik and Electronik.*
Sergei: "Well... We'd better stay here, try to measure it, make calculations..."
You: "I see."
*I didn't actually expect any help from those two.*
Olga: "Then you should get ready, prepare everything you may need..."
*Olga Dmitrievna started to busy around.*
Olga: "Flashlights, warm clothes, walkie-talkie. Do you have a walkie-talkie in the club?"
*She addressed the cyberneticists. They nodded in the affirmative.*
*…*
*In half an hour the 'Investigation Team' gathered at the square: me, Alisa, Lena, Slavya, Ulyana.*
*I was given quite a heavy backpack, packed with warm clothes, flashlights, some other necessities and in my hands I held a short-wave walkie-talkie.*
*I could certainly manage to walk those two or three kilometres wearing it on my shoulders, but why not distribute items among everyone?*
You: "Well, you know..."
*I dropped the backpack on the ground and looked at the camp leader.*
You: "I am the only man here and you immobilise me! Everyone should carry their own share!"
*The girls hesitated.*
*The first one to come to the backpack was Ulyana. She took a flashlight and a warm jacket, grousing.*
*The rest of them followed her example.*
*I didn't expect such boldness from myself, and expected even less for them to agree without question.*
*Even the local pioneers may try to behave logically in critical situations.*
*After couple of minutes we were at the camp's gates.*
Olga: "I hope you understand that I can't go with you... I have to look after the others and..."
You: "It's alright. You don't need to explain."
*I didn't count on Olga Dmitrievna's help, especially as there was some truth in her words.*
Olga: "Good luck! And don't forget that you have the radio!"
*…*
*The summer sun scorched us mercilessly.*
*The warm sweater in the bag seemed a kind of a mockery. I would give it and all the flashlights and even the walkie-talkie away in exchange for the camp leader’s panama hat and a bottle of water.*
*And why didn’t anyone think of bringing a water flask?*
Alisa: "Oh..."
*There were less and less clothes on Alisa with every passing minute.*
Alisa: "Let's have a rest!"
*I slowed down, shaded my eyes with my palm and looked in the direction of the city, which was to the right of us.*
*It didn't seem to be an inch closer.*
Ulyana: "Why not head straight to it?"
*Ulyana sounded annoyed.*
You: "How's that? Straight through the forests and fields?"
Ulyana: "I don't mind! Even that would be better than making detours!"
Slavya: "It would be quicker to go by road. Look! It makes a turn there."
*Slavya tried to reason with her.*
Alisa: "Do as you wish..."
*Alisa flopped down on the grass by the roadside.*
Alisa: "I'll take a break."
*We settled in the shade of a small bush near the power line.*
*I took out the binoculars and looked at the city.*
*The multi-storied buildings still shined in the distance.*
*Why aren't we getting closer? Or is it the heat which is creating an optical illusion?*
*A nearby bush rustled lightly. I turned around and saw a pair of cat ears sticking out of it.*
You: "Wait, I'll be back in a moment..."
*Having walked around the bushes, I gestured to Yulya to follow me and only after making sure we had enough distance from others that they wouldn't see us did I speak.*
You: "So, are you watching us?"
Yulya: "Well, of course. I am interested too!"
You: "Ah, I see. And you surely don't know what awaits us there, do you?"
Yulya: "Surely don't!"
*She smiled.*
You: "And you have no idea why don't we get any closer to the city?"
Yulya: "Actually I do."
*Yulya replied calmly.*
You: "Why then?"
Yulya: "Because you can't leave this place."
*I sighed heavily as usual and leaned against the lone tree.*
You: "Maybe it's the right time to tell me everything?"
*She got lost in thought.*
Yulya: "It was diffrent before. You came, and then... then you left and then you came again. And even if you went out so far, it was all the same. And that city... is your world..."
You: "Why do you always refer to it as my world?"
Yulya: "Because it is not of this place!"
*Yulya was exasperated.*
You: "And what is this place? Can you be any clearer?"
*I certainly wasn't mad at her - it seemed to me that the cat-girl wasn't hiding anything important, but she just did not understand the questions or did not know the answers.*
Yulya: "I don't know."
You: "Alright. Let's do it step by step. How long have you been here?"
Yulya: "Always."
You: "'Always' is too complex a definition for a human. Though, you are probably not human."
*I was lost in thought.*
You: "And what am I doing here?"
Yulya: "You were always here too."
You: "How is that possible? Did I duplicate myself? Because I don't remember anything like that."
Yulya: "Well. It is you and it's like it's not you. There are many of you."
You: "And are you the only one?"
Yulya: "I am the only one."
*Yulya smiled amiably and waved her tail.*
You: "One for all my parallel selves?"
Yulya: "Something like that."
You: "So, are you like... omnipotent?"
*I didn't manage to find a better word for it.*
Yulya: "I don't know."
You: "Do you have any supernatural abilities? Can you fly, throw fireballs, or teleport?"
Yulya: "I can make supplies for the winter."
*She answered in a serious tone.*
You: "Let's consider that a 'no'. And what is the purpose... of all this?"
Yulya: "I don't know."
*If I was rather calm at first, then after all these 'I don't know's I started to lose my temper.*
You: "You know..."
Slavya: "Semyon!"
*I heard Slavya shouting.*
*I turned around and when I looked back at the place where Yulya was standing she had already disappeared.*
You: "There you go again..."
*I gnashed my teeth and went back to the girls.*
*…*
*We had been walking for several hours, but the city still was in the same place.*
*It wasn't getting even a metre closer to or further away from us.*
Ulyana: "I told you we should go straight to it!"
Alisa: "Shut up! I don't understand..."
Lena: "Could it really be an illusion?"
*Lena, who hadn't uttered a word before, said.*
You: "No, even an illusion in a desert disappears if you get close enough to it. Probably..."
Alisa: "So what now?"
*Alisa said, outraged.*
Alisa: "I'm sick and tired of this. Let's go back!"
Slavya: "Go, if you want. Nobody is stopping you!"
*Slavya snarled at her.*
*Everyone looked at her in surprise. It was really strange to hear such things from the role model pioneer.*
Slavya: "Why are you always so unsatisfied with everything? You don't like it – get your ass back!"
Alisa: "Like I asked you..."
*Alisa said uncertainly.*
Lena: "Well, she's right!"
*Lena cut into the conversation.*
Lena: "I'm fed up with your whining!"
*Ulyana got scared and hid behind me.*
Alisa: "Oh, you’re just here to look better at someone else’s expense! Sure! It's easier to stand out with me in the background!"
Lena: "Oh trust me – you won’t be able to stand after what I’ll do to you now!"
*Lena rushed at Alisa, but Slavya stood between them.*
Slavya: "Hell no, let me go first!"
Ulyana: "Stop it!"
*Ulyana yelled, in tears.*
*I had no idea what to do in such a situation, but I couldn't let them fight.*
*However, I didn't have to interfere, Yulya jumped out from nowhere, got between the girls and hissed in rage.*
Yulya: "It shouldn't be like this! This is not right! You must not act like that! It is not your purpose!"
*The girls jumped back. Alisa squealed, Slavya adopted some kind of fighting position and Lena was holding a knife which she'd pulled from God knows where.*
Slavya: "Who are you?"
Lena: "Who is it?"
Alisa: "What is it?"
*I couldn't tell if she was addressing Yulya or me.*
You: "Wait..."
*I stood between them and the cat-girl.*
You: "I can explain everything."
*It's like I'm making excuses... To who? And for what? She should explain everything!*
*The girls relaxed a bit.*
You: "Well... Have you all heard the legend of the cat-girl? So, this is..."
*Yulya kept on hissing, but more quietly,*
Slavya: "She knows."
*Slavya said coldly.*
Slavya: "She knows what this city is. She knows everything!"
You: "She knows nothing."
Yulya: "I know nothing."
*Yulya confirmed.*
Alisa: "Did you ask her properly?"
*Alisa stood up and cracked her knuckles.*
You: "What the hell are you doing?! Stop at once! First the bus, the camp, then you, then her, now that damned city!"
*I started yelling, gritting my teeth, sparks probably flying from my eyes.*
You: "Enough is enough! I’ve had it with the damned uncertainty! Either you explain what is happening here, or I won't move an inch from here! Kill me if you want, I don't care!"
You: "Do you think I can put up with anything? That I would pretend that there is nothing happening and I understand nothing, regardless what you do? I don't care! Everything has a limit..."
*I finished my speech more calmly, having lost my breath from yelling.*
*The blood hammered in my temples, the world became darker for one moment, then the next it painted itself with unimaginable colours.*
*The girls looked at me with surprise and even with fear.*
*Yulya stopped hissing and again looked indifferent to everything around her.*
You: "Alright..."
*I declared and started to walk along the road in the direction of the city, which moved a step further away for every step I took.*
*No one followed me...*
*…*
*The sun started setting beyond the horizon and the city, still visible in the east, was little by little being absorbed by mist.*
*I couldn't tell where it is really located because the fields ahead were disrupted by forests, but its buildings still rose above them as the central element of the diorama.*
*The city stood mute, as if hovering over the world, looking down with silent reproach at my trivial attempts to reach it.*
*According to my calculations, I'd walked much more than two or three kilometres, which was the theoretical distance to the city. I stopped to rest in the shade a couple of times and the evening coolness became my savior.*
*However, there could be no city at all and I am just running like a hamster in a wheel, feeling the exhaustion of the distance I covered, but with my destination somewhere outside the cage...*
*I remembered yesterday's thoughts about the key hanging right under the ceiling.*
*It would certainly be useful to me now! Maybe there are no answers at all. I am too tired even to think about it... Plus that enraged outburst with the girls.*
*Ah, screw it!*
*I sat down on the side of the road, raising a little dust storm from the ground, which covered me and made me cough.*
*Tears filled my eyes.*
*When I opened them again, Yulya stood before me.*
You: "There seem to be advantages to being a cat, you move much faster than humans."
Yulya: "Where are you going?"
*She asked, paying no attention to my words.*
You: "I am going right there!"
*I waved a hand in the direction of the city.*
Yulya: "But why?"
You: "Where are the others?"
Yulya: "They went back to the camp."
You: "I see."
Yulya: "So, why are you going there?"
You: "Because..."
*I got lost in thought.*
You: "What else is there to do? What will happen if I just sit here?"
Yulya: "Nothing."
You: "That's what I mean."
*Yulya looked at me intently and sat beside me.*
Yulya: "I would like to help..."
*She suddenly said in a quiet voice.*
You: "Then help!"
Yulya: "I don't know how..."
You: "Tell me about that city, about this world! Why am I here? How do I get back?"
Yulya: "I don't know... Well, I mean... It always was like that: you come to the camp in a bus, spend a week here and then, regardless of the outcome, everything repeats. And... and... there are many of you, they are all different."
You: "What do you mean different?"
Yulya: "Not like you! You are the only one like this, that's why I can talk to you and the others just don't understand..."
You: "What don't they understand?"
Yulya: "They disappear sometimes."
*Yulya kept talking, ignoring my question.*
Yulya: "That's the way things should be. I have no idea why, but they should. They do not return here after seven days, but then new ones come who are just like the previous ones. Everyone is the same in the beginning, almost the same."
Yulya: "The differences come after some time. Especially when they have understood that everything should repeat itself again and again."
You: "Does that mean that I am destined to walk in circles too?"
Yulya: "I don't know. This time it's different."
You: "Why does it all happen? Who are those others?"
*She looked at me uncomprehendingly.*
Yulya: "But they're you..."
You: "What do you mean me?"
Yulya: "You and all those others..."
*She groused, trying to find the right words.*
Yulya: "You all are the same!"
You: "So are they clones of me or something?"
Yulya: "What are 'clones'?"
You: "Copies. Like two identical mushrooms you prepare for the winter!"
Yulya: "There are no two identical mushrooms."
*Yulya said seriously.*
You: "Imagine that there are!"
Yulya: "Identical mushrooms... Maybe... I don't know."
You: "God, this is a nightmare..."
*I put my head on the knees and closed my eyes.*
*We sat in silence for several minutes.*
*I really wanted to understand what was on Yulya's mind.*
*After all, even if she really knows nothing, then she should at least have some thoughts about the things that are happening.*
You: "Okay. What should I do?"
*I asked in a serious tone.*
*She looked at me uncomprehendingly again.*
You: "What would you advise me to do?"
Yulya: "I don't know."
You: "What would you do in my place?"
Yulya: "Me...? In your place...?"
Yulya: "But that wouldn’t ever happen!"
*Yulya laughed loudly.*
Yulya: "You are you and I am me!"
You: "Just imagine it! You have your mind, then you should have an imagination!"
Yulya: "Well... I wouldn't change anything."
You: "Why not?"
Yulya: "Because it is the way of things, it's better and less troubling this way."
You: "So, is it less troubling to sit in this camp and wait for the endless repetitions?"
Yulya: "Yes."
*I couldn't agree with that. Just couldn't.*
*As long as it's in my power to change something, or even just to try to, I have to act!*
*I rose up from the ground and marched forward towards the distant city, visible in the crimson rays of the faraway sunset.*
*…*
*The road took a sudden turn at last. The buildings, which were just rising above the trees before, disappeared from my sight and the country landscape in front of me was replaced by industrial suburbs.*
*It was dark already. Scattered bright stars filled the sky, still visible from where I stood but disappearing above the city, which was full of distant lights from windows and streetlamps.*
*A silent, dark night reigned behind me, interrupted only by the warbling of a sleepy night bird, the rustle of grass and the monotonous buzzing of insects. While in front of me there was a human anthill which couldn't stop talking even for a minute, happily winking with thousands of lights and shouting with millions of voices.*
*The road I walked seemed stranger. It was empty, as if deserted, used by neither cars nor people.*
*Like a narrow path, leading away from this world into another one.*
*Yulya walked in silence beside me all this time.*
You: "Why are you here?"
*I asked quietly.*
Yulya: "I have to be with you."
You: "Why?"
Yulya: "It's strange. The city always was on the right side and now it's in front of us."
*She ignored my question.*
You: "Not much stranger than everything else. I've walked about ten or twenty kilometres and it is still so far away!"
Yulya: "Far away?"
You: "We may never reach it!"
*I stopped and tried to imagine what awaits me there.*
*Is that city similar to my home one, what is its architecture like, who lives there...?*
*And why did I come to conclusion that there are any people there? That it isn’t just an illusion, one of the lame tricks of this sick world?*
*Even Yulya says that she’s seeing all this for the first time!*
*Suddenly the walkie-talkie I still had with me made a nasty sound and the agitated voice of Olga Dmitrievna said:*
Olga: "Semyon, do you copy? Semyon!"
*After a moment I pushed the button and answered.*
You: "Yes."
Olga: "Semyon, so much is happening! Come back at once!"
You: "What? What is it? What happened?"
*I asked without much interest.*
*The camp leader, the pioneers, the whole camp was left far behind, not just a dozen kilometres, but much further.*
*Everything that happened in the last few days lost any meaning, like a nightmare you start to forget.*
*Now, when there was a real world in front of me... I had no other choice but to believe that when I reach that city, everything will end.*
Olga: "Semyon, hurry! There's no time to explain! It's a disaster..."
*The static grew stronger, drowning out the camp leader’s voice.*
Yulya: "Will you go?"
*Yulya asked, agitated.*
You: "Where? Back there? No, why would I?"
Yulya: "But..."
You: "You want me to go back?"
Yulya: "I don't know. What do you want?"
*Really. What do I want?*
*To get to that city – what I’ve been doing the whole day? Or something more global – to escape from this world?*
*And what if something bad actually happened back there?*
*That thought sent a flash of pain in my head.*
*Something happened to Slavya, to Lena, to Ulyana, even to Alisa...*
*And why is the question 'Why would I care?' not bothering me now?*
*But – yes. I do care!*
*I got so much closer with them recently, I had really got used to the life of the camp!*
*But what will happen to the city? Would it disappear as suddenly as it appeared?*
*And what if everything went the way Yulya described...? No, I should not allow it.*
*The walkie-talkie hissed, but I didn't want to turn it off, in case I heard something again.*
Yulya: "So, what have you decided?"
*I had to make a decision.*
