*Damn that Sovyonok! There is no camp, no pioneers! And it really doesn't matter why I arrived there. My priority is to get out, quickly!*
You: "I'll go forward."
*I shrugged my shoulders, trying to express a minimum of interest.*
*Yulya stared hard at me for some time, but then took a couple of steps forward, as if inviting me to follow her.*
Yulya: "Well, are you going?"
*…*
*It seemed like for the first time today we got a bit closer to the city, like a hundred metres or so.*
*I was almost sure that I would reach it, then I heard sounds of a car horn from behind...*
*A bus, an Icarus, approached us fast, cutting through the night darkness with its lights.*
*I stepped to the roadside.*
You: "That's..."
*Yulya wasn't around.*
*How does she manage to appear and disappear so unnoticeably?*
*The bus slowly stopped next to me, the door opened and...*
*...Olga Dmitrievna stepped out!*
Olga: "Semyon! Why didn't you come back? I asked you to!"
You: "I could ask you the same thing! You said a disaster had happened, and now you..."
Olga: "Okay..."
*She suddenly softened.*
Olga: "Get on the bus."
You: "What...? And what about the city?"
Olga: "That's why we're going there – to see for ourselves!"
*I hesitated.*
*On one hand, it would be faster to go by bus, this road should lead to the city. On the other hand, the actions of the camp leader seemed strange.*
*We're going in the same direction for the time being anyway...*
You: "Okay."
*I agreed and got onto the bus.*
*…*
*The Icarus went in the direction of the mysterious city, bouncing over the bumps.*
*It was too slow in my opinion! I was so tired that my eyes started to close.*
*And what about Yulya? Did I just leave her alone there?*
*It looked like all the pioneers who had been in Sovyonok had got onto this bus!*
*Maybe she wanted to say something to me...*
*However, regardless of my struggle with Morpheus, my loud snoring sounded from the back seat within a couple of minutes.*
*Everything is over now! Or not?*
*I wanted to get out so badly and to not fall asleep.*
*Is exhaustion the reason?*
*Probably not. It was like I got a dose of sedative. People can't lose conciousness just like that and I never suffered from narcolepsy!*
*My thoughts flowed fast and calm, like a wide river.*
*Nothing interfered with their flight, because I was sleeping...*
*But, at the same time, it felt like I was conscious!*
*I am about to open my eyes and...*
*An old, chipped ceiling was looking down at me. A big crack divided it in two parts lengthwise, as if threatening to drop the upper floors on me.*
*The computer fan sounded peaceful, but strained. Thousands of specks of dust danced beautifully in the air.*
*The wind wailed outside the window, licking the frost-covered glass and then flying away, twirling the snowflakes in its wake.*
*The bright, winter-cold moon looked down at my world, winking merrily.*
*There was a ringing in my heavy head and I felt dizzy. A nasty aftertaste filled my mouth, as if I had eaten the contents of an ashtray and washed them down with a bottle of vodka.*
*The realisation didn't come at once.*
*I was intending to go somewhere yesterday and then...*
*And I had a strange dream about summer, a camp, pioneers and their camp leader, about a strange cat-girl and a distant city.*
*I always forget the end of my dreams. Did I get to the city or not?*
*Wait a minute... Was that really a dream?*
*I spent nearly a week in that camp!*
*However, the clock didn't agree with me - according to it, only about twelve hours had passed.*
*I sat up on the bed and tried to remember.*
*My feelings and emotions were really vivid, but the events of that dream were covered in fog.*
*I remembered girls, their tears and smiles, remembered joy and sadness that we experienced together, but their faces and figures were concealed by shadow.*
*And there was a mine of some sort, a bomb-shelter and then an island and a departure. And those damned grasshoppers, which disturbed my sleep!*
*And Slavya, and Lena, and Alisa, and Ulyana, and Masha... and Yulya!*
*But there was something else, something beyond the dream. My life after, seemingly a new level of existence.*
*Yes, I had woken up many times, met those girls while being awake in this world, and then everything started all over again...*
*This huge load of information just couldn't settle in my head, my memory was overflowing. I was forgetting something every second and I couldn't understand what was real and what was not.*
*All the events of the camp blended into one fantastic picture, a collage made from hundreds of works by hundreds of artists with different styles.*
*Scraps of feelings, shadows of emotions, parts of memories. My life was ripped apart and clumsily sewn back together and the result was something like that disfigured doll I had found in the old camp together with Ulyana. Wait... or was it with Slavya?!*
*That night search for Shurik flew before my eyes with all its details, but I couldn't remember the face of a girl who was with me that time.*
*The dream was getting more foggy with every moment. Will it be forgotten soon? I can’t let that happen! I must remember!*
*Even without details, even without faces, maybe even without names...*
*I am sure it is not just a dream! It's something bigger, something very important to me...*
*A voice started to ring in my head and it was not mine, it was someone else's.*
*It was quiet and distant at first, but it was growing louder with every moment and soon I almost could make out the words.*
*But it was probably just my imaginination. One electrical brain impulse contained more thoughts than a thousand books!*
*I remembered something in that dream I'd left unfinished.*
*The city? No, I had reached the city.*
*Yulya!*
*From the depths of my conciousness the image of a cat-girl arose. She stared at me furiously and moved her ears in a funny way.*
*Was it not a dream...? Was the week I had spent in the camp not a dream?!*
*I walked around the room, looked out the window. The outside world was the same as yesterday.*
*I was on the verge of going insane!*
*The silence of my flat was disturbed by the ringing of the door-bell.*
*Who might that be at such an hour?!*
*I didn't want to open the door at first. I was even afraid, but then thought that it was a good opportunity to check: was this a dream?*
*People in the dream and in reality are totally different!*
*I'll open the door and see!*
*I made it to the entrance in two leaps, pulled on the door handle without even looking in the peephole, and...*
*The girls stood in front of the door... The girls from the camp!*
*But something had changed about them.*
*I didn't remember every detail of their appearance in the dream. However, Slavya's hair-do... And Ulyana seemed taller.*
*A heavy silence hung in the air for a moment. I was petrified, my thoughts frozen, feeling no fear or any other emotions.*
*The girls seemed not to be surprised at all...*
You: "…"
Slavya: "Hi!"
*Slavya said happily.*
Ulyana: "Why are you standing around like a dummy?!"
*Exclaimed Ulyana.*
You: "How do you..."
*I got words onto my tongue, but couldn't form a sensible question out of them.*
*I had so many things to ask at once!*
Lena: "Calm down, girls. You shouldn't shock a person like this!"
*I remembered Lena at once, remembered our life after the camp...*
*And Slavya, that conversation at the night bus-stop.*
*And Ulyana. Our encounter at the university.*
*And Alisa at my concert.*
*And even Masha in the other world.*
*But how...?*
Alisa: "Well, yes. To cut a long story short..."
*Alisa started to speak casually.*
Alisa: "Don't be so surprised. Did you think you were the only one...?"
Masha: "In Sovyonok."
Alisa: "Yes, yes, in Sovyonok. You weren't the only one!"
Ulyana: "We were there too!"
You: "But how do you... all together, here..."
Slavya: "The point is that every one of us had her own camp and you had yours. I mean, in ours you behaved... differently."
*Slavya sounded awkward.*
Ulyana: "Really differently! You chased me with that cake, I barely managed to escape!"

*The only conclusion is that Yulya seems to be a prisoner in this camp, the same as I. Just a more mysterious one.*
*What happened next happened by itself.*
*Even if what I was going to do was dangerous, in the end I'm a red-blooded man!*
*At that moment Yulya was not an all-powerful being to me, I was holding an ordinary girl in my arms.*
*…*
*I brought the sleeping Yulya to my cabin. She was surprisingly light.*
*I put her on a bed, collapsed beside her and closed my eyes...*
*But all my attempts to get to sleep failed. I felt a terrible thirst.*
*Quietly, so as not to wake Yulya up, I got out of bed, pulled on my shorts and went outside.*
*On the way to washstands I thought about everything that happened.*
*I didn't care about whether it was right or not. No, that wasn't the main issue.*
*I decided that I just didn't have any other choice in that situation.*
*More important are the possible consequences.*
*Even if Yulya was a little different from me, we could say, she was closer to who (or what) was behind all this. Just because she knows more than me.*
*Which means... However, blindly assuming or drawing conclusions about anything is a difficult task in this camp, I was sure of that by now.*
*…*
*I quenched my thirst and washed myself. I was going back to the camp leader's cabin, whistling a piece from 'Peer Gynt' by Grieg, when somebody called out to me.*
Pioneer: "How did you...?"
*I jumped on the spot, turned and saw the silhouette of that pioneer.*
*There was no chance of seeing his face clearly in this darkness.*
You: "So it's... you again?"
Pioneer: "Who 'me'? Not in the sense that I am the one I that you have already seen, but in a sense of – who, in fact, I am?"
You: "I don't understand."
*I remembered that Yulya told me that he can’t do me any physical harm, and I calmed down a bit.*
Pioneer: "Oh, whatever. Besides, I saw how you were getting it on back there."
*That gave me the heebie-jeebies.*
*No matter how fantastic a situation is, it’s always frustrating when you're caught doing something so intimate.*
You: "Didn't anyone ever tell you that it's not nice to spy on people?"
Pioneer: "You're upset."
You: "No. Why would I be..."
*I snorted and half-turned towards him, trying in vain to see his face.*
Pioneer: "And what has the cat-eared one told you?"
You: "She has a name!"
*I felt a strong attachment to Yulya, so I didn't hesitate to stand up for her.*
Pioneer: "A name? And what is it? An almighty observer? The double-faced Janus?"
You: "Yulya..."
*I said a bit uncertainly.*
Pioneer: "Yulya?!"
*He started laughing like a horse on meth.*
Pioneer: "And who gave it to her? You, probably."
You: "Fine, tell me what you want and get lost!"
Pioneer: "Okay, okay, Your Majesty! Just don't be angry!"
*He bowed awkwardly.*
*The sight was so grotesque that I even shuddered.*
Pioneer: "And what has the so-called Yulya told you?"
*I decided there was no point in hiding the information I'd found out recently.*
You: "She told me that there are many other camps. That you are the same as me. And that after seven days we leave and never come back."
*It was disgusting for me to be in the same boat as him, but a fact was still a fact.*
Pioneer: "Yes, that's about right. And what did she tell you about herself?"
You: "Do you think it's any of your business? Besides, surely you know everything without me."
Pioneer: "Yes I know something. I've dealt with her before."
*His tone was so disgusting that I didn't even want to continue this conversation.*
You: "Well, if you have nothing more to..."
Pioneer: "No, wait a minute! I haven't finished yet."
You: "Now what?"
Pioneer: "Want me to tell you what she’s hiding from you?"
You: "Go on."
*I was sure that Yulya had no secrets from me, but in my situation any information could be useful.*
Pioneer: "“Never come back”?... No, they do come back! And you come back... At least you did before."
You: "I don't understand."
Pioneer: "I did tell you that you had already been here. So after seven days it doesn’t matter whether you leave on a bus or fall asleep in the forest – you will find yourself sitting in the 410 again."
You: "But how...?"
Pioneer: "She told you that we just disappear, right?"
*I did not answer.*
Pioneer: "Well, I can't be sure she is lying. Maybe she just doesn't know everything, but what I said is true! You and I were here many times. Of course I've been here more times, but that doesn't matter."
You: "Okay, then why I don't remember anything?"
Pioneer: "You will remember them all some time later. That’s what happened to me."
You: "And you’re telling me that there is no escape from here?"
Pioneer: "Yes I am."
You: "I remember you told me that what happened today had never happened before, right?"
Pioneer: "True. This is the first time."
You: "And how can you explain that?"
Pioneer: "I won't! You're hoping that something will change? No way it will!"
You: "We'll see about that."
*I decisively turned and walked away.*
*To my surprise, the pioneer did not even try to stop me.*
*I returned to the cabin and found Yulya, carefully combing her tail.*
Yulya: "You were talking to him again."
You: "How do you know?"
*For a moment I had doubts.*
Yulya: "Just guessed. He is supposed to appear when you're alone."
You: "Yes..."
Yulya: "And?"
You: "He told me that nobody disappears. That 'we' come back."
*Yulya didn't answer anything.*
You: "Is that so?"
Yulya: "To tell you the truth, I don't know..."
*I sat on the bed beside her and began to think.*
*…*
*I don't know how long we were sitting there, but soon I started to fall asleep.*
Yulya: "Let's go watch the stars."
You: "Let's go."
*I wanted to sleep badly, but at the same time I felt a sense of incompleteness, and was hoping fresh air would clear my thoughts.*
*A few minutes later we were at the square.*
*I sat on the bench, and Yulya put her head in my lap and stared at the sky.*
Yulya: "Isn't it beautiful?"
You: "It is..."
*We sat in silence for quite a long time.*
You: "So what will happen tomorrow?"
Yulya: "What do you mean?"
You: "Well, tomorrow is the seventh day... So, it's time to leave."
Yulya: "Do you want to leave?"
*Suddenly I was struck by a realisation. I have heard this question many times before.*
You: "According to you and him, even if I don’t want to, I must."
Yulya: "So let's leave."
*She smiled.*
You: "Will you come with me?"
Yulya: "Of course I will! After all this you must definitely marry me!"
You: "I don't know of a single administration that would register marriages with catgirls."
Yulya: "So we'll look for one."
You: "Okay, seriously though, what will happen tomorrow?"
Yulya: "In the evening the bus will come..."
You: "You sure about that?"
Yulya: "Absolutely sure! It always comes."
You: "And?"
Yulya: "And we will take it."
You: "And then?"
Yulya: "Why are you asking all these stupid questions?!"
*Yulya protested.*
Yulya: "How should I know?"
You: "Well, make a guess!"
Yulya: "And... we will go back to your world."
You: "That would be..."
*I stopped*
You: "We'll see."
*I sighed.*
You: "And what about you and your many selves?"
Yulya: "I only look like this here, right? Over there I will just be regular me."
You: "Sure, with cat ears and a tail..."
*Yulya hit me painfully in the ribs.*
You: "Hey! I'm just joking!"
Yulya: "Maybe without a tail."
*She said sadly.*
You: "No, no! I like it! Don’t think anything like that!"
*She said nothing, just closed her eyes.*
Yulya: "And what's it like over there...?"
You: "It's different – that's the best way I can put it. Some things are better, some are worse. We've got internet..."
*I chuckled.*
Yulya: "And what would I do there?"
You: "Well, I don’t know... Let's solve the problems as they come."
Yulya: "Alright..."
*…*
*We sat there for a long time, talking about all sorts of foolish things.*
*Finally Yulya said:*
Yulya: "Let's go sleep!"
You: "Yes, good timing!"
*I felt a wave of a terrible fatigue.*
Yulya: "Tomorrow is time to pack our things."
You: "But I have nothing to pack."
Yulya: "How about that – he has nothing to pack... But you know what... I have!"
You: "For example?"
*I giggled good-naturedly.*
*I just can’t imagine what she was planning to take.*
Yulya: "What about my supplies for the winter? Apples! Nuts! Mushrooms!"
You: "Do you really think you'll need all that?"
Yulya: "Of course!"
*She jumped up and looked at me sternly.*
Yulya: "I’m going to sleep and you can do whatever you want!"
*With these words, Yulya marched briskly towards the camp leader’s cabin.*
You: "Hey, I didn't..."
*I rushed after her.*
*…*
*After entering the cabin Yulya immediately undressed, snuck into the bed and pulled the blanket over her head.*
You: "I didn't mean anything like that... If you want to take your stores, let's take them."
*In the end, they could be useful for us, especially in my situation where anything could happen.*
Yulya: "I was just joking!"
*She peeked out from under the blanket and stuck out her tongue.*
Yulya: "And now – sleep!"
*Commanded Yulya.*
*I didn’t mind it, so I undressed, lay down beside her, and we fell asleep holding each other...*
*I had a strange dream.*
*No, of course being here in this camp was extremely strange by itself, incomparable with any normal nighttime dreams.*
*However, in this dream everything seemed so real that...*
*But when I woke up I couldn’t remember a thing.*
*There were only vague images of a long driveway, an old rusted bus, the rickety gates of the camp, collapsed statues of pioneers and an abandoned square.*
*I ran through Sovyonok back and forth, as if trying to find someone. But exactly who remained a mystery to me.*
*When I woke up, the sun was already setting.*
*A bright sunbeam was lighting up the dust drifting in the silence of the room and painting it with all colors of the rainbow.*
*Reflections on the glass took on different outlines: look from one angle and it's just a spot of sunlight, look from another and it's a pirate waving his cutlass.*
*I stretched lazily and yawned.*
*Turning to the other side I saw Yulya, sleeping peacefully next to me.*
Yulya: "Good morning!"
*Said Yulya, without opening her eyes.*
You: "It's daytime already."
Yulya: "Morning starts when you wake up."
You: "You’re talking just the same way I did before."
Yulya: "So now you've changed your mind?"
You: "Well I don't know… During the last week I got used to getting up in the morning."
*That was not entirely true, because I didn't always wake up with the sunrise and regularly missed the lineups.*
Yulya: "You want to say that you've changed?"
*She giggled.*
You: "I think any man in my position would change, at least a little."
*It seemed quite natural to me.*
Yulya: "Yes, perhaps. I won't argue."
*A long silence followed.*
*The kind of silence where you are not tortured by the need to say something just to break the oppressive awkwardness. This silence could say more than any words.*
You: "Well, we're leaving today?"
*I asked finally.*
Yulya: "I think so."
You: "You think? You mean you are not even sure?"
Yulya: "Not completely. This is happening for the first time."
You: "You mean the disappearance of the pioneers."
Yulya: "Not just that..."
*She got out of bed and started to dress.*
*I looked at her mesmerised, unable to look away.*
Yulya: "What you are looking at? Get up! It's time to pack!"
You: "You mean your berries and mushrooms?"
Yulya: "Of course!"
*Yulya stood arms akimbo and looked at me resentfully.*
Yulya: "Do you want all my supplies to be gone?"
You: "Of course I don't..."
*To tell the truth, I didn't really give a damn about them.*
*To be precise, I just don’t see the point in stocking food for a one-way journey. At least, without a return ticket for sure.*
*…*
*A few minutes later we were standing in the same forest glade, where the day before Yulya had been sprinking a mushroom with sugar.*
*She went behind a tree, threw aside the leaves and pulled out a heavy sack.*
You: "All this..."
Yulya: "This isn't all. This is just what's necessary."
*I couldn’t put what I planned to say in a nice way, so I decided to say nothing.*
*The sack was filled with mushrooms, berries, apples, nuts – all mixed up.*
*I immediately had serious doubts about the fitness for human consumption of this assorted lot.*
Yulya: "Take it."
*Said Yulya, pointing at a sack with an easy smile.*
You: "Well, I hope you understand that I won’t be able to..."
Yulya: "No, no, you're strong. Look how massive you are!"
*She used her hands to indicate the difference in our heights.*
*I tried to lift the sack. It weighed at least thirty kilos.*
You: "Look, let's only take some of it – we won't be able to eat all this anyway."
*I was trying to cheat.*
Yulya: "Why not? Winters are long in these lands."
You: "How would you know that?"
Yulya: "I guessed."
*I tried to make the most painful grimace I could.*
You: "I can manage it to the square at most. Have mercy on me!"
*Yulya thought a little.*
Yulya: "Okay, then throw out the berries!"
*What a great solution – get rid of the lightest stuff.*
*However, I didn’t object and so put my hand into the sack.*
You: "I can’t say it got any lighter."
*I said when I finished with the berries.*
Yulya: "I don't want to hear it!"
*I sighed and sank helplessly to the ground next to the sack.*
You: "Then let's carry it in turns."
Yulya: "But it's heavy!"
*Exclaimed Yulya.*
You: "That's what I'm telling you..."
Yulya: "I mean it's heavy for me."
You: "As if it's light for me..."
*I muttered under my breath trying to make Yulya not hear it.*
Yulya: "It is light for you!"
*It seems I should not underestimate her cat ears.*
You: "Okay, let's come back here later, for now it would be nice to have something to eat!"
Yulya: "Well, maybe... "
*She smiled and held out her hand to me.*
*…*
*The canteen was filled with the smell of fried potatoes.*
*Yulya flittered around me, watching me cook.*
*To tell the truth, I never found any special pleasure in doing this.*
*I always wanted to start eating immediately, without waiting for all the ingredients to be prepared, the water to boil, the dumplings to float up...*
*That’s why I’m usually fine with eating sandwiches or fast food.*
Yulya: "You're doing so well!"
You: "I told you there is nothing special to it."
Yulya: "But... But..."
*She tried to find words.*
Yulya: "But.. You're doing well anyway!"
You: "I'm glad you like it."
Yulya: "Of course I like it!"
*Judging by the way Yulya was demolishing the potatoes, she actually enjoyed my simple culinary creation.*
Yulya: "Are you worried?"
You: "Chew first, then speak."
Yulya: "What a lout!"
You: "You must behave in polite society."
Yulya: "And what kind of society are we in here?"
*Yulya spread her hands to the sides and laughed.*
*That was true, the canteen was empty. Just like the whole camp.*
You: "What do you think, where are they all gone to?"
Yulya: "How should I know..."
*She picked up the last piece with her fork and deftly popped it into her mouth.*
Yulya: "You miss them?"
You: "Sort of."
Yulya: "What about me?! I am better than any stray dog!"
*Another quote... I didn't pay any special attention to it this time.*
You: "Given that you're some kind of a cat, you’ve definitely got your quotes right."
Yulya: "Are you feeling lonely?"
You: "Well, I'm not alone here."
Yulya: "Just the two of us..."
You: "But if what had happened didn't happen, we maybe..."
*I stopped for a moment.*
You: "So, in other realities you and me weren’t so..."
Yulya: "Close?"
*Yulya finished for me.*
You: "Yes."
Yulya: "No."
You: "It's strange."
Yulya: "Why?"
You: "Well, because there are a lot of camps, as you say, and according to the theory of probability..."
You: "Which means that everything that happened within the last two days is really something exceptional..."
Yulya: "You say that as if it's bad."
You: "Of course not!"
*I felt the blood rush to my head.*
You: "Just strange. There are lots of strange things here. That’s why I use that word so often. Anyway, you’re just nitpicking."
Yulya: "Who? Me!? Never!"
*She laughed.*
You: "No, you are seriously nitpicking! Especially when it comes to words!"
Yulya: "Why would I do that?"
You: "I can’t even imagine. You'd know better."
*Seems like for any of my arguments she already had an answer prepared. As if she knew in advance what I will say.*
You: "Forget it... So let's go."
Yulya: "Where?"
*I realised that saying this was a big mistake, now she'll definitely drag me back to that sack.*
You: "Well... there is enough time till the bus arrives. So we could..."
Yulya: "Oh, right! The supplies!"
*I just scratched my chin and followed her. Epic fail!*
*…*
*Carrying nearly twenty five kilos is not easy.*
*Even for a short distance.*
*I stopped every fifty metres to rest.*
*Yulya hurried and encouraged me, but it was just making things worse.*
*I don’t know if I deserved a medal in some strange sack-of-catgirl-supplies-short-distance-carrying event, but about an hour later the sack was transported to the bus stop.*
*I collapsed beside it, exhausted.*
You: "That's it..."
Yulya: "You’re such a hero! See, nothing to be afraid of!"
*My whole body ached, my muscles burned, and rivers of sweat flowed from my forehead, stinging my eyes.*
*I don’t know what reward I was owed for this, but this competition was more like the Olympics for mentally challenged people – though I won, I’m still a retard.*
Yulya: "Look! The bus is coming!"
You: "What?!"
*I jumped up. My fatigue vanished in an instant.*
*Something could indeed be seen in the distance.*
*I narrowed my eyes and saw the Icarus.*
*But why?*
*Yulya told me that it would arrive closer to the night.*
*Moreover, I'd expected the LiAZ bus.*
*Soon the bus stopped in front of us and the door opened, inviting us in.*
*The driver's seat was empty, but I was not really surprised. Much stranger things had happened here.*
Yulya: "Coming?"
*Yulya easily jumped onto the first step and gestured for me to follow her.*
You: "Don’t you think it's weird that buses go by themselves?"
Yulya: "Well..."
*She thought about that.*
Yulya: "Of course, it is strange, but you said yourself that there are plenty of strange things here!"
*Yes, she was right on that one.*
*Anyway, I had no choice.*
*In either case, whether I stay or whether I go on the bus I'm not sure about what will come next.*
*But in case of the second choice I had at least an illusory hope of escaping from this camp.*
*I sighed, and with one last effort lifted the sack and got onto the bus.*
*…*
*We drove for about an hour.*
*Yulya was constantly chattering about something, but I wasn’t listening.*
*I carefully studied the passing landscapes through the window. Forests, fields, river, forests, fields... Absolutely nothing suspicious.*
*On the one hand, this gave me some hope, but on the other it was a sign that in the end nothing will change, because in this world it seems everything is slow and measured, following its well-established rules.*
*That's how it was at least a few days ago.*
*Although maybe I shouldn't be drawing conclusions after having been there only a week...*
Yulya: "Well! Now I am sure everything will be fine!"
*I looked at her carefully.*
*Cat ears, a long tail that moved rhythmically back and forth, slightly enlarged fangs. Yulya seems like a character from a fairy tale.*
*We can decide what to do with her in the real world later.*
*I was turning into one big throbbing vein, ready to burst any moment.*
*I was waiting... waiting for how this will end.*
*The result could be anything. For me it was important not to go crazy ahead of time.*
*My nerves were stretched to the limit and I tried not to think about anything.*
*But it was impossible to distract myself.*
Yulya: "Hey! Are you even listening?"
You: "Huh? No, sorry, I was deep in thought..."
Yulya: "Well, as always!"
*She pouted.*
You: "Now is such a big moment, you know... We can get out... get out of this camp. So it's a very important moment for me."
Yulya: "Well, it's important for me too, but I'm not worried."
You: "You simply can't see this in context."
Yulya: "What do you mean?"
You: "Before, I lived in a different world – the real one, as it seemed. So I have something to compare this camp to. And you, we can say, were born here."
Yulya: "No I wasn’t!"
You: "How do you know?"
Yulya: "I just know! I know that..."
*…*
*The bus peacefully bounced over the bumps, shaking me more and more.*
*The steering wheel was turning on its own and I soon stopped noticing the absence of a driver.*
*My eyes began to close and I dozed off...*
*Some girl bent over me.*
*She was gently whispering something in my ear... So tenderly, that...*
*I felt a strong blow on the head.*
Yulya: "Hey, don't sleep!"
You: "Am I disturbing you?"
*I asked in annoyance, rubbing the bruised place.*
Yulya: "You're not listening to me!"
You: "If we escape from here, we'll have lots of time for conversation."
Yulya: "If...If... And if we don't escape?"
You: "Then we will have even more time."
*I tried to smile, but just thinking that we wouldn’t ever leave this camp frightened me a lot, so I just gave a stupid grin.*
Yulya: "It's better if we don't escape! Because in your world... I don't know what to expect there, but... You won't pay any attention to me at all!"
You: "I will, I promise!"
*I hugged her sincerely.*
Yulya: "Really-truly?"
You: "Really-truly!"
*Yulya leaned against me.*
Yulya: "And you'll listen to me?"
You: "Of course!"
Yulya: "And you'll always agree with me?"
You: "Sure!"
*She pulled away and looked into my eyes.*
Yulya: "Well then, I forgive you!"
*A loud laugh filled the bus cabin.*
Yulya: "But be careful, don't you forget about that, or try to deceive me!"
You: "Want to sign a contract?"
Yulya: "A marriage contract?"
You: "I don't have the property for that anyway."
Yulya: "But I do!"
*Yulya pointed at the bag, lying in the aisle.*
You: "Well, then..."
*I tried to remember what I'd bought with my money.*
You: "Here!"
*I took my mobile phone out of my pocket. By this time it was already out of charge.*
Yulya: "What's that?"
*Yulya asked curiously, taking the mobile.*
You: "A very useful thing in my world – you can communicate with people at a distance."
Yulya: "Wow, that's really cool! Excellent, that will do!"
*She put the mobile on the seat.*
Yulya: "Deal then? My supplies for the winter are from me and from you.... is that thing!"

Yulya: "Alright, now we are husband and wife!"
*She smiled slyly.*
You: "Hey, wait..."
*I suddenly remembered that all this conversation had started with a marriage contract.*
You: "Anyway, without an official registration..."
Yulya: "When we get to your world we will register our marriage. A man without a wife is like a kitchen without a knife."
You: "If we get there, of course..."
*Yulya said nothing, but just stared straight forward with her eyes wide open.*
*I followed her gaze and realised that the bus was full of people!*
*All of them were wearing pioneer uniforms and they all looked exactly like that pioneer.*
*Nobody said a single word. They just looked silently in my direction.*
*I could not see their faces. Clothes, statures – yes, but their faces were shrouded in shadows that seemed to appear from nowhere.*
*It was as if instead of the heads that normal people have they had mini black holes.*
*I started to shiver and my back broke out in goosebumps.*
*Yulya squeezed my hand.*
*With an enormous effort I forced myself to look at her.*
*She was very scared too.*
*If I was alone at that moment I would have probably fainted. But right now I was responsible for more than only my own life.*
You: "Who.. are.. you..."
*I gritted out with difficulty.*
*The pioneers maintained the terrifying silence.*
*It became hard to breathe. I was gasping for breath, but my brain refused to work on low oxygen, and I lost consciousness for a moment.*
Yulya: "Who are you?! What do you want?!"
*I heard Yulya's shout just as I regained my senses.*
*A pioneer stood up from the first seat and walked towards us.*
Pioneer: "Hi, Semyon! We have decided to go back 'home' too."
Everyone: "Too... too..."
*A chorus of voices filled the bus.*
Pioneer: "We'll keep you company."
*I didn't know what to say.*
*This was the strangest situation I had yet experienced in the camp.*
*Neither Yulya, nor the city, nor the disappearance of pioneers, nor this strange person standing before me, were comparable with this...*
Yulya: "I asked you a question!"
*Seems like Yulya was still able to speak clearly. Not a surprise. In the end she was still, you could say, an extraordinary being.*
Pioneer: "I repeat. We are just going home."
*His voice sounded frantic.*
Pioneer: "Are we bothering you?"
Everyone: "Bothering... bothering..."
Yulya: "What do you want from us?"
Pioneer: "Nothing at all."
Everyone: "Nothing... nothing..."
Yulya: "I don't believe you! I know there is a reason for you to be doing all this!"
Pioneer: "It's just your imagination, animal!"
Yulya: "Maybe I am an animal. But what are you? A ghost, a shadow?"
Pioneer: "Maybe. Ghosts have their rights too."
Yulya: "You have the right to get the hell out of here!"
*Yulya shouted so loud that my ears rang. But neither the pioneer nor his companions reacted.*
Pioneer: "I guess we'll stay."
*He said maliciously.*
You: "But how did you manage this? And all the others..."
*At last I gathered the strength to speak.*
Pioneer: "It's simple, my dear friend! Collective mind. Heard about it?"
You: "And... so?"
Pioneer: "Every one of us wanted to wish you luck simultaneously, that's all."
Everyone: "Luck... luck..."
Pioneer: "In person, I would say. That's the reason we are here."
You: "But what will happen next?"
Pioneer: "Honestly, I have no idea."
Yulya: "Get out!"
*Yulya shouted again.*
Pioneer: "Be cool, you – settle down!"
Pioneer: "You see..."
*He addressed me again.*
Pioneer: "I don't want to hide anything from you. You have a good chance to get out of here now. I don't exactly know why, but your actions broke the cycle. Cycles, to be precise, all our cycles. And there is a chance that we won’t have to leave the camp every seven days and return back on the eighth, waking up in this bus."
Yulya: "Then don't return! Just die!"
Pioneer: "It's not that simple. And why shouldn't we have a sense of self-preservation?"
Pioneer: "We should, right?"
*He asked the pioneers.*
Everyone: "Should... should..."
*I heard their response.*
Pioneer: "So we decided to keep you company."
Pioneer: "Now, either we will all get out of here together, or we'll all vanish forever together. Or start another cycle. All three options suit us."
Yulya: "And what if we die because of you?!"

Pioneer: "It's too late. I suggest you calm down and enjoy the flight. Stewardesses will offer you food and drinks in a couple of minutes."

I have not the slightest idea what to do to drive them out of here, but even if I knew, I am sure that nothing would change, nothing would affect the final outcome."
Yulya: "You may be right..."
*Yulya said in a sad voice.*

*…*

*A quiet clap would be enough to make my ear-drums explode.*

*Are they really my colleagues in misfortune?*

*It's stupid to cling to hope while standing on the edge of the cliff, surrounded by countless enemies.*

*I regained conciousness in complete darkness. To be precise, I regained the ability to percive myself as a person. There was nothing else, neither around nor inside me.*
*It was like I ceased to exist, was erased from the universe. But I wasn't dead, no. It was totally different, as if I had moved from three-dimensional space to one-dimensional. The whole world compressed to the size of one dot.*

But how? I clearly remember that I left it and came back to the real world. And then I met Slavya at a bus stop... No, I met Ulyana at the university. No, I met Alisa at a concert! But I had lived with Lena for so many years! No, I had a completely different life with Masha. How is all that even possible? I remembered events of almost five lifespans in the smallest of details. *Just wonderful...*
Zhenya: "But I can't sew!"

*...*
*It started to dawn, the fever made its presence known and seemed to get even stronger.*

*...*

Olga: "Hey, Semyon!"

Pioneer: "At fault for what? For trying to stop you from leaving with cat-eared? I know that was you in that bus!"
*There were still no emotions on the pioneer's face.*
Pioneer: "Maybe it was, or it wasn't - what's the difference now?"
Pioneer: "That means, you… managed to get out?"
Pioneer: "And came back just to mock me?"
Pioneer: "Didn't you do the same?"
Pioneer: "Stop pushing these morals onto me, for god's sake!"
*I was down on my knees and looking at Zhenya, who was slowly getting further and further away.*
*And there she went around a corner. I can't get her back…*
*Anyway, I knew that this wasn't Zhenya - my real Zhenya disappeared yesterday, this was just a soulless doll that looked like her But she looked just like her…*
*The tale can't last forever!*
*This world is a true hell, and I'm the demon. And demons can't ever reach true happiness.*
Pioneer: "Just tell me one thing."
*I killed the silence.*
Pioneer: "Why is everything like this?"
Pioneer: "You had a chance from the very beginning, a choice - you could have done everything differently. Many did it right - different from how you, and others alike, did."
Pioneer: "Yeah, right. They all got out and are now living happily with their dolls in the real world!"
*I grinned.*
Pioneer: " Do you think that your life is better?"
*He clearly emphasized the word «life»*
Pioneer: "If you're the one… If you're the one that took Zhenya away from me…"
*Rage was growig inside of me, I waned to jump on him and beat him to death!*
*But I wasn't sure that he existed in the physical world.*
*But even then, what would change?*
Pioneer: "You could have been happy with every other girl, that's the reason they're all here."
*I didn't expect such an answer.*
Pioneer: "But none of them are real! The only real ones were me… you… us all… Zhenya"
Pioneer: "That's only for you, in your world. You know that there are many realities and in every one of those you pick your own faith. Maybe there was only one Semyon, but this camp gave him multiple possibilities."
Pioneer: "Someone managed to get out and now lives happily, like you said. Someone - stuck, like you."
Pioneer: "Can you tell me what this place is? Who are you?"
Pioneer: "You can think of me as the camp leader."
*The pioneer gave a smile without any trace of mockery or irony - and vanished.*
*I felt a bit easier after hearing his words.*
*The world was suddendly engulfed in fog, and a bright flash appeared in front of me.*
*I looked around and realized that the pioneers are gone, as well as the bus.*
*What again?*
*The gates creaked silently, and I hid behind the pioneer's monument.*
*Semyon walked onto the bus stop - one of the Semyons, but his facial expression was painfully familiar.*
*I've forgotten long ago, that I can look exactly like that.*
*He stared at the road for some time, and headed back into the camp.*
Pioneer: "Don't trust him."
*I said on an impulse.*
You: "Who are you?!"
*Semyon looked surprised.*
Pioneer: "Stop! Don't come any closer!"
You: "Alright, I'll stay here…"
Pioneer: "Have you seen him? Talked to him?"
You: "Who are you even talking about?"
Pioneer: "You know who…"
You: "Yes…"
Pioneer: "What did he tell you?"
You: "Nothing, really…"
Pioneer: "Did he give you advice? Did he tell you what to do? Threaten you?"
You: "No, nothing like that… Of course he seemed pretty weird, but nothing more than that…"
Pioneer: "Remember he may not be alone! Or more likely, he is alone but you may meet many pioneers here who look like him."
You: "And what about you? Who are you? Who are you hiding from?"
Pioneer: "You will understand… In time… Just remember, the most important thing is to find the exit!"
*The wind became really strong for a moment, and the same flash appeared before me.*
*And again, in an instant, the bus and pioneers appeared once again.*
*I don't know what I told him everything for…*
*I thought it was the right thing to do.*
*If only I remembered what remorse and repentance were, then possibly that would be what I am feeling.*
Zhenya: "A pioneer should always be ready!"
*A familiar voice sounded like thunder in the midst of a clear sky, and a familiar thump on my back brought me out of the catatonic state I was in.*
*Zhenya was standing in front of me.*
*I instantly knew that this was Zhenya, not the doll!*
Pioneer: "But…how…"
*Those were the only words I could whisper.*
Zhenya: "I don't know…"
*She smiled, but her voice was trembling.*
Zhenya: "Back then, after the wedding I woke up in a different world… I thought that I'd lost you. And then… and then there were so many loops that I nearly forgot…"
Pioneer: "Sorry."
*I said quietly.*
Pioneer: "Forgive me for everything."
Zhenya: "But that was okay. Then he came and said that he could guide me to the world you're in. I didn't believe it at first, but… here I am!"
*I jumped forward and hugged Zhenya*
Pioneer: "Forgive me! I'd forgotten… everything, forgotten you! I've done so many bad things to you. I didn't believe it, didn't hope for it. I'm sorry!"
Zhenya: "Ugh, you're going to suffocate me!"
*She freed herself from my arms.*
Zhenya: "But now I'm here, so everything is okay!"
*She said through her tears.*
Pioneer: "How can you be so calm?"
Zhenya: "Because I always knew that we were going to be together."
*Zhenya raised her right hand, and on her finger I saw a ring that was woven out of may-lily.*
Pioneer: "I've lost mine, sorry…"
Zhenya: "It's okay, we'll buy a new one!"
*She smiled.*
Olga: "Hey, hop onto the bus, you two!"
*Olga Dmitrievna was screaming discontentedly.*
*…*
*The bus was peacefully bouncing over the bumps and slowly driving towards the district center… or wherever it was going, really!*
Pioneer: "You know, I can't believe that everything will end."
*I've gone through so much in the last week…*
Zhenya: "And once again, you got the most interesting parts!"
*Zhenya sulked.*
Pioneer: "I don't think you'd like to exchange places with me."
Zhenya: "I can imagine! But it's still way more interesting than sitting in the library for days on end."
Pioneer: "You have weird ideas about interesting things…"
Zhenya: "Did you think about it?"
Pioneer: "About what?"
Zhenya: "What will happen next… tomorrow? We still need to meet somehow in the real world!"
Pioneer: "Oh, yeah, let me write your address down."
Zhenya: "Yeah, right, so you can send me a letter right now!"
*I smiled.*
Zhenya: "I'll memorize it, go ahead."
*We exchanged numbers and addresses.*
*It's weird that we didn't have this idea earlier.*
*I assume we never even hoped to get out of this world, and we just didn't want to remind ourselves about our past lives.*
Zhenya: "What do you think it will be like? The usual? We just fall asleep?"
*Zhenya clasped my hand and pressed her entire body against me.*
Pioneer: "I hope so. But in the end, this isn't the worst thing!"
Zhenya: "I'd say one of the better ones."
*Zhenya yawned and closed her eyes.*
Zhenya: "Sweet dreams. See you."
*I didn't say anything and just continued looking out the the window at the landscape that was flying by.*
*The Sovyonok camp was left behind, and I will never return there.*
*Yes, I was sure about that.*
*But it will always be a part of my life.*
*I've changed there, changed multiple times.*
*Compared to the time spent there, the mere 50-60 years that I have remaining in the real world are just a short moment, but I'll make sure to live them like a real human!*
Zhenya: "Yeah, you're probably bad, just as that pioneer said."
*Zhenya mumbled through her sleep.*
You: "What?"
Zhenya: "Nothing, just sleep already!"
*She laughed and pinched me painfully.*
*…*
*I wonder what everyone else felt in my place?*
*The same loss of consciousness in the first moments, the feeling of anxiety, panic?*
*I came back to my old apartment, but I didn't recognize any of it.*
*Yes, it definitely feels like being in a house that you lived in many years ago - everything looks to be in the right place, but you don't remember anything, you just think that this is how it's supposed to be.*
*I've already forgotten the day I've disappeared from this world (and I'm not so sure about the year either), but it's winter outside, and that means that not much time had passed here.*
*Yeah, I'm not 17 years old anymore, but I don't look like my real age either!*
*So, it turns out everything went ok? My return didn't have any unexpected consequences?*
*Zhenya…*
*I rushed to the table and wrote down the address and phone number with a shaking hand.*
*I obviously wouldn't be able to forget them, but it'd be better to have a backup anyway.*
*Now, what's next?*
*How does this world work anyway?*
*The laws are completely different here… none of which, to be honest, I've ever understood.*
*And now I'm like a newborn, forced to live an adult's life!*
*But let's save that for later, for now - I need to find Zhenya!*
*Someone rang the doorbell.*
*Humans. Real humans, not pioneers…*
*I've gotta open the door, what else can I do? I've finally returned, and I have to live in this world now.*
*I slowly walked up to the door, turned the key in the lock, grabbed the handle and froze.*
Zhenya: "So? How long should I stay in the doorway for?"
*I opened the door with a jerk, and I saw Zhenya…*
*She looked just like she did in the camp.*
You: "But… how?"
Zhenya: "Remember, I always arrived in the camp one week earlier than you? And I returned one week earlier."
*I forgot about Sovyonok, forgot about the real world, the only thing that matters is - we're together!*
*I grabbed Zhenya, and carried her into the room.*
Zhenya: "So, are we just going to stand around?"
You: "Ah, sorry…"
*Zhenya lightly jumped down onto the floor.*
Zhenya: "Wait a bit… We need to do this right now, we might not have time for it later."
*She smiled and started digging through her purse.*
Zhenya: "Give me your hand."
*I extended my arm out to her, and Zhenya put a ring on my finger.*
*Just a very basic one - like the one back in the camp.*
*In the dim light of a dusty ceiling lamp a golden ring was shining on her finger.*
You: "I think I should've bought the rings…"
Zhenya: "Well, judging by the looks of your man-cave I don't think you have the money for them."
*We laughed together, sincerely.*
*Real snow was slowly falling outside the window. White, beautiful snow, the darkness of the night sliced by thousands upon thousands of the lights of the big city which was singing with hundreds of voices, reminding us that we're still alive, and still together.*
*I gently moved my hand across Zhenya's cheek. Warm, real…*
You: "You won't disappear this time?"
Zhenya: "You better believe it! You still owe me money for the rings!"
*I hugged Zhenya, and kissed her like never before…*
